title: experimental_output can be caught in "unending stream of whitespace" responses with OpenAI
body:
### Description

### Problem

I've found that the `experimental_output` mode in `streamText` can run into the situation described here, https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/structured-outputs#json-mode, when your system instructions or messages include another JSON schema:

```
When using JSON mode, you must always instruct the model to produce JSON via some message in the conversation, for example via your system message. If you don't include an explicit instruction to generate JSON, the model may generate an unending stream of whitespace and the request may run continually until it reaches the token limit. To help ensure you don't forget, the API will throw an error if the string "JSON" does not appear somewhere in the context.
```

In my understanding, when using `experimental_output`, it seems that AI SDK appends the following text to the first `system` message:

`\n\nJSON schema: {experimental_output_schema}\nYou MUST answer with a JSON object that matches the JSON schema above.`

But if your system prompt includes another JSON schema within it, it can sometimes get confused between the schemas, and then the OpenAI API will go into the "unending stream of whitespace" mode from time to time.

### Solution

While it's possible we might consider this a bug in the OpenAI LLM itself, there does seem to be an easy fix that prevents this from happening.

The fix is to move the `\n\nJSON schema: .... You MUST answer with a JSON object...` text into its own system message at the end of all messages.

So previously the `messages` property sent to the API would be:

```
"messages": [
    {
      "role": "system",
      "content": "{my_system_message}\n\nJSON schema: {experimental_output_schema}\nYou MUST answer with a JSON object that matches the JSON schema above."
    }
   ...otherMessages
]
```

The fix would be:

```
"messages": [
    {
      "role": "system",
      "content": "{my_system_message}"
    }
   ...otherMessages,
    {
      "role": "system",
      "content": "### IMPORTANT: You MUST output your response in a JSON object matching the following schema\n\n{my_json_schema}"
    }
]
```

I've been able to confirm this works by hardcoding that final message into the `messages` parameter in the `streamText` function using `experimental_output`.


### Code example

```typescript
const { experimental_partialOutputStream } = streamText({
    model: model,
    system: `Ask the user to give the information required to return a JSON object that conforms to the following schema:\n\n## JSON Schema\n\n${mySchema}`,
    messages: messages
    experimental_output: Output.object({
        schema: outputSchema
    })
});
```

### AI provider

@ai-sdk/openai 1.3.6

### Additional context

_No response_

title: Agents/Tool Calling: Pass data to subsequent steps without showing it to the LLM (return of execute())
body:
### Feature Description

Right now when you return data from `execute` within a `tool`, that data is included in the next request to the LLM. 

It would be nice if we were able to return some data that could be accessed in following steps or outside of the agent loop, that is nicely tied to a specific step. 

Currently this _is_ possible by keeping external state, but it's kind of ugly.

This is especially important if you have larger data that the LLM does not need to see.

### Use Cases

Tool 2 requires variables/state determined in Tool 1, but the LLM does not need to see that data.

### Additional context

I'm not sure what the right design for this would be, but think it could be nice for the return type of `execute` to have two fields: 

{
exposed: 
hidden: 
}

exposed goes to the LLM (like how it does currently) and hidden: does not. Can use a type guard to make this backwards compatible, if these keys are not seen then we just treat it the same way it is now.

title: Support for Zod v4
body:
Hi Maintainers,

Zod v4 was recently announced ([Introducing Zod 4 beta](https://v4.zod.dev/v4)) and is currently in beta. It brings significant improvements over v3, including:

*   Major performance gains (parsing strings, arrays, objects)
*   Reduced core bundle size
*   Improved TypeScript compiler efficiency
*   New features like `z.interface()`, JSON schema conversion, metadata, etc.

While Zod v4 introduces breaking changes (detailed in the [Migration Guide](https://v4.zod.dev/v4/changelog)), upgrading would allow users of `ai` to benefit from these enhancements, especially when defining complex schemas for tools or input/output validation.

Could you please consider adding support for Zod v4 in `ai`? It would be helpful to understand if there are plans to address compatibility with the upcoming stable release of Zod v4.

Thank you for your great work on this library!

  ## Context
  I'm implementing a system with the AI SDK and have set up an MCP server with both tools and resources. I've successfully integrated the MCP tools with the AI SDK using `experimental_createMCPClient()` and

  const mcpClient = await createMCPClient({

  3. Including resource URIs in the system prompt

title: Google Gemini model fails to use tools properly in follow-up messages (gemini-2.5-pro-preview-03-25)
body:
## Description
We're experiencing inconsistent behavior with the Google Gemini model (`gemini-2.5-pro-preview-03-25`) when used with the Vercel AI SDK's `streamText` function with tools. The model works correctly for the first user message but fails to properly use tools in follow-up messages within the same conversation.

Our implementation follows the same pattern as the RAG chatbot example in the Vercel AI SDK docs (https://sdk.vercel.ai/docs/guides/rag-chatbot), but with multiple tools covering different information areas.

## Environment
- Vercel AI SDK (latest version)
- Google Gemini model: `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-03-25`
- Next.js application App router API routes

## Expected Behavior
The model should consistently select and execute appropriate tools throughout the entire conversation, including follow-up questions that require clarification or additional information from previously used tools.

## Actual Behavior
In follow-up messages, the model:
1. Refuses to use previously used tools that would be appropriate
2. Claims it will use a tool but doesn't actually execute it
3. Hallucinates answers instead of retrieving information
4. Sometimes starts answering without tools, then uses a tool at the very end

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Set up a conversation with the Gemini model using `streamText` with multiple tools
2. Send an initial query that successfully uses tools to retrieve information
3. Send a follow-up question that requires using the same tools again

## Additional Information
- Only occurs with Gemini - Claude models work correctly throughout conversations
- First message always works as expected with proper tool usage
- Filtering out tool messages with `coreMessage.filter((msg) => msg.role !== 'tool')` didn't help
- Each tool retrieves specific contextual information from different information areas

Is this a known issue with the Gemini integration? Any workarounds available?

title: File names in experimental_attachments are replaced with auto-generated IDs when using Bedrock provider
body:
### Description

# Bug: File names in experimental_attachments are replaced with auto-generated IDs when using Bedrock provider

## Issue Description

When using the Vercel AI SDK with Amazon Bedrock to communicate with Claude models, file attachments sent via `experimental_attachments` don't preserve their original filenames. Instead, the SDK generates random IDs with format `file-[randomstring].pdf`, which appear in Claude's XML representation.

### Example

When I send a PDF file with `experimental_attachments[0].name = "my-document.pdf"`, Claude receives and displays the file as:

```xml
<documents allow_instructions=false>
<document index="1">
<source>file-0V2igIJ9w0czZslx.pdf</source>
<document_content>[content of the document]</document_content>
</document>
</documents>
```

The original filename `my-document.pdf` is lost and replaced with `file-0V2igIJ9w0czZslx.pdf`.

## Investigation

The issue occurs in the Amazon Bedrock adapter in the Vercel AI SDK. When converting messages to the Bedrock format, it explicitly ignores the original filename and generates a new one:

```javascript
// In @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock/dist/index.js
bedrockContent.push({
  document: {
    format: (_e = (_d = part.mimeType) == null ? void 0 : _d.split("/")) == null ? void 0 : _e[1],
    name: generateFileId(),  // <-- This is the culprit
    source: {
      bytes: part.data
    }
  }
});
```

The `generateFileId()` function creates a string with the format `file-[randomstring]`:

```javascript
// In @ai-sdk/provider-utils
var generateFileId = (0, import_provider_utils2.createIdGenerator)({ prefix: "file", size: 16 });
```

The file extension appears to be added later, possibly by Bedrock or Claude, based on the MIME type's format field.

## Impact

This behavior creates problems in user experience and functionality:

1. Users can't identify their files by name in Claude's response
2. The random IDs make it difficult to track which file is which
3. Any context provided by the filename is lost to the model
4. Makes debugging more difficult when examining the model's inputs

## Reproduction Steps

1. Create an application using Vercel AI SDK with Amazon Bedrock
2. Configure it to use Claude models (claude-3-5-sonnet, etc.)
3. Include one or more file attachments in `experimental_attachments`
4. Observe that the filenames are replaced with generated IDs in Claude's XML representation

## Expected Behavior

The original filenames from `experimental_attachments[].name` should be preserved when sending files to Claude via Amazon Bedrock. The XML representation should include the original filename:

```xml
<documents allow_instructions=false>
<document index="1">
<source>my-document.pdf</source>
<document_content>[content of the document]</document_content>
</document>
</documents>
```

## Environment

- Vercel AI SDK version: 4.1.54 
- @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock version: 2.1.1
- Claude model: claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0

## Suggested Fix

Modify the `convertToBedrockChatMessages` function in `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` to preserve the original filename when available:

```javascript
bedrockContent.push({
  document: {
    format: (_e = (_d = part.mimeType) == null ? void 0 : _d.split("/")) == null ? void 0 : _e[1],
    name: part.fileName || generateFileId(), // Use original name when available
    source: {
      bytes: part.data
    }
  }
});
```

**Note:** The actual implementation will need to determine exactly which property from the attachment contains the filename, as this may depend on how the SDK structures attachment data internally.

title: Can we make onStepFinish do more?
body:
### Description

Although this project provides many interfaces and implements basic tool calls chain through maxSteps, it is still far from sufficient for building a complete agent system. I believe that these can be achieved by extending the ability of `onStepFinish`, rather than just providing a callback function.

1. (to use cached input, this may no longer be the best solution) Modify the system prompt between steps, the system prompt will provide many status or conditions that will be changed during the call, always use the initial system prompt will bring a lot of problems.
2. Modify the tools between steps, no need to use all the tools in each step.
3. Decide whether 'continue' or 'stop', rather than use the response from model, the ground truth is much more accurate than the model's judgement.

Just let `onStepFinish` return an object contains the above properties, and use them in the next call.

title: [v5] enable `standard-schema` usage where possible
body:
## Background

We want to support [standard-schema](https://github.com/standard-schema/standard-schema) instead of zod schemas in custom validators.

We will keep the `zod` dependency for internal validations (e.g. for user inputs and parts of provider API responses, e.g. [packages/ai/core/generate-object/generate-object.ts](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/7ea4132624d8ab83f1f9713020e4c76bd6c2036b/packages/ai/core/generate-object/generate-object.ts#L61-L70)). The motivation to use `standard-schema` instead of `zod` in the validate type methods is to enable model providers to use their own preferred way of validation that is compatible with `standard-schema`. The same is true for users of our UI adapters like React, users should be able to utilize their schema validation library of choice instead of forcing them to use `zod`.

Users bring validators in two ways

1. Instruct providers to generate structural output following a provided schema (needs conversion to JSON Schema, see also [valibot/src/valibot-schema.ts](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/59e0fcdde18de92ffae75e1fdae5a0dd7ea9d0bd/packages/valibot/src/valibot-schema.ts))
2. Validation library for the frontend. Will become more important in the future for typed tool calls, typed custom data in React components

## Summary

This issue is about updating the type of [the `schema` argument of the `validateTypes()` method](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/4bd27a9b8e8f264bef3a9442906488a725609b16/packages/provider-utils/src/validate-types.ts#L16) used by providers. We want to replace the use of `z.Schema` [here](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/4bd27a9b8e8f264bef3a9442906488a725609b16/packages/provider-utils/src/validate-types.ts#L19) and [here](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/4bd27a9b8e8f264bef3a9442906488a725609b16/packages/provider-utils/src/validate-types.ts#L44) with standard schema. We can keep the custom validators.

The [`validator.validate()` call](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/4bd27a9b8e8f264bef3a9442906488a725609b16/packages/provider-utils/src/validate-types.ts#L55) is currently synchronous, but introducing `standard-schema` makes it possible to set schema requirements with async validations, which means that `validator.validate()` will have to be async, and in turn `safeValidateTypes()` and `validateTypes()` will have to be made async.

It might make sense to decouple the introduction of `standard-schema` to the aync API change, by starting a pull request that simply makes `safeValidateTypes()` async without any other changes.

## Tasks

- [x] #5779
- [ ] replace the use of `z.Schema` [here](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/4bd27a9b8e8f264bef3a9442906488a725609b16/packages/provider-utils/src/validate-types.ts#L19) and [here](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/4bd27a9b8e8f264bef3a9442906488a725609b16/packages/provider-utils/src/validate-types.ts#L44) with standard schema. Potentially other places like [parseJSON](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/7ea4132624d8ab83f1f9713020e4c76bd6c2036b/packages/provider-utils/src/parse-json.ts#L31) and [safeParseJSON](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/7ea4132624d8ab83f1f9713020e4c76bd6c2036b/packages/provider-utils/src/parse-json.ts#L84) and in the UI (e.g. [packages/react/src/use-object.ts](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/59e0fcdde18de92ffae75e1fdae5a0dd7ea9d0bd/packages/react/src/use-object.ts#L29))
- [ ] Add `standard-schema` validator next to [`zodValidator`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/7ea4132624d8ab83f1f9713020e4c76bd6c2036b/packages/provider-utils/src/validator.ts#L52-L61) which would need to be async, therefore [the `Validator.validate()` type](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/7ea4132624d8ab83f1f9713020e4c76bd6c2036b/packages/provider-utils/src/validator.ts#L18-L22) would need to be async 
- [ ] potential follow up: look into replacing internal use of `zod` with a minimal version of `zod`

### Resources

- Compare https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/5479

title: Inconsistent Error Handling: Vertex AI on Edge Runtime Returns Empty Error ({}) and Skips Retries, Unlike Standard Google API
body:
### Description

Hi Vercel AI SDK Team,
We are utilizing the Vercel AI SDK within the Vercel Edge Runtime to interface with Google AI services, specifically comparing the behavior of the Vertex AI provider (@ai-sdk/google-vertex/edge) and the standard Google Generative AI provider (@ai-sdk/google). We've encountered a significant inconsistency in error handling when using the Vertex AI provider on the Edge Runtime.
Problem Description:
When making identical streamText calls (using the same simple test messages and target model ID) within the Vercel Edge Runtime environment, we observe different error handling behaviors depending on the provider used:
Using the vertex(...) client (@ai-sdk/google-vertex/edge): Intermittent failures during the stream generation (often occurring after ~10 seconds, suggesting network issues) result in the onError callback receiving an empty error object ({}). Consequently, the SDK's retry logic does not seem to identify this as a recoverable error, and no retry attempt is made. This leads to a direct failure of the API call.
Using the google(...) client (@ai-sdk/google): Similar intermittent failures under the same conditions manifest as clearly identifiable errors (e.g., ConnectTimeoutError wrapped in AI_APICallError) which include flags like isRetryable: true. The SDK correctly identifies these errors and successfully retries the operation.
This difference in behavior has been consistently observed when switching between the two provider implementations in our configuration, keeping all other factors (Edge runtime, input messages, model ID, SDK version) constant.
Evidence/Logs:
The distinction is clear in our logs:
Vertex AI call log (empty error, no retry):

    [Timestamp][AI-Generation][ERROR]: Streaming generation failed {"error":{},"params":{...},"duration":10241}
    [Timestamp][ErrorHandling][ERROR]: onError callback triggered {"error":{}}

Standard Google AI call log (identifiable error, successful retry):

    [Timestamp][AI-Generation][ERROR]: Streaming generation failed {"error":{"name":"AI_APICallError","cause":{"name":"ConnectTimeoutError",...},"isRetryable":true},"params":{...},"duration":10316}
    [Timestamp][AI-Generation][INFO]: Starting streaming generation {"params":{...}} // Retry initiated
    [Timestamp][AI-Generation][INFO]: Streaming generation finished {"duration":4069,...} // Retry succeeded

(Note: Log prefixes like [AI-Generation], [ErrorHandling] are internal identifiers)
Expected Behavior:
We expect that errors encountered during streamText calls using the @ai-sdk/google-vertex/edge provider on the Edge Runtime, particularly those related to network connectivity or timeouts, would be captured and represented with sufficient detail to allow the core AI SDK's retry mechanisms to function effectively, mirroring the behavior observed with the @ai-sdk/google provider.
Actual Behavior:
The @ai-sdk/google-vertex/edge provider yields an empty error object ({}) for certain failures when run on the Edge Runtime, which bypasses the SDK's retry capabilities.
Impact:
This inconsistency significantly reduces the reliability of using Vertex AI via the AI SDK on the Vercel Edge Runtime compared to using the standard Google Generative AI endpoint, as transient issues cause hard failures instead of being mitigated by retries.
Environment:
Vercel Edge Runtime
Latest Vercel AI SDK packages (including @ai-sdk/google-vertex, @ai-sdk/google, ai)
This leads us to suspect a potential issue within the @ai-sdk/google-vertex/edge package, specifically concerning its error handling and reporting mechanisms within the Vercel Edge environment.
We would appreciate it if you could investigate this behavior. Please let us know if any further information or specific reproduction steps would be helpful.
Thank you for your time and effort on this great library.

 "@ai-sdk/google-vertex": "^2.2.15",
"ai": "^4.3.1",
"@ai-sdk/google": "^1.2.7",

title: [maintenance] trigger CI for "Version Packages" pull requests
body:
### Description

Example: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/5837

These pull requests are created via the `release.yml` workflow:
https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/7206b1f58a6c3fc6d4442999569e2679c28e9017/.github/workflows/release.yml#L39-L48

The reason that these pull requests do not trigger CI is that we pass `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` for authentication. That token is conveniently provided to GitHub workflows automatically, but it has some limitations. One of them is that tasks performed using  `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger other GitHub Actions (except for `workflow_dispatch` and `repository_dispatch` events)

https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-when-your-workflow-runs/triggering-a-workflow#triggering-a-workflow-from-a-workflow

In order to workaround it we can register a single-purpose GitHub app and then utilize the official [actions/create-github-app-token](https://github.com/actions/create-github-app-token) action to create an access token for that app. Up to 100 GitHub apps can be registered per organization, and I think GitHub can bump this limit should it ever become necessary.

### Tasks

- [x] Register private GitHub app on @vercel. e.g. `vercel-ai-skd`. Disable webhooks, permissions: `contents:write` and `pull_requests:write`.

  [<kbd>Register here</kbd>](https://github.com/organizations/vercel/settings/apps/new?name=vercel-ai-sdk&url=https://github.com/vercel&webhook_active=0&contents=write&pull_requests=write)

- [x] Add the GitHub App's Client ID as repository variable (e.g. `VERCEL_AI_SDK_GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID`) and the private key as repository secret (e.g. `VERCEL_AI_SDK_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_PKCS8`)

- [x] Install the GitHub App on the @vercel organization, selected repositories -> only select `ai`

- [x] Before the "Create Release Pull Request or Publish to npm" step in the release workflow ([source](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/7206b1f58a6c3fc6d4442999569e2679c28e9017/.github/workflows/release.yml#L39C15-L39C60)), add a step to create the installation access token, like this

  ```yml
  - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v2
    id: app-token
    with:
      app-id: ${{ vars.VERCEL_AI_SDK_GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
      private-key: ${{ secrets. VERCEL_AI_SDK_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_PKCS8 }}
  ```

- [x] In the "Create Release Pull Request or Publish to npm" step in the release workflow, replace `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` with `${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}` ([source](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/7206b1f58a6c3fc6d4442999569e2679c28e9017/.github/workflows/release.yml#L47))

title: [maintenance] enforce `patch` in `.changeset/*.md` files from contributors
body:
### Description

Vercel does not follow semantic versioning for `vercel/ai` packages. Instead, it uses `patch` for bug fixes and features. See documentation at https://sdk.vercel.ai/docs/migration-guides/versioning

A `minor` version bump is reserved for "marketing" releases that aggregate improvements since the last minor release, accommodated by blog post.

In the past, contributions slipped through with a changeset using `minor` which resulted in confusion due to a lacking blog post. In order to prevent that from happening again, we want to implement a CI check that enforces the use of `patch`, except for pull requests that intentionally release a new minor release. We could either check if [a migration guide has been added](https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/5290/files#diff-91799f77862f5738c951936e6af443fb4b1d88afae225eefc54bac8a526d9a10) or look for the presence of a dedicated label

title: Support propertyOrdering for google models
body:
### Description

Property ordering is extremely important when generating JSON. Google's API requires you to set a 
propertyOrdering key when sending requests to its API in order to guarantee a specific ordering: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/structured-output?lang=node#property-ordering

This is currently not exposed to the user in the Vercel SDK. I tried setting it through the middleware but unfortunately in the actual provider implementation it's being ripped out.

While making this actually part of the interface might be difficult since this is not a standard json schema property, a one-liner way to support this would simply be to pass the property through if it exists here: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/google/src/convert-json-schema-to-openapi-schema.ts#L33

i.e. It will be the user's responsibility to modify the json schema to have the `propertyOrdering` property, vercel SDK will simply pass it through to Vertex if it exists.

title: Feature Request: Expose Unified AI Providers
body:
### Description

Most people are using Vercel SDK to build multiple unified providers anyways. Why not build it in the library itself for once?

Provider a common API to support multiple providers and directly expose them.

Examples include: https://github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master/pull/240 but I've seen many others in the wild (also implementing one myself)

Maybe a cookbook might be helpful or if there's a way to expose it in the library without increasing its size via tree-shaking. The current `@ai-sdk/*` seems like it is done the same way since I install different npm packages.

For example:

```ts
import { createAnthropic } from '@ai-sdk/anthropic'
import { createGoogleGenerativeAI } from '@ai-sdk/google'
import { createOpenAI } from '@ai-sdk/openai'

export function createAIClient(id: string, apiKey: string) {
	switch (id) {
		case 'openai':
			return createOpenAI({ apiKey })
		case 'anthropic':
			return createAnthropic({ apiKey })
		case 'gemini':
                default:
			return createGoogleGenerativeAI({ apiKey })
}

...
// some more code that exposes a common api... modelInstance is the model selected by end user (not developer) from a particular provider
...

unifiedAPI.generateText({ model: modelInstance, maxTokens, temperature, messages })

```

I think this will save insane amount of time rather than re-implementing the same code again & again which most people are doing. And instead of supporting 5, all of the APIs can be supported at once since most are copying OpenAI anyways. Only need few methods like generateText, generateImage, streamText, etc...

All chat apps like poe.com, typingmind.com, etc... support multiple providers & this can be tested at once.

Even the above code implementation can be simplified by not having to install 5 different provider libraries. Can even do a simple web app that gives code to install only the libraries that are needed in your fav package managers like pnpm or bun.

For example:

```ts
import { createUnifiedProvider } from '@ai-sdk/unified'

const unifiedAPI = createUnifiedProvider({ providers: ['gemini', 'openai'] , apiKeys: { gemini: 'xxxx', openai: 'xxxx' } })

unifiedAPI.generateText({ provider: endUserProvider, model: endUserModel, maxTokens, temperature, messages })
```

What do ya'll think?

### Description

The `maxImagesPerCall` setting sets the number of images that are requested in a single API call

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/9bd5ab57a32142e55654ee805134b609ef33f605/packages/provider/src/image-model/v2/image-model-v2.ts#L35-L39

Providers have defaults per image model:

We want to support use cases where the `maxImagesPerCall` number is not known at the time of the `generateImage()` call, which will require `maxImagesPerCall` to be retrieved asynchronously before the actual API call is done

<!--

In future, a minimal SDK that uses an API gateway might not have the information of how many images can be requested per API call at the time of the request, since the model can be set to a string instead of a model object. In order to be able to retrieve `maxImagesPerCall` for a given model from the API gateway, the `maxImagesPerCall` getter needs to be made async

title: Urgent Guidance Needed: Server `onFinish` lacks consistent Message ID access between `streamText` & `streamObject`
body:
### Description

Hi Vercel AI SDK Team,

We are building a complex agent system using `ai/react` (v4.3.7) and the core `ai` package. We rely heavily on `useChat` (client) and both `streamText`/`streamObject` (server).

**The Core Problem (Refined):**

Our server-side `onFinish` callback (handling results from `streamText` or `streamObject`) **critically needs a reliable message identifier** associated with the completed assistant response *at the time `onFinish` executes*. This is essential for database linking, feedback correlation via annotations, and logging.

**Our Investigation & Source Code Findings:**

After extensive research and **diving into the SDK source code** (`stream-text.ts`, `stream-object.ts`, `use-chat.ts`), we've pinpointed the challenge:

1.  **`streamText` Behavior:** We confirmed `streamText` (via its internal `streamStep` logic) generates an ID (`backendMessageId`) early in the process. This ID *is* accessible within its server-side `onFinish` callback via the `StepResult` parameter (specifically through structures containing `responseMessages`). While `useChat` on the client generates its own `frontendMessageId` (likely using the same default generator, causing apparent consistency sometimes), the key is that `streamText`'s `onFinish` *does* receive a backend-generated ID.
2.  **`streamObject` Discrepancy:** Our source code analysis confirms that `streamObject`'s internal implementation **fundamentally differs**. It focuses directly on parsing the target object from the stream and does *not* employ the same multi-step tracking or `StepResult` structure. Consequently, its `onFinish` callback **does not receive** an equivalent early-generated `backendMessageId`. The parameters (`object`, `usage`, `response` metadata) reflect its object-centric goal, lacking the message-level ID context available in `streamText`.
3.  **The Inconsistency:** This difference means our server-side `onFinish` handler faces an **inconsistent situation**: it can get a message ID when the underlying call was `streamText`, but *cannot* when it was `streamObject`. This prevents us from having a unified logic flow in our handler that reliably uses a message ID.
4.  **Other Approaches Re-evaluated:** Knowing this discrepancy reinforces why other methods failed to provide a direct solution:
    *   *Server-generated ID + Early Annotation:* Still faces the difficulty of forcing `useChat` to adopt it reliably.
    *   *`experimental_streamData`:* Excellent for sending a *server* ID (like `workId`) to the *client*, but doesn't give the *server `onFinish`* the needed ID when `streamObject` is used.
    *   *Client-side `onFinish` / `generateId`:* Operate purely on the client, not helping the server callback.

**The Dilemma & Urgency (Updated):**

This **confirmed inconsistency** between `streamText` and `streamObject` regarding message ID availability in the server `onFinish` callback is the core of our struggle. It forces us towards workarounds like using a separate `workId` generated earlier in the backend, passing it via `experimental_streamData`, and requiring the client to manually associate this `workId` with the `useChat`-generated `frontendMessageId`.

While functional, this workaround feels indirect and adds complexity primarily because the SDK provides inconsistent ID accessibility in the `onFinish` callbacks of its two main streaming functions.

We are urgently seeking guidance on the **intended or recommended pattern** for reliably associating backend completion logic (in `onFinish`) with the specific assistant message, **especially considering the differing behaviors of `streamText` and `streamObject`**.

*   Is there a mechanism we've missed to get a consistent identifier in `onFinish` for *both* stream types?
*   Given the confirmed implementation difference, is the `workId` + `experimental_streamData` + client-side association the expected approach to handle this?

Clarification on how to best manage this, ensuring robust server-side processing that can reliably reference the corresponding message, would be **immensely helpful**. We are very keen to align with the SDK's best practices.

Thank you for your time and the powerful library!

(Using `ai` package version: 4.3.7)

title: The attachment url is not passed to the LLM
body:
### Description

I followed the [multimodal guide](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/guides/multi-modal-chatbot) and noticed that the LLM doesn’t seem to receive attachment metadata, only the raw file data.

My use case is that I have an image editing tool using the gpt-image-1 model, which takes a list of image URLs. When I add attachments using `Attachment[]`, I expected the LLM to get the URL information from the list and use it with the tool. It seems that this info isn’t passed to the LLM call.

As a workaround, I’m calling a `processMessages` function before invoking the LLM. It extracts the attachment info and includes it as extra text part in the user message.

Is there a better way to include additional metadata in the current message? `prepareRequestBody` doesn’t quite work for this since it’s not tied to a specific message and doesn’t persist across calls.

title: `ImagePart`s sent via experimental_telemetry are bloated
body:
### Description

For `doGenerate` spans, image data is sent as `Uint8Array`, on which `JSON.stringify` acts very weirdly, resulting in a 5-10x bloat on average:

```
Welcome to Node.js v23.3.0.
Type ".help" for more information.
> JSON.stringify(new Uint8Array([42, 33, 22]))
'{"0":42,"1":33,"2":22}'
// I would expect '[42, 33, 22]' probably
```

As a telemetry provider (Laminar), we can implement some conversions on our backend, but I believe this is rather a client side bug than a feature. My understanding is that Uint8Arrays are compact (about 3/4 the size of a base64 string) and easy to carry around in JS, that's why we convert image data to that format. But I'd say such stringification goes against the whole purpose of using a compact data structure.

I tried tracing where and why this happens. Roughly:

`JSON.stringify(promptMessages)` in [core/generate-text/generate-text.ts](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/ai/core/generate-text/generate-text.ts#L373-L375)
->
`convertToLanguageModelPrompt` in [core/prompt/convert-to-language-model-prompt.ts](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/ai/core/prompt/convert-to-language-model-prompt.ts#L24)
-> (via several calls in the same file)
`convertDataContentToUint8Array` in [core/prompt/convert-to-language-model-prompt.ts](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/ai/core/prompt/convert-to-language-model-prompt.ts#L317)
->
`convertBase64ToUint8Array` in [core/prompt/data-content.ts](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/ai/core/prompt/data-content.ts#L52)

See also [MDN docs examples of JSON.stringify](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/stringify#examples)

title: Feature request: Adding prioritization to prompts
body:
### Description

Motivation: Some of the application that can be built using Vercel AI could be making multiple model calls at the same time, through multiple agents doing different tasks running at the same time. 
In these scenarios we may hit limit for tokens, or may want to prioritize some model calls over other.
Alternatively, we could be sending too many requests to a single AI model, so we may hit limits there as well. 
In these cases simple prompt may not go through, we may need to add some prioritization to prompts as well as models to have more control over the user experience.

Proposed feature: We integrate a prioritized prompts and prioritized model selection to Vercel's AI SDK. These features will make it much more powerful tool.

Inspiration:
https://github.com/anysphere/priompt
We could directly use this library maybe to allow prioritization for prompts.

It seems like a slightly larger effort, I am willing to work on it though, please let me know your thoughts.

title: tool-calls will silently fail while LLM generate a wrong json when using `streamText` in `openai-compatible` provider
body:
### Description

### Background:

I am trying to use @ai-sdk/openai-compatible with Vllm 0.9.0 and Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B.

```text
docker run --device=[nvidia.com/gpu=all](http://nvidia.com/gpu=all) \
	--name "Qwen3-30B-A3B" \
	-d \
    --ipc=host \
    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
	--env "HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com/" \
    --env "HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN=xxxxxxx" \
    --env "NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1" \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    vllm/vllm-openai:v0.9.0 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \
    --api-key xxxxxxxxxxxxx \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser hermes \
    --enable-reasoning \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
    --disable-log-requests
```

### Issue Description:​

Certain sessions unexpectedly terminate with finishReason: "tool_calls" without any actual tool call being sent. Upon investigation, it appears the LLM generated malformed JSON for the tool parameter(s), which caused the processing pipeline to block tool call invocation.

I attempted to use `experimental_repairToolCall` to handle the invalid JSON, but the function was never triggered. 

### Why it will happen

Since the current method checks whether the parameters generated by LLM are legal JSON before sending a tool-call, this causes that if LLM generates an illegal JSON, we cannot send a tool-call in the existing processing flow, and also makes `experimental_repairToolCall` unable to perceive the error and thus not be called.

```ts
                // check if tool call is complete
                if (
                  toolCall.function?.name != null
                  && toolCall.function?.arguments != null
                  && isParsableJson(toolCall.function.arguments) // <-- here
                ) {
                  controller.enqueue({
                    type: 'tool-call',
                    toolCallType: 'function',
                    toolCallId: toolCall.id ?? generateId(),
                    toolName: toolCall.function.name,
                    args: toolCall.function.arguments,
                  });
                  toolCall.hasFinished = true;
                }
```


### A passable way to fix

Add the following code as the final safeguard in the existing processing pipeline: ​​send all tool-calls unconditionally​​, regardless of parameter validity. If parameter errors exist, they will then be handled by `experimental_repairToolCall`.

```ts
            if (finishReason === 'tool-calls') {
              for (const toolCall of toolCalls) {
                if (toolCall.hasFinished) {
                  continue;
                }
                controller.enqueue({
                  type: 'tool-call',
                  toolCallType: 'function',
                  toolCallId: toolCall.id,
                  toolName: toolCall.function.name,
                  args: toolCall.function.arguments ?? '',
                });
              }
            }
```

title: prepareStep should allow response message modification
body:
### Description

**Motivation**
When `maxSteps` is greater than 1, the `onStepFinish` callback receives `response.messages` as cloned copies, preventing modification of the messages before the subsequent step. In agentic workflows, it is often beneficial to modify message content - for example, to manage context length or remove redundant/irrelevant messages - before the next iteration.

**Solution**
Introduce an optional `beforeNextStep` (or `experimental_beforeNextStep`) function within `streamText`/`generateText`. This function will receive an array of messages from the previous steps and should return a new array of messages to be used in the next iteration. The default behavior will be to return the received array of messages unchanged.

title: Feature Request: Add endTool behavior to terminate agent run after specific tool is called
body:
### Description

Hi Vercel team,

Thank you for building the Vercel AI SDK — the `experimental_activeTools` feature is already very helpful for managing tool availability within constrained model contexts.

I’d like to propose a related feature: **a way to stop the entire agent run immediately after a specific tool is invoked**. For example, I’d like to define a tool such that once it is called, **the agent halts execution and does not continue with further tool invocations or text generation**.

### Use Case

In many agent workflows, there is a clear “termination condition” — e.g., the user triggers a `submit`, `confirm`, or `exit` tool. Once this happens, the assistant should **not continue generating any response**, nor invoke any additional tools.

Right now, even if a tool is invoked, the agent might continue with follow-up messages, which can be undesirable in certain structured flows.

### Proposed Feature: `endTool`

A potential API could look like:

```ts
tools: {
  submitForm: {
    call: async () => { ... },
    endTool: true
  }
}
```

Or a separate runtime behavior:

```ts
const result = await generateText({
  model: openai('gpt-4o'),
  tools: myToolSet,
  experimental_activeTools: ['submitForm', 'otherTool'],
  endToolNames: ['submitForm'], // agent stops once submitForm is called
});
```

### Benefits

(1) Enables clean workflow cut-off behavior
(2) Avoids undesired assistant output after critical actions
(3) Makes tool-based agent orchestration easier and more predictable

Would love your thoughts on this! I believe this behavior would be very helpful in designing multi-step tools with clear termination conditions.

Thanks again for your fantastic work on this SDK.

title: [Feature Request] Add native citation support when using Cohere's Command A model
body:
### Description

We are currently trying to support Cohere's Command A model in our documentation chatbot. One necessary feature for go-live is citations - we need the LLM to return a list of URLs to the documents it used to generate its response. When using other models like Claude 3.5, we're able to get the model to consistently output URLs in its response with the system prompt, but Command A isn't as malleable in this way.

When working with the Cohere team, they recommended we use their native Citations feature, which involves turning on this flag (https://docs.cohere.com/v2/reference/chat-stream#request.body.citation_options) when streaming text, which will force the LLM to output a list of URLs after it's done responding. This flag is available when working with Cohere's SDK directly, but not when going through AI-SDK currently.

Was wondering if it would be possible to add support for this Cohere SDK Citations feature in AI-SDK to unblock us working with Cohere.

For additional context on their native Citations feature, here's another relevant page from their docs: https://docs.cohere.com/v2/docs/tool-use-citations#accurate-citations

title: Reasoning parts should include a `summary_index` field to distinguish between different reasoning summaries
body:
### Description

Openai returns many reasoning summaries, each one has a different `summary_index` number, for example a reasoning delta can have the following shape:

```js
{
  type: 'response.reasoning_summary_text.delta',
  item_id: 'rs_6840931d804c81989497d944ce3842010581aba909b8922e',
  output_index: 0,
  summary_index: 2,
  delta: '!'
}
```

The reasoning items returned by `ai` `fullStream` instead have the following shape:

```json
{
  "type": "reasoning",
  "reasoning": "..."
}
```

Because of this issue if the UI tries to render the reasoning summaries there will be parts where 2 summaries are put one besides the other, where the next summaries starts after a dot without a space, for example:

`... the weather for each in a final output.**Planning weather calls**\n\nI need to ca`



Without this field it's impossible to render the reasoning summaries nicely because there is no new line between reasoning summaries 

### AI SDK Version

Both v5 and v4 miss this field

## Context

The field would be added here:
https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/02357659fd09eef79d75f011b789cda63eb43380/packages/openai/src/responses/openai-responses-language-model.ts#L485

### Description

Hi! Thanks for the great SDK.

I noticed an issue that Zod schema for a `generateText` structured outputs tool call doesn't respect `multipleOf` or `step`. I'm using `parameters` attr for `generateText`, w/ `('gpt-4.1', {structuredOutputs: true })` and `toolChoice: 'required'`:

```
const schema = z.object({
    myVar: z.number().min(-3).max(3)
})

and I always get a number e.g. `{ myVar: 2 }` related to the prompt.

But this does not work:
```
const schema = z.object({
    myVar: z.number().min(-3).max(3).multipleOf(1)
})
```
and I only get `{ myVar: 0 }` (same exact prompt as previous schema and tested a bunch of times).

Same issue for:

```
const schema = z.object({
    myVar: z.number().min(-3).max(3).step(1)
})
```

And doesn't matter if I do something other than 1 for the `step` or `multipleOf` either.

Not sure if it's a limitation/mistake in [OpenAI docs](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/structured-outputs?api-mode=responses#supported-schemas) but they do say they now support `multipleOf` (which I know is a relatively recent development for them).

Side question: what is the canonical best/most reliable way to guarantee object structure back if using OpenAI w/ AI SDK? I assume it's `generateText` w/ `structuredOutputs: true` and `toolChoice: 'required`, and didn't see AI SDK docs mention structured outputs in `generateObject`.

Much appreciated!

createVertex({

Currently, in the v5 branch, there's an inconsistency in how file Content-Type is handled. title: `providerOptions.stream_options` No Longer Effective in Latest SDK, Preventing Usage Data for DeepSeek/Volcengine
body:
### Description

As suggested in issue #4929 (https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/4929#issuecomment-2753145492), setting the custom parameter `stream_options` via `providerOptions` was the solution to correctly receive `usage` information when calling the DeepSeek API (Alibaba Cloud / Volcengine). This solution worked as recently as March.

However, after the merge of pull request #5873, `providerOptions.stream_options` is no longer effective. Consequently, even when setting `stream_options: { include_usage: true }`, the SDK fails to retrieve the correct `usage` data, which consistently returns as `null`.

**Steps to Reproduce**
1.  Use the latest versions of `ai-sdk` and `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`.
2.  Pass `stream_options: { include_usage: true }` via `providerOptions`.
3.  Observe that the returned `usage` remains `null`.

**Expected Behavior**

We expect the ability to pass `stream_options` to the underlying request to be restored or provided via a new mechanism (either still within `providerOptions` or another parameter). This is essential to receive the `usage` information correctly.

*   Related Historical Issue: #4929
*   Related PR: #5873

title: Support global endpoint for Vertex AI models
body:
### Description

Currently, the SDK assumes that all Vertex AI models are hosted in region-specific endpoints like:

```
https://${region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${project}/locations/${region}/publishers/google
```

However, this pattern **fails for the `global` region**, which uses a different base URL:

```
https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/...
```

[Google’s official documentation](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/locations#genai-partner-models) confirms that some models are **only available in the global region**, especially on initial release. For example, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`.

When attempting to use such models with `GOOGLE_VERTEX_LOCATION="global"`, the following error occurs:

```
APICallError [AI_APICallError]: Publisher Model `projects/[PROJECT_ID]/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-06-17` was not found...
```

The request is incorrectly sent to:

```
https://global-aiplatform.googleapis.com/...
```

Instead of:

```
https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/...
```

### Related PR

title: [Bug]: Metro resolution failed in React Native (Expo) for "eventsource-parser/stream"
body:
### Description

### Environment

- **OS**: macOS
- **Platform**: React Native (Expo)
- **Bundler**: Metro
- **@ai-sdk/google**: `^2.0.0-beta.2`
- **@ai-sdk/openai**: `^2.0.0-beta.1`
- **@ai-sdk/react**: `^2.0.0-beta.1`
- **ai**: `^5.0.0-beta.1`
- **eventsource-parser**: `^3.0.2`

### Description

When bundling a React Native (Expo) application for iOS, the Metro bundler fails to resolve the module `eventsource-parser/stream`. This dependency seems to be used by `@ai-sdk/provider-utils`.

The main dependency `eventsource-parser` is listed in `package.json`, but its `/stream` subpath cannot be resolved in a React Native environment. This is a common issue with packages that are not explicitly authored for React Native's Metro bundler, which has limited support for certain module resolution features used in the wider JavaScript ecosystem.

### Error Message
iOS Bundling failed
Unable to resolve "eventsource-parser/stream" from "node_modules/@ai-sdk/provider-utils/dist/index.js"

### Steps to Reproduce

1.  Set up a React Native project using Expo.
2.  Install `@ai-sdk/react` and a provider package like `@ai-sdk/openai`.
3.  Attempt to bundle the application for a native platform (iOS or Android).
4.  The build fails with the resolution error.

### Relevant `package.json` dependencies

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@ai-sdk/google": "^2.0.0-beta.2",
    "@ai-sdk/openai": "^2.0.0-beta.1",
    "@ai-sdk/react": "^2.0.0-beta.1",
    "ai": "^5.0.0-beta.1",
    "eventsource-parser": "^3.0.2",
    "expo": "53.0.12",
    "react-native": "0.79.4",
    // ... other dependencies
  }
}
```

### Suggested Solution

The packages should be updated to ensure compatibility with React Native's Metro bundler, possibly by avoiding deep/subpath imports or providing a `react-native` field in `package.json` to point to a compatible entry point.

### AI SDK Version

- @ai-sdk/google: ^2.0.0-beta.2
- @ai-sdk/openai: ^2.0.0-beta.1

title: Last `text-delta` before `tool-call-delta` is streamed after
body:
### Description

Sorry, I don't have very good repro code for this, but I believe this is a bug.

I am using `streamText` and then `onChunk` to catch the streamed chunks and tool calls. When LLM responds with some message and after that tool call is following the chunk sequence looks like this:
```
-----CHUNK---- response-metadata
-----CHUNK---- text-delta
... (more text-delta)
-----CHUNK---- text-delta
-----CHUNK---- text-delta
-----CHUNK---- tool-call-delta
... (more tool-call-delta)
-----CHUNK---- tool-call-delta
-----CHUNK---- tool-call
-----CHUNK---- text-delta     <-----
-----CHUNK---- finish
```

The last `text-delta` before the `finish` is the last chunk of the text from the message that is before the tool call, meaning that in the UI while the tool call is streaming, the text message before is not finished until the tool call finishes streaming.

The behavior can be seen on the following video, where the "review" is streamed only after the tool call streaming is done.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/30d1c1e4-87ed-452f-83c6-94f5818a59b0)

title: Support correct and lossless reconstruction of OpenAI messages when streaming for multi-turn conversation (needed for deep research etc.)
body:
### Description

**Streaming Response Message Reconstruction Issue:** 

The current streaming implementation cannot correctly reconstruct the `(await result.response).messages` array from streaming deltas, which prevents proper multi-turn conversation continuity. Specific issues include:

- **Complex Reasoning Structure**: Reasoning items can contain arrays of summary texts that cannot be properly reconstructed from individual deltas
- **Missing Output Index**: The `output_index` needed to correctly place chunk deltas in the final array structure is not exposed to consumers
- **Incomplete State Building**: The streaming parser does not correctly build the final message state from deltas, particularly for complex reasoning content
- **Multi-turn Conversation Breakage**: For deep research models and similar advanced reasoning models, users cannot continue conversations with the correct message prefix without implementing custom parsing logic

This means that for streaming scenarios with reasoning models, developers currently need to either:
1. Use non-streaming mode for multi-turn conversations, or  
2. Implement custom delta parsing logic (which lacks access to necessary metadata like `output_index`)

See real output from responses API to highlight this issue:

```
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "o3-deep-research",
    "input": "Research the economic impact of semaglutide on global healthcare systems. Include specific figures, trends, statistics, and measurable outcomes. Prioritize reliable, up-to-date sources: peer-reviewed research, health organizations (e.g., WHO, CDC), regulatory agencies, or pharmaceutical earnings reports. Include inline citations and return all source metadata. Be analytical, avoid generalities, and ensure that each section supports data-backed reasoning that could inform healthcare policy or financial modeling.",
    "tools": [
      { "type": "web_search_preview" }
    ],
    "reasoning": {
      "effort": "medium", 
      "summary": "auto"
    },
    "include": ["reasoning.encrypted_content"],
    "stream": true
  }'
```

title: Add Eleven Labs Integration to AI SDK Speech Generation API
body:
### Description

The current AI SDK Beta 5 speech generation API only supports OpenAI, LMNT, and Hume voice providers. We request adding Eleven Labs as a supported provider to enable custom voice selection from their extensive voice library.

### Current Limitations:
- AI SDK speech generation only supports a limited set of providers (OpenAI, LMNT, Hume)
- No way to use custom voices from Eleven Labs with the current `generateSpeech` API
- Projects requiring custom voices need to implement separate integrations outside the AI SDK

### Requested Features:

1. **Add Eleven Labs as a First-Class Provider:**
   - Implement an Eleven Labs provider similar to existing providers
   - Support Eleven Labs' voice selection capabilities
   - Enable custom voice IDs from Eleven Labs catalog

2. **API Compatibility:**
   - Maintain consistent API with existing speech providers
   - Support all Eleven Labs voice customization parameters
   - Allow streaming audio for real-time playback

3. **Example Implementation:**
```typescript
import { experimental_generateSpeech as generateSpeech } from 'ai';
import { elevenlabs } from '@ai-sdk/elevenlabs';

const audio = await generateSpeech({
  model: elevenlabs.speech('eleven_multilingual_v2'),
  text: 'Hello, world!',
  voice: 'custom_voice_id', // Support for Eleven Labs voice IDs
  providerOptions: {
    elevenlabs: {
      stability: 0.5,
      similarity_boost: 0.5,
      style: 0.0,
      use_speaker_boost: true
    },
  },
});
```

### Technical Requirements:
- Create a new `@ai-sdk/elevenlabs` package
- Implement proper error handling for Eleven Labs API responses
- Support all Eleven Labs voice customization parameters
- Enable streaming audio output for real-time playback

This integration would greatly enhance the AI SDK's capabilities by allowing developers to use Eleven Labs' high-quality voice synthesis and custom voices without implementing separate integrations.

title: OpenAI o3 model throws "Invalid schema for function" error when optional parameters are not included in 'required' array
body:
### Description

# Description
When using the OpenAI o3 model with function calling through the AI SDK, the model throws a validation error for function schemas that have optional parameters not listed in the required array. This behavior differs from other OpenAI models (like GPT-4o, o1, o3-mini, etc.) which handle optional parameters correctly.

# Error Message
Invalid schema for function 'semantic_scholar_search': In context=(), 'required' is required to be supplied and to be an array including every key in properties. Missing 'limit'.

# Expected Behavior
The o3 model should handle function schemas with optional parameters the same way as other OpenAI models. Optional parameters (those marked with .optional() in Zod schema) should be treated as optional, not required.

# Current Behavior
The o3 model appears to require ALL properties defined in the function schema to be included in the required array, even if they are meant to be optional parameters.

 # Reproduction Steps
  1. Define a function tool with optional parameters using Zod:

```
  semantic_scholar_search: {
    description: "Search academic papers using Semantic Scholar API.",
    parameters: z.object({
      query: z
        .string()
        .describe(
          "The text to search for. Always convert the question to a make sense search query before passing it in.",
        ),
      limit: z
        .number()
        .int()
        .optional()
        .describe("The maximum number of results to return. Min 5, max 100."),
      offset: z
        .number()
        .int()
        .nonnegative()
        .optional()
        .describe(
          "Used for pagination. When returning a list of results, start with the element at this position in the list.",
        ),
      year: z
        .number()
        .int()
        .optional() 
        .describe(
          "Restricts results to the given publication year or range of years, formatted as YYYY (Specific year).",
        ),
    }),
  }
```

  2. Use the function with OpenAI o3 model:
```
  import { generateText } from "ai";
  import { openai } from "@ai-sdk/openai";

  const result = await generateText({
    model: openai("o3"),
    tools: {
      semantic_scholar_search: {
        description: "Search academic papers using Semantic Scholar API.",
        parameters: /* Zod schema from above */
      }
    },
    prompt: "Search for papers about machine learning",
  });
```

  3. The error occurs when the SDK converts the Zod schema to OpenAI's function schema format.

# Environment

  - AI SDK version: ^4.3.16
  - @ai-sdk/openai version: ^1.3.22
  - Node.js version: 22.15
  - OpenAI model: o3
  - Using Zod for schema validation

# Additional Context
  - This issue only occurs with the o3 model
  - Other OpenAI models (gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, o1, o3-mini, o4-mini) work correctly with the same function schemas
  - The issue seems to be related to how the o3 model validates function schemas differently from other models
  - The error suggests o3 expects the required field to contain ALL properties from the schema, not just the non-optional ones



### AI SDK Version

_No response_

title: SDK does not respect rate limit headers from API providers
body:
### Description

When providers like Anthropic and OpenAI return 429 rate limit errors, they include `retry-after` headers that specify when the client should retry. Currently, the Vercel AI SDK doesn't automatically respect these headers and uses standard exponential backoff instead, which can lead to unnecessary failed retries.

Both the [Anthropic SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/blob/main/src/client.ts#L747-L775) and [OpenAI SDK](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/blob/master/src/client.ts#L753-L781) implement the same logic for handling these headers.

### Current Behavior

The SDK uses exponential backoff for all retries, ignoring any `retry-after` or `retry-after-ms` headers from the provider.

### Expected Behavior

The SDK should automatically parse and respect rate limit headers following the same approach as Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs:

1. Check for `retry-after-ms` header (milliseconds)
2. Fall back to `retry-after` header (seconds or HTTP date format)
3. Only use the header value if it's reasonable (between 0 and 60 seconds)
4. Fall back to exponential backoff if:
   - No rate limit headers are present
   - The headers contain invalid values
   - The delay is unreasonable (negative or >= 60 seconds)

This ensures the SDK respects provider rate limits while still maintaining reasonable retry behavior.

### Example

When Anthropic returns:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
retry-after-ms: 5000
```

The SDK should wait 5 seconds before retrying instead of using exponential backoff.

### Environment

- ai version: 5.x
- Runtime: Node.js / Edge / Browser

title: Partial UIMessage collection on abort or error
body:
### Description

Currently, `createUIMessageStream` only invokes the `onFinish` callback when the stream completes successfully. 

In cases where the stream is aborted (e.g., by the user) or an error occurs mid-way, we don’t get access to any partial `UIMessage`s that were emitted before termination.

In long-running sessions that involve side effects (e.g., saving to disk, modifying state, committing to a DB, etc.), losing this in-progress output is problematic and can result in lost work or inconsistent state.

It would be valuable to have:
* An `onAbort` and/or `onError` callback that receives the partial messages.
* Or a modified `onFinish` that is always called, with an additional argument indicating whether the stream was aborted, failed, or completed.

I’m considering maintaining a `partialMessages: ResponseMessage[]` variable by collecting the output from onStepFinish. However, I’m not sure if there’s a util function available to convert `ResponseMessage[]` into a valid UIMessage. 

+don't want to lose the usage data when error or abort occurs.

thanks!

Currently, using v5, but the issue existed in v4 as well.

title: Azure OpenAI v1 Preview API Support - Endpoint URL Incompatibility
body:
### Description

Hello,
Thank you for great AI SDK maintenance every time.
I found that Azure OpenAI the new API structure has changed endpoints.
So I wish it will be supported in AI SDK.

## Summary
Vercel AI SDK currently uses the legacy Azure OpenAI endpoint format, which prevents users from accessing the latest `api-version=preview` features. Azure OpenAI has introduced a new v1 API architecture with different endpoint URLs that require AI SDK updates.

## Background
Microsoft has significantly changed their Azure OpenAI API strategy starting May 2025. They introduced a new generation of v1 APIs.

References: 
- [[Azure OpenAI API version lifecycle](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/api-version-lifecycle?tabs=key#api-evolution)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/api-version-lifecycle?tabs=key#api-evolution)
- [Preview API (`api-version=preview`) documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/reference-preview-latest)
- [Legacy API (`2025-04-01-preview` and earlier) documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/reference-preview)

## Compare Endpoints

**New v1 API endpoint format (required for latest features):**
```
* Chat Completions: POST {endpoint}/openai/v1/chat/completions?api-version=preview
* Embeddings: POST {endpoint}/openai/v1/embeddings?api-version=preview
* Responses: POST {endpoint}/openai/v1/responses?api-version=preview
```

**Legacy endpoint format (currently used by Vercel AI SDK):**
```
* Chat Completions: POST {endpoint}/openai/deployments/{deployment-id}/chat/completions?api-version=2025-04-01-preview
* Embeddings: POST {endpoint}/openai/deployments/{deployment-id}/embeddings?api-version=2025-04-01-preview
* Responses: POST {endpoint}/openai/responses?api-version=2025-04-01-preview
```

- Please also confirm that "**v1**" has been added to the new endpoints.
- And the old Responses API endpoint "v1" is not existing.

## Impact
- Users cannot access the latest Azure OpenAI features available in `api-version=preview`
- Missing support for new Responses API capabilities like:
  - input PDF files streamTest on Responses API.

title: Streaming not working on first load / hard refresh (fixes after fast-refresh) on local dev
body:
### Description

Text Streaming is not working on first page load / hard refresh on nextjs in development mode.
If I send a message asking for a long response after a hard refresh, the network streaming tab shows the chunks coming in, but the `messages` array from useChat only updates with the first step-start and state: streaming, and then at the very end with the final message.

If I leave the page open and cause an update with Fast Refresh, then streaming works properly until I reload the page.

title: Feature: Add optional modelName param to Azure .languageModel() for accurate telemetry (e.g., fix Langfuse cost calculation)
body:
### Description

When using the Vercel AI SDK with Azure OpenAI, the `.languageModel(deploymentName)` method requires passing the custom Azure deployment name (e.g., 'custom-deployment') for the API call to succeed, as Azure strictly validates this in the endpoint URL. However, this sets the OpenTelemetry span attribute `ai.model.id` to the deployment name, which is not a standard OpenAI model name (e.g., 'gpt-4o'). As a result, observability tools like Langfuse cannot match it to their pricing tables, leading to missing or zeroed-out cost calculations in traces, even though the LLM call works and token usage is ingested.

This is a known integration gap with Azure, as the SDK doesn't separate the deployment name (for API) from the model name (for telemetry). Libraries like LangChain/LangGraph handle this out-of-the-box with separate params: `azure_deployment` for the API and `model_name` for tokenizers/metadata/cost. Adding an optional `modelName` param to `.languageModel()` (e.g., `.languageModel(deploymentName, { modelName: 'gpt-4.1' })`) would allow using the deployment for the API while setting `ai.model.id` (or a new metadata field) to the model name for better telemetry compatibility.

**Reproduction Steps**  
1. Set up an Azure OpenAI resource with a deployment named 'custom-deployment' (underlying model: gpt-4o or similar).  
2. In code:  
   ```ts  
   import { createAzure } from '@ai-sdk/azure';  
   const azure = createAzure({ resourceName: 'your-resource', apiKey: 'your-key' });  
   const model = azure.languageModel('custom-deployment'); // Or 'gpt-4.1' to trigger the alternative behavior  
   // Use in a call, e.g., generateText({ model, prompt: 'Hello' })  
   ```  
3. Integrate with Langfuse (or similar) via OpenTelemetry.  
4. Observe traces: With deployment name, API succeeds but Langfuse cost is 0/missing. With model name, API errors but cost shows.  

**Expected Behavior**  
The SDK should support an optional param to specify the underlying model name for telemetry, decoupling it from the deployment name required by Azure. This could set `ai.model.id` to the model name or add it to metadata (e.g., `experimental_telemetry.metadata.actualModel`).  

**Related Issues**  
- #7269 (Telemetry bugs with Azure showing 0 cost/duration in observability tools)  
- #6378 (Expose deploymentName for tracing)

### AI SDK Version

**Environment**  
- Node.js version: 20.14.0 
- Azure API version: 2024-12-01-preview
- @ai-sdk/azure: 1.3.17
- ai: 4.3.9

title: Image downloads are unreliable
body: ### Description We're having reliability issues using multiple images with Google models because the SDK attempts to [download all images in parallel](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/ai/src/prompt/convert-to-language-model-prompt.ts#L236-L242) [using `fetch`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/ai/src/util/download.ts#L9). We may have 20-30 images, which when run concurrently results in excessive connection creation and connection timeouts. `fetch` doesn't retry and the `fetch` implementation is not currently configurable. Retrying the overall SDK operation exacerbates the problem by relaunching the concurrent image fetch. # Possible solutions 1. Allow configuration of the fetch/download implementation. [`convertToLanguageModelPrompt`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/ai/src/prompt/convert-to-language-model-prompt.ts#L24) actually has a `downloadImplementation` parameter, but it is not exposed from `generateText` or `generateObject`, so the default of `download` is always used. It would be quite easy to expose, since it just needs to be added in those two places. 2. Use the existing `maxRetries` parameter or add a new `maxDownloadRetries` parameter and support retries for image downloads, as is already done for LLM API calls. 3. Introduce a maximum parallelism parameter for image downloads. Libraries like `p-limit` make this straightforward. #1 allows users to implement #2 and #3 themselves. Providing #2 and #3 is more convenient and makes #1 less necessary. # Workarounds 1. Pre-download all images in the prompt. This is suboptimal for models that support image URLs and partially defeats the purpose of having the SDK handle model quirks. 2. Monkey-patch `fetch` to throttle and retry. This could have unintended consequences with other libraries, such as duplicate/excessive retries. I'm happy to submit a PR once I know which solution(s) are acceptable. ### AI SDK Version - ai: 4.3.14 - @ai-sdk/google: 1.2.16 - @ai-sdk/openai: 1.3.21

author: dipbhi

title: Support OTEL span transformation hook
body:
### Description

Currently, the conversion from AI SDK response values to OTEL span occurs entirely internally within the language model classes.

However, not everything from the AI SDK response is populated onto the span, and are cases where users wish to use OTEL to interact with metadata fields (e.g. advanced usage) that are present in the AI SDK response but not the exported span.

I'd propose allowing the user to pass `transformCreatedSpan` function into `generate/StreamText/Object` calls that runs right before the span finalizes, takes the current span and actual AI SDK response (which often includes the raw response from the model provider) as a second param, and allows the user to return a modified version of the span. Within this function, the user could add additional span attributes.

It'd definitely be more advanced functionality but would unblock some observability use-cases. The alternative would be something like duplicating the entire raw provider response onto each span, which would have other performance implications.

Creating this issue as requested by @lgrammel

body:
### Description # Explanation I noticed a strange delay between submitting and receiving my first message from the chat. I’m displaying a loader for the status 'submitted'. However, the status is changing almost immediately to 'streaming' while it does not stream any actual responses. It degrades the UX. It could be reproduced for both `google` and `openai` providers. Twitter discussion with @nicoalbanese with video recordings: https://x.com/serhiichernenko/status/1949072682135253197 # Solution that didn't help Even if I push `step-start` manually earlier, the status will be incorrect (already `streaming`). So, this is not a solution ```ts const stream = createUIMessageStream({ execute({ writer }) { writer.write({ type: 'start' }) writer.write({ type: 'start-step' }) const result = streamText() writer.merge(result.toUIMessageStream({ sendStart: false, ``` # Solution that works I duplicated the loader with a different statement. So the first loader still displays on `status === 'submitted'` as it was expected initially. And this second loader is displayed when the `status` changes to `streaming` but `start-step` is not received yet. And ofc it’s displayed only for the last message in the messages array. ```vue
``` https://github.com/besidka/besidka/pull/29/files#diff-4a0f00da4dc24ee18c199397b411b1cbc04799fb7b5d6e9231196edecc15addaR12 # Expected behavior The `status` remains `submitted` until the `start-step` received. # Code examples Loader statement: https://github.com/besidka/besidka/blob/main/app/pages/chats/%5Bslug%5D.vue#L74 API: https://github.com/besidka/besidka/blob/main/server/api/v1/chats/%5Bslug%5D/index.post.ts#L150 Related PR: https://github.com/besidka/besidka/pull/29 # Play around Production URL: https://www.besidka.com/chats/new Preview URL: - Issue appears: https://64aa39df-besidka-preview.chernenko.workers.dev/chats/new - The issue was fixed with the duplicated loader: https://4f5f84f2-besidka-preview.chernenko.workers.dev/ PS: Google and GitHub OAuth couldn't be configured for Cloudflare Workers preview URLs (because they are always dynamic). Please consider using the email and password sign-up flow on Preview. # Screenshots The `status` changes to `streaming` immediately when the message is created. Results from file search are not returned as messages by default from the File Search tool in OpenAI Responses tool https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/tools-file-search?lang=javascript#include-search-results-in-the-response.

const response = await openai.responses.create({
    model: "gpt-4o-mini",
    input: "What is deep research by OpenAI?",
    tools: [{
        type: "file_search",
        vector_store_ids: ["<vector_store_id>"],
    }],

title: Surprising behavior when sendAutomaticallyWhen and stopWhen used together
body:
### Description

I am using steamText on the server and useChat on the client. Some tools have an `execute` method and perform work on the server (e.g.: call an API), and other tools wait for user input on the client (where I call `addToolResult`). For the tools with an `execute` method, they occasionally _also_ require user input (e.g.: authentication failed, and the user needs to re-auth). 

With the recent v5 updates, I intended to support this by using:
- `stopWhen` on server: the agent loop can continue a certain number of iterations, OR a certain tool response was detected (e.g.: integration tool with `authFailed: true`)
```
    stopWhen: [
      stepCountIs(10),
      isWaitingForSetupIntegrationToolToFinishAuthenticating() as StopCondition<any>,
    ],
```
- `sendAutomaticallyWhen` on client: when the user adds a tool response, the server should pick it up and the agent loop should continue

However, it seems like `sendAutomaticallyWhen` causes this to break. 
- When set to `false`, my `stopWhen` criteria works as expected.
- When set to `true`, the agent loop continues even after the `stopWhen` criteria evaluated to true (confirmed with logging)

I _think_ this is a bug, and that this worked fine before the introduction of `sendAutomaticallyWhen`. My expected behavior is that `sendAutomaticallyWhen` only adjusts client behavior, so if the server stops the agent loop then it would only be picked back up if the user sent a new message or tool response.

However, this is fairly new (#7536), so it may be user error.

title: Duplicate streamText Assistant Messages with Client Tool Continuations
body:
### Description

# Bug Report: Duplicate Assistant Messages with Client Tool Continuations

## Summary
When using client-side tools with `sendAutomaticallyWhen`, the assistant message gets duplicated in the client state instead of being updated.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Send a user message that triggers server-side tool calls requiring client execution
2. Client tools execute and `sendAutomaticallyWhen` returns `true`
3. Second request is automatically sent back to server with tool results
4. streamText adds a new Assistant message then finishes it.

## Expected Behavior
The existing assistant message should be updated, not duplicated.

## Actual Behavior
The client useChat receives a duplicate assistant message that is added to the client state.

## Root Cause
In `packages/ai/src/generate-text/stream-text.ts` at line 1127:

```typescript
let stepResponse: { id: string; timestamp: Date; modelId: string } = {
  id: generateId(), // ← Always generates new ID
  timestamp: currentDate(),
  modelId: model.modelId,
};
```

When `streamText` handles client tool continuations, it unconditionally generates a new message ID instead of reusing the existing assistant message ID from the conversation history. This causes the client's `replaceLastMessage` logic in `chat.ts` to fail, resulting in `pushMessage` being called instead.

Even with a hack of generateId to return the existing id  of the assistant message it still adds a second message to the stream state messages creating an issue with saving the messages onFinish

## Additional Context
- This appears to be a regression from pre-AI SDK 5 behavior
- Workaround attempted: overriding `generateId` to return existing message ID, but this still creates duplicates
- The issue occurs because `streamText` lacks awareness that it's continuing an existing assistant message rather than starting a new one

## Suggested Fix
For client tool continuations, `streamText` should detect when the last message in history is an assistant message with pending client tools and reuse that message's ID instead of generating a new one.

## Environment
- AI SDK version: 5.x
- Framework: [Your framework here]
- Client transport: Custom DefaultChatTranspor

### Description

Issue:
Error is thrown when using anthropic "claude-4-sonnet-20250514" model on the last assistant message. The last assistant message requires a `thinking` block, according to the anthropic spec.

We recommend you include thinking blocks from previous turns. To avoid this requirement, disable `thinking`. Please consult our documentation at https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/extended-thinking
```

title: `lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls` should support dynamic tool calls
body:
### Description

## Problem

Currently, `lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls` checks for `isToolUIPart` in the last tool invocation to see if it has finished streaming output.

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/6fb1b4378f5f9f390d08ef932660bc17e65c186b/packages/ai/src/ui/last-assistant-message-is-complete-with-tool-calls.ts#L29

However, `isToolUIPart` does not support `dynamic-tool`s.

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/6fb1b4378f5f9f390d08ef932660bc17e65c186b/packages/ai/src/ui/ui-messages.ts#L274-L278

This makes `lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls` return `false` wherever dynamic tools are used.

## Possible solutions

Checking for `dynamic-tool` part along with `isToolUIPart` `lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls` would solve this issue.

Changing `isToolUIPart` could be dangerous as it is used in many places other than `lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls`

## Workarounds

Implementing `lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls` with support for dynamic tools and plugging it into `sendAutomaticallyWhen` of `useChat` is one workaround.

- `ai: 5.0.0`
