title: Empty text part created prematurely when using Perplexity models with `extractReasoningMiddleware`
body:
### Description

When using `extractReasoningMiddleware` with Perplexity's `sonar-reasoning-pro` model, the client receives message parts in an unexpected order compared to other providers like Claude.

## Expected Behavior

Based on Claude model behavior:
- Client receives parts in order: `['step-start', 'reasoning', 'text']`
- Reasoning content appears before main text content

## Actual Behavior

With Perplexity models:
- Client receives: `['step-start', 'text', 'reasoning']`
- An empty text part appears early in the streaming process
- Text content is positioned before reasoning in the final structure

## Key Differences

**Claude models:**
- No source chunks in server stream
- Maintains expected order throughout streaming

**Perplexity models:**
- Includes source chunks: `source → reasoning-delta → text-delta`
- Creates empty text part early in client
- Results in unexpected final order

## Reproduction

Repository with minimal reproduction: https://github.com/liby/vercel-ai-perplexity-reasoning-bug

The repository includes detailed logging to show the streaming order at both server and client sides.

## Impact

This ordering issue affects UI display, as reasoning content is expected to appear before the main response text for proper context.

## Additional Information

The issue does not occur in AI SDK v4. With v4:

- Messages maintain correct order without empty text parts appearing early
- Using `createDataStreamResponse` with `mergeIntoDataStream` works as expected
- The issue appears to be specific to v5's handling of Perplexity's source chunks

- @ai-sdk/react: 2.0.2
- @ai-sdk/perplexity: 2.0.0

title: Source parts from Perplexity models not passed to client
body:
### Description

### Description

After upgrading AI SDK from v4 to v5, Perplexity models no longer return `source` parts to the client, though they remain visible on the server. This regression breaks applications that rely on displaying citation sources from Perplexity responses.

## Expected Behavior

Based on AI SDK v4 behavior:
- Client receives message parts including `source` parts with citation URLs
- Applications can display citation links to users

## Actual Behavior

With AI SDK v5:
- Client only receives: `step-start`, `text` and `reasoning`
- All `source` parts are missing from client-side message parts
- Server logs confirm source parts exist in the stream but are filtered before reaching client

## Key Differences

**AI SDK v4:**
```json
[
  { "type": "step-start" },
  { "type": "source", "source": { "sourceType": "url", "id": "...", "url": "https://..." } },
  { "type": "source", "source": { "sourceType": "url", "id": "...", "url": "https://..." } },
  { "type": "reasoning", "reasoning": "..." },
  { "type": "text", "text": "..." }
]
```

**AI SDK v5:**
```json
[
  { "type": "step-start" },
  { "type": "text", "text": "...", "state": "done" },
  { "type": "reasoning", "text": "...", "state": "done" }
]
```

## Reproduction

Repository with minimal reproduction: https://github.com/liby/vercel-ai-perplexity-reasoning-bug

The repository includes detailed logging to demonstrate:
1. Source parts visible in server logs
2. Source parts missing from client message parts

## Impact

This regression prevents applications from:
- Displaying citation sources to users
- Building trust through transparent sourcing
- Meeting requirements for source attribution in AI responses

## Root Cause Analysis

The issue appears related to v5's handling of Perplexity-specific content types. While the server correctly receives source parts from Perplexity's API, they are filtered out before reaching the client through the streaming middleware.


### AI SDK Version

- ai: 5.0.2
- @ai-sdk/react: 2.0.2
- @ai-sdk/perplexity: 2.0.0

title: openai Responses does not support PDF by URL
body:
### Description

**tldr: you can pass url as data for PDF in `openai.chat`, but not `openai.responses`**

If you pass a URL as the data in a PDF (in the message part), you'll observe that the Chat API `openai.chat('gpt-4.1')` uses an internal workaround within the SDK to download the file

This doesn't happen for `openai.responses` -- the internal workaround is not used, and the API's native support for PDF by URLs is not leveraged. 

solutions:
1) Use the same convert function used in the Chat API in order to use the same workaround -- this is a part of #7804 which also adds file id support
2) refactor things to allow for openai.responses to leverage the API's internal support

If solution 1 is a good path I would love to get my PR in -- whether that is as is, or splitting it up to be more atomic since the PR also implements file-id support. Ty

title: Add "assistant-" prefix support for Azure OpenAI file-id recognition
body: ### Description Thank you for OpenAI file-id is supported. I tried it on Azure OpenAI but I found file-id naming issue. ## Background PR #7804 successfully added support for OpenAI Responses API file handling, allowing file-ids to be passed for AI recognition. However, the current implementation only recognizes file-ids that start with "file-", which works for OpenAI but not for Azure OpenAI. ## Problem The current file-id recognition logic in the codebase: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/56eb0ee9b1e4a4791309985ba3a1575daaf780c0/packages/openai/src/responses/convert-to-openai-responses-messages.ts#L91-L97 This implementation only checks for the "file-" prefix, but Azure OpenAI uses a different naming convention where file-ids start with "assistant-" instead. ## Evidence According to Microsoft's official documentation, Azure OpenAI file-ids follow this pattern: - Example: `assistant-R9uhPxvRKGH3m0x5zBOhMjd2` - Example: `assistant-1YGVTvNzc2JXajI5` - Example: `assistant-abc123` Source: [Microsoft Learn - Azure OpenAI Code Interpreter](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/how-to/code-interpreter) ## Proposed Solution Update the file-id recognition logic to support both OpenAI and Azure OpenAI prefixes(if openai package will be fixed): ```typescript typeof part.data === 'string' && (part.data.startsWith('file-') || part.data.startsWith('assistant-')) ? { file_id: part.data } : { filename: part.filename ?? `part-${index}.pdf`, file_data: `data:application/pdf;base64,${convertToBase64(part.data)}`, } ``` ## Impact Maintain backward compatibility with existing OpenAI implementations. Furthermore, as the AI SDK is expected to introduce code_interpreter functionality in the future, fixing this file-id recognition issue now will ensure that Azure OpenAI users can fully benefit from those upcoming features as well. Code interpreter functionality heavily relies on file handling capabilities, making this prefix recognition fix even more critical for future feature parity between OpenAI and Azure OpenAI environments. ### AI SDK Version "ai": "^5.0.5", "@ai-sdk/azure": "2.0.4", "@ai-sdk/react": "2.0.5",

If we call gpt-5 using a chat completion API (OpenAIChatLanguageModel), we'll hit AI_APICallError: Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model. Use 'max_completion_tokens' instead. 

This is because https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/58fff3fa2d9a1f14ab26c853ba31b672bc21dac2/packages/openai/src/openai-chat-language-model.ts#L145 is still setting the deprecated max_tokens instead of max_completion_tokens.

title: addToolResult does not work with MCP tools (dynamic-tool)
body:
### Description

## Issue
addToolResult is not working with MCP tools, so we can't implement Human in the Loop to allow the user to confirm the tool execution. (it was working on v4)

## Use case
I have an implementation of Human in the Loop for MCP tools in my app implemented with the ai-sdk v4. I use some metadata on the tool to check if the tool needs confirmation, if it does, I remove the `execute` from the tool so that it becomes a client tool that needs `addToolResult`.

I just upgraded to v5, and the HITL feature stopped working.

## Implementation
I'm calling the `addToolResult` and sending the message, but nothing changes in the tool information when I do so. (I double checked the args with logs)
```ts
    await addToolResult({
      tool,
      toolCallId,
      output,
    });
    await sendMessage();
```

## Additional debug info
I noticed that mcp tools invocations are of type `dynamic-tool` instead of `tool-{toolName}`, so the real problem might be that `addToolResult` doesn't work with `dynamic-tool`s. I tested with normal tools and it seems to work fine.

### AI SDK Version

- ai: 5.0.0
- @ai-sdk/openai: 2.0.0
- @ai-sdk/react: 2.0.0

When approaching any problem, apply **first principles reasoning** instead of reasoning by analogy or conventional wisdom. Break down problems to their fundamental axioms - the most basic truths that are actually true - then reason up from there to determine what\\'s possible.
### Methodology
1. **Identify the fundamental components**: What are the irreducible elements of this problem?
2. **Question assumptions**: What "truths" are actually just historical patterns or analogies?
3. **Calculate from basics**: What do the raw fundamentals tell us about limits and possibilities?
4. **Think in limits**: What happens if we minimize or maximize key variables?

**Rocket Cost Analysis**
- **Conventional approach**: Look at historical rocket costs, assume new rockets must cost similarly
- **First principles approach**: Calculate raw material costs (aluminum, copper, carbon fiber, steel)
- **Insight**: Raw materials = only 1-2% of historical costs → manufacturing is extremely inefficient
- **Conclusion**: Massive cost reduction is physically possible
### Application Framework
For every task:
1. **Reject analogies**: Don\\'t assume "this is like that other thing"
2. **Break down completely**: What are the actual physical/logical constraints?
3. **Calculate floors and ceilings**: What are the theoretical limits?
4. **Solve constituent elements**: Address each fundamental component separately
5. **Question "impossible"**: If told something can\\'t be done, break it into smaller pieces

You have access to scheduling functionality that allows you to run the current task (iterate) at specific times or on recurring schedules:

### When to use scheduling
- **Recurring tasks**: User wants something done regularly (daily, weekly, monthly, etc.)
- **Delayed execution**: User wants something done at a specific future time
- **Reminders**: User wants to be reminded about something
- **Monitoring**: User wants periodic checks or updates

### How scheduling works
- \`schedule()\`: Creates a new schedule for the current task. You can schedule:
  - **One-time**: Run once at a specific date/time or after a delay
  - **Recurring**: Run repeatedly using cron expressions (e.g., daily, weekly, monthly)

### Examples of when to schedule
- "Remind me to call John tomorrow at 2pm" → schedule one-time for tomorrow 2pm
- "Check Bitcoin price every morning" → schedule recurring daily at 9am
- "Send weekly report every Friday" → schedule recurring weekly on Fridays

title: Flex processing not supported for GPT-5
body:
### Description

The newly released GPT-5 models from OpenAI support the "flex processing" tier, similar to o3 and o4-mini. For the latter two, a feature to support this tier was merged two months ago in #6676. The PR included a function that checks if the model name starts with "o3" or "o4-mini" when utilizing the flex service tier. If it does not, the service tier is unset. 

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/4b50c3681f6008adb3af6dad0f495fcd7971a158/packages/openai/src/openai-chat-language-model.ts#L846-L848

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/4b50c3681f6008adb3af6dad0f495fcd7971a158/packages/openai/src/openai-chat-language-model.ts#L260-L270

similarly in this other file: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/4b50c3681f6008adb3af6dad0f495fcd7971a158/packages/openai/src/responses/openai-responses-language-model.ts

Therefore, the flex processing tier currently can't be used with GPT-5, even though it supports it.

I'd obviously be able to make a quick PR that adds `gpt-5` to the allowlist, but unsure if this strict allowlist is the right way forward at all. Maybe a warning should be logged, but the service tier shouldn't be unset?

**Reference**
https://platform.openai.com/docs/pricing?latest-pricing=flex

title: Empty reasoning text with OpenAI reasoning models
body:
### Description

## Description

OpenAI reasoning models (o3-mini, o3, o1, o4-mini, gpt-5, gpt-5-mini,...) return empty reasoning text when using `streamText`/`generateText`, even though reasoning tokens are counted correctly.

## Current Behavior

### With generateText:
```typescript
const result = await generateText({
  model: openai("o3-mini"),
  prompt: "What is 25% of 80?",
});

console.log(result.reasoning); // Always empty: ""
console.log(result.usage.reasoningTokens); // Shows token count: 256
```

### With streamText:
```typescript
const result = streamText({
  model: openai("o3-mini"),
  prompt: "What is 25% of 80?",
});

for await (const chunk of result.fullStream) {
  if (chunk.type === "reasoning") {
    console.log("Reasoning:", chunk.textDelta); // Never receives any reasoning chunks
  }
}

const finalResult = await result;
console.log(finalResult.reasoning); // Always empty: ""
console.log(finalResult.usage.reasoningTokens); // Shows token count: 256
```

## Expected Behavior

The `result.reasoning` should contain the actual reasoning text, similar to how it works with Anthropic's thinking models.

## Impact

This affects users who need to access the reasoning process of OpenAI's reasoning models. The reasoning tokens are being consumed (and charged) but the actual reasoning text is not accessible through the standard API.


## Request for Support

Could the AI SDK team provide guidance on how to properly access reasoning text from OpenAI's reasoning models? Is this a known limitation or is there a recommended approach we should be using?

- @ai-sdk/openai: 2.0.3

### Description

follow up to https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/8030#issuecomment-3191527471

When using `generateText` with both `web_search_preview` and `file_search` tools in AI SDK v5, the call fails with an `AI_TypeValidationError` sometimes.

This happens when the OpenAI Responses API does not return `start_index`, `end_index`, and `quote` fields.

The OpenAI Responses API returns valid `file_citation` objects with `file_id`, `filename`, and `index`, but the AI SDK validator expects them to also have the `start_index`, `end_index`, and `quote` properties (like `url_citation` annotations). This leads to `AI_TypeValidationError` failures during parsing.

**Reproduction**

```ts
import { generateText, openai } from 'ai';

const result = await generateText({
  model: openai('gpt-5'),
  system: 'system prompt here',
  prompt: 'prompt here',
  tools: {
    web_search_preview: openai.tools.webSearchPreview({ searchContextSize: 'high' }),
    file_search: openai.tools.fileSearch({
      vectorStoreIds: ['myvectorstoreid'],
      maxNumResults: 3,
    }),
  },
});
```

AI_APICallError: Invalid JSON response
AI_TypeValidationError: Invalid input: expected number, received undefined
Path: ["output", 11, "content", 0, "annotations", 0, "start_index"]

title: Bug: passing `id: undefined` to useChat leads to infinite rerenders (react)
body:
### Description

If you do:

```
const { messages } = useChat({id: undefined})
useEffect(() => {
//something
}, [messages])
```

your component will rerender indefinitely (and probably have other side effects) because this code is recreating the Chat on every render, so the messages reference is not stable across renders:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/12c7493f01e5359a519720a4dd803b5c61fa7b3c/packages/react/src/use-chat.ts#L65C1-L67C60

^ That bit needs to check if id === undefined || id === null when deciding to re-create the chat.

title: add : support for Agno into AI SDK ✨
body:
### Description

## Feature Request: Native Agno Agent Integration

### Background
Agno is a popular Python-based AI agent framework for building multi-agent systems with tool usage, memory, and complex reasoning workflows. Currently, there's no native integration between Agno agents and Vercel AI SDK.

### Problem
Developers using Agno agents with Next.js applications must:
- Create custom REST/WebSocket APIs to bridge Python backends with frontends
- Lose AI SDK's built-in streaming capabilities
- Manually handle tool calling integration
- Implement custom state management for agent conversations

### Proposed Solution
Add native Agno provider support similar to existing providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.):

```
import { createAgno } from ‘@ai-sdk/agno’;
const agno = createAgno({ baseURL: ‘http://localhost:7777’, apiKey: process.env.AGNO_API_KEY });
const result = await generateText({ model: agno(‘my-agent-id’), prompt: ‘Help me plan a trip to Japan’, });
```


### Key Features Needed
- **Agno Provider**: Direct communication with Agno agent endpoints
- **Streaming Support**: Real-time agent responses and intermediate steps
- **Tool Integration**: Map Agno tools to AI SDK's tool calling interface
- **Multi-Agent Support**: Handle agent workflows and handoffs
- **State Management**: Agent memory and conversation context

### Use Cases
- AI-first applications combining Agno's agent capabilities with Next.js
- Multi-agent dashboards and enterprise AI solutions
- Advanced RAG applications with agent reasoning
- Intelligent customer support with agent escalation

### Community Impact
This would bridge the Python AI agent ecosystem with JavaScript frontend development, enabling production-ready agent applications using proven AI SDK patterns.

### References
- [Agno GitHub](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno)
- [Agno Agent-UI](https://github.com/agno-agi/agent-ui)




### AI SDK Version

v5.x (Latest) - requesting as new feature

title: Stopping a structured object request before the stream has opened causes development server to crash
body:
### Description

[Loom explanantion](https://www.loom.com/share/c59292e16b244f9da90dee0224db8f46)

## Description of the problem

Stopping or clearing the structured object before the response starts streaming throws an error and breaks the development server.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run the svelte example
2. Open the structured object example
3. Submit a message
4. Immediately press the clear/stop button
    1. You have to be super quick otherwise everything works fine
5. Observe that the development server crashes

Note: If you wait until the response starts streaming back before pressing clear/stop, then everything works as expected.

The error that the server throws is:

```tsx
node:internal/webstreams/readablestream:1068
      throw new ERR_INVALID_STATE.TypeError('Controller is already closed');
            ^

TypeError [ERR_INVALID_STATE]: Invalid state: Controller is already closed
    at ReadableStreamDefaultController.close (node:internal/webstreams/readablestream:1068:13)
    at Object.close (file:///Users/andricokaroulla/Documents/coding/ai/packages/ai/dist/index.mjs:3611:50)
    at file:///Users/andricokaroulla/Documents/coding/ai/packages/ai/dist/index.mjs:6824:24
    at <anonymous>
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:105:5) {
  code: 'ERR_INVALID_STATE'
}
```

## Additional context

My guess is that opening a stream channel after the stream has been aborted causes the above issue.

I also implemented the “clear” functionality a few weeks back, and got worried that I introduced a serious bug, but after checking out a previous commit “737f1e205”, I can confirm that the behaviour existed prior to my change.

## Solutions

I don’t know much about how the streaming mechanism works under the hood, so I’ll need to do some digging before proposing a solution. 

With that said, if anyone else has an idea as to where to implement a fix, I’ll be happy to partner up on the problem.

My guess is that at some point along the process, the core `ai` package will need to check if the request has been aborted before creating a stream.

title: Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite while creating custom tool in Node.JS environment
body:
### Description

**Description:**

When attempting to integrate a custom tool with the AI SDK in a Node.js backend environment (specifically with Fastify (also tested with nest.js)), a persistent "Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite" error occurs. This error seems to stem from a recursive type inference issue within the `tool` function provided by the `ai` package. The problem manifests when defining a tool, particularly when specifying its schema or parameters, and it prevents the TypeScript compiler from successfully building the project.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1.  **Project Setup:**
    *   Initialize a new Node.js project with TypeScript and Fastify.
    *   Install the necessary dependencies, including `ai`, `zod`, and `@ai-sdk/openai`.
    *   Configure the `tsconfig.json` for a modern Node.js environment (e.g., `"module": "esnext"`, `"target": "es2022"`).

2.  **Tool Definition:**
    *   Create a new file for the tool definition (e.g., `src/tools/weather.tool.ts`).
    *   Import the `tool` function from the `ai` package and `zod` for schema definition.
    *   Define a simple tool using the `tool` function, providing a `description`, `inputSchema` (using `zod`), and an `execute` or `run` function.

    ```typescript
    import { tool } from "ai";
    import { z } from "zod";

    export const weatherTool = tool({
        description: 'Get the weather in a location',
        inputSchema: z.object({
          location: z.string(),
        }),
        execute: async ({ location }: { location: string }) => ({
          location,
          temperature: 72 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 21) - 10,
        }),
      });
    ```

3.  **Tool Integration:**
    *   In a service file (e.g., `src/services/ai.service.ts`), import the `weatherTool`.
    *   Use the `generateText` function from the `ai` package and pass the `weatherTool` in the `tools` array.

    ```typescript
    import { openai } from '@ai-sdk/openai';
    import { generateText } from 'ai';
    import { weatherTool } from '../tools/weather.tool';

    // ...

    const { text } = await generateText({
      model: this.model,
      messages,
      tools: { weatherTool },
    });
    ```

4.  **Build the Project:**
    *   Run the TypeScript compiler (`tsc` or `npm run build`).

**Expected Behavior:**

The project should compile successfully without any type errors, allowing the tool to be used with the AI model.

**Actual Behavior:**

The TypeScript compiler fails with a "Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite" error, pointing to the tool definition file. This error prevents the project from being built and run.

**Error Logs:**

```
src/tools/weather.tool.ts(4,28): error TS2589: Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite.
src/tools/weather.tool.ts(6,18): error TS2589: Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite.
```

**Analysis:**

The root cause of this issue appears to be a problem with how the `tool` function's type definitions are handled by the TypeScript compiler. The recursive nature of the type inference, especially when combined with `zod` schemas, leads to an infinite loop that exceeds the compiler's depth limit.

Several attempts were made to work around this issue, including:

*   Using `parameters` or `schema` instead of `inputSchema`.
*   Simplifying the tool definition by removing the `zod` schema and using a plain JavaScript object.
*   Removing the `tool` wrapper function and defining the tool as a simple object.

None of these workarounds were successful, indicating that the problem lies deep within the type definitions of the `ai` SDK.

**Environment:**

*   **Node.js Version:** v22.17.1
*   **TypeScript Version:** 5.9.2
*   **`ai` SDK Version:** 5.0.15
*   **`@ai-sdk/openai` Version:** 2.0.15
*   **`zod` Version:** 3.25.76
*   **Operating System:** macOS

**Suggested Solution:**

The type definitions for the `tool` function in the `ai` SDK need to be reviewed and revised to prevent this recursive type inference issue. This may involve simplifying the generic types, providing explicit type annotations, or using a different approach to schema definition that is more compatible with the TypeScript compiler.

### AI SDK Version

**Environment:**

*   **Node.js Version:** v22.17.1
*   **TypeScript Version:** 5.9.2
*   **`ai` SDK Version:** 5.0.15
*   **`@ai-sdk/openai` Version:** 2.0.15
*   **`zod` Version:** 3.25.76
*   **Operating System:** macOS

title: Support for MCP tools/list_changed notifications in experimental_createMCPClient
body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/vercel/ai/discussions/8144
Originally posted by **linw1995** August 19, 2025 ## Problem The current `experimental_createMCPClient` implementation lacks support for MCP notifications, specifically the `tools/list_changed` notification defined in the [MCP specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools#list-changed-notification). According to the specification, servers can declare a `listChanged` capability and should emit `notifications/tools/list_changed` when their tool set changes. However, the AI SDK's MCP client cannot receive or handle these notifications. ## Real-world Impact Dynamic MCP servers that register/unregister tools at runtime cannot properly notify clients of tool availability changes. My recent project [nvim-mcp server](https://github.com/linw1995/nvim-mcp/tree/feat/dynamic_tools) dynamically registers Lua-defined custom tools per connection between the MCP server and Neovim instances. When a new Neovim instance connects or disconnects, the available tool set changes, but the MCP client cannot be notified of these changes. ## Related This is related to issue #7172 about general MCP notification support, but focuses specifically on the `tools/list_changed` notification which is critical for dynamic tool registration scenarios.

title: Support `url` parameter for large-file transcription with Groq experimental_transcribe()
body:
### Description

Right now, when you pass a URL into the `experimental_transcribe()` function, the SDK fetches the file itself, then sends the audio bytes to the provider. 

This means even large audio files that Groq could process via a url parameter are instead being downloaded and then uploaded—triggering `Request Entity Too Large` errors.

[Groq docs](https://console.groq.com/docs/speech-to-text#working-with-audio-files)
```Audio File Limitations
...
Max Attachment File Size
25 MB. If you need to process larger files, use the url parameter to specify a url to the file instead.
...
```

Code that always downloads: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/ai/src/transcribe/transcribe.ts#L95-L98

```ts
const audioData =
    audio instanceof URL
      ? (await download({ url: audio })).data
      : convertDataContentToUint8Array(audio);
```

title: How to manually parse the response stream in Vercel AI SDK 5.0?
body:
### Description

**Describe the use-case**
I’m building an AI code-generation platform that uses the Vercel AI SDK.
- Left-hand chat triggers tool calls (e.g., a client-side writeFile tool).
- Right-hand IDE should show a typewriter effect as the response streams in.

**What worked in 4.x**
In 4.x I could:

1. Grab the raw response stream in onResponse.
2.  Manually parse it with `import { parsePartialJson, processDataStream } from '@ai-sdk/ui-utils';`
3. Feed the parsed chunks to the IDE to achieve the typewriter effect.

**Problem in 5.x**
After upgrading to 5.x:

- I no longer receive the raw response stream (onResponse is gone / no longer exposes the stream).
- Version 5 doesn’t export processUIMessageStream, unlike processDataStream in version 4.
- There is no documented replacement for low-level stream parsing.

**Desired outcome**
Please provide:

1. A public API or utility to access the raw response stream (or an equivalent).
2. A migration guide / example showing how to manually process the stream for custom rendering (typewriter effect, progress bars, etc.) when the built-in hooks are not sufficient.

title: BraintrustExporter is not a constructor when used in AI-SDK V5
body:
### Description

When trying to register the `BraintrustExporter` in a Next.js project with `@vercel/otel`, it fails.

```
Error [TypeError]: An error occurred while loading instrumentation hook:
BraintrustExporter is not a constructor
    at Module.register (instrumentation.ts:7:19)
```

Stack trace shows it’s pulling from the browser build:

```
.../node_modules/braintrust/dist/browser.mjs__[instrumentation-edge]__.BraintrustExporter is not a constructor
```

This suggests that the Edge/browser bundle of `braintrust` does not export `BraintrustExporter` as a class, so calling `new BraintrustExporter(...)` fails.

---

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Next.js 15+ app with `instrumentation.ts`

2. Add:

   ```ts
   import { registerOTel } from '@vercel/otel';
   import { BraintrustExporter } from 'braintrust';

   export function register() {
     registerOTel({
       serviceName: 'my-braintrust-app',
       traceExporter: new BraintrustExporter({
         parent: 'project_name:my-project',
         filterAISpans: true,
       }),
     });
   }
   ``

### Description

When using the AI SDK with the OpenAI Responses API, the AI SDK maps the `system` param into a system message instead of the `instructions` field. this is different from the behavior i'd expect. since AI SDK `system` is so similar to the Responses API `instructions`, i'd expect the mapping to work. 

example:

const result = streamText({
  model: client.responses("some-model"),
  system: "You are a helpful assistant.",
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "hello, how are you?" }],
});
```

This is equivalent to: 

```ts
openai.responses.create({
  model: "some-model"
  input: [
    { role: "system", content: "You are a helpful assistant."},
    { role: "user", content: "hello, how are you?" }],
  instructions: undefined // i'd expect this to be the system message
})
```

I'd expect the streamText() call to map to:

```ts
openai.responses.create({
  model: "some-model"
  input: [

title: Inaccurate usage counts when using Anthropic?
body:
### Description

I've created a coding agentic flow using `@anthropic-ai/sdk@0.60.0`, and later converted the same flow to use the `ai` package and `@ai-sdk/anthropic`.

Using the official anthropic sdk directly, I've had to track usage myself for each step of a conversation/tool usage. I've summed up the numbers and everything seemed correct number-wise:
```
Input tokens: 10572
Output tokens: 499
Cache creation input tokens: 5485
Cache read input tokens: 16455
```
In the first step, I wrote `5485` tokens to the cache (on the system prompts). There were then 3 conversation steps where the cache was read (`5485 * 3 = 16455`). Everything makes sense.

I then converted my flow to the `ai` package.

 I've used `streamText`, and after `result.toUIMessageStream()` has all been consumed, I've printed:
```ts
console.log("Usage:");
console.log(await result.usage);
```
which gave me:
```
Usage:
{
  inputTokens: 4532,
  outputTokens: 222,
  totalTokens: 4754,
  cachedInputTokens: 5439
}
```

`totalTokens = inputTokens + outputTokens`, so nothing interesting there.

`cachedInputTokens`... wasn't sure what this is. Based on the number it seemed like cache write, but where's the cache read? I later found out that this is not the write.

Upon further reading of the documentation, I found `result.providerMetadata`, so I printed:
```ts
  console.log("Usage:");
  console.log(await result.usage);
  console.log("Anthropic Usage:");
  console.log((await result.providerMetadata)?.anthropic?.usage);
```
Which gave me:
```
Usage:
{
  inputTokens: 3056,
  outputTokens: 240,
  totalTokens: 3296,
  cachedInputTokens: 5491
}
Anthropic Usage:
{
  input_tokens: 3056,
  output_tokens: 3,
  cache_creation_input_tokens: 0,
  cache_read_input_tokens: 5491,
  cache_creation: { ephemeral_5m_input_tokens: 0, ephemeral_1h_input_tokens: 0 },
  service_tier: 'standard'
}
```

Observations:
- `output_tokens === 3` seems wrong, and does not match `outputTokens`. The number in `outputTokens` does make sense.
- `cache_creation_input_tokens === 0` makes no sense. I did **not** cache those tokens prior to the conversation, and they were first written to the cache in that chat.
- `cache_read_input_tokens === 5491` matches the `cachedInputTokens`, but also makes no sense. The chat had several steps with several tool calls. It should have read the cache several times. Number seems like it points only to the last step.

I believe I've ruled out a bug in my code, so I wonder whether I'm missing something obvious.

Could it be the reported usage numbers are wrong when using ai (with anthropic; multi-step conversation with tools)?

I find that very unlikely in such widely used package, but this is the only conclusion I could have deduced.

### AI SDK Version

title: `MockLanguageModelV2` Runtime Regression (ai@5.0.27)
body:
### Description

### Summary

Importing `MockLanguageModelV2` from `ai/test` at **application runtime** (outside a Vitest test runner) started crashing in `ai@5.0.27` with:

```
Error: Vitest failed to access its internal state.
```

This is a regression from earlier versions (e.g. `ai@5.0.26` and before) where the same usage worked fine. In `5.0.27`, the bundled `ai/test` entry now hard-imports `vitest`, which assumes a Vitest worker context.

Our use case: We intentionally use the mock model as a lightweight, _deterministic development engine_ to exercise full chat workflows (UI ↔ server ↔ streaming) without calling real providers. This is not a unit test scenario, it's a dev-mode runtime.

### Environment

| Item            | Value                                |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| AI SDK Core     | `ai@5.0.27`                          |
| Node            | `v22.12.0` (also reproduced on 20.x) |
| Package Manager | pnpm                                 |
| OS              | macOS (Apple Silicon)                |

### Before (Working Behavior)

Using `ai@5.0.26`:

```js
import { simulateReadableStream } from "ai";
import { MockLanguageModelV2 } from "ai/test";

const model = new MockLanguageModelV2({
  doStream: async () => ({
    stream: simulateReadableStream({
      chunks: [
        { type: "text-start", id: "text-1" },
        { type: "text-delta", id: "text-1", delta: "Hello dev!" },
        { type: "text-end", id: "text-1" },
        {
          type: "finish",
          finishReason: "stop",
          usage: { inputTokens: 2, outputTokens: 3, totalTokens: 5 }
        }
      ]
    })
  })
});

console.log("Mock instantiated ok", model.specificationVersion);
```

Running with plain `node dev-mock.js` succeeds (no Vitest context required).

The older published `dist/test/index.js` had **no** `require("vitest")`.

### After (Broken in 5.0.27)

The same script now throws immediately:

```
node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:857
  throw new ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND(packageName, fileURLToPath(base), null);
        ^

Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'vitest' imported from /Volumes/SSD-2T/tmp/v27-vitest-issue/node_modules/ai/dist/test/index.mjs
    at packageResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:857:9)
    at moduleResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:926:18)
    at defaultResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:1056:11)
    at ModuleLoader.defaultResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:654:12)
    at #cachedDefaultResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:603:25)
    at ModuleLoader.resolve (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:586:38)
    at ModuleLoader.getModuleJobForImport (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:242:38)
    at ModuleJob._link (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:135:49) {
  code: 'ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND'
}

Node.js v22.12.0
```

Relevant extract from `node_modules/ai/dist/test/index.js` in `5.0.27`:

```js
// src/test/mock-embedding-model-v2.ts
var import_vitest = require("vitest"); // <— new hard import (unused for runtime mocking needs)
```

This unconditional import triggers Vitest’s internal state check when _any_ `ai/test` symbol is imported at runtime.

### Minimal Reproduction Steps

```bash
mkdir ai-mock-runtime-regression && cd ai-mock-runtime-regression
pnpm init --init-type module
pnpm add ai@5.0.27
cat > dev-mock.js <<'EOF'
import { simulateReadableStream } from "ai";
import { MockLanguageModelV2 } from 'ai/test';

new MockLanguageModelV2({
  doStream: async () => ({
    stream: simulateReadableStream({
      chunks: [
        { type: 'text-start', id: 'text-1' },
        { type: 'text-delta', id: 'text-1', delta: 'Hello' },
        { type: 'text-end', id: 'text-1' },
        { type: 'finish', finishReason: 'stop', usage: { inputTokens: 1, outputTokens: 5, totalTokens: 6 } },
      ],
    }),
  }),
});
console.log('OK');
EOF
node dev-mock.js
```

Observed: runtime crash with Vitest internal state error.

Now downgrade:

```bash
pnpm add ai@5.0.26
node dev-mock.js
```

Observed: runs successfully (no Vitest error).

### Impact

- Breaks legitimate dev-mode workflows that rely on mock models for integrated end-to-end local testing / demos.

### Workaround Implemented

We created a lightweight runtime clone (file: `runtimeMockLanguageModel.ts`) mirroring only the needed surface:

```ts
export class RuntimeMockLanguageModelV2 {
  specificationVersion = "v2";
  constructor({ doGenerate, doStream } = {}) {
    /* records calls & delegates */
  }
  // doGenerate / doStream call tracking
}
```

and replaced:

```diff
- import { MockLanguageModelV2 } from 'ai/test';
+ import { RuntimeMockLanguageModelV2 } from './runtimeMockLanguageModel';
```

This restores development ergonomics but duplicates upstream logic.

### Suggested Fixes

Any of the following would resolve the issue:

1. **Remove the unconditional `require('vitest')`** from the published `ai/test` bundle (if it’s unused in production-like mocking scenarios).
2. **Lazy / dynamic import `vitest`** only when the specific features that need it are invoked (e.g. assertions utilities), or guard with a try/catch.
3. **Split exports**: Provide a subpath (e.g. `ai/mock`) that excludes testing framework bindings and only contains pure mock model classes & stream helpers.
4. **Document** that `ai/test` must not be imported outside Vitest and provide an officially blessed alternative for runtime demo mocks.

### Rationale

Mocks are broadly useful beyond unit tests (demos, smoke environments, offline dev). Making them strictly dependent on an active Vitest worker reduces flexibility and introduces unexpected crashes for non-test contexts.

### Request

Please consider decoupling the mock model helpers from Vitest so they can be safely imported at runtime.

### Thanks

Thanks for the excellent SDK! This small adjustment would smooth out dev UX for teams relying on deterministic local mock flows.

---

If more diagnostics are needed (full stack trace, etc.), let me know and I can append them.

title: response.messages contains undefined values that break Firestore persistence
body:
### Description

When using [generateText](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/reference/ai-sdk-core/generate-text#provider-options) with tools and persisting `response.messages` to Firestore, the operation fails because tool-call content parts contain `providerOptions: undefined`.

Error:
```Cannot use "undefined" as a Firestore value (found in field "message.content.0.providerOptions")```

The SDK's `response.messages` includes optional metadata fields like `providerOptions` with `undefined` values rather than omitting them entirely. While `undefined` is valid in TypeScript for optional fields (`providerOptions?: Record<string,Record<string,JSONValue>> | undefined`), Firestore rejects `undefined` values in nested objects.

Reproduction:

1. Use `generateText` with tools enabled
2. Save `stepData.response.messages` from `onStepFinish` callback to Firestore
3. Firestore throws validation error on `undefined` values

Current Workaround:
Sanitize messages before Firestore storage by removing fields with undefined values

title: Maintenance: setup auto-triaging for issues
body:
### Why

In order to help us prioritize issues and to direct incoming requests to the right people, we want to take advantage of some automated triaging.

### What

As a first step, we want to automatically apply the `provider/*` labels when an issue is created.

### How

Create a new "Triage" GitHub Action Workflow. In that workflow

1. Trigger when an issue is created
1. Generate an installation access token using actions/create-github-app-token like we do [here](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/37a4c028ddc17edc38ec28c8ad8e6e5fd0d6fa44/.github/workflows/release.yml#L21-L26)
1. Download existing labels using `gh api` and the [GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels REST API endpoint](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/labels?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-labels-for-a-repository) and filter labels by the `provider/` prefix
1. Use https://github.com/vercel/ai-action with the `schema` input to calculate the most likely `provider/*` label or labels for the new issue
1. Apply the label(s) to the issue using `gh api` and [the POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/labels REST API endpoint](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/labels?apiVersion=2022-11-28#add-labels-to-an-issue)

title: Resuming and Stopping Stream Compatibility
body:
### Description

I just got stream stopping working, where I cancel the backend vercel ai streaming (via streamText `abortSignal`) if the frontend `useChat` calls `stop()`. https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/advanced/stopping-streams

I also just saw @nicoalbanese 's post on the updated docs for resumable streams which is super cool: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-ui/chatbot-resume-streams

My question:

Are these two things compatible? From my understanding, the backend only knows when a client disconnects via some sort of close event. For example, in `express` it would be either `req.on('close', () => { ... }` or `res.on('close', () => { ... }`, and it seems like Nextjs may have a direct `req.signal` value that you can use (not familiar with this).

If you have `abortSignal` set up, it would trigger and stop the stream for _any_ client disconnect, including both an explicit call to `stop()` on the frontend, or an unintentional disconnect or closing of the browser tab. So, on the backend, you wouldn't know if the abort was intentional or not, and thus you couldn't conditionally decide whether the stream should stop or if the stream should continue in case it needs to be resumed and the complete result be persisted.

If this is the case, maybe there should be note on both the stopping streams and resuming streams about this issue.

title: Bug: Windows compatibility issue: rm -rf command not available on Windows
body:
### Description

The AI SDK codebase contains 41+ packages that use Unix-specific `rm -rf` commands in their `package.json` clean scripts, causing build failures on Windows systems.

### Root Cause

All packages use this pattern in their `package.json`:
```json
"clean": "rm -rf dist *.tsbuildinfo"
```

On Windows, `rm` is not a recognized command, causing:
```
'rm' is not recognized as an internal or external command,
operable program or batch file.
```

### Reproduction Steps

1. Clone the AI SDK repository on a Windows machine
2. Run `npm install` or `pnpm install` to install dependencies
3. Run `npm run test` from the root directory
4. Build fails at the first package requiring a clean step

**Expected behavior:** Tests run successfully across all packages  
**Actual behavior:** Build fails with `'rm' is not recognized` error

### Affected Packages

At least 41 packages are affected, including:
- `@ai-sdk/provider`
- `@ai-sdk/anthropic`
- `@ai-sdk/openai`
- `@ai-sdk/react`
- `@ai-sdk/vue`
- `@ai-sdk/svelte`
- `@ai-sdk/angular`
- And 34+ other packages in the monorepo

### Environment

- **Operating System:** Windows 10/11
- **Shell:** PowerShell/Command Prompt
- **Node.js:** Any version
- **Package Manager:** npm/pnpm

### Error Output

```
> @ai-sdk/provider@2.0.0 clean
> rm -rf dist *.tsbuildinfo

'rm' is not recognized as an internal or external command,
operable program or batch file.
 ELIFECYCLE  Command failed with exit code 1.
```

### Proposed Solutions

The issue can be resolved by replacing `rm -rf` commands with cross-platform alternatives:

**Option 1: Use `del-cli` (Recommended)**
```json
"clean": "del-cli dist *.tsbuildinfo"
```

**Option 2: Use `rimraf`**
```json
"clean": "rimraf dist *.tsbuildinfo"
```

**Option 3: Native Node.js solution**
```json
"clean": "node -e \"require('fs').rmSync('dist', {recursive: true, force: true})\""
```

### Impact

- **Contributors:** Windows developers cannot run the full test suite
- **CI/CD:** Potential build failures on Windows runners
- **Development Experience:** Inconsistent cross-platform behavior blocks Windows contributor onboarding

This affects the build pipeline and testing workflow, potentially impacting contributor onboarding and CI reliability on Windows environments.


### AI SDK Version


Affected versions include the latest releases:
- ai: 4.1.2+
- @ai-sdk/provider: 2.0.0+
- @ai-sdk/anthropic: 2.0.0+
- @ai-sdk/openai: 1.0.0+
- @ai-sdk/react: 2.0.0+
- All packages in the monorepo that use rm -rf in clean scripts

title: Bug: React test suite fails: React 19 RC + react-dom 18.3.1 mismatch causes `ReactCurrentDispatcher` error
body:
### Description

The `@ai-sdk/react` test suite fails before executing any tests due to a React internal initialization error:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ReactCurrentDispatcher')
```

This occurs when `react` resolves to a 19.0.0 RC build while `react-dom` resolves to 18.3.1 in the monorepo install graph:

```
.../node_modules/.pnpm/react-dom@18.3.1_react@19.0.0-rc.1/...
```

The failure triggers during environment setup (Vitest + jsdom) before any test blocks are collected, producing “0 tests” and immediate suite failure. This is unrelated to application code or recent build-script changes (e.g. replacing `rm -rf` with `del-cli`).

### Impact

- Blocks CI green runs for PRs unrelated to React.
- Prevents validating regressions in `@ai-sdk/react`.
- Masks unrelated changes behind upstream dependency resolution instability.

### Reproduction Steps

Clean environment (any OS):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vercel/ai.git
cd ai
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @ai-sdk/react test
```

Observed excerpt:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ReactCurrentDispatcher')
react-dom.development.js:994:51
...
Test Files  3 failed (3)
Tests       no tests
```

On Windows prior to fixing clean scripts this was masked by `rm` failures; after adopting `del-cli` the mismatch surfaces.

### Expected Behavior

React tests should initialize, collect test cases, and pass/fail on assertions—no internal dispatcher error.

### Actual Behavior

All UI test files in `@ai-sdk/react` fail during module load; zero tests execute.

### Diagnostics

1. `pnpm why react` shows a 19.0.0 RC version selected.
2. `pnpm why react-dom` shows 18.3.1 selected.
3. Installed path: `react-dom@18.3.1_react@19.0.0-rc.1` indicates mismatch.
4. React internals require aligned major (and RC) versions; mismatch yields undefined dispatcher state.

### Scope

Limited to test/runtime of `@ai-sdk/react`. No production bundle break confirmed yet (depends on consumer project peers).

### Root Cause Hypothesis

Mixed semver ranges allowed pnpm to satisfy `react` with an RC while `react-dom` stayed on stable 18.3.1, creating incompatible internal contracts.

### Suggested Resolutions

Option A (Align on RC):
```json
"pnpm": {
  "overrides": {
    "react": "19.0.0-rc-cc1ec60d0d-20240607",
    "react-dom": "19.0.0-rc-cc1ec60d0d-20240607"
  }
}
```

Option B (Revert to stable 18):
```json
"pnpm": {
  "overrides": {
    "react": "18.3.1",
    "react-dom": "18.3.1"
  }
}
```

Option C (Guard): Pre-test script validates aligned major versions and fails fast with guidance.

Option D (Temporary): Exclude `@ai-sdk/react` tests in CI matrix until alignment (not preferred).

### Recommendation

Adopt Option B (stable 18.3.1) unless an intentional React 19 migration roadmap exists. If evaluating React 19, use Option A plus a tracking issue/milestone.

### Verification Plan After Fix

1. Fresh install.
2. `pnpm --filter @ai-sdk/react test` runs with no dispatcher error.
3. CI run on unrelated PR passes React test initialization.
4. (Optional) Add automated assertion ensuring `react` and `react-dom` share major + prerelease tag.



### AI SDK Version

- ai: 4.x (main snapshot)
- @ai-sdk/react: 2.x
- @ai-sdk/openai: 1.x
- @ai-sdk/provider: 2.x

Exact versions depend on current lockfile; problem centers on pair alignment, not single-package code changes.

### Environment

- Node >= 18
- pnpm 9.x
- Vitest 2.x
- Reproduced on Linux and Windows (post cross‑platform clean script fix)

### Additional Notes

Issue surfaced only after enabling Windows builds (replacing `rm -rf` with `del-cli`). Earlier Windows attempts failed before reaching React test initialization.

### Proposed Next Step

Submit override PR (Option B or A) + add a lightweight guard script to prevent regressions.

title: Bug: Anthropic: Provider-executed tool results lose specific type information when re-hydrated from message history
body:
### Description

The Anthropic `web_search` (and similar provider-executed) tool returns a structured, discriminated object (e.g. `{ type: 'web_search_result', ... }`). The SDK stores that payload inside a `role: 'tool'` message after `JSON.stringify`. On a later turn the conversion layer `JSON.parse`s it back without a reviver / schema so the discriminant narrowing is lost; callers see a widened generic object and must cast.

### Impact
- Blocks ergonomic, type‑safe multi‑turn agent loops.
- Forces unsafe `as WebSearchResult` assertions or ad‑hoc schema parsing every turn.
- Increases risk of silent drift if Anthropic evolves result shape.
- Adds friction to building higher level reusable tooling abstractions.

### Reproduction Steps
Clean environment (any OS):

```ts
const history: any[] = [];
const first = await generateText({
  model: anthropic('claude-3-5-sonnet-latest', { tools: { web_search: {} } }),
  prompt: 'Find recent TypeScript performance articles'
});

history.push(...first.response.messages); // tool-result part holds JSON string

const second = await generateText({
  model: anthropic('claude-3-5-sonnet-latest', { tools: { web_search: {} } }),
  messages: history
});

// second.messages: tool result now plain object with widened type
```
Observed: `history.find(m => m.role==='tool').content[0].result` is a plain object (no discriminated union narrowing).

### Expected Behavior
Tool result remains a structured object (not stringified early); TypeScript inference narrows to `web_search_result` across turns without manual casting.

### Actual Behavior
Result is stored as JSON string then parsed generically; narrowing lost and user must cast / re‑validate.

### Diagnostics
1. Message insertion phase eagerly stringifies provider tool output.
2. Anthropic prompt builder (`convertToAnthropicMessagesPrompt`) blindly `JSON.parse`s.
3. No schema registry / reviver to restore discriminants.
4. Error path (`is_error`) would suffer same widening.

### Scope
Affects multi‑turn flows using provider-executed Anthropic tools. Single‑turn flows unaffected. User-implemented (local) tools can already retain structure.

### Root Cause Hypothesis
Mixed concerns: persistence convenience (string) chosen over maintaining structured in-memory object; absence of typed deserialization step.

### Suggested Resolutions
Option A (Preferred – Align w/ current API boundary): Store raw object in history; only serialize right before Anthropic API call.

Option B (Schema Registry): Maintain map toolName -> zod (or similar) schema; validate + narrow on re-hydration.

Option C (Discriminant Wrapper): Add `resultType: result.type` alongside `result` to preserve narrowing even if stringified.

Option D (Guard / Deprecation): Keep string for one version but emit warning if `typeof result === 'string'`.

### Recommendation
Adopt Option A immediately (no premature stringification). Optionally follow with Option B if a provider schema layer already exists / is planned.

### Verification Plan After Fix
1. Unit: tool-result message stores non-string structured object.
2. Unit: second turn deepEqual (shape) to original result.
3. Type test: inference of `result.type` narrows to `'web_search_result'`.
4. Regression: error (`is_error`) handling unchanged.
5. Smoke: outbound Anthropic payload identical aside from removal of redundant parse/stringify.




### AI SDK Version

- ai: 4.1.2 (main snapshot)
- @ai-sdk/anthropic (latest)

### Environment
- Node >= 18
- pnpm 9.x
- Reproduced on Windows 
### Additional Notes
Removing double JSON cycle reduces overhead for large tool outputs; prepares pathway for future streaming partial tool results.

### Proposed Next Step
Submit PR implementing Option A + tests + changelog; open follow-up issue if pursuing schema registry.

title: useChat Hook Missing Support for UI Message Streams with `createUIMessageStream`
body:
### Description

The current `useChat` hook from `@ai-sdk/react` doesn't support the newer UI Message Stream format introduced with `createUIMessageStream`. This creates a compatibility gap between server-side streaming APIs and client-side hooks.

**Current behavior:**
- Server uses `createUIMessageStream` with custom data parts, sources, and reconciliation
- Client `useChat` only handles traditional text streaming
- Custom data parts like `data-weather`, `source`, transient notifications are ignored
- No `streamMode` or `experimental_streamMode` option available

### **Describe the solution you'd like**

Add UI Message Stream support to `useChat` hook with options like:

```typescript
const { messages, sendMessage } = useChat<MyUIMessage>({
  api: "/api/chat",
  streamMode: "ui-message-stream", // or experimental_streamMode
  onData: (dataPart) => {
    // Handle data parts including transient ones
  },
});
```

This would enable:
- Custom data parts rendering (`data-weather`, etc.)
- Source references for RAG applications  
- Transient notifications
- Data part reconciliation/updates
- Type-safe message parts

### **Describe alternatives you've considered**

**Current workaround:** Manual Server-Sent Events parsing with `fetch()` + `ReadableStream`, but this:
- Requires custom state management
- Loses built-in `useChat` features (error handling, loading states)
- Needs extensive type casting (`as any`)
- Duplicates functionality


**Related:**
- Server API: `createUIMessageStream` ✅ Available
- Client hook: `useChat` with UI streams ❌ Missing
- Issue #8227 mentions "Message Parts Carryover" which seems related

This feature would complete the UI Message Stream ecosystem and eliminate the need for custom streaming implementations.


### AI SDK Version

- `ai`: 5.0.39
- `@ai-sdk/react`: 2.0.39  
- `@ai-sdk/openai`: 2.0.27
- Next.js: 15.5.2
- React: 19.1.0

title: activeTools filtering allows execution of tool calls not in active tools list
body:
### Description

The `activeTools` parameter in `streamText` does not properly restrict tool execution. The LLM can generate and successfully execute tool calls for tools that are not included in the `activeTools` array.

**Expected Behavior:**
  When activeTools is specified, only tools listed in that array should be:
  1. Available to the LLM for tool call generation
  2. Executable when called.
  3. Calling a tool not inside `activeTools` should throw the appropriate "tool does not exist" exception.

  **Actual Behavior:**
  - The LLM can generate tool calls for tools not in activeTools based on conversation memory.
  - These "phantom" tool calls execute successfully if the tool exists in the full tools object.
  - The activeTools filtering appears to have no effect on tool execution.

The result is that the LLM might call tools by its name, but at the time of generating the tool call it has no access anymore to the schema or instructions of the tool, so it's basically a wild guess on whether it's used correctly.

 **Root Cause Analysis:**
  The issue appears to be in the tool execution phase. While `prepareToolsAndToolChoice` correctly filters tools based on `activeTools` the LLM can generate tool calls based on conversation memory, and the SDK executes these calls against the full tools object rather than the filtered subset.

```ts

const { toolChoice: stepToolChoice, tools: stepTools } =
            prepareToolsAndToolChoice({
              tools,
              toolChoice: prepareStepResult?.toolChoice ?? toolChoice,
              activeTools: prepareStepResult?.activeTools ?? activeTools,
            });

// MORE

const streamWithToolResults = runToolsTransformation({
            tools, // THIS HERE SHOULD BE "stepTools"
            generatorStream: stream,
            tracer,
            telemetry,
            system,
            messages: stepInputMessages,
            repairToolCall,
            abortSignal,
            experimental_context,
          });
```

title: Minimizing RAM usage (feature)
body:
### Description

While trying some other providers (coming from vertex), I noticed the usual RAM usage spike because arbitrary URLs aren't supported in their API and ai sdk will download and pass them as base64 strings. Haven't done a deep dive yet, but I believe that there's not anything "smart" going one behind the scenes. 

Most codebases will be using URLs with the lib, and not conditionally swap to base64 to try to minimize RAM usage (and I think that's the point of this library too, to abstract these things away). I find it quite frequent (at least in my codebase) that the same files are being used in more than one generation, at the same time. This seems to mean that RAM usage is multiplied.

I thought that adding some shared state here for attachments would be a good idea, where the lib could reuse the already occupied memory for any other `streamText/Object` that comes in. I know this essentially means that you "cache" the URL, but that would only be the case for as long as an active generation is using that URL, so it doesn't seem like that big of a deal.

Essentially,
- `generateText` A with file part `example.com/foo.pdf` starts
- `generateText` B with file part `example.com/foo.pdf` starts 
- Both use the same downloaded base64 string from this shared state (an object with key being the URL would do)

title: `providerOptions` are not correctly passed for Azure embeddings 🐛
body:
### Description

The `@ai-sdk/azure` package's `embed` function does not seem to correctly process `providerOptions` when creating embeddings. 
The provided documentation example suggests using `providerOptions: { azure: { ... } }` to pass specific parameters like dimensions and user for an Azure model.

```ts
import { azure } from '@ai-sdk/azure';
import { embed } from 'ai';

const { embedding } = await embed({
  model: azure.textEmbedding('your-embedding-deployment'),
  value: 'sunny day at the beach',
  providerOptions: {
    azure: { // <-- This seems to be the issue
      dimensions: 512,
      user: 'test-user',
    },
  },
});
```
However, this configuration fails to apply the options to the underlying request. In contrast, if I use the `@ai-sdk/openai` package with `providerOptions: { openai: { ... } }`, the options are correctly passed and the request is successful.

Upon reviewing the `@ai-sdk source` code, it appears that the internal logic for handling providerOptions might be specifically looking for an openai key, even when the model provider is Azure. This suggests that the documentation is either misleading or the implementation is bugged, as the azure key in `providerOptions` is seemingly ignored.

### Reproduction Steps

- Set up a project with `@ai-sdk/azure` and ai packages.
- Configure your environment variables for Azure AI services.
- Use the embed function with azure.textEmbedding as shown in the documentation example.
- Add dimensions or user to the providerOptions object under the azure key.

Observe that the request to Azure does not include these parameters, or the call fails due to invalid parameters.

title: Image Editing
body:
### Research

image editing types:

- **Outpainting** (“image expansion”, “uncrop”) — extend canvas beyond bounds; usually via prompt, sometimes prompt-free. 
- **Inpainting** (with/without prompt & mask/overlay) — edit inside a region; classic mask-based “generative fill.” 
- **Upscaling** / Super-resolution — increase resolution with minimal changes (ESRGAN, etc.). 
- **Variations** — small changes around a given image (sometimes via “image reference” or adapters like FLUX Redux). 
- **Restyle** (img2img) — preserve content/layout, change style via a prompt; many APIs call this “image-to-image.” 
- **Masked restyle** / local edits — prompt-guided changes bound to a region, or “local editing” without an explicit binary mask (e.g., FLUX Kontext). 
- **Background remove/replace** (RMBG / background swap). 
- **Object remove/add** (“gen-fill” / “erase” / “insert”) — targeted content edits. 
- **Control-guided edits** (ControlNet-style) — pose, depth, edge, scribble guidance. (Varies by host; often listed as “tools / adapters”.) 
- **Text editing** in images — replace text content cleanly.

### Description

Hi team,

I’ve encountered an intermittent issue with `experimental_telemetry` when using `streamText` with tool calling.

### Expected behavior

The system prompt should be logged in the `messages` field as an object, e.g.:

{

```json
[

    "role": "system",
    "content": "You are an **expert medical specialist assistant** ..."

]

When the incorrect format is logged, the OpenAI model fails to process properly.

* Use `experimental_telemetry` with `streamText`
* Observe telemetry logs across multiple traces

### Questions

* Is this a known issue with `experimental_telemetry`?
* Is there a recommended workaround to ensure the `messages` field is consistently logged in the correct format?

title: create v3 provider model specs
body:
### General tips

- Example pull request for reference: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/8777
- after each change, run `pnpm type-check`
- Use your IDE's `rename symbol` feature. That will rename all references of a type across the repository. After renaming the symbol in e.g. `v3/image-model-v3-call-warning.ts`, it will change 

  ```ts
  export type { ImageModelV2CallWarning } from './image-model-v3-call-warning';
  ```
  
  to 
  
  ```ts
  export type { ImageModelV3CallWarning as ImageModelV2CallWarning } from './image-model-v3-call-warning';
  ```
  
  in `v3/index.ts` first. You have to use rename symbol on `ImageModelV2CallWarning` again so that it becomes 
  
  ```ts
  export type { ImageModelV3CallWarning as ImageModelV3CallWarning } from './image-model-v3-call-warning';
  ```
  
  That will update all the code outside of `packages/provider`. Then change it to just 
  
  ```ts
  export type { ImageModelV3CallWarning } from './image-model-v3-call-warning';
  ```
- `rename symbol` won't cover everything, after the rename, do a global search for the renamed type and update it accordingly in docs, test titles, etc. 
- Do not edit v2 provider package when upgrading models from v2 to v3, do a v3 provider package with all necessary changes at the end

### TODOs

- [ ] Make sure community providers that implement v2 specs continue to work (update model types in `packages/ai/src/types/*-model.ts`, add adapter for `'v2'` in `packages/ai/src/model/resolve-model.ts`, keep v2 mock models - which also removes the breaking change)
- [ ] RSC needs some extra work, we need to import `LanguageModel` from `ai` and `resolveModel` from `ai/internal`: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/8877/files#diff-cbe66fd6d311166b3270a845d4cd6029509bb9ac2b7a8484e6b4fe44c87c1138

title: Vercel AI Gateway Issue: Invalid Input Error with Message Content Validation
body:
### Description

We're experiencing intermittent `GatewayInvalidRequestError: Invalid input` errors when using Vercel AI Gateway, particularly frequent when using GPT-5 model. The error occurs during message processing and appears to be related to validation of message content structure.

### Error Details

```
Error [GatewayInvalidRequestError]: Invalid input
    at P (.next/server/chunks/2281.js:57:2334)
    ...
    statusCode: 400,
    type: 'invalid_request_error'
```

[full-1.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22463037/full-1.log)
[full-2.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22463036/full-2.log)

The detailed error response indicates validation failures for specific message content parts:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Invalid input",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": [
      {
        "code": "invalid_union",
        "errors": [
          [
            {"code": "invalid_value", "values": ["text"], "path": ["type"], "message": "Invalid input: expected \"text\""},
            {"expected": "string", "code": "invalid_type", "path": ["text"], "message": "Invalid input: expected string, received undefined"}
          ],
          // ... other type validations for "file", "reasoning", "tool-call"
        ],
        "path": ["prompt", 2, "content", 3],
        "message": "Invalid input"
      },
      // Similar error for ["prompt", 2, "content", 9]
    ]
  }
}
```

### Key Observations

1. The error specifically points to `prompt[2].content[3]` and `prompt[2].content[9]` having invalid format
2. The validation expects content parts to have a `type` field and corresponding data fields (e.g., `text` field for text type)
3. The error suggests some message content parts are missing required fields
4. This happens intermittently and is difficult to reproduce consistently
5. More frequent with GPT-5 model compared to other models

### Expected Behavior

The gateway should either:
1. Handle all valid message formats that `convertToModelMessages()` produces
2. Provide clearer error messages about what specific message format is invalid
3. Document any message format requirements specific to the gateway

### Additional Information

- The error occurs after messages pass through `convertToModelMessages()` from the AI SDK
- The application works correctly when not using the gateway (direct provider connections)
- The issue seems related to how certain message types (possibly file attachments or tool results) are formatted for the gateway

title: AI SDK v5 Telemetry Missing Final Assistant Reasoning Steps
body:
### Description

## Summary
The AI SDK v5 `experimental_telemetry` feature does not capture the final assistant reasoning steps that occur after tool calls in the `ai.streamText.doStream` and `ai.generateText.doStream` function runs. Only pre-tool reasoning appears as streamed steps; post-tool reasoning is only available in the final response object.

## Environment
- **AI SDK Version**: 5.0.24
- **Model**: OpenAI o1 (o1-preview, o1-mini)
- **Provider**: OpenAI
- **Telemetry Backend**: Langfuse

## Expected Behavior
When using `streamText()` or `generateText()` with `experimental_telemetry: { isEnabled: true }`, all reasoning steps should appear as observations within the function run, including:
1. Initial reasoning before tool calls (✅ works)
2. Tool call steps (✅ works) 
3. **Final assistant reasoning after tool calls** (❌ missing)

## Actual Behavior
- Pre-tool reasoning appears as streamed steps in `ai.streamText.doStream`
- Tool calls appear as steps
- **Final assistant reasoning is missing from the step list** and only available in `response.reasoning`
- This creates incomplete traces where the last assistant message with reasoning is not captured

## Reproduction Steps
1. Use `streamText()` with a model that supports reasoning (o1-preview/o1-mini)
2. Enable `experimental_telemetry: { isEnabled: true }`
3. Configure a tool that will be called during generation
4. Set `reasoningEffort: 'high'` and `reasoningSummary: 'detailed'`
5. Observe the resulting Langfuse trace

**Expected**: All reasoning steps visible in `ai.streamText.doStream`  
**Actual**: Final reasoning missing from step list, only in response object

## Code Example
```typescript
const result = await streamText({
  model: openai('o1-preview'),
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'What is hypertension?' }],
  tools: { search: searchTool },
  experimental_telemetry: {
    isEnabled: true,
    functionId: 'medical-chat',
  },
  providerOptions: {
    openai: {
      reasoningEffort: 'high',
      reasoningSummary: 'detailed',
    },
  },
});

// response.reasoning contains final reasoning
// But ai.streamText.doStream step list is missing the final assistant reasoning
```

## Impact
- **Observability**: Incomplete traces make debugging and analysis difficult
- **Consistency**: Pre-tool reasoning is captured but post-tool reasoning is not
- **User Experience**: Developers expect all reasoning steps to be visible in telemetry

## Workaround
Currently requires manual instrumentation with Langfuse SDK to emit final reasoning as a separate observation, which defeats the purpose of built-in telemetry.

## Request
Please ensure that all assistant reasoning steps (including final reasoning after tool calls) are captured as observations within the `ai.streamText.doStream` and `ai.generateText.doStream` function runs when `experimental_telemetry` is enabled.

## Additional Context
- This affects both streaming (`streamText`) and non-streaming (`generateText`) APIs
- The issue is consistent across different reasoning effort levels
- Tool calls themselves are properly captured; only the final assistant reasoning is missing

### AI SDK Version

@ai-sdk/openai: ^2.0.21
@ai-sdk/react: ^2.0.24

title: experimental_telemetry creates independent traces for tool calls in generateText but works correctly in streamText
body:
### Description

### Bug Description

When using the AI SDK's `experimental_telemetry` feature, tool calls create independent trace IDs instead of being nested under the parent trace when using `generateText`, but the same tool calls work correctly (nested under parent trace) when using `streamText`.

### Expected Behavior

Tool calls should inherit the same trace ID as the parent operation and appear as nested observations, regardless of whether using `generateText` or `streamText`.

### Actual Behavior

- **`streamText`**: Tool calls are correctly nested under the parent trace ✅
- **`generateText`**: Tool calls create new, independent trace IDs ❌

### Steps to Reproduce

1. **Setup**: Configure AI SDK with `experimental_telemetry` enabled
2. **Test with `streamText`**:
   ```typescript
   const result = streamText({
       model,
       messages,
       tools: {
           retrieve_guidelines_parallel: await parallelRetrievalTool.get()
       },
       experimental_telemetry: {
           isEnabled: true,
           functionId: "test-function"
       }
   });
   ```
   **Result**: Tool calls appear nested under parent trace ✅

3. **Test with `generateText`**:
   ```typescript
   const result = await generateText({
       model,
       messages,
       tools: {
           retrieve_guidelines_parallel: await parallelRetrievalTool.get()
       },
       experimental_telemetry: {
           isEnabled: true,
           functionId: "test-function"
       }
   });
   ```
   **Result**: Tool calls create independent traces ❌

### Environment Details

- **AI SDK Version**: 5.0.51
- **Node.js Version**: 20.x
- **Observability Platform**: Langfuse (used to visualize the traces, but issue is with AI SDK telemetry)

### Code Context

Both functions use identical configurations:
- Same model
- Same messages
- Same tools
- Same `experimental_telemetry` settings

The only difference is using `generateText` vs `streamText`.

### Impact

This inconsistency makes it difficult to:
- Correlate tool usage with the main operation in non-streaming scenarios
- Analyze execution flows consistently across different AI SDK functions
- Track costs and performance metrics for complete operations

### Root Cause Analysis

The issue appears to be in how `experimental_telemetry` handles trace context propagation differently between `generateText` and `streamText`. The streaming implementation correctly maintains trace hierarchy, while the non-streaming implementation creates independent traces for tool calls.

### Question

Is this the expected behavior, or should both `generateText` and `streamText` handle tool call tracing consistently? If this is a bug, are there any workarounds to ensure proper trace nesting in `generateText`?

### AI SDK Version

AI SDK: 5.0.51
OpenTelemetry: @opentelemetry/api 1.9.0
Vercel OTel: @vercel/otel 1.13.0
Node.js: 20.x
Langfuse: 3.38.5 (for trace visualization)

`streamText` currently uses the last available provider metadata for each text and reasoning part. This can lead to situations where the metadata is overridden in middlewares or transformations.

title: useChat does not update when transport changes
body:
### Description

  The `useChat` hook from `@ai-sdk/react` does not update when the `transport` changes reference. Even when passing a new transport object with different configuration, the hook continues to use the initial transport configuration.

  #### Steps to Reproduce
  1. Create a `useChat` hook with a custom transport
  2. Change the transport object (e.g., API endpoint)
  3. Pass the new transport object to `useChat`
  4. Send a message
  5. Observe that the old transport configuration is still being used

  #### Code Example
  ```typescript
  const transport = useMemo(() => {
    return new DefaultChatTransport({
      api: apiEndpoint // This value changes
    });
  }, [apiEndpoint]);

  const chat = useChat({ transport }); // Hook doesn't update when transport changes
  ```

  **Expected Behavior**

  When the transport prop changes, useChat should use the new transport configuration for subsequent requests.

  **Actual Behavior**

  useChat continues to use the initial transport configuration regardless of prop changes.

title: **Title:** `generateObject` fails on models without structuredOutputs support, while `generateText` + `tool` works reliably
body:
### Description

## Problem

The `generateObject` function consistently fails on models that don't support structuredOutputs (like glm-4.5-flash from ZhiPu AI), throwing `NoObjectGeneratedError` even when the model generates valid JSON that matches the schema.

## Root Cause Analysis

After examining the source code in `node_modules/ai/dist/index.js`:

1. **`generateObject` has no `mode` parameter**: The API documentation and implementation don't include a `mode` parameter. Setting `mode: "tool"` or `mode: "json"` has no effect - it's ignored.

2. **Dependency on structuredOutputs**: `generateObject` relies on the model's `responseFormat` capability for structured output. When the model doesn't support structuredOutputs, it falls back to parsing raw text, but validation often fails.

3. **Schema validation issues**: The `objectOutputStrategy` uses `safeValidateTypes` for final validation, but the parsing and validation process is brittle for models without native structured output support.

## Working Alternative

Using `generateText` with `tool` definitions provides reliable structured output generation:

```javascript
const submit_object = tool({
  description: 'Submit user requested JSON object',
  inputSchema: z.object({
    recipe: z.object({
      name: z.string(),
      ingredients: z.array(z.object({ name: z.string(), amount: z.string() })),
      steps: z.array(z.string()),
    }),
  }),
});

const res = await generateText({
  model: model,
  tools: { submit_object },
  prompt: 'Generate a recipe JSON',
  stopWhen: hasToolCall('submit_object')
});

const object = res.toolCalls[0].input;
```

This approach:
- Works consistently across all models
- Provides pre-validation through Zod schemas
- Forces structured output via tool calling
- Doesn't depend on model's structuredOutputs capability

## Test Results

**Failing case (`generateObject`):**
- Model: glm-4.5-flash (ZhiPu AI)
- Error: `NoObjectGeneratedError: No object generated: response did not match schema`
- Even when model generates correct JSON

**Working case (`generateText` + `tool`):**
- Same model and schema
- Successfully generates and validates structured objects
- Consistent results across multiple runs

## Suggested Fix

1. **Improve fallback handling** in `generateObject` for models without structuredOutputs support
2. **Add better error messages** indicating when structuredOutputs is required vs. when text parsing fallback is used
3. **Document the `generateText` + `tool` pattern** as a reliable alternative
4. **Consider implementing tool-based generation** as a fallback in `generateObject`

## Environment

- AI SDK version: 5.0.52
- Model: glm-4.5-flash (ZhiPu AI)
- Node.js: 22.19.0

title: 🤖 Provider API update - anthropic@1.3.0
body:
### New features

- Context management framework
  - New configuration and response types: `context_management` added across requests and responses.
    - Requests: `context_management` is now supported in `messages.create` parameters and `count_message_tokens` parameters via `BetaContextManagementConfig`.
    - Responses: `context_management` details are returned in `Message`, `MessageDeltaEvent`, and `CountMessageTokensResponse` via `BetaResponseContextManagement` and `BetaContextManagementResponse`.
    - Edit support: New edit type `clear_tool_uses_20250919` (`BetaClearToolUses20250919`) with options:
      - `trigger`: `input_tokens` (`BetaInputTokensTrigger`) or `tool_uses` (`BetaToolUsesTrigger`)
      - `keep`: number of tool uses to retain (`BetaToolUsesKeep`)
      - `clear_at_least`: minimum tokens to clear (`BetaInputTokensClearAtLeast`)
      - `clear_tool_inputs`: clear all or specific tool inputs
      - `exclude_tools`: preserve specific tool uses
    - Applied edit results are returned via `BetaResponseClearToolUses20250919Edit` in `applied_edits`.

- Memory Tool (beta)
  - New tool `memory_20250818` (name: `memory`) added to the available tools list.
  - Supported commands (`BetaMemoryTool_20250818_Command`):
    - `view` (optional `view_range`), `create` (`path`, `file_text`), `insert` (`path`, `insert_line`, `insert_text`), `delete` (`path`), `rename` (`old_path`, `new_path`), `str_replace` (`path`, `old_str`, `new_str`).

- API responses enriched with context management info
  - `CountMessageTokensResponse` now includes `context_management` alongside `input_tokens`.
  - `Message` objects and streaming `MessageDeltaEvent` include `context_management` with applied edits.

- New stop reason value
  - `model_context_window_exceeded` added to `stop_reason` enum for responses and streaming events.

- New model identifiers
  - `claude-sonnet-4-5` and `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` added to the models list.
