title: useChat throws "No tool output found for apply patch" error despite all tool results being present
body:
### Description

When using useChat with client-side tool execution (onToolCall), the SDK throws an error claiming a tool output is missing for the apply_patch tool, even though all tool results have been successfully added via addToolResult. This occurs when the LLM includes multiple apply_patch tool calls in a single streaming response.

`Error: No tool output found for apply patch call call_DQpB1915HkfJA8yMqNxPTNDj.
    at process-ui-message-stream.ts:659:25
    at chat.ts:622:11
    at Array.<anonymous> (serial-job-executor.ts:26:17)
    at SerialJobExecutor.processQueue (serial-job-executor.ts:15:25)
    at serial-job-executor.ts:33:17
    at new Promise (<anonymous>)
    at SerialJobExecutor.run (serial-job-executor.ts:23:12)
    at runUpdateMessageJob (chat.ts:621:26)
    at Object.transform (process-ui-message-stream.ts:102:15)`                                                                                                                


Steps to Reproduce:                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                        
  1. Set up useChat with sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls                                                             
  2. Define an apply_patch client-side tool in onToolCall that executes quickly (~20-50ms)                                                              
  3. Have the LLM stream a response that includes multiple apply_patch tool calls (as few as 2, more consistent with 5+, and the calls should create or delete files, although I think updating caused an error once for me too)
  4. The LLM streams all tool calls in the response (not calling one and waiting for the result before calling the next)                                
  5. Each onToolCall handler executes sequentially on the client and successfully calls addToolResult with output                                       
  6. After all tools complete, the SDK throws: Error: No tool output found for apply patch call call_xxxxx                                              

Expected Behavior:                 

All tool results are present in the message parts, so the SDK should recognize all tools are complete and either auto-send the next message (due to sendAutomaticallyWhen) or transition to a ready state.                                                                                                

Actual Behavior:                                                                                                                                      

The SDK throws an error claiming an apply_patch tool output is missing. However, inspection of the message parts shows:                               
  - The "missing" tool call has state: "output-available" or "output-error"                                                                             
  - It has a valid output or errorText property                                                                                                         
  - All other tool calls also have complete outputs                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                        
Evidence:                                                                                                                                             

  From browser console logs showing the message parts when the error occurs:                                                                            

  // Error message:                                                                                                                                     
  Error: No tool output found for apply patch call call_DQpB1915HkfJA8yMqNxPTNDj                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                        
  // But the message parts show it's present:                                                                                                           
  {                                                                                                                                                     
    "toolCallId": "call_DQpB1915HkfJA8yMqNxPTNDj",                                                                                                      
    "toolName": "apply_patch",                                                                                                                          
    "state": "output-available",                                                                                                                        
    "hasOutput": true                                                                                                                                   
  }                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                        
  Example scenarios where this occurs:                                                                                                                  
  - 2 apply_patch calls to create files (occasional)                                                                                                    
  - 5+ apply_patch calls to create files (consistent)                                                                                                   
  - 31+ (probably less too but haven't tested) apply_patch calls to delete files (consistent)                                                    
                                                                                                                                                        
All tool calls show state: "output-available" or "output-error" with hasOutput: true, yet the SDK claims one specific apply_patch call is missing.    
                                                                                                                                                        
Additional Context:                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                               
  - The specific apply_patch tool call ID that triggers the error varies between occurrences                                                            
  - Only observed with the apply_patch tool - have not seen this with other tools like readFiles, restart, etc.                                         
  - Client-side logging confirms:                                                                                                                       
    - onToolCall is called for each tool                                                                                                                
    - addToolResult is called with valid output                                                                                                         
    - addToolResult returns successfully                                                                                                                
    - All tool calls show wasParallel: false (no concurrent execution in the handler)                                                                   
  - Re-calling addToolResult for the "missing" tool doesn't fix the internal state

### AI SDK Version

title: Replicate provider hard‑codes Prefer: wait (60s cap) and fails on long predictions
body:
### Description

The Replicate provider passes `prefer: 'wait'` to all image generations

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/fad04b2e4ad6f927daebb5e7e342f0a98d35c3cd/packages/replicate/src/replicate-image-model.ts#L67-L69

According to Replicate's docs here: https://replicate.com/docs/reference/http/#predictions.create

> The request will wait up to 60 seconds for the model to run. If this time is exceeded the prediction will be returned in a "starting" state and need to be retrieved using the predictions.get endpoint.

And on the docs under create a prediction: https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/create-a-prediction#timeout-duration

> The default duration for sync mode is 60 seconds, but you can specify a different timeout duration in the header if needed. For example, Prefer: wait=5 will wait for 5 seconds.

> If the model doesn’t finish within the specified duration, the request will return the incomplete prediction object with status set to starting or processing. You can then fetch the prediction again via the URL provided in the Location header, or the urls.get field as with [Async mode](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/create-a-prediction#async-mode-default).

So currently, any prediction that is longer than 60s just fails. This happens often with popular models like nano banana pro (in my own usage). 

Suggestion: allow configuring the wait duration (e.g., Prefer: wait=n) or allow disabling sync wait entirely (no Prefer header). Alternative: detect non‑terminal prediction status and poll internally (or expose a helper to do so).

### AI SDK Version

- ai: 5.0.102
- @ai-sdk/replicate version: 1.0.18

title: Allow editing tool input in addToolApprovalResponse
body:
### Summary
The `addToolApprovalResponse` function should support modifying tool inputs during the approval workflow. Currently, users must use a cumbersome deny-then-resubmit pattern to edit inputs, which creates poor UX and unnecessary complexity.

### Problem Description

When using tool execution approval in the AI SDK, human users often need to modify tool inputs before approval (e.g., correcting a city name, adjusting parameters, fixing typos). The current `addToolApprovalResponse` function only supports approving or denying the original input

```typescript
export type ChatAddToolApproveResponseFunction = ({  
  id,  
  approved,  
  reason,  
}: {  
  id: string;  
  approved: boolean;  
  reason?: string;  
}) => void | PromiseLike<void>;
```
This limitation forces users to implement a workaround pattern:

1. Deny the original approval request
2. Submit a new tool call with modified input using addToolOutput
3. This creates UI complexity and can show unwanted "denied" states

### Proposed Solution

Extend `addToolApprovalResponse` to accept an optional `input` parameter that allows modifying the tool input during approval:

```typescript
export type ChatAddToolApproveResponseFunction = ({  
  id,  
  approved,  
  reason,  
  input, // New optional parameter  
}: {  
  id: string;  
  approved: boolean;  
  reason?: string;  
  input?: unknown; // Modified tool input  
}) => void | PromiseLike<void>;
```

When `input` is provided:

- The backend should validate the new input against the tool's schema
- If validation passes, execute the tool with the modified input
- If validation fails, return an error to the user

### Use Cases

1. Correcting typos: User wants to change "New Yrok" to "New York" in a weather tool
2. Adjusting parameters: Fine-tuning chart configuration values before generation
3. Security review: Modifying potentially dangerous command parameters
4. Data validation: Fixing malformed input while preserving the approval workflow

### Implementation Considerations

- The modified input must be validated against the tool's `inputSchema` before execution
- The approval UI should provide input editing capabilities alongside approve/deny buttons
- Backward compatibility must be maintained for existing implementations

### Current Workaround Complexity

The current approach requires users to:

- Update UI state with `setMessages` (only affects display)
- Call `addToolApprovalResponse` with `approved: false`
- Call `addToolOutput` with the modified input
- Handle potential validation errors manually

This pattern is documented in the human-in-the-loop examples , but it's unnecessarily complex for a common use case.

title: xAI provider: Schema mismatch error when using sources with AI SDK v6
body:
### Description

# Post-Mortem: xAI Integration Failure

## Root Cause
**Schema Mismatch:** The code passed `sources` as strings (`['web', 'x']`), but `@ai-sdk/xai` (v2.0.41) requires objects (`[{ type: 'web' }, { type: 'x' }]`).
**Error:** `AI_InvalidArgumentError` (Validation failed: expected object, received string).

## Resolution
1.  **Fix Code:** Update `providerOptions` in `lib/llm.ts` to use the object format.
2.  **Verify:** Ensure `@ai-sdk/xai` is `^2.0.41`.

## Why Downgrading to AI SDK v5 Worked
**Validation Strictness:**
*   **SDK v6 (Beta):** Strictly enforces the schema locally, crashing on the mismatch.
*   **SDK v5:** Permissive validation. It passed the "invalid" payload to the API.
*   **xAI API:** Accepts the legacy string format, so the request succeeded despite the SDK schema violation.

**Takeaway:** The downgrade bypassed client-side validation, but the correct fix is aligning the code with the schema.

title: Feature Request: Preserve provider-specific fields in @ai-sdk/openai-compatible message conversion
body:
### Description

# Feature Request: Preserve provider-specific fields in @ai-sdk/openai-compatible message conversion

## Description

When using `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` with providers that return extended response fields (like `reasoning_details`), these fields are lost during message conversion in multi-turn conversations. This breaks compatibility with providers that require these fields to be sent back in subsequent requests.

## Affected Package

- `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` v1.0.27

## Use Case

Venice.ai's Gemini 3 models return `reasoning_details` containing encrypted `thought_signature` data in assistant messages. For multi-turn conversations with tool calls, Venice requires these `reasoning_details` to be included in subsequent requests. Without them, the API returns HTTP 400 errors.

### Example Venice API Response (abbreviated)

```json
{
  "choices": [{
    "message": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": null,
      "tool_calls": [...],
      "reasoning_details": [
        {
          "type": "reasoning.encrypted",
          "thought_signature": "encrypted-signature-data..."
        }
      ]
    }
  }]
}
```

### Expected Behavior

When the conversation continues, the SDK should preserve and send back the `reasoning_details` field in the message history.

### Actual Behavior

The `convertToOpenAIChatMessages()` function only preserves standard OpenAI fields (`role`, `content`, `tool_calls`, `name`), discarding provider-specific fields like `reasoning_details`.

## Reproduction

1. Configure `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` with Venice.ai endpoint
2. Use a Gemini 3 model (e.g., `gemini-3-flash-preview`)
3. Start a conversation that triggers tool calls
4. Observe that the second API request fails because `reasoning_details` is missing

```typescript
import { createOpenAICompatible } from "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible";
import { generateText } from "ai";

const venice = createOpenAICompatible({
  name: "venice",
  baseURL: "https://api.venice.ai/api/v1",
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.VENICE_API_KEY}` },
});

const result = await generateText({
  model: venice.chatModel("gemini-3-flash-preview"),
  tools: { /* ... */ },
  prompt: "Read and summarize file.txt",
  maxSteps: 5, // Multi-turn with tool calls fails on step 2+
});
```

## Proposed Solution

Add a mechanism to preserve provider-specific fields through message conversion. Options:

### Option A: `providerOptions` passthrough

Allow providers to specify fields that should be preserved:

```typescript
const venice = createOpenAICompatible({
  name: "venice",
  baseURL: "https://api.venice.ai/api/v1",
  preserveFields: ["reasoning_details"], // New option
});
```

### Option B: Generic metadata preservation

Preserve all non-standard fields in a `providerMetadata` object that gets passed through message conversion.

### Option C: Message transformation hook

Allow a custom transformer function:

```typescript
const venice = createOpenAICompatible({
  name: "venice",
  baseURL: "https://api.venice.ai/api/v1",
  transformMessage: (msg) => {
    // Custom logic to preserve/restore fields
    return msg;
  },
});
```

## Workaround

Currently we work around this by:
1. Intercepting `fetch()` to capture `reasoning_details` from responses
2. Storing them in AsyncLocalStorage keyed by message index
3. Re-injecting them into messages before sending subsequent requests

This works but is fragile and requires significant custom code.

## Related

- Venice.ai API documentation on reasoning models
- Similar issue may affect other providers with extended response fields

## Environment

- Node.js: v22.x
- Bun: 1.3.4
- @ai-sdk/openai-compatible: 1.0.27
- ai: 4.3.15

title: [Bug] Gemini 3 Pro/Flash Preview models output internal JSON as text when tools are provided
body:
### Description


### Environment
- `@ai-sdk/google`: 3.0.0
- `ai`: 6.0.1
- Node.js: (latest)

### Problem
When using Gemini 3 Pro Preview (`gemini-3-pro-preview`) or Gemini 3 Flash Preview (`gemini-3-flash-preview`) models with tool definitions, the model outputs its internal JSON format as plain text instead of making proper tool calls.

Example output when just saying "hi" with tools defined:
```json
{ "thought": "The user has initiated the conversation with a greeting. I should respond professionally...", "call": null }
```

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure `streamText` with `gemini-3-pro-preview` model
2. Provide any tool definitions
3. Send a simple message like "hi"
4. Model outputs JSON with `thought` and `call` fields as text instead of responding normally

### Expected Behavior
The model should either:
- Respond with normal text when no tool call is needed
- Make a proper `tool-call` when a tool is appropriate

### Actual Behavior
The model outputs an internal JSON structure containing `thought` and `call` fields as plain text, regardless of:
- `thinkingConfig` settings (tried all combinations)
- `toolChoice` settings (auto, required, etc.)
- `structuredOutputs` setting

### Notes
- Gemini 2.5 Pro works correctly with the same tool definitions
- Removing tools entirely makes the model respond normally
- This appears to be a fundamental incompatibility between Gemini 3 Preview models and tool calling in the current SDK

### AI SDK Version

- `@ai-sdk/google`: 3.0.0
- `ai`: 6.0.1

title: npx @ai-sdk/devtools fails due to scoped bin name
body:
The `@ai-sdk/devtools` package uses a scoped bin name:

```json
"bin": {
  "@ai-sdk/devtools": "./bin/cli.js"
}
```

This causes `npx @ai-sdk/devtools` to fail with `sh: devtools: command not found`.

**Workaround:** `node node_modules/@ai-sdk/devtools/bin/cli.js`

**Suggested fix:** Rename the bin to `ai-devtools` or similar unscoped name.

title: Can't use @ai-sdk/devtools with Cloudflare Workers
body:
### Description

`@ai-sdk/devtools` cannot be used during local development with `wrangler dev` because it requires filesystem access to write to a local `.devtools` directory. Wrangler's Workers environment doesn't support writing to the host OS filesystem.

### Cause

Even with Cloudflare's [`nodejs_compat`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/nodejs/) and `enable_nodejs_fs_module` compatibility flags, the `node:fs` implementation provides only an **ephemeral virtual filesystem** that is isolated per request:

> The virtual file system is ephemeral with each individual request having its own isolated temporary file space. Files written to the file system will not persist across requests and will not be shared across requests or across different Workers.

https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/2025-08-15-nodejs-fs/

### Possible solutions
- Support for alternative storage adapters


### AI SDK Version

```
npm ls | grep ai-sdk
│ ├── @ai-sdk/devtools@0.0.1
│ ├── @ai-sdk/google@3.0.1
│ ├── @ai-sdk/openai@3.0.1
│ ├── @ai-sdk/react@3.0.3

title: Bug in langchain adapter: `toBaseMessages` creates orphaned AIMessages with tool_calls in multi-turn conversations
body: ## Description When using `@ai-sdk/langchain` with LangGraph agents that have tools, multi-turn conversations fail with: ``` 400 An assistant message with 'tool_calls' must be followed by tool messages responding to each 'tool_call_id'. The following tool_call_ids did not have response messages: call_xxxxx ``` ## Reproduction **Repository:** https://github.com/tuntisz/ai-sdk-langchain-bug-repro ```bash git clone https://github.com/tuntisz/ai-sdk-langchain-bug-repro cd ai-sdk-langchain-bug-repro pnpm install pnpm test ``` The tests fail, showing: ``` AIMessages with tool_calls: 2 ToolMessages: 1 ORPHANED tool call IDs: [ 'call_8xtoEZ2bDLCMkKhK1wQ1Y3XC' ] ``` ### Visual reproduction 1. Set `OPENAI_API_KEY` and run `pnpm dev` 2. Open http://localhost:3000 3. Type: `do maths with 123` → works 4. Type: `do maths with 345` → works 5. Type: `do maths with 999` → **ERROR** ## Root Cause The bug is in `toUIMessageStream`'s handling of LangGraph `values` events: 1. When LangGraph emits a `values` event, it contains the full message history including AIMessages with `tool_calls` from previous turns 2. `processLangGraphEvent` (case "values", ~line 540-560 in adapter.ts) iterates through ALL messages and emits `tool-input-start`/`tool-input-available` for any AIMessage with `tool_calls` that hasn't been emitted in the current stream 3. **The bug:** It emits these events for **historical** tool calls but does NOT emit corresponding `tool-output-available` events for them 4. The client builds a `UIMessage` with tool parts in state `input-available` (no output) 5. When `toBaseMessages` converts this back, it creates an `AIMessage` with `tool_calls` but no `ToolMessage` follows ### Evidence from stream On the third request, the stream shows: ``` {"type":"start"} {"type":"tool-input-start","toolCallId":"call_HISTORICAL",...} <- Re-emitted from history {"type":"tool-input-available","toolCallId":"call_HISTORICAL",...} {"type":"start-step"} {"type":"tool-input-start","toolCallId":"call_CURRENT",...} <- Current turn {"type":"tool-input-available","toolCallId":"call_CURRENT",...} {"type":"tool-output-available","toolCallId":"call_CURRENT",...} <- Only current gets output! {"type":"error","errorText":"400 An assistant message with 'tool_calls'..."} ``` ## Suggested Fix In `processLangGraphEvent` case "values", when iterating through historical messages, either: 1. **Skip emitting tool events for historical tool calls** - they're already in the client's message history and shouldn't be re-emitted 2. **Or emit both input AND output events** for historical tool calls to keep them consistent Option 1 seems cleaner since the client already has the complete tool call history. ## Environment - `@ai-sdk/langchain`: 2.0.3 - `ai`: 6.0.3 - `langchain`: 1.2.3 - `@langchain/openai`: 1.2.0 - Node.js: 20.x ## Screenshot Notice that each turn with a tool call sees the prior turns tool call started, but not completed. The request fails on the third message with a tool call.

title: `@ai-sdk/mcp`: support `structuredContent` / `outputSchema` for typed tool outputs
body:
### Description

MCP allows specifying `outputSchema` for tools to provide better type information. When specified, tools must populate `structuredContent` in their result as well as JSON encode structured data in `.content` text for backwards compatibility.

Currently, there's no way to leverage this type information with AI SDK's MCP client. I'd expect a way to read `.structuredContent` just as I'd read `.content`, but with type information from a defined `outputSchema`.

Spec:

- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools#structured-content
- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools#output-schema

`MCPClient.tools()` accepts a `schemas` option for type checking of tool inputs. Currently this only recognizes `inputSchema` to type tool inputs, while tool outputs are untyped.

- https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/reference/ai-sdk-core/create-mcp-client#tools.options.schemas

- https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-core/mcp-tools#schema-definition

Comparatively, regular tool() definitions accept an outputSchema for typed outputs:

- https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/reference/ai-sdk-core/tool#tool.tool.output-schema

### AI SDK Version

- @ai-sdk/mcp: 1.0.1

title: Feature: provide abort reason for abort chunk
body:
### Description

In my project, I combined two abort signals. In my scenario, I need to allow users to manually abort the request while also triggering an abort due to a timeout after a certain period of time.

```typescript
  const timeoutSignal = AbortSignal.timeout(timeout)
  const signals = [timeoutSignal]
  if (externalSignal) {
    signals.push(externalSignal)
  }
  const finalSignal = AbortSignal.any(signals)
```

However, the reason fields for these two types of abort signal are different. At present, when an abort is triggered, the abort chunk returned by the aisdk does not include the reason for the abort. I would like to be able to determine the abort reason directly from the abort chunk so that I can clearly inform the user about why the request was aborted.

Of course, I know I could achieve this by managing my finalSignal separately, but that seems a bit too cumbersome for me.

title: Gemini 3 models support structured output with code execution but SDK returns errors
body:
### Description

Google's official documentation explicitly states that **Gemini 3 series models** (`gemini-3-pro-preview` and `gemini-3-flash-preview`) support combining structured output with built-in tools including Code Execution.

**Source:** [ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/structured-output](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/structured-output?example=recipe#structured_outputs_with_tools)

> Structured outputs work with built-in tools **only on Gemini 3 series models** (`gemini-3-pro-preview` and `gemini-3-flash-preview`). Compatible tools include:
> - Grounding with Google Search
> - URL Context  
> - **Code Execution**

However, when using `@ai-sdk/google` with Gemini 3 models, combining `google.tools.codeExecution()` with `Output.object()` throws `AI_NoOutputGeneratedError`.

**Error:**
```
Error Type: AI_NoOutputGeneratedError
Error Message: No output generated.

Stack Trace:
AI_NoOutputGeneratedError: No output generated.
at DefaultGenerateTextResult.get output
(/node_modules/.pnpm/ai@6.0.1_zod@4.2.1/node_modules/ai/src/generate-text/generate-text.ts:1006:13)
```

**Model Compatibility Summary (per Google docs):**
| Model | Structured Output | + Code Execution |
|-------|------------------|------------------|
| Gemini 3 Pro Preview | ✓ | ✓ (Google docs) |
| Gemini 3 Flash Preview | ✓ | ✓ (Google docs) |
| Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash | ✓ | ✗ |
| Gemini 2.0 Flash | ✓* | ✗ |

*Requires explicit `propertyOrdering`

**Expected Behavior:**
Gemini 3 models should successfully combine `google.tools.codeExecution()` with structured output (`Output.object()`) as documented by Google.

**Actual Behavior:**
The SDK throws `AI_NoOutputGeneratedError: No output generated` when combining code execution tool with structured output on Gemini 3 models.

**Reproduction Steps:**

```typescript
import { generateText, Output } from 'ai';
import { google } from '@ai-sdk/google';
import { z } from 'zod';

const result = await generateText({
  model: google('gemini-3-flash-preview'),
  tools: {
    code_execution: google.tools.codeExecution(),
  },
  output: Output.object({
    schema: z.object({
      answer: z.number(),
      explanation: z.string(),
    }),
  }),
  prompt: 'Calculate the sum of the first 50 prime numbers. Show your work.',
});

// Throws: AI_NoOutputGeneratedError: No output generated.
console.log(result.output);
```

**Additional Context:**

I think this could be more of a Gemini 3 issue too.

### AI SDK Version

- `ai`: `6.0.1`
- `@ai-sdk/google`: `3.x`
- `zod`: `4.2.1`

title: Implicit caching not working with Gemini 3 Flash when tools are defined
body:
## Description

Implicit caching does not appear to work when using `@ai-sdk/google` with Gemini 3 Flash Preview and tools defined, even when token counts exceed the documented 1024 minimum.

## Environment

- `@ai-sdk/google`: ^3.0.2
- `ai`: ^6.0.6
- Model: `google/gemini-3-flash`

## Reproduction

```typescript
import { google } from '@ai-sdk/google';
import { Experimental_Agent as Agent } from 'ai';

const agent = new Agent({
  model: 'google/gemini-3-flash',
  instructions: '...large system prompt...',
  tools: {
    google_search: google.tools.googleSearch({}),
    url_context: google.tools.urlContext({}),
  },
});

// Multiple calls with same message prefix
const result = await agent.stream({ messages });
const usage = await result.usage;

console.log(usage?.inputTokenDetails?.cacheReadTokens); // Always 0
```

## Observed Behavior

- `inputTokens`: 1004-1599 (above 1024 minimum)
- `cacheReadTokens`: **always 0**
- Even with identical message prefixes across requests, no cache hits occur

## Expected Behavior

According to [Google's documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/caching):
> "Implicit caching is enabled by default... Gemini 3 Flash Preview minimum is 1024 tokens"

Cache hits should occur when:
1. Token count exceeds minimum (✅ met)
2. Requests share common prefixes (✅ met)
3. Requests sent close together in time (✅ met)

## Related Issues

- #3333 - Context caching breaks with `generateObject` due to tools
- #3212 - Gemini context caching feature request
- [Google Forum: Implicit caching not working with Gemini 3](https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/implicit-context-caching-does-not-work-with-gemini-3-pro-preview/111253)

## Hypothesis

The presence of `tools` in the request may be preventing implicit caching from activating. Google's API returns this error for explicit caching with tools:
> "CachedContent cannot be used with GenerateContent request setting system_instruction, tools or tool_config"

It's possible implicit caching has the same limitation but silently fails instead of erroring.

## Questions

1. Is implicit caching expected to work when tools are defined?
2. If not, should the SDK warn users or document this limitation?
3. Are there workarounds (e.g., separating tool definitions from cached content)?

## Workaround Attempted

None successful. The only known workaround from #3212 involves overriding fetch to strip tools when cachedContent is present, but this requires explicit caching setup.

title: Azure Provider does not support Anthropic models
body:
### Description

## Description

The Azure AI SDK provider cannot generate the correct Azure endpoint for Anthropic models. While OpenAI models use an endpoint structured as `https://resourcename.region.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/...`, Anthropic models require `https://resourcename.region.openai.azure.com/anthropic/...`, omitting the `/openai` path segment entirely.

### Reproduction Steps
1. Install `@ai-sdk/azure` and configure it via environment variables or:
```typescript
import { createAzure } from '@ai-sdk/azure';
const azure = createAzure({
  resourceName:  'your-resource-name',
  apiKey: 'your-azure-key',
});
const model = azure('claude-sonnet-4-5');
```
2. Try to use `generateText` or equivalent with Anthropic deployment.

**Expected:**
Request is sent to `https://resourcename.region.openai.azure.com/anthropic/...`

**Actual:**
Request is sent to `https://resourcename.region.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/...` or with `/openai/deployments/...`, neither of which work for Anthropic models.

### Background
- The provider always includes the `/openai` path segment in its produced URLs.
- Neither `useDeploymentBasedUrls` nor `baseURL` allow users to produce the necessary `/anthropic` endpoint.
- OpenAI GPT models work as expected at `/openai/v1/...`, but Anthropic endpoints must not contain `/openai`.
- Azure Anthropic endpoints may also require the region to be present in the resource hostname.

### Impact
- The SDK is currently incompatible with Anthropic models on Azure (tested with `claude-sonnet-4-5`), limiting supported model families.

### Suggestion
- Allow full customization of the base URL and the path prefix, so the SDK can support arbitrary Azure-hosted model families (OpenAI `/openai/v1`, Anthropic `/anthropic`, etc.).
- Consider future model families that may use other prefixes or host patterns.

title: [Feature Request] Support Google Search Grounding with Structured Outputs - Gemini 3
body:
### Description

### Summary

  The native Gemini API now supports combining Google Search grounding with structured outputs in a single call (Gemini 3+), but `@ai-sdk/google` doesn't expose this capability yet.

  ### Native Gemini API Support

  From the [official Gemini documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/structured-output):

  > "Gemini 3 lets you combine Structured Outputs with built-in tools, including **Grounding with Google Search**, URL Context, Code Execution, and File Search."

  This is available for `gemini-3-pro-preview` and `gemini-3-flash-preview` models. Ultimately they are now used with `latest`.

  ### Current Limitation in @ai-sdk/google

  When using `@ai-sdk/google`, you cannot use Google Search grounding (`useSearchGrounding: true`) together with structured outputs. This forces a workaround with two separate API calls:

  1. **Phase 1:** Call with grounding enabled to search and gather information (no structured output)
  2. **Phase 2:** Call without grounding to extract structured JSON from the Phase 1 results

  This adds latency, doubles API costs, and introduces complexity in matching grounding sources between phases.

  ### Desired Behavior

  Allow combining grounding with structured outputs in a single call, matching what the native Gemini API supports:

  ```typescript
  const result = await generateObject({
    model: google("gemini-3-flash-preview", {
      useSearchGrounding: true,
    }),
    schema: mySchema,
    prompt: "Research this topic and return structured data",
  });

  // result.object contains structured data
  // result.experimental_providerMetadata?.google?.groundingMetadata contains sources
```

  References

  - Gemini structured output docs: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/structured-output
  - Gemini grounding docs: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/grounding

title: [Bug] Anthropic extended thinking: reasoning blocks lost during multi-step tool calls
body:
## Description

When using `streamText` with Anthropic thinking models (e.g., `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`), reasoning content is lost during multi-step tool call workflows.

**Two related issues:**

1. **`response.messages` reasoning parts are missing `providerMetadata` with signatures** - The signature is only available in the separate `reasoning` array, making it impossible to properly reconstruct messages for subsequent turns.

2. **In `onFinish`, reasoning is lost from consolidated `response.messages`** - When using AI SDK's built-in agent loop (`maxSteps`), `onStepFinish` shows reasoning on all turns, but `onFinish` loses 75% of reasoning blocks.

---

## Reproduction

Gist: https://gist.github.com/p3droml/503c5d4888182a75222377109bfdd291

To run:
git clone https://gist.github.com/p3droml/503c5d4888182a75222377109bfdd291.git mre
cd mre && npm install
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your-key npx tsx anthropic-thinking-bug.ts

### ProviderMetadata Issue

When extracting reasoning from `response.messages`, the signature is **not included**:

```typescript
// response.messages reasoning part:
{ type: "reasoning", text: "..." }  // NO providerMetadata!

// separate reasoning array:
{ type: "reasoning", text: "...", providerMetadata: { anthropic: { signature: "Esg..." } } }
```

---

## Root Cause Analysis

### The Pattern Explained

1. **Turn 1**: User message → Model generates thinking + tool call → reasoning present ✅
2. **Turn 2-4**: Tool results sent back → Model processes results without generating NEW thinking → reasoning missing ❌

The model doesn't always generate new thinking blocks when processing tool results. This is expected model behavior. However:

1. **`response.messages` reasoning parts don't include `providerMetadata` with signatures** - making it impossible to properly forward thinking blocks
2. **`onFinish` loses reasoning that was present in `onStepFinish`** - consolidation drops 75% of reasoning

### Anthropic's Requirements

From Anthropic's Extended Thinking Documentation:

> "When thinking is enabled, a final assistant message must start with a thinking block (preceding the lastmost set of tool_use and tool_result blocks). We recommend you include thinking blocks from previous turns."

> "You must include the complete, unmodified thinking or redacted_thinking block back to the API."

---

## Related Issues

- [openai/openai-agents-js#770](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/issues/770) - "Anthropic with reasoning and tool calling fails to send thinking content back up on subsequent turn"
- [vercel/ai#4992](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/4992) - `appendResponseMessages` ignores reasoning (fixed in PR #5041)
- [vercel/ai#8823](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/8823) - Post-tool reasoning missing from steps
- [vercel/ai#5087](https://github.com/vercel/ai/discussions/5087) - Reasoning promises undefined with streamText

---

## Environment

```
ai: 6.0.16
@ai-sdk/anthropic: 3.0.8
Model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514
Node.js: 22.x
OS: macOS
```

---

## Expected Behavior

1. Reasoning should be preserved and available in `onFinish` for ALL responses
2. The `response.messages` array should include reasoning blocks with `providerMetadata` (signatures)
3. The separate `reasoning` parameter should be consistent with `response.messages`
4. Multi-step tool call workflows should maintain reasoning context throughout

---

## Actual Behavior

1. `response.messages` reasoning parts are missing `providerMetadata` with signatures
2. In `onFinish`, 75% of reasoning is lost (even though `onStepFinish` shows reasoning on all turns)
3. Both `response.messages` and the separate `reasoning` array are empty for turns 2-4

---

## Additional Context

The issue was tested both before and after upgrading from:
- `ai@6.0.3` → `ai@6.0.16`
- `@ai-sdk/anthropic@3.0.1` → `@ai-sdk/anthropic@3.0.8`

The bug persists across versions.

### AI SDK Version

ai: 6.0.16
@ai-sdk/anthropic: 3.0.8
Model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514
Node.js: 22.x
OS: macOS

title: BYOK credentials override explicit provider `order` configuration in AI Gateway routing
body:
## Description

When configuring the AI Gateway with both BYOK credentials and an explicit provider `order`, the gateway prioritizes BYOK providers over the specified routing order. This makes it impossible to use BYOK as a fallback while preferring system-credentialed providers first.

## Expected Behavior

The explicit `order` array in `providerOptions.gateway` should take precedence over BYOK credential availability. BYOK should only affect *which credentials are used* for a provider, not override the routing priority.

## Actual Behavior

BYOK-enabled providers are automatically promoted to the front of the execution order, ignoring the configured `order` array.

The planning reasoning confirms this:

```
planningReasoning: "Provider set restricted to: cerebras, groq, bedrock. BYOK credentials available for: bedrock. BYOK execution order prioritizes bedrock over routing preference cerebras. System credentials planned for: cerebras, groq, bedrock. Total execution order: bedrock(BYOK) → cerebras(system) → groq(system) → bedrock(system)"
```

## Reproduction

**Desired routing priority:**

1. `openai/gpt-oss-120b` on Cerebras
2. `openai/gpt-oss-120b` on Groq
3. `openai/gpt-oss-120b` on Bedrock (BYOK)
4. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` on Bedrock (BYOK)
5. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` on Anthropic

**Configuration:**

```typescript
{
  modelName: 'openai/gpt-oss-120b',
  providerOptions: {
    gateway: {
      only: [
        AIModelProviderEnum.cerebras,
        AIModelProviderEnum.groq,
        AIModelProviderEnum.bedrock,
        AIModelProviderEnum.anthropic,
      ],
      order: [AIModelProviderEnum.cerebras, AIModelProviderEnum.groq],
      models: ['anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5'],
    },
  },
}
```

**Actual execution order:**

```
bedrock(BYOK) → cerebras(system) → groq(system) → bedrock(system)
```

## Use Case

We have credits on Bedrock and want to use BYOK for cost savings, but only as a fallback when faster providers (Cerebras, Groq) are unavailable. Currently, there's no way to achieve this—BYOK always takes priority.

## Suggested Solution

Either:

1. Respect the explicit `order` configuration regardless of BYOK status
2. Add a new option like `byokPriority: 'respect-order' | 'prefer-byok'` to control this behavior

title: GLM 4.7 Reasoning Support - Native reasoning_content Field Not Parsed
body:
### Description

# GLM 4.7 Reasoning Support - Native `reasoning_content` Field Not Parsed

## Summary

The Vercel AI SDK's OpenAI provider does not parse the native `reasoning_content` field from GLM 4.7 model responses. This field contains the model's reasoning/thinking process and should be exposed as `reasoning-delta` stream parts, similar to how DeepSeek R1's reasoning is handled.

## Problem Description

GLM 4.7 (via z.ai API) returns reasoning content in a dedicated `reasoning_content` field in the SSE stream:

```json
{
  "choices": [{
    "delta": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "reasoning_content": "The model's thinking process..."
    }
  }]
}
```

However, the AI SDK's OpenAI provider (`@ai-sdk/openai`) filters out this unknown field before it reaches middleware or the application. The reasoning content is lost and never exposed as `reasoning-delta` stream parts.

### Current Workaround

The workaround is to instruct the model to use XML tags (`<reasoning>...</reasoning>`) via system prompt and parse those tags in custom middleware. This is unreliable because:
1. The model may not consistently follow the instruction
2. It adds unnecessary token overhead
3. The native `reasoning_content` field is being ignored

## Expected Behavior

The AI SDK should:
1. Recognize and parse `reasoning_content` from GLM 4.7 responses
2. Emit it as `reasoning-delta` stream parts
3. Make it available in `result.reasoning` for non-streaming responses

This would be consistent with how DeepSeek R1's reasoning is handled (see issue #4461).

## Minimal Reproduction

```typescript
import { createOpenAI } from '@ai-sdk/openai';
import { streamText } from 'ai';

const client = createOpenAI({
  apiKey: '...',
  baseURL: 'https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4/',
});

const result = await streamText({
  model: client('glm-4.7'),
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'What is 2+2?' }],
});

// GLM 4.7 returns reasoning_content, but it never appears in the stream
for await (const chunk of result.fullStream) {
  console.log(chunk);
  // No reasoning-delta chunks appear, even though the model returned reasoning_content
}
```

## Raw SSE Stream Example

Actual raw response from GLM 4.7:

```
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-xxx","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","reasoning_content":"Let me think about this..."},"finish_reason":null}]}
```

The `reasoning_content` is present but filtered out by the OpenAI provider.

## Related Issues

- #4461 - DeepSeek R1 reasoning support (similar `reasoning_content` field)

## Suggested Solution

Add `reasoning_content` parsing support to the OpenAI provider, similar to how other provider-specific fields are handled. The field should:
1. Be detected in the delta
2. Emitted as `reasoning-delta` stream parts
3. Collected in `result.reasoning` for non-streaming

Alternative: Allow middleware to access the raw parsed JSON before field filtering, or provide a hook to transform the raw SSE stream at the provider level.

## Environment

- AI SDK version: 6.x
- Provider: `@ai-sdk/openai`
- Model: GLM 4.7 (via z.ai)
- Runtime: Node.js / Edge runtime

## Additional Context

API documentation: https://docs.z.ai/api-reference/llm/chat-completion

The current workaround using XML tags + middleware works but is suboptimal compared to native field support.

title: [RACE CONDITION] Immediate sendMessage with resume: true causes onFinish call to error
body:
## Reproduction

1. useChat with resume: true and a defined onFinish callback
2. The resumption GET endpoint returns 204
3. useEffect with sendMessage on initial render

## Root Cause

1. useChat's internal effect calls resumeStream() → makeRequest({ trigger: "resume-stream" })
2. External effect calls sendMessage() → makeRequest({ trigger: "submit-message" })
3. These now race to the onFinish (finally) block, where the first call [clears this.activeResponse](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/55e23bb1cd801347c6fc172ae2d1be593787da20/packages/ai/src/ui/chat.ts#L699) and the second call [crashes accessing it](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/55e23bb1cd801347c6fc172ae2d1be593787da20/packages/ai/src/ui/chat.ts#L685-L688)

## Occurrence
 
This bug occurs in the fairly reasonable use case of creating a new chat with resumption on and a client-side onFinish callback.

## Fix

Assuming that allowing concurrent sendMessage calls to race is intentional (instead of canceling the currently in-flight request), at the very least onFinish callbacks should not crash. Best solution is to move the local activeResponse creation up in scope and access that variable in the finally block. There also appears to be stop() race conditions as well, but that's a separate issue.

title: useChat UIMessageStream throws TypeError when text-delta/text-end emitted without text-start (unhelpful error, masks original failure)
body:
## Summary
When using `@ai-sdk/react` `useChat` with a custom transport that returns a `UIMessageStream` (from `ai`), the client can crash with:

`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'text')`

This occurs when the stream emits a `text-delta` (or `text-end`) chunk for an `id` that never received the corresponding `text-start` chunk.

In real integrations this happens easily in **error paths**, e.g. when an upstream request fails **before any tokens are streamed** and the transport tries to write an inline error message to the UI stream.

The resulting `TypeError` is not actionable and can **mask the original error** (e.g. network failure), because the crash happens while attempting to write an error message.

## Why it happens
`processUIMessageStream` maintains internal state for “active” text parts, keyed by chunk `id`.

If it receives a `text-delta` for an `id` that does not exist in the active map (because no `text-start` for that id was seen), the implementation attempts to do something equivalent to:

```ts
const textPart = state.activeTextParts[chunk.id]; // undefined
textPart.text += chunk.delta;                     // boom
```

So instead of surfacing the *real* upstream failure, the user sees `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'text')`.

## Minimal repro (conceptual)
Any `UIMessageStream` that emits this invalid order will reproduce:

- `{ type: "text-delta", id: "x", delta: "..." }` (without a prior `{ type: "text-start", id: "x" }`)

## A more realistic repro scenario (what developers typically do)
Many custom transports do something like:

1. Make a network request to an upstream endpoint.
2. If it fails **before** streaming begins, write an inline error message into the UI stream:

```ts
writer.write({ type: 'text-delta', id: errorId, delta: '⚠️ Request failed...' });
```

If the developer forgets to emit `text-start` (and `text-end`) for the same `id`, the SDK crashes, and the original network error is hidden.

## Expected behavior
One of the following (either is fine, but (1) is likely the safest):

1. **Actionable invariant error**:
   - Example: “Received `text-delta` for missing text part with ID `x`. Ensure a `text-start` chunk is sent before any `text-delta` chunks.”
2. **Graceful fallback**:
   - Optionally treat missing `text-start` as implicit start (less strict; might hide real bugs).

## Actual behavior
Unhelpful runtime crash:

`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'text')`

## Other scenarios that can trigger the same class of crash
Even if the developer emits `text-start`, this still happens with:

- **ID mismatch**: `text-start` uses id `a`, `text-delta` uses id `b` (easy to do if generating a new id per chunk).
- **Out-of-order chunks** due to merging/interleaving streams:
  - `text-delta` arrives before `text-start`.
- **Premature end**:
  - `text-end` emitted without `text-start`, or `text-delta` emitted after `text-end`.

The same invariant likely applies to other stateful “start/delta/end” chunk families, such as:

- `reasoning-start` / `reasoning-delta` / `reasoning-end`
- `tool-input-start` / `tool-input-delta` / `tool-input-end`

## Environment (from where this was observed)
- `ai@6.0.3`
- `@ai-sdk/react@3.0.3`
- React `19.2.1`
- Node `>=18`

## Related PR
- PR :   [vercel/ai#11463](https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/11463)

title: Standard Schema (ArkType) outputs missing `additionalProperties: false` - inconsistent with Zod handling
body:
### Description

## Issue

When using `Output.object()` with a Standard Schema compliant library like ArkType, aisdk does not apply `addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema()` to the generated JSON Schema. 

This causes LLMs produce invalid or unexpected outputs because the schema is too permissive.

## Cause

The utility function [addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema()](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/a95804d2f62dd633c558aa53bedeac855062b077/packages/provider-utils/src/add-additional-properties-to-json-schema.ts#L6) that recursively sets `additionalProperties: false` on all object schemas is only applied to zod schemas [here](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/a95804d2f62dd633c558aa53bedeac855062b077/packages/provider-utils/src/schema.ts#L220C1-L226C27). 

It is not applied to standard schemas [here](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/a95804d2f62dd633c558aa53bedeac855062b077/packages/provider-utils/src/schema.ts#L151-L153).

### Reproduction Steps

- Create an ArkType schema for structured output.
- Call generateText
- Observe that the llm receives a schema **without** `additionalProperties: false` causing invalid responses

title: `createAsyncIterableStream`: `return()` throws when called after completion
body:
### Description

Hello,

First of all thanks for the work on this library!

I noticed an issue when using the streams with [Effect](https://effect.website/docs/stream/creating/#fromasynciterable). As mentioned in the title, the async iterator returned by `createAsyncIterableStream` throws when `return()` is called after the iterator has already completed.

In practice the following is happening:

`next()` performs cleanup on natural completion by cancelling the ReadableStreamDefaultReader and releasing its lock.
Later, `return()` unconditionally calls the same cleanup logic again, which attempts to cancel an already-detached reader and throws:

```
TypeError [ERR_INVALID_STATE]: The reader is not attached to a stream
```

In the case of Effect - and likely other libraries providing wrappers around streams - `return()` is likely called as a way to make sure all the resources are cleaned up upon completion, but the code is assuming that `return()` is only way to return early as mentioned in [the comment](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/d386b7d7cb0086fc498a16ff614abcb971279bcc/packages/ai/src/util/async-iterable-stream.ts#L69). If we have a look into the [ECMAScript spec](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-asynciterator-interface), nothing is mentioning that `return()` should exclusively be for early return.

The expected behaviour would be pretty simple: `clean()` should check first if the stream is done before trying to clean it as it will result in an error

### AI SDK Version

- ai: `5.0.116`

title: useChat crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'text')" when text generation resumes after tool calls
body:
### Description

The `useChat` hook crashes when text generation resumes after a tool call completes. The SDK's `processUIMessageStream` receives `text-delta` chunks for a text part ID that was never initialized with a `text-start` chunk.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use `useChat` with `streamText` that includes tools (e.g., `code_execution`)
2. Send a message that triggers a tool call
3. Wait for tool to complete (`tool-result` received)
4. Text generation resumes
5. Error occurs: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'text')`

### Expected Behavior

The stream should continue processing text deltas after tool completion without crashing. If a `text-start` chunk is missing, the SDK should either:
- Initialize the text part automatically, or
- Gracefully handle the missing chunk and continue

### Actual Behavior

The SDK crashes with:
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'text')
at processUIMessageStream (node_modules/ai/dist/index.mjs:9129:32)
```

### Error Details

**Error Message:**
```
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'text')
```

**Stack Trace:**
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'text')
at processUIMessageStream (node_modules/ai/dist/index.mjs:9129:32)
```

**When it occurs:**
- After `tool-result` chunks are processed
- When `textPartsCount` transitions from 1 → 2
- SDK receives `text-delta id="X"` but no `text-start id="X"` was received

### Logs/Evidence

From client-side logging:
```javascript
// Before error:
partsCount: 8, textPartsCount: 1

// Error occurs when:
partsCount: 9, textPartsCount: 2  // ← New text part appears
// Immediately followed by error
```

**Sequence:**
1. Tool call executes (`tool-call` chunk)
2. Tool completes (`tool-result` chunk)
3. Text generation resumes
4. SDK receives `text-delta id="9"` (or similar)
5. SDK tries to access `parts[id="9"].text` but part doesn't exist
6. Crash

### Workaround

Currently using `onError` handler to catch and suppress this specific error:

```typescript
useChat({
  transport,
  onError: (error) => {
    if (
      error.message?.includes('Cannot read properties of undefined') &&
      error.message?.includes("reading 'text'")
    ) {
      console.warn('SDK stream ID mismatch (known bug) - stream will continue');
      return; // Don't throw
    }
  },
});
```

This prevents crashes but doesn't fix the root cause.

### Additional Context

- This occurs consistently when using Anthropic's `code_execution` tool with skills
- Also occurs in production with older SDK versions
- The bug exists across multiple SDK versions (tested 6.0.3, 6.0.31, etc.)
- Messages still save to database via `onFinish`, but the error breaks the UI stream

### Related Issues

- Similar to: "text part X not found" errors reported in other issues
- Likely related to how `processUIMessageStream` manages text part IDs during tool→text transitions

### AI SDK Version

- **Package Versions:**
  - `ai`: `6.0.3`
  - `@ai-sdk/react`: `3.0.3`
  - `@ai-sdk/anthropic`: `3.0.0`
  - `@ai-sdk/provider-utils`: `4.0.0` (pinned via overrides)
- **Framework:** Next.js 16.0.7
- **React:** 19.2.1
- **Provider:** Anthropic (Claude Sonnet 4.5)

title: OpenAI-Compatible provider limits supported file types even if model can handle them
body:
### Description

Currently, the `openai-compatible` provider only supports attaching files with `image/*` mediaType. It explicitly throws an exception when files of a different type are provided (see [convert-to-openai-compatible-chat-messages](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/openai-compatible/src/chat/convert-to-openai-compatible-chat-messages.ts#L45)).

Many models that are available through openai-compatible endpoints do support a wide variety of filetypes though. For example, Gemini supports:
- Text: text/plain, text/csv, text/xml, text/markdown, text/html, text/javascript
- PDF: application/pdf
- Image: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/heic, image/heif
- Audio: audio/wav, audio/mp3, audio/aiff, audio/aac, audio/ogg, audio/flac
- Video: video/mp4, video/mpeg, video/mov, video/avi, video/x-flv, video/mpg, video/webm, video/wmv, video/3gpp

I see a few options to handle this:
- **Option 1**: Allow any file type and let the model itself handle error messages (this is similar to what the vertex, bedrock & gateway providers do)
- **Option 2**: Provide an array of supported filetypes in the `createOpenAiCompatible` method

I'm leaning towards **Option 1**. 

Related, some models support URLs directly (instead of passing binary data) and download them internally, without the need of special tool calls (e.g. Gemini). But when passing a URL, the AI SDK downloads the attachment automatically. For this case, it would be helpful to be able to set [supportedUrls](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/community-providers/custom-providers#native-url-support) as an option on `createOpenAICompatible`, to disable the automatic download.

@aayush-kapoor I saw that you recently worked on the openai-compatible provider, what do you think about this suggestion?

title: DevTools 0.0.5 shows 'Development Mode' page instead of UI
body:
## Description

After updating to `@ai-sdk/devtools@0.0.5` (released Jan 14, 2026), running `bunx @ai-sdk/devtools` shows a "Development Mode" page that points to `http://localhost:5173` instead of serving the bundled UI.

Clicking "Open DevTools UI →" leads to a broken page:
> **This site can't be reached**
> localhost refused to connect.

This is because nothing is running on port 5173 — that's the Vite dev server port only used during package development.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `bunx @ai-sdk/devtools` (gets 0.0.5)
2. Open `http://localhost:4983`
3. See "Development Mode" page with "Open DevTools UI →" pointing to port 5173
4. Click the link → "localhost refused to connect"

## Expected Behavior

The bundled UI should be served at port 4983, as it was in 0.0.4.

## Workaround

Pin to the previous version:
```bash
bunx @ai-sdk/devtools@0.0.4
```

## Root Cause

In `dist/viewer/server.js`, the `isDevMode` check appears to be incorrectly evaluating to `true` for published packages:

```js
var isDevMode = __dirname.includes("/src/") || process.env.NODE_ENV === "development";
```

When `isDevMode` is true, the server returns a dev mode HTML page instead of serving from `dist/client/index.html`.

The bundled client files exist in the package (`dist/client/index.html` and `dist/client/assets/`), but they're not being served.

## Environment

- macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Bun 1.x
- `@ai-sdk/devtools@0.0.5`

title: GA Gemini 3 models don’t support Google Search grounding + structured outputs (preview-only)
body:
## Follow-up: GA Gemini 3 models don’t support Google Search grounding + structured outputs

This is a follow-up to #11599, which was closed after confirming that Google Search
grounding can be used together with structured outputs when using **preview**
models (e.g. `gemini-3-pro-preview`).

However, this capability does not appear to be available when using **GA / non-preview**
Gemini 3 models, which makes it difficult to rely on this feature in production.

### Current behavior

- Google Search grounding + structured outputs works with:
  - `gemini-3-pro-preview`
- The same setup does **not** work with:
  - `gemini-3-pro` (GA)
  - other non-preview Gemini 3 models

Example:

```ts
import { google } from '@ai-sdk/google';
import { generateText, Output } from 'ai';

await generateText({
  model: google('gemini-3-pro'), // GA model
  tools: {
    google_search: google.tools.googleSearch({}),
  },
  output: Output.object({
    schema: mySchema,
  }),
  prompt: 'Search and return structured data',
});
```

This works when switching the model to gemini-3-pro-preview, but not with the GA model.

### Expected behavior

One of the following would be helpful:
	•	Support Google Search grounding + structured outputs on GA Gemini 3 models, or
	•	Clarify whether this capability is intentionally limited to preview models, or
	•	Share whether GA support is planned and (if possible) an approximate timeline

### Why this matters

Preview models are generally not suitable for production workloads.
Since the native Gemini API supports combining structured outputs with grounding on
Gemini 3, having parity on GA models in @ai-sdk/google would unblock production use.

Thanks for the work on the SDK, any clarification here would be greatly appreciated.

title: Inconsistent providerOptions key naming in openai-compatible package
body:
## Description

There's an inconsistency in the `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` package regarding the key used for provider options:

- **Top-level `providerOptions`** uses kebab-case: `'openai-compatible'`
- **Per-message `providerOptions`** uses camelCase: `openaiCompatible`

## Locations

### Kebab-case usage (`'openai-compatible'`)

Used in `parseProviderOptions` for top-level provider options:

- `packages/openai-compatible/src/chat/openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts:134`
- `packages/openai-compatible/src/embedding/openai-compatible-embedding-model.ts:81`

```typescript
parseProviderOptions({
  provider: 'openai-compatible',
  providerOptions,
  schema: openaiCompatibleProviderOptions,
})
```

### CamelCase usage (`openaiCompatible`)

Used for per-message provider options:

- `packages/openai-compatible/src/chat/convert-to-openai-compatible-chat-messages.ts:12`

```typescript
function getOpenAIMetadata(message: {
  providerOptions?: SharedV3ProviderMetadata;
}) {
  return message?.providerOptions?.openaiCompatible ?? {};
}
```

## Expected Behavior

The key naming should be consistent across both top-level and per-message providerOptions.
