title: useChat resumeStream fails when resumed UI stream starts with text-delta for an existing part
body:
## Problem

`useChat({ resume: true })` appears to fail when a resumed UI message stream starts with a `text-delta` for a text part that was already opened before the disconnect.

In our case, the transport resumes from a server-side cursor and reconnects to the UI message stream successfully, but the resumed stream may begin in the middle of an already-open text part. The SDK then throws during stream processing and the app falls into a reconnect loop.

## What we see

Frontend log:

```txt
Attempting to resume stream due to error TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'text')
```

A resumed SSE response can look like this:

```txt
id:1772776842768-0
data: {"type":"text-delta","id":"fAgr4Vwwmgw9NjN5","delta":" and loved well"}

id:1772776842770-0
data: {"type":"text-delta","id":"fAgr4Vwwmgw9NjN5","delta":", and that"}

id:1772776842772-0
data: {"type":"text-delta","id":"fAgr4Vwwmgw9NjN5","delta":" thou depar"}
```

Those lines are valid UI message chunks, but the matching `text-start` for `id = "fAgr4Vwwmgw9NjN5"` was sent before the reconnect cursor.

## Why this seems to fail

On resume, the chat runtime creates a fresh streaming state:

- `chat.ts` creates a new `activeResponse.state`
- `process-ui-message-stream.ts` initializes `activeTextParts` as `{}`
- the resumed stream then delivers `text-delta(id=A)`
- `process-ui-message-stream.ts` looks up `state.activeTextParts[A]`
- it is missing, so processing fails

The relevant check is:

```ts
case 'text-delta': {
  const textPart = state.activeTextParts[chunk.id];
  if (textPart == null) {
    throw new UIMessageStreamError({
      chunkType: 'text-delta',
      chunkId: chunk.id,
      message:
        `Received text-delta for missing text part with ID "${chunk.id}". ` +
        `Ensure a "text-start" chunk is sent before any "text-delta" chunks.`,
    });
  }
```

That behavior makes sense for a fresh stream, but it seems incompatible with resuming from an arbitrary transport cursor unless the server replays the missing structural chunks.

## Expected behavior

One of these should be true:

1. `resumeStream()` should support resumed UI streams that continue an already-started text part, or
2. the documented contract should require resumed streams to replay any necessary `text-start` / structural state before resuming deltas, or
3. the runtime should reconstruct `activeTextParts` from the existing message state before consuming resumed chunks.

## Minimal repro

1. Start a streaming response that emits:
   - `text-start(id=A)`
   - several `text-delta(id=A)` chunks
2. Disconnect after a few deltas
3. Resume from a cursor after `text-start(id=A)` but before `text-end(id=A)`
4. Feed the resumed stream into `useChat({ resume: true })`
5. Observe parser failure and/or frontend crash / reconnect loop

## Version

Observed in the current `ai` package installed on March 6, 2026.

## Related

title: ai.generateText.doGenerate OTel span not emitted when all retries fail with provider error (e.g. 429)
body:
### Description

When generateText encounters a provider error (e.g. Vertex AI 429 rate limit) and all retry attempts fail, the                     `ai.generateText.doGenerate` span is never emitted. The error only surfaces as an exception event on a parent span, with no status.message set on any ai.* span. This makes it impossible to detect LLM provider errors using standard OTel span queries against ai.* spans.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Call generateText() with experimental_telemetry enabled
2. Have the provider return a 429 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED error consistently (e.g. exceed Vertex AI TPM quota)
3. AI SDK retries 3 times via _retryWithExponentialBackoff, all fail
4. Observe the exported OTel spans

Expected behavior:

An ai.generateText.doGenerate span should be emitted with:
- error = true
- status.code = ERROR
- status.message containing the error details (e.g. "Resource exhausted. Please refer to
- https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/error-code-429")

This would allow standard OTel queries like: where name startswith 'ai.' and error == true and status.message has '429'

Actual behavior:

- No ai.generateText.doGenerate span is created for the failed attempts
- The error bubbles up as an AI_RetryError exception event on a parent span (e.g. run())
- The exception details are in events[].attributes.exception.message, not in any span's status.message
- No ai.* span has error = true for this failure


Possible way to fix:

In record-span.ts / the retry wrapper, when all retries are exhausted, emit the ai.generateText.doGenerate span with the error status before throwing. Alternatively, set status.message on the parent ai.generateText span when the retry error is caught.

### AI SDK Version

Environment:
  - ai: 6.0.111                                                                                    
  - @ai-sdk/google-vertex: 4.0.73                                                                                
  - experimental_telemetry: { isEnabled: true }
  - OTel exporter: Axiom OTLP

title: Feature: Agent Action Receipt (AAR) middleware for provable tool calls
body:
## Problem

The Vercel AI SDK powers agent tool calls, structured outputs, and multi-step reasoning — but there's no built-in mechanism for cryptographically proving what an agent did. As AI moves from chat into consequential actions (payments, data mutations, API calls), unsigned execution logs aren't sufficient for auditability.

## Proposal: Agent Action Receipt (AAR) Support

AAR is a lightweight open standard for Ed25519-signed proof of agent actions:

- **What** — action name, scope, input/output SHA-256 hashes
- **Who** — agent identity, principal (user/system that authorized it)
- **When** — ISO 8601 timestamp
- **Proof** — Ed25519 detached signature, offline-verifiable

The SDK is <10KB, zero external dependencies, works in Edge Runtime.

## Integration surface

Natural fit as a `streamText` / `generateText` middleware or `experimental_telemetry` extension:

```typescript
import { generateText } from "ai";
import { withAAR } from "botindex-aar/vercel";

const result = await generateText({
  model: openai("gpt-4"),
  prompt: "Analyze this contract",
  experimental_telemetry: withAAR({ agent: "contract-analyzer" }),
});
// result.receipt → signed AAR receipt
```

Every tool call gets a receipt. Receipts chain for multi-step provenance.

## Resources

- Spec: https://github.com/Cyberweasel777/agent-action-receipt-spec
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/botindex-aar
- Landing: https://aar.botindex.dev
- Active in: crewAI, FINOS AI Governance, AWS Agent Squad
author: Cyberweasel777

title: Provider-executed tools (e.g. web_search) never emit tool-result in stream, so UI stays on "input-available"
body:
## Description
When using the xAI Responses API with provider-executed tools such as xai.tools.webSearch(), the stream emits tool-call (and tool-input-* chunks) but never emits a tool-result when the tool completes. The AI SDK therefore never sends a tool-output-available chunk to the client, so UIs that rely on it (e.g. processUIMessageStream / ToolCallStatus) stay stuck on the “in progress” state (e.g. “Searching the web”) instead of moving to “completed”.

## Expected behavior
When a provider-executed tool (e.g. web_search_call, x_search_call, code_execution_call) finishes, the stream should emit a tool-result part (with providerExecuted: true), so that:

The AI SDK’s UI stream includes a tool-output-available chunk.
Client UIs can show a “completed” state (e.g. “Web search concluded”) instead of “Searching the web”.

## Actual behavior
For file_search_call, the adapter correctly emits tool-result on response.output_item.done (see xai-responses-language-model.ts around lines 472–489).
For web_search_call, x_search_call, code_execution_call, view_image_call, view_x_video_call, custom_tool_call, and mcp_call, the adapter only emits tool-input-start, tool-input-delta, tool-input-end, and tool-call. It never emits tool-result, so the tool call never transitions to “output available” in the UI.

## Environment
@ai-sdk/xai: (your version, e.g. ^3.0.67)
ai: (e.g. ^6.0.3)
Model: Responses API, e.g. xai.responses('grok-4-fast-non-reasoning') with tools: { webSearch: xai.tools.webSearch() }

## Suggested fix
In doStream in xai-responses-language-model.ts, when handling response.output_item.done for provider-executed tool types (web_search_call, x_search_call, code_execution_call, etc.), emit a tool-result chunk in addition to the existing tool-call, similar to file_search_call. The result payload can be a minimal object (e.g. {}) or any structured result the xAI API provides for that item, so long as the stream emits a tool-result with the same toolCallId and providerExecuted: true. That will cause the AI SDK to emit tool-output-available and fix the stuck UI state.

## Workaround
Clients can work around this by treating input-available as “completed” when the stream has finished (e.g. when status === 'ready') for known provider-executed tools, but that is fragile and tool-specific; fixing it in the provider is the right long-term solution.

title: [bug] useChat: changing id during streaming does not abort the previous stream
body:
### Description

When the `id` prop passed to `useChat` changes while a response is being streamed, the hook recreates the internal `Chat` instance (correct behavior), but **does not call `stop()` on the previous instance**. This leaves the old `fetch` request alive, wasting network and memory resources.

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Use `useChat` with a dynamic `id` (e.g. a chat room switcher)
2. Send a message and start streaming
3. While streaming, change the `id` to a different value (e.g. navigate to a different chat room)
4. Observe: the previous `fetch` request remains open and continues streaming until it completes

A minimal reproduction page is available at: https://github.com/Grit03/ai/pull/1

#### Expected behavior

When `id` changes during an active stream, the previous `Chat` instance's stream should be aborted (equivalent to calling `stop()`).

#### Actual behavior

The previous stream runs to completion. Confirmed via:
- Browser DevTools → Network tab: the old request is not cancelled
- Server logs: prints `COMPLETED` instead of `ABORTED` even after the chat was switched

#### Root cause

In `packages/react/src/use-chat.ts`:

```ts
if (shouldRecreateChat) {
  chatRef.current = // old Chat instance is simply overwritten
    'chat' in options ? options.chat : new Chat(optionsWithCallbacks);
}
```

`chatRef.current` is replaced without calling `chatRef.current.stop()` first. The `AbortController` inside the old `Chat` instance is never triggered.

#### Why this is the library's responsibility

The `shouldRecreateChat` branch has two cases:

| Case | Who creates the `Chat`? | Who should clean up? |
|---|---|---|
| `{ chat: externalInstance }` | Developer | Developer |
| `id` changes | **Library** | **Library** |

When the developer passes `id` and the library auto-creates/replaces the `Chat` instance, the developer has no reliable way to abort the previous stream — they would need to call `stop()` before every state update that could change `id`, which is impractical (routing changes, parent component state, etc.).

#### Workaround (until fixed)

Call `stop()` synchronously before the state update that changes `id`:

```ts
const { stop } = useChat({ id: chatId, ... });

const switchChat = (newId: string) => {
  stop();           // abort before re-render
  setChatId(newId);
};
```

Note: this only works when the id change is triggered by an explicit user action. It won't help with route-based or parent-driven id changes.

- @ai-sdk/react: 4.0.0-beta.10

title: Feature: Support array-based system prompts with per-block cache control in streamText
body:
### Description

**Feature: Support array-based system prompts with per-block cache control in streamText**

**Problem**

Anthropic's API supports passing the system prompt as an array of content blocks, each with independent `cache_control`. This is critical for prompt caching when the system prompt contains both static and dynamic content:

```json
"system": [
  { "type": "text", "text": "<large static persona prompt>", "cache_control": { "type": "ephemeral" } },
  { "type": "text", "text": "<dynamic per-request context>" }
]
```

The static block gets cached (90% cost reduction on subsequent requests), while the dynamic block changes freely without invalidating the cache.

Currently, `streamText` only accepts `system` as a single string. This means any dynamic content (timestamps, RAG context, per-request metadata) in the system prompt invalidates the entire cache prefix on every request — resulting in 100% cache misses and a net cost *increase* from the 25% cache write premium.

**Real-world impact**

I'm using `@ai-sdk/anthropic` (3.0.58) with `ai` (6.0.116). My system prompt is ~5k tokens of static persona/instructions + ~500-2k tokens of dynamic RAG context per request. I implemented the `addCacheControlToMessages` pattern from the cookbook for message-level caching, but the system prompt is the bigger win — it's identical across all requests except for the dynamic suffix.

With the current string-only `system` parameter, I get `cache_creation_input_tokens` on every single request and `cache_read_input_tokens: 0` — paying more than without caching.

**Proposed API**

Allow `system` to accept an array of content blocks with `providerOptions`, similar to how messages already work:

```typescript
streamText({
  model: anthropic('claude-sonnet-4-6'),
  system: [
    {
      type: 'text',
      text: STATIC_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
      providerOptions: {
        anthropic: { cacheControl: { type: 'ephemeral' } }
      }
    },
    {
      type: 'text',
      text: dynamicRagContext
    }
  ],
  messages: convertedMessages,
});
```

**Workarounds considered**

- Moving dynamic content into a synthetic user message: works but semantically wrong, and the model may treat system vs user context differently
- Passing the entire system prompt as a single cached block: invalidated every request by dynamic content
- Using `addCacheControlToMessages` for message-level caching only: helps for multi-turn but doesn't address the system prompt, which is the largest repeated cost

**Environment**
- `@ai-sdk/anthropic`: 3.0.58
- `ai`: 6.0.116
- Node 18+, Next.js 16

title: Pre-execute tools to reduce latency
body:
### Description

We're noticing that in cases where we know the model is going to need a certain tool call, that there is a pretty massive latency penalty in letting it call the tool vs preempting it by just injecting the result of the tool call in the prompt body.

It'd be nice to get better DX and reusability when doing this kind of thing, and it'd be ideal if the internal representation was as close to identical as possible between the preempt vs not, to minimize subtle bugs or changes in context/accuracy.

One possible approach would be an argument like `toolCalls` of the form:

```
toolCalls: [
  {
    tool: getUserData,
    args: { userId, page: 0 },
  },
]
```

Another option would be combining it with prompt/messages:

```
messages: [
  ...getUserData.toMessages({ userId, page: 0 }),
]
```

A useful consideration to the above would be how easy it makes it for client side code to make/preempt the tool call, of course without any access to the actual execute function, but this would further simplify things, since at least in our case certain buttons on the client should combine a message with some natural tool calls that go with that message.

As mentioned, we can currently do something like:

```
const args = { userId, page: 0 };
prompt: `... getUserData(${JSON.stringify(args)}) = ${getUserData.execute(args)} ...`
```

But it's not the prettiest and will have a quite different internal representation, where that difference may increase or decrease between subsequent library versions. We can try to make it look closer to a real tool call by looking at the existing representation used by the lib, but this further exacerbates the library version sensitivity / coupling aspect.

title: anthropic: empty compaction content persisted then rejected on re-send
body:
## Description

When using Anthropic's native compaction (`compact_20260112` context management), the API can return a compaction block with empty/null `content`. The `@ai-sdk/anthropic` provider persists this faithfully (the **response** schema allows `content: string().nullish()`), but when the message is re-sent on the next turn, the **request** schema requires non-empty `content`, causing the API to reject the entire request:

```
messages.67.content.0.compaction.content: content can't be empty
```

## Reproduction

1. Use `streamText` with Anthropic provider and compaction enabled:
   ```ts
   providerOptions: {
     anthropic: {
       contextManagement: {
         edits: [{
           type: "compact_20260112",
           trigger: { type: "input_tokens", value: 150_000 },
           instructions: "Summarize...",
         }],
       },
     },
   }
   ```
2. Have a long conversation that triggers compaction
3. In some cases, the compaction block arrives with empty content
4. The SDK converts it to a text part with `text: ""` and `providerMetadata.anthropic.type === "compaction"`
5. When persisted (e.g. via `AIChatAgent`) and re-sent on the next turn, `convertToModelMessages` produces `{ type: "compaction", content: "" }`
6. Anthropic API rejects: `content can't be empty`

## Root cause

**Response parsing** (in `@ai-sdk/anthropic`): compaction blocks are converted to `{ type: "text", text: part.content }`. If `content` is empty/null, `text` becomes `""`.

**Request building**: text parts with `anthropic.type === "compaction"` become `{ type: "compaction", content: part.text }`. If `part.text` is `""`, the API rejects it.

**Schema asymmetry**:
- Response: `content: z.string().nullish()` ✅ allows empty
- Request: `content: z.string()` ❌ requires non-empty

## Suggested fix

In the response-to-internal conversion, skip compaction blocks with empty/null content. Or in the request builder, filter out compaction blocks where `content` is falsy.

## Versions

- `ai`: 6.0.116
- `@ai-sdk/anthropic`: 3.0.46

title: React example — AI recipe assistant with useChat, streamText, tool(), and Generative UI
body:
Hi Vercel!

**Summary**
I built a recipe search platform where users can find recipes based on ingredients they have.
This also includes an AI-powered recipe assistant where users can ask in chat and get recipe suggestions.
I’d love to contribute this as an example.

**What the Example Would Cover**

- useChat: Chat UI for ingredient-based queries
- streamText: Real-time streaming responses
- tool(): Searches a local recipe database and returns structured results
- Generative UI: Dynamically renders recipe cards, ingredient checklists, and step-by-step guides based on tool call results

**Workflow**

1. User asks a question in the chat.
2. LLM calls the searchRecipes tool.
3. Results stream back to the users.
4. UI components render inline in the chat interface.


**Why**
Under the examples folder, there’s great coverage across frameworks, but I didn’t see a standalone React example.
Since many developers use React and I saw some people who wanted Vercel AI in React ([Link](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/1650)), I thought this could be a useful addition.

Would this be a good fit for the examples directory?
Happy to adjust scope or structure based on your feedback.

title: Feature Request: Lazy Tool Discovery
body:
### Description

## Summary
Add support for lazy tool discovery a mechanism that withholds tool definitions from the LLM until it explicitly requests them, reducing token usage and improving tool selection accuracy in large tool sets.

## Motivation
As AI applications scale, it’s common to register many tools (20, 30, 50+). 

Today, every tool’s full description and JSON schema is sent to the LLM on every request, regardless of whether the tool is relevant. This creates real problems:
	∙	Token waste: Detailed tool schemas can burn 3,000–5,000 tokens before the conversation even starts.
	∙	Degraded accuracy: LLMs perform worse at tool selection as the number of choices grows. Irrelevant tools add noise.
	∙	Higher costs: More tokens per request = higher API bills at scale.
The only workaround today is to build a custom routing/pre-filtering layer, which is complex and brittle.

## Proposed API
A simple ‘lazy: true’ flag on tool definitions

## Prior Art
TanStack AI shipped this feature: https://tanstack.com/blog/tanstack-ai-lazy-tool-discovery
Their implementation uses a ‘lazy: true’ flag on tool definitions and a LazyToolManager class that handles the separation, dynamic injection, and cleanup. It’s entirely opt-in if no tools have ‘lazy: true’, behavior is identical to today.

Happy to contribute or prototype this if it aligns with the roadmap. Thanks for considering it!

title: AI Gateway seems to delay/batch tool input deltas for long string fields compared to Vertex provider
body:
### Description

### Problem

  I’m seeing different tool input streaming behavior between:

  - Vercel AI Gateway
  - Vertex provider

  For the same app flow, when a tool input contains a long string field, AI Gateway appears
  to delay streaming for that field until the JSON value is complete, while Vertex starts
  streaming it incrementally earlier.

  I am observing this via the tool-level `onInputDelta` callback.

  ### My observation

  From testing, it looks like:

  - earlier tool input fields stream first
  - if a later field is a long string value, AI Gateway does not start streaming that field
  immediately
  - instead, it seems to wait until that JSON value has been fully produced, then starts
  emitting the corresponding deltas in a burst

  So the behavior looks like “the long string field does not stream while the value is
  still incomplete; it only starts streaming once that JSON value is effectively complete”.

  With Vertex provider, I do not see this behavior.

  ### Expected

  If the upstream provider is already producing tool input deltas, I would expect AI
  Gateway to preserve those deltas as they are generated, including for incomplete long
  string values.

  ### Actual

  With AI Gateway, a long string field appears to be delayed until much later, as if
  streaming of that field is blocked until the JSON value is complete.

  Representative logs from `onInputDelta`:

  ```ts
  { sequence: 11, elapsedMs: 910, totalLength: 60, rawPreview:
  '{"flag":true,"title":"..."}' }
  { sequence: 12, elapsedMs: 15527, totalLength: 67, rawPreview:
  '{"flag":true,"title":"...","longField' }
  { sequence: 13, elapsedMs: 15531, totalLength: 77, rawPreview:
  '{"flag":true,"title":"...","longField":"...' }
```

  The notable part is the large gap between finishing earlier fields and the start of the
  long string field.

  ### Minimal shape of the tool input

  This reproduces with input roughly like:

```ts
  z.object({
    flag: z.boolean(),
    title: z.string(),
    longField: z.string(),
  })
```

  ### How I observed it

  I logged raw tool input deltas using onInputDelta:

```ts
  onInputDelta: ({ toolCallId, inputTextDelta }) => {
    const nextRaw =
      (rawInputByToolCallId.get(toolCallId) ?? '') + inputTextDelta;

    rawInputByToolCallId.set(toolCallId, nextRaw);

    console.log({
      toolCallId,
      deltaLength: inputTextDelta.length,
      totalLength: nextRaw.length,
      nowIso: new Date().toISOString(),
      rawPreview: nextRaw.slice(Math.max(0, nextRaw.length - 240)),
    });
  }
```

  ### Notes

  - This is not a part.input partial-JSON parsing issue.
  - The behavior is already visible in raw tool input delta logs.
  - Switching from AI Gateway to Vertex provider removes the problem.

### AI SDK Version

  `ai@6.0.127`

title: MCP tool integration has no per-message authentication or integrity verification
body:
## Summary

The Vercel AI SDK supports MCP tool calling, but MCP itself provides no cryptographic identity or message integrity layer. Any agent can call any tool, messages are unsigned, and tool definitions can be tampered with.

## The gap

- **No agent identity**: No passport or certificate mechanism for agents calling MCP tools.
- **No message signing**: JSON-RPC messages are unsigned -- parameters can be modified in transit.
- **No tool integrity**: Tool definitions from `tools/list` are not signed. Tool poisoning (OWASP MCP03) is a known attack vector.
- **No replay protection**: Same tool call can be replayed indefinitely.

OWASP has published an [MCP Top 10](https://owasp.org/www-project-mcp-top-10/) covering these risks.

## Existing work

An IETF Internet-Draft has been published to address this:

- **IETF Datatracker**: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-sharif-mcps-secure-mcp/
- **Reference implementations**: [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-secure) / [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/mcp-secure/) (zero dependencies)
- **Interactive demo**: https://agentsign.dev/playground

The spec adds agent passports (ECDSA P-256), per-message signing, tool definition signatures, and nonce-based replay protection -- fully backward-compatible with current MCP.

Happy to discuss integration approaches.

title: Provider type has rerankingModel as required, but ProviderV3 has it as optional
body:
## Description

The `Provider` type exported from `ai` package has `rerankingModel` as **required**, but `ProviderV3` from `@ai-sdk/provider` has it as **optional** (`?`). This inconsistency causes type errors when assigning a `ProviderV3` implementation (e.g. from `@ai-sdk/open-responses`) to a `Provider` typed variable.

## Source references

`rerankingModel` is **required**

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/8b1e7ad43c03a75e5d4b81ef5caef8acba342580/packages/ai/src/types/provider.ts#L44-L54

`rerankingModel` is **optional** (`?`):

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/8b1e7ad43c03a75e5d4b81ef5caef8acba342580/packages/provider/src/provider/v3/provider-v3.ts#L82-L92

## Reproduction

```typescript
import { createOpenResponses } from '@ai-sdk/open-responses'
import type { Provider } from 'ai'

// TS2322: Type 'OpenResponsesProvider' is not assignable to type 'Provider'.
//   Types of property 'rerankingModel' are incompatible.
//     Type '((modelId: string) => RerankingModelV3) | undefined' is not assignable to
//       type '(modelId: string) => RerankingModelV3'.
const provider: Provider = createOpenResponses({
  name: 'test',
  url: 'http://localhost/v1/responses'
})
```

## Expected behavior

`Provider` type should have `rerankingModel` as optional (`?`), consistent with `ProviderV3`.

The runtime code already handles this correctly — `asProviderV3()` in `wrap-provider.ts` sets `rerankingModel: void 0` for V2 providers, showing it's expected to be optional.
author: EurFelux

title: @ai-sdk/open-responses does not support reasoning parameters (reasoningEffort, reasoningSummary)
body:
## Description

`@ai-sdk/open-responses` does not pass `reasoningEffort`, `reasoningSummary`, or any other provider options to the API request body. The `providerOptions` parameter is destructured in `getArgs()` but never used — it is completely discarded.

These are **standard OpenAI Responses API parameters** ([API reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses/create)), not OpenAI-specific extensions:

- `reasoning.effort` — Controls reasoning effort (`none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`)
- `reasoning.summary` — Controls reasoning summary output (`auto`, `detailed`)

## Version

- `@ai-sdk/open-responses@1.0.6` (stable)
- `@ai-sdk/open-responses@2.0.0-beta.1` (beta) — same issue

## Source

In `getArgs()`, `providerOptions` is accepted but never referenced. The returned `body` object has no reasoning-related fields:

No reasoning related parameters here:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/8b1e7ad43c03a75e5d4b81ef5caef8acba342580/packages/open-responses/src/responses/open-responses-language-model.ts#L54-L68

providerOptions is fully ignored and not being used:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/8b1e7ad43c03a75e5d4b81ef5caef8acba342580/packages/open-responses/src/responses/open-responses-language-model.ts#L130-L145

## Expected behavior

`@ai-sdk/open-responses` should support passing reasoning parameters through `providerOptions`, similar to how `@ai-sdk/openai` handles them. For example:

```typescript
const result = await generateText({
  model: openResponses('my-reasoning-model'),
  providerOptions: {
    openai: {  // or whatever the provider name is
      reasoningEffort: 'high',
      reasoningSummary: 'detailed',
    },
  },
});
```

Should produce a request body containing:

```json
{
  "model": "my-reasoning-model",
  "reasoning": {
    "effort": "high",
    "summary": "detailed"
  }
}
```

## Context

We are trying to use `@ai-sdk/open-responses` for third-party OpenAI-compatible providers that support the Responses API, specifically to avoid the model ID allowlist in `@ai-sdk/openai` that silently drops reasoning params for non-canonical model IDs (see #13438). However, `@ai-sdk/open-responses` cannot be used as a replacement because it doesn't support these parameters at all.

title: @ai-sdk/mcp should allow custom fetch for HTTP/SSE transports
body:
`@ai-sdk/mcp` hardcodes `globalThis.fetch` in its HTTP and SSE transports.

This breaks same-app MCP calls on runtimes that need a request-local/internal fetch instead of external HTTP. A concrete case is Nitro on Cloudflare Workers: when the client points to the same worker's `/mcp` route, Cloudflare blocks the self-fetch with error `1042`, so this setup is currently broken.

Downstream context:
- Docus PR: [nuxt-content/docus#1309](https://github.com/nuxt-content/docus/pull/1309)

A small upstream fix would be to allow a custom fetch on MCP transport config, for example:

```ts
createMCPClient({
  transport: {
    type: 'http',
    url,
    fetch: event.fetch,
  },
})
```

I think this should apply to both `http` and `sse`, and the same fetch should also be used for OAuth-related transport requests.

This would avoid downstream custom transports while keeping the solution generic rather than Nitro-specific.

I’m happy to submit a PR if this approach makes sense.
author: onmax

title: AI SDK v6: tool().parameters not read by prepareToolsAndToolChoice (uses inputSchema which is undefined)
body:
## Root Cause Found

`tool()` sets the schema on `.parameters`, but `prepareToolsAndToolChoice` and `doParseToolCall` read `.inputSchema` — which is `undefined`. This causes all tool schemas to fall through to the empty default `{"properties":{},"additionalProperties":false}`.

**One-line fix** in two locations in `ai/dist/index.mjs`:

```diff
- inputSchema: await asSchema(tool2.inputSchema).jsonSchema,
+ inputSchema: await asSchema(tool2.inputSchema ?? tool2.parameters).jsonSchema,
```

```diff
- const schema = asSchema3(tool2.inputSchema);
+ const schema = asSchema3(tool2.inputSchema ?? tool2.parameters);
```

## How We Found It

```javascript
const { tool } = require('ai');
const z = require('zod');
const t = tool({ description: 'test', parameters: z.object({ q: z.string() }), execute: async () => {} });

console.log(Object.keys(t));       // ['description', 'parameters', 'execute']
console.log(t.inputSchema);        // undefined
console.log(typeof t.parameters);  // object (zod schema)
```

`tool()` stores the zod schema on `parameters`. But `prepareToolsAndToolChoice` (line 1779) reads `tool2.inputSchema` which doesn't exist → `asSchema(undefined)` → returns the empty fallback `{"properties":{},"additionalProperties":false}`.

Similarly, `doParseToolCall` (line 3714) uses `asSchema3(tool2.inputSchema)` for validation → empty schema → validation against empty schema either fails or produces wrong results.

## Impact

This breaks ALL tool calling for ALL providers when using `tool()` with Zod schemas in AI SDK v6. The model receives no parameter information, so:

1. It guesses parameter names (sometimes `query`, sometimes `q`, sometimes `{}`)
2. Even when the model guesses correctly, `doParseToolCall` validates against the empty schema and may reject valid inputs

## Verification

With the patch applied:
- API receives correct tool schema with all properties
- Model returns correct arguments 100% of the time
- `parseToolCall` validates and passes correctly
- **8/10 → limited only by model non-determinism, not SDK bugs**

Without the patch: **0/10** — every tool call gets empty schema, model guesses, SDK rejects.

## Environment

- `ai`: 6.0.116
- `zod`: 4.3.6
- Tested with: Cloudflare Workers AI, `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`
- Both `streamText` and `generateText` affected

## Previous Report (Updated)

The original report described two separate bugs. After investigation, **both symptoms trace to this single root cause**:

- "Empty schema sent to API" → `tool2.inputSchema` is undefined, fallback produces `{}`
- "SDK drops valid tool arguments" → `doParseToolCall` validates against empty schema, marks calls as invalid or produces wrong parsed values

The streaming-specific `arguments: "{}"` from Cloudflare was a red herring — it only happened because the empty schema gave the model no parameter guidance. With the correct schema, Cloudflare's streaming endpoint also returns correct arguments.

## Related

This likely supersedes #12020 ("AI SDK v6 + Zod: Tool input_schema is empty when using Anthropic") — same root cause.
author: LucasCzechia

title: Bug: @ai-sdk/openai-compatible sends content:"" for assistant messages with only tool calls, causing Bedrock ValidationException
body:
## Summary

In `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` (v1.0.32), the `convertToOpenAICompatibleChatMessages` function always outputs `content: text` (where `text` is initialized as `""`) for assistant messages. When an assistant message contains only `tool-call` parts and no text parts, this results in `content: ""` being sent in the API request.

Providers backed by AWS Bedrock reject this with:
```
ValidationException: messages: text content blocks must be non-empty
```

## Root Cause

In `dist/index.mjs` (line ~103-109):
```js
case "assistant": {
  let text = "";
  // ... loops over content parts ...
  messages.push({
    role: "assistant",
    content: text,  // <-- empty string when no text parts exist
    tool_calls: toolCalls.length > 0 ? toolCalls : void 0,
    ...metadata
  });
}
```

When the assistant message only contains `tool-call` parts (no `text` parts), `text` remains `""` and the output is `content: ""` rather than `content: null`.

The same pattern exists in `@ai-sdk/openai`'s `convertToOpenAIChatMessages`.

## Proposed Fix

Change `content: text` to `content: text || null` for assistant messages:

```js
messages.push({
  role: "assistant",
  content: text || null,  // null instead of empty string
  tool_calls: toolCalls.length > 0 ? toolCalls : void 0,
  ...metadata
});
```

This matches the OpenAI API spec where `content` is nullable for assistant messages with tool calls.

## Reproduction

1. Use `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` with a Bedrock-backed endpoint
2. Have a multi-turn conversation involving tool calls
3. After 2-5 rounds, an assistant message with only tool-call parts is sent with `content: ""`
4. Bedrock returns HTTP 400: `ValidationException: messages: text content blocks must be non-empty`

## Environment

- `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`: 1.0.32
- `@ai-sdk/openai`: 2.0.89 (same issue)
- Provider backend: AWS Bedrock Runtime

## Related

- [anomalyco/opencode#15715](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/15715)
- [anomalyco/opencode#5028](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/5028)
- [anomalyco/opencode#17742](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/17742) (opencode-side workaround)

title: Tool Call Initialization State Not Visible with Google Gemini
body:
### Description

**Problem**: When using `streamText` with `google.chat('gemini-2.5-pro')`, the UI shows no tool card until tool execution completes. The user
  sees a frozen interface while the model generates large tool arguments (e.g., full document content for).

  **Root Cause**: Google Gemini does not stream tool call arguments incrementally. The `@ai-sdk/google` provider emits `tool-input-start`,
  `tool-input-delta`, `tool-input-end`, and `tool-call` **synchronously from a single chunk**
  (`node_modules/@ai-sdk/google/dist/index.mjs:1305-1330`). This means:

  1. The model generates the entire function call internally (no streaming to client during generation)
  2. All four events arrive at the client simultaneously
  3. Tool `execute()` runs immediately after, often completing quickly (DB save)
  4. The `input-streaming` → `input-available` → `output-available` states flash by in one render cycle


### AI SDK Version

```
  ┌────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┐
  │        Package         │               Version               │
  ├────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ ai                     │ 6.0.68                              │
  ├────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ @ai-sdk/google         │ 3.0.20                              │

title: @ai-sdk/mcp transports should expose option to control HTTP redirect behavior
body:
### Description

The SSE and HTTP transports in @ai-sdk/mcp pass all fetch() calls through with the default redirect: 'follow' behavior. This means a server can return a 3xx redirect response to silently redirect the client to an unintended host (e.g. an internal service), which is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vector.

The SSE transport already has a hard-coded origin check for server-provided endpoint event URLs ([mcp-sse-transport.ts L150-154](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/mcp/src/tool/mcp-sse-transport.ts#L150-L154)), but HTTP redirects bypass this entirely since the redirect is handled by the runtime before the response reaches application code.

### AI SDK Version

title: Cerebras Qwen 3 235B requests fail with `body.enableThinking` unsupported after SDK upgrade
body:
### Description

We are seeing what looks like a compatibility/regression issue with Cerebras after upgrading AI SDK dependencies in our project.

In our app, requests to the Cerebras model **Qwen 3 235B Instruct** started failing with a 500 error after upgrading from:

- `@ai-sdk/cerebras`: `^2.0.34` -> `^2.0.39`
- `ai`: `^6.0.97` -> `^6.0.116`

The error returned by Cerebras is:

```txt
body.enableThinking: property 'body.enableThinking' is unsupported
```

From the user report, this happens even when the provider options are empty.

We are tracking the downstream issue here:
https://github.com/mengxi-ream/read-frog/issues/1146

It would be helpful to know:

1. whether this is an SDK-side regression,
2. whether `enableThinking` is being sent to Cerebras unintentionally for this model/provider,
3. and which version range is expected to work correctly.

### Reproduction / context

Downstream user report:
- Model: `Qwen 3 235B Instruct` on Cerebras
- App version: `1.30.4`
- Browser: Waterfox / Firefox-based
- Result: any translation request returns 500 with `body.enableThinking` unsupported

We suspect this may be related to the dependency upgrade mentioned above, because the issue appeared after updating packages.

### AI SDK Version

title: Improve DX of custom loop control
body:
This is part of our effort to improve compatibility with Workflow (#12165) and at the same time introduce better support for custom/external loop control of streaming responses. To achieve that goal, we are separating out individual reusable functions from streamText. Ideally, `streamText()` becomes a composite method of lower level methods and is only responsible to manage the singular stitch stream returned by the method. ### Goal - enable AI SDK users to build their own loop with either generate or stream / let users have full control of the mutli-step loops. ### Plan 1. ✅ Refactor streamText() to have a single place for LanguageModel to MessageModel transformations. This includes extracting transforms from [run-tools-transformation.ts](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/80d4dde6cb4037ece45e6345af497af71fafadd4/packages/ai/src/generate-text/run-tools-transformation.ts) 2. ✅ Separate generation (llm call) from tool calling. Remove bookkeeping of the `response-metadata` part from `streamText()`. 3. ✅ Combine the `model.toStream()` with retry wrapper and the stream transform into a single exportable function 4. ✅ Introduce new events to model call step (language model call) 5. ✅ Replace `createExecuteToolsTransformation` with method that accepts stream like `invokeToolCallbacksFromStream` 6. Remove callbacks from `createExecuteToolsTransformation` and instead handle all telemetry events in `invokeToolCallbacksFromStream()` 7. Introduce new telemetry events to wrap tool calling as well as model message parts 8. Export new reusable function for tool calling 9. Refactor `generateText()` to have a similar structure to `streamText()` 10. refactor `streamText()` and `generateText()` to share more code composed of exported underlying methods which could be used for custom loop control.## ✅ 1. Refactor transformations to a single place
Here is a dummy code to show case how `streamText()` works today, taken form #13541 ``` initial model messages response model messages stitchable stream do { prepare step convert step input messages (after prepare step) to language model v4 messages stream = doStream (with language model v4 messages) run tools transformation on stream transforms spec format to user friendly format executes tools and injects tool results into stream tool approval? pipe stream with tool results through further transforms transforms: add start-step filter out empty text chunks tool input start filter raw chunks when not enabled add finish-step add finish bookkeeping timeout mgmt events: telemetry, tool input delta add transformed stream with minor augmentation to stitchable stream add new response model messages by converting the assembled step output to additional response model messages } while ( not ( any of the stop conditions is met or finish reason is not tool-calls or tool without execute is called or tool that needs approval is called or there are deferred tool calls ) ) unified stream stream 1 -- stream 2 -- stream 3 ``` Transforms are happening at different places. The general transform flow is 1. streamText receives a [ModelMessage](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/provider-utils/src/types/model-message.ts) array 2. it converts it to [LanguageModelV4Message](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/provider/src/language-model/v4/language-model-v4-prompt.ts) 3. the `model.doStream()` method is called which also returns `LanguageModelV4Message` 4. mix of injecting new chunks, filtering out chunks, transforms, calling hooks, tool handling, tool calling We can't do the transform entirely right after we receive the stream result from `model.doStream()` since we need the finish chunk from the llm call at the end of the `streamText()` loop step, and maybe other reasons, but we will try to find a way around it. As part of that work, we should be able to remove the duplicated code between - [SingleRequestTextStreamPart](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/34fd05191f298be66b50c9cf047cc10154d151cd/packages/ai/src/generate-text/run-tools-transformation.ts#L30) - [TextStreamPart](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/f7d4f010fae81edbd47e2a3a302d316dad63657e/packages/ai/src/generate-text/stream-text-result.ts#L370) As a first step, we need to separate transformation steps such that each transformation has a single responsibility. Done via - https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/13530 - https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/13539 - https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/13596 - https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/13605 - https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/13629
### ✅ 2. Separate llm call (generation) from tool calls in `streamText()` Apply change from https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/13388 but without introducing the flag. Done via - https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/13638 ### ✅ 3. Combine the `model.toStream()` with retry wrapper and the stream transform into a single exportable function - #13647 ### ✅ 4. Introduce new events to wrap generation (llm call) and tool calling - introduce start-generation/finish-generation (name tbd) parts -- this will enable removing the finish part delay in tool execute - introduce start-execute-tools/end-execute-tools ### ✅ 5. Replace `createExecuteToolsTransformation` with method that accepts stream like `invokeToolCallbacksFromStream` - https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/15262 ### Follow ups - [x] consider removing retry logic or at least move outside of stream model call - [ ] extracting stream part types on language model - [ ] move stream part types to separate file - [ ] consider adding -call to execute-tools (stream) - [x] Add glossary / ubiquitous language doc to repository (triggered by "language model call" naming) - [x] further refine types in first transform (rename `UglyTransformedStreamTextPart`) - [ ] https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/14652

title: fix(amazon-bedrock): trimIfLast must not be applied to reasoning blocks with a signature
body:
## Bug Report

### Summary

In `packages/amazon-bedrock/src/convert-to-bedrock-chat-messages.ts`, `trimIfLast()` is applied to reasoning block text even when a cryptographic `signature` is present. This corrupts the text/signature pair, causing Bedrock to reject the request.

### Error

```
ValidationException: The model returned the following errors:
messages.N.content.M: `thinking` or `redacted_thinking` blocks in the latest assistant message 
cannot be modified. These blocks must remain as they were in the original response.
```

### Root Cause

```typescript
// packages/amazon-bedrock/src/convert-to-bedrock-chat-messages.ts (line ~298)
case 'reasoning': {
  if (reasoningMetadata.signature != null) {
    bedrockContent.push({
      reasoningContent: {
        reasoningText: {
          text: trimIfLast(        // ← BUG: trims text even when signature is present
            isLastBlock,
            isLastMessage,
            isLastContentPart,
            part.text,
          ),
          signature: reasoningMetadata.signature,  // signature is for ORIGINAL (untrimmed) text
        },
      },
    });
  }
}
```

The `trimIfLast()` function trims trailing whitespace from the reasoning text when it's the last content part of the last message. However, the `signature` was computed by Anthropic over the **exact original bytes** of the reasoning text. Trimming even a single trailing newline invalidates the signature, causing Bedrock to reject with "cannot be modified".

### Fix

```typescript
// Never trim reasoning text when a signature is present — the signature validates exact bytes
text: reasoningMetadata.signature != null
  ? part.text
  : trimIfLast(isLastBlock, isLastMessage, isLastContentPart, part.text),
signature: reasoningMetadata.signature,
```

### Why `trimIfLast` Exists

The trimming was added to handle Bedrock's restriction on trailing whitespace in **pre-filled** assistant responses. However, this restriction does not apply to reasoning blocks in conversation history — they must be returned verbatim with their original signature.

### Affected Versions

- `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock`: 3.0.82 (current at time of filing)
- Reproducible with Claude Opus 4 on Amazon Bedrock with extended thinking (`reasoning: { type: 'enabled' }`)

### Related

- Related opencode issue: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/18078
- Anthropic API docs: reasoning blocks must be returned verbatim in subsequent turns

title: validateUIMessages re-validates input on output-error tool parts, bricking conversations
body:
## Bug

`validateUIMessages` re-validates tool `.input` against the Zod schema for parts in `output-error` state. This bricks conversations permanently when an LLM produces a tool call with invalid input.

## Expected behavior

A tool part with `state: 'output-error'` represents a **completed** failure — the SDK already handled the bad input, returned an error to the LLM, and the conversation moved on. Re-validating the input on subsequent turns should not happen.

## Reproduction

1. Define a tool with a complex `inputSchema` (discriminated union)
2. LLM calls the tool with malformed input (e.g. passes a JSON string instead of an object)
3. SDK correctly rejects it → sets `state: 'output-error'` with error text, **persists the bad `.input`**
4. LLM receives the error, retries or moves on — conversation continues fine
5. User sends the **next** message
6. `validateUIMessages` iterates all historical parts → hits the old `output-error` part → re-validates `.input` → throws `TypeValidationError`
7. **Conversation is permanently bricked** — every subsequent message triggers the same error

## Root cause

[`validate-ui-messages.ts` L421-426](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/ai/src/ui/validate-ui-messages.ts):

```typescript
if (
  toolPart.state === 'input-available' ||
  toolPart.state === 'output-available' ||
  (toolPart.state === 'output-error' &&
    toolPart.input !== undefined)          // ← re-validates known-bad input
) {
  await validateTypes({ value: toolPart.input, schema: tool.inputSchema });
}
```

## Suggested fix

Remove `output-error` from the validation condition. The input already failed — that's why the part is in `output-error` state.

```typescript
if (
  toolPart.state === 'input-available' ||
  toolPart.state === 'output-available'
) {
```

## Environment

- `ai`: 6.0.115
- Provider: `@ai-sdk/anthropic` 3.0.58
- Runtime: Cloudflare Workers (Durable Objects with `@cloudflare/ai-chat`)

title: convertToModelMessages sends rawInput string as tool_use.input, causing Anthropic 400 on retry
body:
## Bug Report

### Description

When a tool call has `state: "output-error"` with `input: undefined` and `rawInput` set to a string (because the model generated invalid JSON for the tool input), `convertToModelMessages` sends the raw string as the `tool_use.input` value to Anthropic.

Anthropic's API requires `tool_use.input` to be a JSON object/dictionary, so it rejects the request with:

```
400: messages.N.content.M.tool_use.input: Input should be a valid dictionary
```

This creates an **unrecoverable loop** in multi-turn conversations: the corrupted tool call is part of the message history, so every subsequent inference attempt replays the same invalid message and gets the same 400 error.

### Root Cause

In `convertToModelMessages`, when processing tool UI parts with `state === "output-error"`:

```js
input: part.state === "output-error"
  ? (_a = part.input) != null ? _a : "rawInput" in part ? part.rawInput : void 0
  : part.input,
```

When `part.input` is `undefined` (as set during streaming when JSON parsing fails), it falls back to `part.rawInput` — which is a **string**, not an object. Anthropic (and likely other providers) requires `input` to be a dict/object.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Use `streamText` with Anthropic and tools that have structured input schemas
2. The model generates a tool call with syntactically invalid JSON in the input (e.g., an unquoted string value like `"to": John Doe <john@example.com>`)
3. The AI SDK correctly catches the parse error and creates a part with `state: "output-error"`, `input: undefined`, `rawInput: "<the invalid JSON string>"`
4. On the next turn (or retry), `convertToModelMessages` converts this part back to a model message with `input` set to the raw string
5. Anthropic returns `400: messages.N.content.M.tool_use.input: Input should be a valid dictionary`
6. The conversation is now permanently stuck — every retry replays the same broken history

### Expected Behavior

`convertToModelMessages` should ensure `tool_use.input` is always a valid object when converting `output-error` parts. Options:
- Attempt to parse `rawInput` as JSON; if it fails, use `{}` or `{ "raw": rawInput }`  
- Always use `{}` as a fallback when `input` is undefined, regardless of `rawInput`

### Related

- #11154 — tracks the broader cleanup of error message state (v6/v7 TODO)
- #11719 — LLM generating invalid JSON in tool arguments

### Environment

- `ai` SDK version: 5.x (latest)
- Provider: `@ai-sdk/anthropic`
- Runtime: Node.js (AWS Lambda)
author: jb-chief

title: Extract modelCall() from streamText() for reusable single-model-invocation primitive
body:
Part of #13570 (step 3: Combine the `model.doStream()` with retry wrapper and the stream transform into a single exportable function).

## Problem

`streamText()` currently contains a tightly coupled sequence: retry-wrapped `model.doStream()` call and stream parsing transform. This makes it impossible for external consumers like DurableAgent (vercel/workflow) to use just the "single model call" primitive without reimplementing the entire step loop.

## Solution

Extract a `modelCall()` function exported from `ai/internal` that encapsulates:

1. **Retry wrapper** via `prepareRetries` + `model.doStream()`
2. **Stream parsing** via `createStreamTextPartTransform` (raw `LanguageModelV4StreamPart` -> typed stream parts with parsed tool calls, normalized usage/finish)

Tool execution (`createExecuteToolsTransformation`) stays **outside** `modelCall()` — it's the caller's concern, piped through separately.

## Design

`modelCall()` is **synchronous** like `streamText()`. Returns immediately with:
- `stream` — `ReadableStream` that produces chunks when the async model call resolves
- `request` — `Promise<LanguageModelRequestMetadata>` resolving after `doStream` returns
- `response` — `Promise<{ headers?: ... } | undefined>` resolving after `doStream` returns

```typescript
const { stream, request, response } = modelCall({
  model: stepModel,
  callSettings,
  maxRetries,
  tools: stepTools,        // V4-level tool specs for doStream
  toolChoice: stepToolChoice,
  prompt: promptMessages,  // LanguageModelV4Prompt
  // ... other doStream options
  userTools: tools,        // User-level TOOLS with execute functions (for parsing transform)
  system,
  messages: stepInputMessages,
  repairToolCall,
});

// Caller handles tool execution separately
const streamWithToolResults = stream.pipeThrough(
  createExecuteToolsTransformation({ ... }),
);
```

## Implementation

1. Move `StreamTextOnToolCallStartCallback`/`StreamTextOnToolCallFinishCallback` from `stream-text.ts` to `core-events.ts` (breaks circular dependency)
2. Create `packages/ai/src/generate-text/model-call.ts` with synchronous `modelCall()` function
3. Refactor `streamText` to use `modelCall` internally
4. Export `modelCall`, `createExecuteToolsTransformation`, and types from `ai/internal`
5. Add tests for `modelCall`

## Files

title: Bug: `sendAutomaticallyWhen` never fires when any tool approval is denied
body:
### Description

# Bug: `sendAutomaticallyWhen` never fires when any tool approval is denied

## What happened

When using `sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithApprovalResponses` and a user denies a tool call via `addToolApprovalResponse({ approved: false })`, the predicate permanently returns `false` — the conversation never resumes.

## Root cause

`last-assistant-message-is-complete-with-approval-responses.ts` is missing `output-denied` in its `.every()` check:

```ts
// Current (broken)
lastStepToolInvocations.every(
  part =>
    part.state === 'output-available' ||
    part.state === 'output-error' ||
    part.state === 'approval-responded',
)
```

`output-denied` is a valid terminal state (emitted when `approved: false` is passed to `addToolApprovalResponse`). Because it's not listed, a denied tool invocation is treated as still-pending and the predicate never returns `true`.

## Expected behavior

A denial (`approved: false`) is a terminal state. The predicate should return `true` once all tool invocations are in any terminal state — including `output-denied`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Define a tool with `needsApproval: true`
2. Use `useChat` with `sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithApprovalResponses`
3. Trigger a tool call
4. Call `addToolApprovalResponse({ approved: false })` to deny it
5. Observe: `sendAutomaticallyWhen` never fires — chat is permanently stalled

## Fix

```ts
lastStepToolInvocations.every(
  part =>
    part.state === 'output-available' ||
    part.state === 'output-error' ||
    part.state === 'output-denied' || // add this
    part.state === 'approval-responded',
)
```

## Environment

- `ai` version: `6.0.116`
- Affects: `useChat` with `sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithApprovalResponses`
- Related file: `packages/ai/src/ui/last-assistant-message-is-complete-with-approval-responses.ts`

## Notes

Searched existing issues — no open tracker for this specific omission. A related partial fix was applied for `createAgentUIStream` in #12209, but this predicate was not updated.


### AI SDK Version

- `ai` version: `6.0.116`

title: openai-compatible: chat content arrays with thinking parts fail validation
body:
### Description

When using some OpenAI-compatible backends (for example [Ollama](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api/openai-compatibility.mdx) with [Mistral Small 4](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-small-4)), chat responses can return structured content arrays instead of plain strings:

- Non-stream: `choices[].message.content` can be an array
- Stream: `choices[].delta.content` can be an array

Some providers include `thinking` parts (for example `{ "type": "thinking", "thinking": [{ "type": "text", "text": "..." }] }`).

Current behavior rejects these payloads in `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` with validation errors like:

`Type validation failed ... expected string, received array`

This breaks both generate and stream flows for otherwise OpenAI-compatible providers.

## Reproduction

1. Use `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` with a provider that emits content arrays with `thinking` parts.
2. Call `doGenerate` or `doStream`.
3. Observe schema/type validation error when content is array-based.

Example stream chunk:

```json
{
  "id": "de2d54af68ac42b49519a72022e3c5c3",
  "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
  "model": "mistral-small-latest",
  "choices": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "delta": {
        "content": [
          {
            "type": "thinking",
            "thinking": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Hello" }]
          }
        ]
      },
      "finish_reason": null
    }
  ]
}
```

## Expected Behavior

- `content` should accept string and array forms for OpenAI-compatible providers.
- Known parts should be normalized:
  - `type: "text"` -> text output
  - `type: "thinking"` -> reasoning output
- Unknown part types should not crash parsing/validation.

### AI SDK Version

- `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`: current `master` / `3.0.0-beta.9` in repo

title: bug: uiMessageChunkSchema strict validation breaks backward due to providerMetadata addition
body:
## Problem
The uiMessageChunkSchema uses strict Zod validation that rejects unrecognized keys. When new fields are added to stream events server-side, clients with cached bundles from a previous version fail to parse them, throwing `AI_TypeValidationError`.

This was exposed by  78c0e26 (released in ai@6.0.120), backported in https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/13184 which added providerMetadata to stream events like tool-output-available. Clients still running the previous schema reject the new field as unrecognized.

## Reproduction

- Deploy an app using ai@6.0.119 or earlier
- Users load the app (client JS bundle is cached)
- Upgrade to ai@6.0.120+ and redeploy
- Users with cached bundles receive stream events from the new server and get:
- AI_TypeValidationError: Type validation failed
- Value: {"type":"tool-output-available","toolCallId":"...","output":{...},"providerMetadata":{"openai":{"itemId":"..."}}}
- The Zod discriminated union tries every variant. The tool-output-available variant matches on type, toolCallId, and output, but fails with:

```
{
  "code": "unrecognized_keys",
  "keys": ["providerMetadata"],
  "message": "Unrecognized key: \"providerMetadata\""
}
```

## Expected behavior
The stream protocol should be forward-compatible across patch/minor versions. The uiMessageChunkSchema should use .passthrough() (or equivalent) so that unrecognized keys are silently ignored rather than rejected. This way, adding optional fields to stream events doesn’t break older clients.

## Environment
ai: 6.0.116 → 6.0.134
@ai-sdk/react: 3.0.118 → 3.0.136
@ai-sdk/provider-utils: 4.0.19 → 4.0.21
zod: 4.3.6
Framework: Next.js (App Router)

- it contains HTTP request level settings (e.g. timeout, abort signal)

title: Horrific debugging experience, due to misuse of async (...) => promiseReturningFunction(...)
body:
### Description

Throughout the code in the SDK, the pattern async (...) => promiseReturningFunction(...) is used.

This is a huge problem for debugging, because this pattern can cause async stack traces to omit or degrade the current call site, especially across layered wrappers and streaming/telemetry boundaries; replacing it with return await ... at public abstraction boundaries improves debuggability

The proper pattern should be:
async (...) => await promiseReturningFunction(...)

And never:
async (...) => promiseReturningFunction(...)

Here is an example:

```
  "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
  server: "llama.cpp",
},
 responseBody: "{\"error\":{\"code\":400,\"message\":\"request (45000 tokens) exceeds the available context size (44800 tokens), try increasing it\",\"type\":\"exceed_context_size_error\",\"n_prompt_tokens\":45000,\"n_ctx\":44800}}",                                                                                                                                                           
 isRetryable: false,
       data: {
  error: [Object ...],
},
 vercel.ai.error: true,
 vercel.ai.error.AI_APICallError: true,

      at /home/mdierolf/gitprojects/tokenring/node_modules/.bun/@ai-sdk+provider-utils@4.0.21+3c5d820c62823f0b/node_modules/@ai-sdk/provider-utils/dist/index.mjs:2548:18
      at /home/mdierolf/gitprojects/tokenring/node_modules/.bun/@ai-sdk+provider-utils@4.0.21+3c5d820c62823f0b/node_modules/@ai-sdk/provider-utils/dist/index.mjs:2391:34
      at processTicksAndRejections (native:7:39)

```

The culprit is this:

```
export const postJsonToApi = async <T>({
  url,
  headers,
  body,
  failedResponseHandler,
  successfulResponseHandler,
  abortSignal,
  fetch,
}: {
  url: string;
  headers?: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  body: unknown;
  failedResponseHandler: ResponseHandler<APICallError>;
  successfulResponseHandler: ResponseHandler<T>;
  abortSignal?: AbortSignal;
  fetch?: FetchFunction;
}) =>
  postToApi({
    url,
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      ...headers,
    },
    body: {
      content: JSON.stringify(body),
      values: body,
    },
    failedResponseHandler,
    successfulResponseHandler,
    abortSignal,
    fetch,
  });

```

After changing the above to: 
async postJsonToApi => await postToApi(...)

We can see more of the stack, until we lose the stack yet again in the telemetry wrapper around doStream:

```
 vercel.ai.error.AI_APICallError: true,

      at /home/mdierolf/gitprojects/tokenring/node_modules/.bun/@ai-sdk+provider-utils@4.0.21+3c5d820c62823f0b/node_modules/@ai-sdk/provider-utils/dist/index.mjs:2548:18
      at /home/mdierolf/gitprojects/tokenring/node_modules/.bun/@ai-sdk+provider-utils@4.0.21+3c5d820c62823f0b/node_modules/@ai-sdk/provider-utils/dist/index.mjs:2391:34
      at doStream (/home/mdierolf/gitprojects/tokenring/node_modules/.bun/@ai-sdk+openai-compatible@2.0.37+3c5d820c62823f0b/node_modules/@ai-sdk/openai-compatible/dist/index.mjs:733:43)
      at /home/mdierolf/gitprojects/tokenring/node_modules/.bun/ai@6.0.138+3c5d820c62823f0b/node_modules/ai/dist/index.mjs:8403:18
      at /home/mdierolf/gitprojects/tokenring/node_modules/.bun/ai@6.0.138+3c5d820c62823f0b/node_modules/ai/dist/index.mjs:2736:133
      at processTicksAndRejections (native:7:39)

```

If I walk up through the code, changing every:
async () => promiseReturningFunction 
to 
async() => await promiseReturningFunction

I can slowly get meaningful debug messages.

Underlying all this, is the fact that the openai-compatible provider is barfing errors within the stream transform as unhandled exceptions which get written to stdout, which is completely ruining my ability to build a CLI with this library, and it is extremely difficult to identify the exact call site for where the thrown error from the promise is happening

title: Bug: @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock computes negative noCacheTokens for cached requests
body:
## Description

The `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` provider computes a negative `noCacheTokens` value when prompt caching is used with Bedrock Claude models.

## Version

`@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock@4.0.4`

## Root Cause

In the Bedrock usage conversion, the formula is:

```javascript
noCache: inputTokens - cacheReadTokens,
```

However, Bedrock's `inputTokens` field represents only the **non-cached, non-cache-write** tokens — it does NOT include cached tokens in its count. This differs from OpenAI/Google where `prompt_tokens` is the total.

For example, Bedrock returns:
```json
{
  "inputTokens": 1,
  "cacheReadInputTokens": 6512,
  "cacheWriteInputTokens": 791
}
```

The SDK then computes:
- `noCache: 1 - 6512 = -6511` ❌ (should be `1`)
- `total: 1` (also wrong — should be `1 + 6512 + 791 = 7304`)

## Expected Behavior

For Bedrock, the conversion should match the Anthropic provider's approach:
- `noCache: inputTokens` (use the raw value directly, since it already excludes cached tokens)
- `total: inputTokens + cacheReadTokens + cacheWriteTokens`

## Comparison with Anthropic Provider

The `@ai-sdk/anthropic` provider handles this correctly:
```javascript
noCache: inputTokens,           // Direct assignment — correct
cacheRead: cacheReadTokens,
cacheWrite: cacheCreationTokens
```

The Bedrock provider should use the same approach, since Bedrock Claude returns the same semantics for `inputTokens`.

## Suggested Fix

In `packages/amazon-bedrock/src/bedrock-chat-language-model.ts` (or equivalent), change:

```diff
- noCache: inputTokens - cacheReadTokens,
+ noCache: inputTokens,
```

And fix the total:

```diff
- total: inputTokens,
+ total: inputTokens + cacheReadTokens + cacheWriteTokens,
```

title: Anthropic web search tool (webSearch_20260209) crashes toUIMessageStreamResponse with TypeError
body:
## Description

Using Anthropic's native web search tool (`anthropic.tools.webSearch_20260209()`) with `streamText` + `toUIMessageStreamResponse()` causes a server-side crash:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'type')
```

The error occurs during stream serialization — the `server_tool_use` and `web_search_tool_result` content blocks from Anthropic's API can't be mapped to UIMessage parts.

## Reproduction

```typescript
import { streamText } from "ai";
import { anthropic } from "@ai-sdk/anthropic";

const result = streamText({
  model: anthropic("claude-sonnet-4-6"),
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "What is the weather in NYC?" }],
  tools: {
    ...myCustomTools,
    ...anthropic.tools.webSearch_20260209({ maxUses: 3 }),
  },
});

// This crashes:
return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse();

// Note: toDataStreamResponse() was not tested
```

## Environment

- `ai`: 6.0.141
- `@ai-sdk/anthropic`: 3.0.64
- `@ai-sdk/react`: 3.0.143
- Next.js 16.1.7

## Expected behavior

Web search results should be serialized into UIMessage parts (perhaps as a tool-call/tool-result pair, or as a text part with citations).

## Actual behavior

Server throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'type')` during stream processing. The POST returns 200 but the client receives no usable response.

## Workaround

Using a custom web search tool (e.g., DuckDuckGo scraping) instead of Anthropic's native server tool.

## Context

Anthropic's web search returns non-standard content blocks (`server_tool_use`, `web_search_tool_result`) that `toUIMessageStreamResponse` doesn't know how to transform into UIMessage parts. The same web search tool works fine when using the Anthropic SDK directly with non-streaming `messages.create()` and returning plain JSON.

title: AI Gateway: Cached tokens billed at full input price for Moonshot/Kimi — 6x cost vs direct API
body: ### Description ### Description When using `moonshotai/kimi-k2.5` via AI Gateway, cached tokens are **reported correctly** in the dashboard but **billed at full input price**. The same workload costs ~$0.64 via Moonshot's direct API vs ~$4.00 via Gateway (6x more). ### Evidence Single blog generation session (multi-turn, 50+ turns): | Metric | Value | |--------|-------| | Input Tokens | 6.2M | | Cache Read Tokens | 5.8M (93.5% hit) | | Output Tokens | 72K | | **Actual cost** | **~$4.00** | | **Expected cost** | **~$1.28** | The $4.00 matches all input billed at full price: 6.2M × $0.60/M + 72K × $2.40/M = **$3.89**. With cache discount applied: 400K × $0.60/M + 5.8M × $0.15/M + 72K × $2.40/M = **$1.28**. ### What we tried - **`caching: 'auto'`** via `providerOptions.gateway` — no effect (expected, since [docs](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/provider-options#automatic-caching) say it only works for explicit-caching providers like Anthropic/MiniMax, not implicit-caching like Moonshot) - **`GET /v1/generation`** — `native_tokens_cached` is populated but `total_cost` reflects full-price billing ### Possible causes 1. **Gateway billing doesn't apply cache discount** for implicit-caching providers (Moonshot, OpenAI, DeepSeek) 2. **Multi-backend routing** — Gateway may route to backends (Groq, DeepInfra, Fireworks) that don't honor Moonshot's cached pricing 3. **Related to #8349** — Moonshot uses the Anthropic-compatible endpoint (`api.moonshot.ai/anthropic`), same `@ai-sdk/anthropic` code path where cache token aggregation bugs were already found in multi-step workflows ### Environment - Model: `moonshotai/kimi-k2.5` - AI Gateway (`ai-gateway.vercel.sh`) - Multi-turn agentic workflow via Claude Code SDK + Vercel Sandbox ### Related Issues - #8349 — Inaccurate cache token counts in multi-step Anthropic workflows - #9921 — Token Usage Normalization proposal - #2845 — Prompt token usage inaccurate with caching - #8367 — Cache write tokens not in response usage ### Questions 1. Are cached tokens from implicit-caching providers billed at full input price through the Gateway? 2. Does multi-backend routing affect whether cache discounts are applied? 3. Any workaround, or should we use direct provider APIs for cost-sensitive workloads? ### AI SDK Version - `ai@6.0.41` - `ai-sdk-provider-claude-code@3.3.3` - `@ai-sdk/anthropic@3.0.15` - Model: `moonshotai/kimi-k2.5` via AI Gateway (`ai-gateway.vercel.sh`) - Multi-turn agentic workflow via Claude Code SDK + Vercel Sandbox ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

title: `@ai-sdk/google`: Support combining provider-defined tools with function tools (Gemini 3 tool combination)
body:
## Description

`prepareTools` in `@ai-sdk/google` drops all function tools when provider-defined tools (e.g., `googleSearch`) are present. The function returns early with only provider tools, so custom function declarations are never sent to the Gemini API.

This is a hard block for any application that needs both Google Search grounding and custom function calling in the same agent.

## Root Cause

In `google-prepare-tools.ts`, when `hasProviderTools` is true, the function returns early with only the provider tool entries. Function tools are completely excluded from the request:

```ts
if (hasProviderTools) {
  // ... processes provider tools into googleTools
  return { tools: googleTools, toolConfig: undefined, toolWarnings };
  // ↑ function tools never reach the API
}
```

## Gemini API Support

The Gemini API officially supports combining built-in tools with function declarations since Gemini 3. From [Google's documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3#combine_built-in_tools_and_function_calling):

> Gemini 3 series models support the option to combine built-in tools with custom tools in a single turn.

The expected API request format is:

```json
{
  "tools": [
    { "googleSearch": {} },
    { "functionDeclarations": [{ "name": "my_tool", ... }] }
  ]
}
```

This works on both Google AI Studio API and Vertex AI API (`aiplatform.googleapis.com`).

## Verified Fix

We patched `prepareTools` to combine both tool types instead of the early return. The fix is minimal:

1. Process provider tools into an array (instead of returning early)
2. Continue to process function tools as normal
3. Combine both: `[...providerToolEntries, { functionDeclarations }]`

With this patch, we confirmed the following works on Vertex AI (`gemini-3-flash-preview`):
- Builtin tool only (Google Search) → ✅
- Custom tool only → ✅
- Both registered, model selects builtin → ✅
- Both registered, model selects custom → ✅
- **Both called in a single conversation** → ✅

## Reproduction

```typescript
import { createVertex } from "@ai-sdk/google-vertex"
import { Agent } from "@mastra/core/agent"
import { tool } from "ai"
import { z } from "zod"

const vertex = createVertex({ project: "my-project", location: "global" })

const agent = new Agent({
  model: vertex("gemini-3-flash-preview"),
  tools: {
    google_search: vertex.tools.googleSearch({}),
    get_inventory: tool({
      description: "Get inventory count for a product.",
      parameters: z.object({ productId: z.string() }),
      execute: async ({ productId }) => ({ productId, count: 42 }),
    }),
  },
})

// This should use both tools but currently only sends googleSearch
const result = await agent.generate([{
  role: "user",
  content: "Check inventory for SKU-123 and search the web for Seoul weather.",
}], { maxSteps: 10 })
```

**Current behavior:** Warning `"combination of function and provider-defined tools" is not supported`, only `googleSearch` is sent to API, `get_inventory` is silently dropped.

**Expected behavior:** Both tools sent to API, model can invoke either or both.

## Note on `include_server_side_tool_invocations`

Google's [documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3#combine_built-in_tools_and_function_calling) states that `include_server_side_tool_invocations: true` must be set in `toolConfig` to enable tool context circulation. However:

- **Vertex AI** (`aiplatform.googleapis.com`): Tool combination works WITHOUT this flag. Setting it results in `Unknown name "includeServerSideToolInvocations" at 'tool_config': Cannot find field.`
- **Google AI Studio** (`generativelanguage.googleapis.com`): The flag may be required per the docs.

The SDK should handle this difference between the two API backends.

## Environment

- `@ai-sdk/google`: 3.0.53
- `@ai-sdk/google-vertex`: 4.0.95
- `ai`: 6.0.116
- Model: `gemini-3-flash-preview`
- API: Vertex AI (`aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1`)

## Related Issues

- #11695 (closed without fix — error message improved but tools still dropped)
- #8258 (AI SDK 5 version of same issue)
- #10251 (PR that only improved the warning message)

title: AI Gateway + streamText structured output intermittently returns 503 for Anthropic model while plain text succeeds
body:
## Versions

- `ai`: `6.0.99`
- `@ai-sdk/gateway`: `3.0.55`
- `zod`: `4.3.5`
- Node: `v24.12.0`

## What happens

When calling Vercel AI Gateway with `streamText` plus structured output against `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`, I intermittently get:

```txt
GatewayInternalServerError: Service temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.
```

The failure comes back with provider metadata showing that all three Anthropic-family routes failed with `503`:

- `anthropic`
- `vertexAnthropic`
- `bedrock`

This appears to be specific to the structured-output path. In the same environment, a plain-text `streamText` repro succeeds repeatedly.

## Minimal repro

```js
import { createGateway, Output, streamText } from 'ai'
import { z } from 'zod'

const model = createGateway().chat('anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6')
const output = Output.object({ schema: z.object({ ok: z.boolean() }) })

const result = streamText({
  model,
  system: 'Return only structured output.',
  prompt: 'Return {"ok": true}.',
  output,
  temperature: 0.1,
  maxOutputTokens: 3000,
  providerOptions: {
    anthropic: {
      effort: 'low',
      thinking: { type: 'disabled' },
    },
  },
})

console.log(await result.output)
```

I wrapped that in a small loop to run multiple attempts. The same repro sometimes succeeds and sometimes fails.

## Observed behavior

A recent failing request returned:

- `x-vercel-id`: `sin1::fra1::4lnbm-1774960059784-cce1def8beee`
- Date: `Tue, 31 Mar 2026 12:27:40 GMT`

The nested response body included:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Service temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.",
    "type": "service_unavailable_error"
  },
  "providerMetadata": {
    "gateway": {
      "routing": {
        "originalModelId": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6",
        "attempts": [
          {
            "provider": "anthropic",
            "statusCode": 503,
            "error": "Service temporarily unavailable"
          },
          {
            "provider": "vertexAnthropic",
            "statusCode": 503,
            "error": "Service temporarily unavailable"
          },
          {
            "provider": "bedrock",
            "statusCode": 503,
            "error": "Service temporarily unavailable"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Another failing request ID from an earlier run:

- `sin1::fra1::fwvcs-1774958838510-f8df7d1406b4`

## Comparison

Using the same Gateway/model path, a plain-text `streamText` repro without structured output succeeded `10/10` in a short run.

So the current evidence points to the structured-output path rather than a general outage for all Gateway requests.

## Expected behavior

Either:

- the request succeeds, or
- Gateway returns a failure mode that makes it clear this is a provider-side outage on the structured-output route

but it should not intermittently fail on such a small schema if the plain-text path is healthy.

## Notes

I have also seen separate Anthropic structured-output `400` errors for unsupported schema features and grammar compilation timeouts, but this issue is specifically about the intermittent `503` path after using a valid, tiny schema.

If helpful, I can provide the exact repro script and more request IDs.
