title: OAuth resource parameter gets trailing slash from URL.href, breaking auth servers that do exact matching
body:
### Description

When the MCP server's Protected Resource Metadata returns a pathless resource URL (e.g., https://mcp.example.com), the resource parameter sent to the authorization server gets an unwanted trailing slash (https://mcp.example.com/). This is because `new URL("https://mcp.example.com").href` returns "https://mcp.example.com/" per the URL spec.

Auth servers that do exact matching on the resource parameter reject the request because the trailing slash makes it a different URI than what was registered.

**Reproduction:**

Set up an MCP server whose /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource returns a pathless resource URL:
```json
{
  "resource": "https://mcp.example.com",
  "authorization_servers": ["https://auth.example.com"]
}
```
Attempt to connect — the OAuth token exchange fails because the resource parameter is sent as https://mcp.example.com/ instead of https://mcp.example.com

**Root cause:**

resource.href is used in three places, all of which add the trailing slash:

- `startAuthorization`
- `exchangeAuthorization`
- `refreshAuthorization`

The MCP spec itself recommends the form without the trailing slash (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization#canonical-server-uri):

> implementations SHOULD consistently use the form without the trailing slash for better interoperability

**Related issues:**                                                                                                                                                                                          
- modelcontextprotocol/inspector#927 

### AI SDK Version

@ai-sdk/mcp: 1.0.30

title: Consider aligning `FilePart` and how files are handled in `ToolResultOutput`
body:
`FilePart` (as part of `ContentPart`) uses a single `type: "file"` with an overloaded `data` field (`DataContent | URL`, further expanded in #13816). In contrast, file content within `ToolResultOutput` already uses distinguishable types: `file-data`, `file-url`, `file-id`, etc.

This inconsistency causes practical problems:

- A `string` value in `data` is always assumed to be base64. Using it for anything else (e.g. a URL string) is brittle or requires hacky workarounds. See #7804 for prior workaround, plus this was a real constraint #12995 where we wouldn't be able to support a string-based provider reference because of this.
- Providers must inspect the runtime type of `data` (string vs URL vs Uint8Array) to determine intent, rather than matching on a discriminated `type` field.

### Proposal

- Split `FilePart` into multiple discriminated types, mirroring what `ToolResultOutput` already does.
- Maintain the current types (e.g. `"file"`) as deprecated parts of the union, which can be auto-mapped to the new discriminated types.
- In the provider spec, we can make this change potentially without maintaining that back compat layer, because it has much lower exposure on the ecosystem, and helps keep the spec simple.

Note: This affects both `packages/provider-utils/src/types/content-part.ts` and `packages/ai/src/prompt/content-part.ts`.

**Aside:** we should also consider getting rid of the `file` vs `image` distinction, because an image is simply a file with a specific media type. That's a separate change though, potentially to implement before this one.

title: Resume of partial static tool calls crashes in createStreamingUIMessageState
body:
### Description

There appears to be a bug in the UI resume path for in-progress static tool calls.

When `useChat` / `Chat.resumeStream()` resumes from a partially-hydrated assistant message that already contains a static tool part in `input-streaming` state, AI SDK crashes while rebuilding the streaming state.

The error we see is:

```txt
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')
    at getStaticToolName (.../ui-messages.ts)
    at createStreamingUIMessageState (.../process-ui-message-stream.ts)
```

The problematic code in `process-ui-message-stream.ts` is in `createStreamingUIMessageState(...)`:

```ts
toolName:
  part.type === 'dynamic-tool'
    ? String((typedPart.toolName as string | undefined) ?? '')
    : getStaticToolName(part.type),
```

`getStaticToolName` expects the full tool part, not `part.type`. Passing `part.type` causes the function to do `part.type.split(...)` on a string argument, which becomes `undefined.split(...)` internally.

Changing that line to this fixes the issue for us:

```ts
: getStaticToolName(part),
```

### Why this happens

This only seems to happen on resume/hydration flows, because `createStreamingUIMessageState` is rebuilding `partialToolCalls` from an existing last assistant message that already contains an unfinished tool part.

In our case the last assistant message contained a static tool call with:

- `type: "tool-create_document"`
- `state: "input-streaming"`
- `toolCallId: "..."`
- partial `rawInput`

A fresh stream does not hit this path in the same way, but resume does.

### Minimal Repro

1. Start a streaming response that begins a static tool call.
2. Let the message contain a tool part in `input-streaming` state.
3. Persist/hydrate that partial assistant message.
4. Call `resumeStream()` / resume the UI message stream.
5. `createStreamingUIMessageState` crashes before the resumed chunks can be processed.

### Expected behavior

The SDK should successfully reconstruct partial static tool calls during resume.

### Actual behavior

Resume fails with:

```txt
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')
```

### AI SDK Version

- `ai`: `6.0.142`
- also reproducible in both frontend and backend code paths that use the same UI resume state builder

### Additional context

This seems related to the broader class of resume-state reconstruction bugs, for example #13160, but this issue is specifically about partial static tool call reconstruction.

title: convertToModelMessages sends images as FilePart instead of ImagePart — providers that support vision but not file parts can't see images
body:
### 📝 Description

**The Issue** When using `useChat`, uploaded images are sent as `FileUIPart`:
* **Type:** `"file"`
* **MediaType:** `"image/png"`
* **URL:** `"https://..."`

This is the only option available in `UIMessage.parts` — there is no `type: "image"`.

**The Conversion Problem** `convertToModelMessages` converts these to `FilePart` (type: `"file"`) in the `ModelMessage`, even when the `mediaType` is `image/*`. Many vision-capable models/providers **do not support file parts**, as documented:

> Only a few providers and models currently support file parts: Google Generative AI, Google Vertex AI, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenAI (for pdf).

**The Impact** Models like **Xiaomi MiMo**, **GLM-5** (via AI Gateway), and others accessed through **OpenRouter** support vision, but they don't support file parts. When they receive the image as `type: "file"`, they simply don't recognize it.

---

### 🔄 Current Behavior

| Layer | Structure |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Client (`useChat`)** | `{ type: "file", mediaType: "image/png", url: "https://..." }` |
| **Server (`ModelMessage`)** | `{ type: "file", mediaType: "image/png", data: "https://..." }` |

**Result:** Vision-capable models that don't support file parts ignore the image entirely — they respond as if no image was sent.

---

### 🛠 Technical Details

* **AI SDK Version:** `ai` version 6.x
* **Affected:** Any vision-capable model/provider accessed via AI Gateway or OpenRouter that doesn't support file parts (e.g. Xiaomi MiMo, GLM-5, DeepSeek, etc.)

---

title: AI SDK drops "" reasoning blocks but these MUST be included for validation
body:
### Description

We've noticed intermittent errors of type `Bedrock API Error: The model cannot modify thinking or redacted_thinking blocks in assistant messages. These blocks must remain as they were in the original response.` 

I thought that the change in https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/13972 would fix this but am still getting this error upon upgrading to `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock": "^4.0.86`

This causes the indices of the messages to be screwed up:

 The original Bedrock response had 5 content blocks:
  [0] reasoningContent  (thinking)

  [2] reasoningContent  (thinking)
  [3] text

  [0] reasoningContent  (thinking)   ← matches original [0] ✓

  [2] text
  [3] toolUse
```

title: AI Gateway BYOK Bedrock routing fails with empty region in endpoint URL
body:
### Description

When using the AI Gateway with BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) AWS credentials configured for Bedrock, every request to an Anthropic model fails at the Bedrock provider attempt because the constructed endpoint URL contains an **empty region segment**.

**Actual endpoint:** `bedrock-runtime..amazonaws.com` (note the double dot — region is empty)
**Expected endpoint:** `bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com`

The gateway silently falls back to the Anthropic direct API using system credentials, so the request eventually succeeds — but BYOK Bedrock is never actually used.

#### Reproduction

```ts
import { createGateway } from "@ai-sdk/gateway"
import { generateText } from "ai"

const gateway = createGateway({
  baseURL: "https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/ai",
  apiKey: "<your-gateway-api-key>"
})

const { text, providerMetadata } = await generateText({
  model: gateway("anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"),
  prompt: "Say hello",

console.log(JSON.stringify(providerMetadata.gateway.routing, null, 2))

System credentials planned for: anthropic, vertexAnthropic, bedrock. Total execution order: bedrock(BYOK) → anthropic(system) → vertexAnthropic(system) → bedrock(system)",

The same behavior is consistently reproducible across all Anthropic models (`claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-haiku-4.5`, `claude-sonnet-4.5`). Tested multiple times — Bedrock BYOK always fails with the same DNS error, then falls back to Anthropic direct.

- **Every Anthropic model request** incurs an unnecessary failed Bedrock attempt before falling back, adding extra latency per request.
- BYOK Bedrock credentials are effectively unusable — all traffic goes through Anthropic direct API with system credentials.
- Users cannot leverage their own AWS Bedrock pricing/quotas as intended.

title: openai-compatible docs say providerOptions use camelCase, but chat/completion still require the raw provider name
body:
## Summary

The [OpenAI Compatible Providers docs](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/openai-compatible-providers#chat-model-options) say:

> Note that the providerOptions key will be in camelCase. If you set the provider name to provider-name, the options still need to be set on providerOptions.providerName.

However, in the currently published `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` implementation, chat/completion appear to look up provider options by the raw provider name prefix, not a camelCased version of it.

## Why this seems inconsistent

`createOpenAICompatible({ name })` stores the raw provider name.

For chat/completion, the lookup path appears to be:
- provider name is derived from `config.provider.split('.')[0]`
- `parseProviderOptions(...)` then checks `providerOptions?.[provider]` exactly

Relevant source files in the published package:
- `src/chat/openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts`
- `src/completion/openai-compatible-completion-language-model.ts`
- `@ai-sdk/provider-utils/src/parse-provider-options.ts`

In contrast, the image model explicitly merges both the raw key and `toCamelCase(...)`, which suggests the current chat/completion behavior is not doing the same fallback.

## Repro

```ts
const provider = createOpenAICompatible({
  name: "provider-name",
  baseURL: "https://api.example.com/v1",
  apiKey: "dummy",
});

await generateText({
  model: provider.chatModel("model-id"),
  prompt: "hello",
  providerOptions: {
    providerName: {
      reasoningEffort: "low",
    },
  },
});
```

Expected from docs: `providerOptions.providerName` should be honored.

Observed from current published code: chat/completion appear to require `providerOptions["provider-name"]` instead.

## Request

Could you clarify which behavior is intended?

Either:
1. update chat/completion to honor the documented camelCase key behavior, or
2. update the docs if the current exact raw-name lookup is the intended contract.

Thanks!

title: @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock: explicit accessKeyId/secretAccessKey should not merge AWS_SESSION_TOKEN from env
body:
### Package

`@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` — `createAmazonBedrock`

### Problem

When passing explicit `accessKeyId` and `secretAccessKey`, SigV4 credential resolution still uses `loadOptionalSetting` for `sessionToken`, which falls back to **`process.env.AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`**.

On hosts that always set that variable (e.g. **EKS IRSA**, ECS task role, Lambda), the environment holds a **session token for the workload identity**, not for the IAM user key pair passed in options. The merged credentials are invalid and AWS returns **"The security token included in the request is invalid."**

Locally this often goes unnoticed because `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` is unset.

### Expected behavior

If both `accessKeyId` and `secretAccessKey` are **explicitly** provided as options, treat that as static IAM user (or otherwise complete) credentials: **do not** implicitly attach `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` from the environment unless the caller opts in (e.g. explicit `sessionToken` option or a documented flag).

Alternatively, document prominently that BYOK / static-key call sites **must** use `credentialProvider` returning only `{ accessKeyId, secretAccessKey }` when the process may define `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`.

### Workaround (callers)

Use `credentialProvider: () => Promise.resolve({ accessKeyId, secretAccessKey })` instead of passing keys directly, so the env session token path is not used.

### Reference

Related downstream report: https://github.com/8monkey-ai/hebo-platform/issues/351

title: Branded message id not allowed
body:
### Description

We use branded ids for all primary/foreign keys. Same for the `message` table where we store the messages.

We use the `useChat` hook as follows:

```ts
import type { UIDataTypes, UIMessage } from "ai"
import { z } from "zod"
import { useChat } from "@ai-sdk/react"

const SomeMessageMetadata = z
  .object({
    // ...
  })
  .nullish()

const someDataSchemas = {} satisfies UIDataTypes

type SomeUIMessage = UIMessage<
  z.infer<typeof SomeMessageMetadata>,
  typeof someDataSchemas
>

const useSomeChat = () =>
  useChat<SomeUIMessage>({
    dataPartSchemas: someDataSchemas,
    messageMetadataSchema: SomeMessageMetadata,
    // ...
  })
```

This works. However, if we want to use branded message ids by substituting `UIMessage` as follows:

```ts
import type { UIDataTypes, UIMessage as AiUIMessage, UITools } from "ai"

import type { Message } from "#src/db/schema.ts"

export type UIMessage<
  METADATA = unknown,
  DATA_PARTS extends UIDataTypes = UIDataTypes,
  TOOLS extends UITools = UITools,
> = AiUIMessage<METADATA, DATA_PARTS, TOOLS> & {
  id: Message["id"] // the branded message id
}
```

then we get a type error for `messageMetadataSchema` above. The type error can be resolved by removing `.nullish()` on the schema. This fix has nothing to do with the brand, so it feels like an oversight in how this hook is typed (albeit an edge case).

title: AI Gateway: Google Gemini 3 Flash returns 503 with no automatic fallback
body:
## Description

When using the Vercel AI Gateway with `google/gemini-3-flash`, the Gateway intermittently returns `503 Service Temporarily Unavailable`. The response metadata shows `"fallbacksAvailable": []` — even though the AI SDK supports `providerOptions.gateway.models` for fallback configuration, many developers may not be aware of this feature and experience complete failures during provider outages.

## Expected Behavior

When a provider returns a 503 (transient/retryable error), ideally the Gateway should:
1. Retry the same provider at least once (the response includes `"isRetryable": true`)
2. Or clearly surface in documentation/examples that fallback models should be configured for production use

## Current Behavior

The Gateway makes a single attempt to the resolved provider. If it fails, the error is returned immediately with no retry, even when the error is marked as retryable.

## Gateway Routing Metadata (from error response)

```json
{
  "originalModelId": "google/gemini-3-flash",
  "resolvedProvider": "google",
  "resolvedProviderApiModelId": "gemini-3-flash-preview",
  "fallbacksAvailable": [],
  "modelAttemptCount": 1,
  "totalProviderAttemptCount": 1,
  "isRetryable": true
}
```

Key observations:
- `modelAttemptCount: 1` — only one attempt was made
- `isRetryable: true` — the error was transient/retryable, but no retry happened
- `fallbacksAvailable: []` — no fallback chain configured

## Reproduction

Intermittent — depends on Google API capacity. More likely during peak hours or with preview models.

```typescript
import { streamText } from 'ai';
import { createGateway } from '@ai-sdk/gateway';

const gateway = createGateway();

// This fails with 503 when Google has capacity issues
const result = await streamText({
  model: gateway.languageModel('google/gemini-3-flash'),
  prompt: 'Hello',
});
```

## Questions

1. **Is there a way to configure automatic retries at the Gateway level** (without adding fallback models)? The `isRetryable: true` flag suggests the Gateway knows the error is transient, but it doesn't retry.

2. **Should `providerOptions.gateway.models` be more prominently documented** as a production best practice? The [Model Fallbacks docs](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/model-fallbacks) exist but are easy to miss.

3. **Is there a plan to add automatic retry for retryable errors** (503, 429) at the Gateway level before falling through to fallback models?

## Environment

- `@ai-sdk/gateway`: latest
- `ai`: v6.x
- Model: `google/gemini-3-flash` (resolves to `gemini-3-flash-preview`)
- Region: EU (fra1)

title: `ToolLoopAgent.prepareStep` activeTools changes bust provider prompt cache
body:
### Description

When using `ToolLoopAgent` with `prepareStep` to dynamically change `activeTools` between steps, it invalidates the provider's prompt cache (tested with Anthropic Claude via OpenRouter). This makes dynamic tool activation via `prepareStep` significantly more expensive than expected.

The `prepareStep` callback is the intended mechanism for dynamic tool activation, but the current implementation reconstructs the tool list in each API request, which invalidates prompt caching on providers that cache based on request structure.

## Expected Behavior

Changing `activeTools` in `prepareStep` should preserve prompt caching where possible. Providers like Anthropic support `cache_control` breakpoints that allow caching portions of the request independently. The SDK could:

1. Use strategic `cache_control` placement so system prompt and messages remain cached even when the tool list changes
2. Keep all tools in the request but use provider-specific mechanisms to mark tools as unavailable (preserving cache structure)
3. At minimum, document this cost implication so users can make informed architectural decisions

## Actual Behavior

Each time `prepareStep` returns a different `activeTools` array, the entire prompt cache is invalidated because the tool definition list in the API request changes. This happens even though the system prompt and message history are identical.

## Reproduction

```typescript
import { ToolLoopAgent } from "ai";

const agent = new ToolLoopAgent({
  model: anthropic("claude-sonnet-4-6"),
  instructions: "You are a helpful assistant.",
  tools: allTools, // Large tool set
  activeTools: ["tool_a", "tool_b"], // Initial subset
  prepareStep: async ({ messages }) => {
    // Dynamically determine which tools should be active based on conversation
    // e.g., a "tools_search" tool that activates other tools
    const activeTools = computeActiveToolsFromMessages(messages);
    return { messages, activeTools };
  },
});

const result = await agent.stream({ messages });
```

When `prepareStep` returns `activeTools: ["tool_a", "tool_b", "tool_c"]` (adding `tool_c`), the next API call has a different tool list, busting the cache.

## Use Case

We implement a tool deferral system where:

1. Agent starts with a small set of "discovery" tools (e.g., `tools_search`)
2. User asks to perform an action ("search reddit")
3. Agent calls `tools_search` which returns relevant tools to activate
4. `prepareStep` reads tool call results and activates the returned tools
5. Agent can now use the newly activated tools

This pattern keeps the initial tool list small (better for model focus and cost), but the cache busting on tool activation negates much of the cost benefit.

## Related Issues

- [#9743](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/9743) - prepareStep should allow updating tools (implemented, but with this cache side effect)
- [#7787](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/7787) - Dynamic tool support for Agent Swarm architecture
- [#8653](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/8653) - activeTools filtering allows execution of tool calls not in active tools list
- [#10482](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/10482) - add experimental_context parameter to prepareStep callback

### AI SDK Version

Node.js: 25.x

title: Use process.emitWarning() for deprecation warnings
body:
### Problem

Runtime deprecation warnings currently use `console.warn`. This output is easy to miss and not machine-actionable. `@deprecated` JSDoc tags are IDE-only — they don't alert at runtime.

### Proposal

Replace `console.warn`-based deprecation warnings with Node.js [`process.emitWarning()`](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v20.x/api/process.html#processemitwarningwarning-type-code-ctor) using `type: 'DeprecationWarning'` and unique codes.

This is **not** a replacement for `@deprecated` JSDoc tags — those stay for IDE support. This replaces `console.warn` as the runtime mechanism.

```ts
process.emitWarning(
  'generateImage is deprecated. Use generateImage from ai instead.',
  { type: 'DeprecationWarning', code: 'AISDK_DEP001' }
);
```

### Why

- Node.js prints each deprecation code **once** by default — no log spam
- Users can run tests with `--throw-deprecation` to surface all deprecated usage before a major upgrade
- `--no-deprecation` silences them entirely
- Follows Node.js ecosystem conventions (Express, Node core, etc.)

### Implementation ideas

- Add a helper in `packages/ai/src/logger/` that wraps `process.emitWarning` with SDK-specific codes
- Call it at runtime when deprecated functions/options are used
- Maintain a registry of deprecation codes (e.g. `deprecations.ts`) for discoverability
- Could start with a few high-value deprecations (e.g. `experimental_` prefixed APIs being replaced) and expand

### Scope considerations

- Browser/edge runtimes don't have `process.emitWarning` — guard with `typeof process !== 'undefined'` or limit to the warning logger path

title: AI Gateway: Vertex rejects thought signatures from Google AI Studio on mid-conversation failover
body:
### Description

When using the AI Gateway with `order: ['google', 'vertex']`, mid-conversation provider failover causes Vertex to reject the request with 400: "Unable to submit request because Thought signature is not valid."

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use `google/gemini-3-flash` with `order: ['google', 'vertex']` in providerOptions
2. Run a multi-step agent session (10+ tool call steps using streamText with tools)
3. Wait for Google AI Studio to return 503 (intermittent capacity issue on preview models)
4. Gateway automatically fails over to Vertex for the next step
5. Vertex rejects with 400: "Thought signature is not valid"

### What happens

Steps 1-10 run fine on Google AI Studio. Each step generates tool calls with thought signatures. On step 11, Google returns 503. The Gateway tries Vertex as the next provider in the order. Vertex receives the full conversation history including thought signatures generated by Google AI Studio, and rejects them as invalid.

### Error from Gateway routing metadata

```json
{
  "modelAttemptCount": 1,
  "providerAttempts": [
    { "provider": "google", "statusCode": 503, "error": "Service temporarily unavailable" },
    { "provider": "vertex", "statusCode": 400, "error": "Unable to submit request because Thought signature is not valid." }
  ]
}
```

The full URL Vertex tried to hit: 

```
https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/141030677902/locations/global/publishers/google/models/gemini-3-flash-preview:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse
```

### Workaround

Using \`only: ['google']\` prevents the failover and avoids the error. But this means we lose Vertex as a fallback when Google has capacity issues (503s), which happen regularly with preview models.

We also added \`models: ['moonshotai/kimi-k2.5']\` as a model-level fallback so when Google 503s, it falls back to a completely different model instead of trying Vertex with incompatible signatures.

### Environment

- ai: 6.0.141
- @ai-sdk/gateway: 3.0.83
- @ai-sdk/google: 3.0.53 (transitive)
- Model: google/gemini-3-flash (resolves to gemini-3-flash-preview)
- Using Vercel AI Gateway with OIDC auth on Vercel deployment

### Related issues

- #11413 - Original thought_signature issue, fixed namespace lookup via PR #13060
- #13908 - Parallel tool call signature propagation (open, separate but related)
- #13055 - Turn ordering error on Gateway failover (open, similar failover scenario)
- #14148 - Our earlier report about Google 503s with no fallback

title: AI Gateway breaks SDK retry: GatewayInternalServerError not recognized by maxRetries
body:
### Description

The AI Gateway's error handling converts retryable `APICallError` instances into `GatewayInternalServerError` instances before they reach the SDK's retry logic. Since the retry function checks `APICallError.isInstance(error)`, Gateway errors are never retried regardless of the `maxRetries` setting.

### Proof

Ran this in Node.js with the installed packages:

```javascript
const gateway = require('@ai-sdk/gateway/dist/index.js');

const gErr = new gateway.GatewayInternalServerError({ message: 'test', statusCode: 503 });
const apiCallMarker = Symbol.for('vercel.ai.error.AI_APICallError');

console.log('Has APICallError marker:', apiCallMarker in gErr);  // false
console.log('isRetryable:', gErr.isRetryable);                    // undefined
console.log('statusCode:', gErr.statusCode);                      // 503
```

The error has the Gateway marker (`vercel.ai.gateway.error`) but NOT the APICallError marker (`vercel.ai.error.AI_APICallError`), so `maxRetries` never activates.

### Root cause

In `@ai-sdk/gateway`, the `doStream()` and `doGenerate()` methods catch errors and convert them:

```javascript
// @ai-sdk/gateway/dist/index.js, line ~875
} catch (error) {
  throw await asGatewayError(error, ...);
}
```

`asGatewayError()` (line ~433) takes a retryable `APICallError` (statusCode 503, isRetryable: true) and converts it to a `GatewayInternalServerError` which extends `GatewayError` (NOT `APICallError`).

The SDK's retry function at `ai/dist/internal/index.mjs:1207` then fails:

```javascript
if (error instanceof Error 
    && APICallError.isInstance(error)      // FALSE for GatewayError
    && error.isRetryable === true          // undefined for GatewayError
    && tryNumber <= maxRetries) {
  // This NEVER executes for Gateway errors
}
```

### Impact

Any application using `@ai-sdk/gateway` with `maxRetries > 0` gets zero retries on transient errors (503, 429). The setting is silently ignored. This affects `streamText`, `generateText`, `generateObject`, and `streamObject`.

Applications using provider SDKs directly (`@ai-sdk/google`, `@ai-sdk/openai`) are not affected because their errors pass through as `APICallError`.

### Expected behavior

Gateway errors with retryable status codes (503, 429, 408) should be retried according to `maxRetries`.

### Possible fixes

1. Make `GatewayError` extend `APICallError` (or carry the marker)
2. Make `GatewayError` set `isRetryable` based on status code
3. Update the retry function to also check `GatewayError.isInstance()`
4. Don't convert retryable `APICallError` to `GatewayError` in the catch block

### Environment

- ai: 6.0.141
- @ai-sdk/gateway: 3.0.83
author: shtefcs

title: Feature: Support Gemma 4 thinking format in `extractReasoningMiddleware`
body:
## Summary

`extractReasoningMiddleware` cannot handle the reasoning token format used by Gemma 4 (available on Google Vertex AI). Gemma 4 uses asymmetric, non-XML tokens for its thinking output, which the current `tagName`-based API cannot express.

## Background

Gemma 4 thinking format (from [Vertex AI Model Garden](https://console.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/publishers/google/model-garden/gemma4)):

- **Thinking is triggered** by including `<|think|>` at the start of the system prompt.
- **Model output structure** when thinking is enabled:
  ```
  <|channel>thought
  [internal reasoning content]<channel|>[final answer]
  ```
- **Opening token**: `<|channel>thought\n` (literal string, includes a newline)
- **Closing token**: `<channel|>`
- **Empty block** (thinking disabled but model still emits tags):
  ```
  <|channel>thought
  <channel|>[final answer]
  ```

## Problem

The current API only accepts a single `tagName` string and constructs symmetric `<tagName>`/`</tagName>` markers:

```ts
// packages/ai/src/middleware/extract-reasoning-middleware.ts:25-26
const openingTag = `<${tagName}>`;
const closingTag = `<\/${tagName}>`;
```

Gemma 4's opening token (`<|channel>thought\n`) and closing token (`<channel|>`) are:
1. **Asymmetric** — opening and closing have completely different shapes.
2. **Not XML-compatible** — `|` and `>` placement doesn't match `<tag>`/`</tag>`.
3. **Include a newline** in the opening token, which may affect streaming buffer logic.

There is no way to configure this today without forking the middleware.

## Proposed Fix

Allow `tagName` to accept either a plain string (existing behaviour) or an object with `opening` and `closing` properties:

```ts
// existing usage (unchanged):
extractReasoningMiddleware({ tagName: 'think' })

// new usage for Gemma 4:
extractReasoningMiddleware({
  tagName: { opening: '<|channel>thought\n', closing: '<channel|>' },
})
```

The internal resolution becomes:

```ts
const openingTag =
  typeof tagName === 'string' ? `<${tagName}>` : tagName.opening;
const closingTag =
  typeof tagName === 'string' ? `<\/${tagName}>` : tagName.closing;
```

Special regex characters in the delimiter strings (e.g. `|`) must be escaped before use in `wrapGenerate`'s `new RegExp(...)` call. The `wrapStream` path uses `indexOf`-based matching and requires no changes.

## Multi-turn note

Gemma's docs state that **thoughts must not appear in conversation history** — only the final answer should be kept between turns. This matches the existing middleware behavior (reasoning is stripped from the text part), so no additional work is needed for multi-turn handling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tagName` accepts `string | { opening: string; closing: string }`.
- [ ] Passing `tagName: { opening: '<|channel>thought\n', closing: '<channel|>' }` correctly extracts Gemma 4 reasoning in both `generateText` and `streamText`.
- [ ] Existing `tagName: string` usage is fully backward-compatible (no breaking change).
- [ ] Unit tests cover the Gemma 4 token format (including the empty-block case when thinking is disabled but tags are still emitted).
- [ ] Changeset added (patch).
- [ ] A `examples/ai-functions/src/stream-text/google-vertex/gemma4-reasoning.ts` example is added.

## Affected file

- `packages/ai/src/middleware/extract-reasoning-middleware.ts`

| Term | Definition | Aliases to avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **AI Function** | A user-facing function that orchestrates a model call (e.g., `generateText`, `streamText`) | Helper, wrapper, utility |
| **Provider Model Api Client** | ... | ... |
| **Model** | ... | ... |
| **Model ID** | A provider-specific string identifying a particular model variant (e.g., `"gpt-4o"`, `"claude-3-opus"`) | Model name, model identifier |
| **Model Specification** | An interface that defines the contract a provider must implement for a given model type (e.g., `LanguageModelV4`) | Model interface, model API, model contract |
| **Provider** | A package that implements one or more model specifications for a specific AI service (e.g., `@ai-sdk/openai`) | Adapter, connector, integration, client |
| **Provider Options** | An opaque key-value object passed through to a specific provider without SDK interpretation | Provider metadata, provider config, extra options |

## Prompts & Messages

| Term | Definition | Aliases to avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Prompt** | The complete input to an AI function, combining an optional system message with either a `prompt` string or a `messages` array | Input, request, query |
| **Message** | A discrete unit of communication in a prompt, with a role and content | Turn, entry, chat message |
| **System Message** | A message that defines the model's behavior, personality, or role | System prompt, instructions |
| **User Message** | A message from the human user, which can contain text, images, or files | Human message, input message |
| **Assistant Message** | A message previously generated by the model, containing text, reasoning, tool calls, or tool results | AI message, bot message, model message |
| **Tool Message** | A message containing the result of a tool execution, sent back to the model | Function result message |
| **Content Part** | A typed segment within a message (text, image, file, tool call, tool result, reasoning) | Block, chunk, element |

## Tools

| Term | Definition | Aliases to avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Tool** | A function the model can invoke, defined with a description and input schema | Function, action, plugin, capability |
| **Tool Call** | An instance of the model requesting to invoke a tool, with a name, arguments, and unique ID | Function call, tool invocation, tool use |
| **Tool Call ID** | A unique identifier linking a tool call to its result | Call ID, invocation ID |
| **Tool Result** | The output returned after executing a tool call, sent back to the model | Function result, tool output, tool response |
| **Tool Choice** | Configuration controlling how the model selects tools: `auto`, `none`, `required`, or a specific tool name | Function calling mode |
| **Dynamic Tool** | A tool defined at runtime rather than declared upfront (e.g., MCP tools) | Runtime tool |
| **Provider-Executed Tool** | A tool that the provider executes on its server rather than returning the call to the client | Server-side tool, remote tool |

## Structured Output

| Term | Definition | Aliases to avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Schema** | A formal specification of expected data structure that constrains model output (can be JSON Schema, Zod, or Standard Schema) | Type, shape, format, template |
| **Output** | Configuration for how to parse the model's response: text (default), object, array, or enum | Response format, return type |
| **Strict Mode** | A tool or schema setting that forces the model to strictly adhere to the schema, potentially limiting supported schema features | Exact mode, validated mode |

## Streaming

| Term | Definition | Aliases to avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Stream** | An incremental sequence of typed chunks emitted as the model generates output | Feed, subscription, channel |
| **Stream Part** | A single typed event in a stream, discriminated by type (e.g., `text-delta`, `tool-call`, `finish`) | Chunk, event, frame, packet |
| **Delta** | An incremental text or tool-input fragment within a stream | Diff, partial, fragment |
| **Finish** | The terminal stream part signaling generation is complete, carrying usage and finish reason | Done, end, complete |

## Generation Flow

| Term | Definition | Aliases to avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Step** | A single model invocation within an agentic loop; a multi-step generation contains one step per round trip | Turn, iteration, round, cycle |
| **Finish Reason** | The reason a model stopped generating: `stop`, `length`, `content-filter`, `tool-calls`, `error`, or `other` | Stop reason, end reason, completion reason |
| **Context** | User-defined state that flows through generation steps (e.g., user info, tool execution state) | State, metadata, payload |
| **Call Warning** | A non-fatal issue during a model call (e.g., unsupported setting); the call still succeeds | Deprecation notice, soft error |

## Tokens & Usage

| Term | Definition | Aliases to avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Token** | The atomic unit of text that models consume (input) or produce (output) | Word, character, unit |
| **Usage** | Token accounting for a model call: input tokens, output tokens, and their breakdowns | Cost, consumption, metrics |
| **Input Tokens** | Tokens in the prompt/context sent to the model | Prompt tokens |
| **Output Tokens** | Tokens in the model's generated response | Completion tokens |
| **Reasoning Tokens** | Output tokens consumed by the model's extended reasoning process (e.g., o1/o3 models) | Thinking tokens |
| **Cached Tokens** | Input tokens served from a provider's cache, typically at reduced cost | Cache hits |

## Middleware

| Term | Definition | Aliases to avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Middleware** | A composable layer that intercepts and transforms model calls via `transformParams`, `wrapGenerate`, and `wrapStream` | Plugin, interceptor, hook, decorator |

## Reasoning

| Term | Definition | Aliases to avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Reasoning** | Explicit thinking text from models that shows the model's thought process before responding | Thinking, chain-of-thought, inner monologue |
| **Reasoning Effort** | A parameter controlling a model's reasoning depth: `provider-default`, `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` | Think level, reasoning budget |

## Relationships

- An **AI Function** uses exactly one **Model Specification** type
- A **Provider** implements one or more **Model Specifications**
- A **Prompt** contains an optional **System Message** and either a prompt string or an array of **Messages**
- A **Message** contains one or more **Content Parts**
- A **Tool Call** produces exactly one **Tool Result**
- A **Step** contains zero or more **Tool Calls** and ends with a **Finish Reason**
- **Middleware** wraps a **Language Model** to intercept `doGenerate` and `doStream` calls
- **Usage** is reported per **Step** and aggregated across all steps


## Ambiguities

- **"model"** is used to mean both the abstract specification interface (`LanguageModelV4`) and a concrete provider implementation (`OpenAIChatLanguageModel`). When precision matters, use **Model Specification** for the interface and **Provider** (or the specific class name) for the implementation.
- **"prompt"** can refer to both the complete input object (system + messages/text) and the simple `prompt` string parameter. Use **Prompt** for the complete input and "prompt string" or "text prompt" when referring to the single-string shorthand.
- **"output"** can mean the model's raw text response or the `output` configuration parameter (text/object/array/enum). Use **Output** for the configuration and "generated text" or "response" for what the model produces.
- **"context"** can mean the user-defined state passed through steps or the model's context window (token limit). Use **Context** for the user-defined state object and "context window" for the token limit.
- **"completion"** appears in token accounting ("completion tokens") but should be avoided — use **Output Tokens** instead. The SDK does not use "completion" as a generation concept.


</details>

title: @ai-sdk/anthropic: adapter produces orphaned tool_use without matching tool_result for output-error state tools
body:
## Description

The `@ai-sdk/anthropic` adapter (v3.0.67) produces Anthropic API payloads where `tool_use` blocks have no matching `tool_result` in the following message, causing the Anthropic API to reject the request with:

```
messages.57: `tool_use` ids were found without `tool_result` blocks immediately after: toolu_01R4gLPydCvYg7gc5G9rCkKp
```

## Root Cause

The issue occurs when an assistant message contains a tool call in `output-error` state (a tool that was invoked but failed/was interrupted). The `convertToModelMessages` function correctly produces both `tool-call` and `tool-result` parts at the ModelMessage level — verified with 0 orphaned tool-calls across 63 model messages. However, the `@ai-sdk/anthropic` adapter's internal conversion from LanguageModelPrompt to the Anthropic API JSON format drops or misplaces the `tool_result` for the errored tool.

## Reproduction

The failing message has this structure at the ModelMessage level:
- **Assistant message**: `[text, tool-call(output-error, id=A), text, tool-call(output-available, id=B)]`
- **Tool message**: `[tool-result(id=A, error-text), tool-result(id=B, text)]`

Both tool-calls have matching tool-results. After the adapter converts this to Anthropic API format, the API reports that `tool_use` id=A has no matching `tool_result`.

The error tool part data:
```json
{
  "type": "tool",
  "callID": "toolu_01R4gLPydCvYg7gc5G9rCkKp",
  "tool": "edit",
  "state": {
    "status": "error",
    "input": {},
    "error": "Tool execution aborted",
    "time": { "start": 1775707868534, "end": 1775707868534 }
  }
}
```

This produces `output-error` state with `errorText: "Tool execution aborted"` and `input: {}` (empty object). The `createToolModelOutput` correctly returns `{ type: "error-text", value: "Tool execution aborted" }`.

## Key diagnostic evidence

1. `convertToModelMessages` produces 63 ModelMessages with **0 orphaned tool-calls** (verified by collecting all `tool-result` toolCallIds and checking every `tool-call` has a match)
2. `ProviderTransform.message()` (OpenCode's normalization layer) preserves all 28 tool messages — none removed
3. The Anthropic API consistently rejects at `messages.57` with the same orphaned tool_use id
4. The error reproduces on every retry because the conversation history is rebuilt identically from the database

## Session-poisoning effect

Once this error occurs, the session is permanently stuck:
1. Every turn rebuilds the same message history from the database
2. The adapter produces the same broken API payload
3. The API rejects with 400 (not retryable)
4. The error is set on the NEW assistant message, not the historical one
5. The historical message has no error flag, so it's never skipped

This is a widespread issue — see also [anthropics/claude-code#6836](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/6836).

## Environment

- `ai`: 5.0.124
- `@ai-sdk/anthropic`: 3.0.67
- API endpoint: Azure Anthropic (delphos-general-github-foundry.services.ai.azure.com)
- Model: claude-opus-4-6

title: feat(@ai-sdk/anthropic): support advisor tool (advisor_20260301)
body:
### Description

Anthropic released the [advisor tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/docs/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool) (`advisor_20260301`), a new server-side tool type that lets a cheaper executor model (Sonnet/Haiku) consult a more capable advisor model (Opus) mid-generation — all within a single `/v1/messages` request. No orchestration code needed.

This is similar in shape to the existing `computer_20250124`, `bash_20250124`, and `text_editor_20250124` provider tools already supported by `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, and should follow the same pattern in `anthropic-prepare-tools.ts`.

## API shape

The advisor is added to the `tools` array with a dedicated type:

```json
{
  "type": "advisor_20260301",
  "name": "advisor",
  "model": "claude-opus-4-6",
  "max_uses": 3,
  "caching": { "type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "5m" }
}
```

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | _required_ | Must be `"advisor_20260301"` |
| `name` | string | _required_ | Must be `"advisor"` |
| `model` | string | _required_ | Advisor model ID (e.g. `"claude-opus-4-6"`) |
| `max_uses` | integer | unlimited | Per-request cap on advisor calls |
| `caching` | object \| null | `null` | Prompt caching for the advisor's transcript: `{"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "5m" \| "1h"}` |

**Beta header required:** `advisor-tool-2026-03-01`

## Response content blocks

The advisor introduces two new content block types in the assistant response:

1. **`server_tool_use`** with `name: "advisor"` and empty `input: {}` — signals the advisor call start.
2. **`advisor_tool_result`** — contains one of:
   - `{ type: "advisor_result", text: "..." }` — plaintext advice
   - `{ type: "advisor_redacted_result", encrypted_content: "..." }` — opaque blob (must be round-tripped verbatim)
   - `{ type: "advisor_tool_result_error", error_code: "max_uses_exceeded" | "overloaded" | ... }` — non-fatal error

These blocks must be preserved in message history on subsequent turns. If the advisor tool is removed from `tools`, all `advisor_tool_result` blocks must also be stripped from messages to avoid a `400 invalid_request_error`.

## Usage reporting

Advisor tokens are reported separately in `usage.iterations[]`:

```json
{
  "usage": {
    "input_tokens": 412,
    "output_tokens": 531,
    "iterations": [
      { "type": "message", "input_tokens": 412, "output_tokens": 89 },
      { "type": "advisor_message", "model": "claude-opus-4-6", "input_tokens": 823, "output_tokens": 1612 },
      { "type": "message", "input_tokens": 1348, "output_tokens": 442 }
    ]
  }
}
```

Top-level `usage` reflects executor tokens only. Advisor tokens are billed at the advisor model's rates.

## Streaming behavior

The advisor sub-inference does **not** stream. The executor's stream pauses while the advisor runs. The `advisor_tool_result` arrives fully formed in a single `content_block_start` event (no deltas). This is important for `streamText()` — the stream will pause but should not timeout.

## Proposed AI SDK integration

### Provider tool definition

Following the existing pattern for `anthropic.computer_20250124`:

```typescript
// Usage in streamText()
streamText({
  model: anthropic('claude-sonnet-4-6'),
  tools: {
    advisor: anthropic.tools.advisor({
      model: 'claude-opus-4-6',
      maxUses: 3,
      caching: { type: 'ephemeral', ttl: '5m' },
    }),
    // ... other tools
  },
});
```

Or alternatively via provider options (simpler, since the advisor has no user-defined schema):

```typescript
streamText({
  model: anthropic('claude-sonnet-4-6'),
  providerOptions: {
    anthropic: {
      advisor: {
        model: 'claude-opus-4-6',
        maxUses: 3,
      },
    },
  },
});
```

### Implementation scope

1. **`anthropic-prepare-tools.ts`**: Add `advisor_20260301` case alongside existing provider tool types. Add `advisor-tool-2026-03-01` to the betas set.
2. **Response parsing**: Handle `server_tool_use` (already exists for other server tools), `advisor_tool_result`, and `advisor_redacted_result` content blocks. Map them to appropriate AI SDK message parts so they round-trip correctly through `useChat` / message history.
3. **Usage mapping**: Expose `usage.iterations[]` so consumers can distinguish executor vs. advisor token costs. Currently `usage` only reports top-level tokens.
4. **Streaming**: Ensure `streamText()` tolerates the mid-stream pause without timing out. The `content_block_start` for `advisor_tool_result` should be handled like other non-streaming content blocks.

## Valid model pairs

| Executor | Advisor |
|---|---|
| `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | `claude-opus-4-6` |
| `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `claude-opus-4-6` |

## Benchmark context

- Sonnet + Opus advisor: **+2.7pp on SWE-bench Multilingual**, **-11.9% cost** vs Sonnet solo
- Haiku + Opus advisor on BrowseComp: **19.7% -> 41.2%** (>2x improvement)

## References

- [Advisor tool documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/docs/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool)
- [Blog post](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/the-advisor-strategy)
- [Server tools docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/server-tools)


### AI SDK Version

- ai: 6.0.91
- @ai-sdk/anthropic: 3.0.68

title: WorkflowAgent: provider-executed tool approvals are silently dropped on resume
body:
## Problem

When a provider-executed tool (e.g., MCP tool via Responses API) requires approval and the client approves/denies it, the WorkflowAgent's approval resume path silently drops the approval response instead of forwarding it to the provider.

### Root cause

In `packages/workflow/src/workflow-agent.ts` (lines ~1045-1141), `collectToolApprovalsFromMessages` collects all approval responses. For locally-executed tools this works correctly — the tool is executed and results are added. But for provider-executed tools:

1. The tool either isn't in `this.tools` or has no `execute` function, so the `if (tool && typeof tool.execute === 'function')` check at line 1067 fails silently
2. No tool result is created for the approval
3. Lines 1111-1131 strip **all** `tool-approval-request` and `tool-approval-response` parts from messages
4. The provider never receives the approval response → the tool never gets executed

This is the inverse of the bug fixed in #14289 (where approval responses were sent to the provider **twice**). Here they are sent **zero times**.

### Note

The agent loop already handles provider-executed tools correctly during normal execution (lines ~1406-1410, using `providerExecutedToolResults` from the stream). The gap is specifically in the approval resume path.

### Suggested fix

`collectToolApprovalsFromMessages` needs to distinguish provider-executed approvals from local ones by tracking the `providerExecuted` flag from the original `tool-call` part. For provider-executed approvals, keep both `tool-approval-request` and `tool-approval-response` in messages so the provider can process them. Only strip/replace approval parts for locally-executed tools.

title: Timeout configuration for generateText/streamText
body:
Tracking issue for the `timeout` setting in `generateText` and `streamText`.

The `timeout` option accepts either a number (milliseconds) or an object with granular controls:

- **`totalMs`** — Overall timeout for the entire call, encompassing all steps
- **`stepMs`** — Timeout for each individual step in multi-step generations
- **`chunkMs`** — (Streaming only) Timeout between stream chunks; aborts if no new chunk arrives within this duration
- **`toolMs`** — Default timeout for all tool executions; aborts and returns a tool-error on timeout
- **`tools`** — Per-tool timeout overrides via `{toolName}Ms` keys (e.g., `weatherMs`), taking precedence over `toolMs`

Docs: https://ai-sdk.dev/v7/docs/ai-sdk-core/settings#timeout

- [x] Add `toolMs` to timeout configuration (#13365)

title: Add Vequil as an observability provider — OpenTelemetry span exporter for the AI SDK
body:
## Request: list Vequil at ai-sdk.dev/providers/observability

[Vequil](https://vequil.com) is a reliability and observability layer for AI agent operators — detects anomalies (loops, retry storms, cost spikes), tracks spend by agent and tool, and generates shareable weekly report cards.

## Integration with the AI SDK

The `vequil` npm package ships a `VequilSpanExporter` — an OpenTelemetry `SpanExporter` that captures spans from the AI SDK's `experimental_telemetry` and forwards them to the Vequil workspace.

```ts
import { NodeTracerProvider } from '@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-node'
import { SimpleSpanProcessor } from '@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base'
import { VequilClient } from 'vequil'
import { VequilSpanExporter } from 'vequil/integrations/otel'
import { generateText } from 'ai'
import { openai } from '@ai-sdk/openai'

const vq = new VequilClient({ workspaceKey: 'vk_ws_...' })
const provider = new NodeTracerProvider()
provider.addSpanProcessor(new SimpleSpanProcessor(new VequilSpanExporter(vq)))
provider.register()

// All AI SDK calls are captured automatically
const { text } = await generateText({
  model: openai('gpt-4o'),
  prompt: 'Hello',
  experimental_telemetry: { isEnabled: true, functionId: 'my-agent' },
})
```

The exporter maps AI SDK span attributes (`ai.model.id`, `ai.usage.promptTokens`, `ai.telemetry.functionId`, etc.) to Vequil's event model and estimates cost from token counts.

## What gets captured

- Every `generateText`, `streamText`, `generateObject` call
- Model ID, token usage, duration
- Errors and chain failures
- Cost estimates by model and agent

## Install

```bash
npm install vequil
```

## Links

- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/vequil
- GitHub: https://github.com/nxd914/vequil
- OTel exporter source: https://github.com/nxd914/vequil/blob/main/sdk/js/src/integrations/otel.ts
- Quickstart: https://vequil.com/quickstart

Would love to be listed alongside Braintrust on the observability providers page. Happy to provide any additional info.

title: [Security] MCP transports use raw JSON.parse + mergeObjects prototype pollution
body:
## Summary
Two prototype pollution vectors:

### 1. MCP Transports Use Raw JSON.parse (Medium)
All MCP transport files use native `JSON.parse()` instead of the SDK's own `secureJsonParse()`. MCP transports parse data from external, untrusted MCP servers.
**Files:** `packages/mcp/src/tool/mcp-http-transport.ts`, `mcp-sse-transport.ts`, `mcp-stdio-transport.ts`, `oauth.ts`
**Fix:** Replace with `secureJsonParse()` already available in the codebase.

### 2. mergeObjects Missing Proto Filter (Medium-High)
`packages/ai/src/util/merge-objects.ts` deep merges without filtering `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype`. Called from `process-ui-message-stream.ts:334` where `messageMetadata` from SSE chunks is merged.
**Fix:** Filter dangerous keys in `mergeObjects()`.

## Impact
Crafted MCP server responses or SSE chunks could achieve prototype pollution.

title: @ai-sdk/google-vertex@4.0.106: unconditional streamFunctionCallArguments breaks all Vertex unary API calls
body:
### Description

All `@ai-sdk/google-vertex` `generateText` / `generateObject` calls (Vertex unary endpoint `generateContent`) return 400 after upgrading to 4.0.106:

```
Unable to submit request because streaming function call is not supported in unary API.
Learn more: https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/model-reference/gemini
```

Even without any tools, **all Vertex models** (gemini-2.5-flash-lite, gemini-3-flash-preview, etc.) fail 100%. The streaming endpoint (`streamGenerateContent`) is not affected.

### Root Cause

4.0.106 (released 2026-04-09, likely from #11126) unconditionally adds to the request body:

```json
{
  "toolConfig": {
    "functionCallingConfig": {
      "streamFunctionCallArguments": true
    }
  }
}
```

Two issues:
1. This parameter must **not** be sent to the unary endpoint (`generateContent`) — Vertex API rejects it
2. This parameter should **not** be sent when no tools/functionDeclarations are present

### Bisection

| Version | toolConfig in body | Result |
|---------|-------------------|--------|
| 4.0.105 | none | ✅ works |
| **4.0.106** | `{streamFunctionCallArguments: true}` | ❌ 400 |

### Code example

```typescript
import { createVertex } from "@ai-sdk/google-vertex";
import { generateText } from "ai";

const vertex = createVertex({ apiKey: process.env.GOOGLE_VERTEX_API_KEY });

// Works in 4.0.105, fails in 4.0.106
const { text } = await generateText({
  model: vertex("gemini-2.5-flash-lite"),
  prompt: "Say hello",
});
```

Fetch intercept confirms the difference:
- **4.0.105**: `{"generationConfig":{}, "contents":[...]}` — clean
- **4.0.106**: `{"generationConfig":{}, "contents":[...], "toolConfig":{"functionCallingConfig":{"streamFunctionCallArguments":true}}}` — breaks

### AI SDK Version

6.0.156

### AI SDK Provider + Version

@ai-sdk/google-vertex 4.0.106

### Other information

- **Runtime**: Bun 1.3.10 (also reproducible with Node.js)
- **Vertex API mode**: Express Mode (API Key auth)
- **Models affected**: all tested models (gemini-2.5-flash-lite, gemini-3-flash-preview, etc.)
- **Workaround**: pin to 4.0.105

### Suggested fix

`streamFunctionCallArguments` should:
1. Only be set for the streaming endpoint (`streamGenerateContent`), not unary (`generateContent`)
2. Only be set when tools/functionDeclarations are present
3. Or be opt-in rather than default-on

title: feat: Export `ToolCallState` type for developer usability
body:
### Description

Currently, the `state` property within `UIToolInvocation` and `DynamicToolUIPart` is typed using inline literal strings (e.g., `{ state: 'input-streaming'; ... }`). While this enables TypeScript's discriminated union narrowing, it creates a major usability gap for SDK consumers.

Because the union of these literal strings is not exported as a standalone named type, developers cannot cleanly reference the possible states in their own applications.

## Problem

Without an exported `ToolCallState` type, developers are forced into brittle or repetitive patterns when handling tool invocation states.

This impacts several common use cases:

1. **Typing Component Props**
   Cannot define props like `{ state: ToolCallState }`.

2. **Reusable Helper Functions**
   Cannot safely group or abstract logic (e.g., `isTerminalState(state)`).

3. **Handler / Mutation Types**
   Difficult to define shared handler signatures like:

   ```ts
   type MutationHandler = (state: ToolCallState) => void;
   ```

## Proposed Solution

Export a named string union type:

```ts
export type ToolCallState =
  | 'input-streaming'
  | 'input-available'
  | 'output-streaming'
  | 'output-available'
  | 'error'
  | 'canceled'
  | 'unknown';
```

Then reuse this type across `UIToolInvocation` and `DynamicToolUIPart` instead of inline literals.

## Benefits

* Improves developer experience significantly
* Enables type-safe abstractions and reusable components
* Eliminates duplication of string literals in userland
* Maintains full backward compatibility

## Additional Context

A PR has already been opened implementing this change:
👉 [https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/13443](https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/13443)

The PR:

* Extracts and exports `ToolCallState`
* Re-exports it from the main `ai` package
* Adds type tests to ensure correctness
* Updates documentation
* Preserves existing discriminated union behavior

## Impact

This is a **non-breaking enhancement** that improves SDK ergonomics without affecting existing functionality.

---

Would love feedback on whether this aligns with the project's direction. Happy to iterate if needed 🙌

When using Anthropic structured outputs via Vercel AI SDK, valid Zod schemas can cause 400 errors because unsupported JSON Schema keywords (e.g. `exclusiveMinimum`) are passed through without sanitization.

- convert Zod / JSON Schema into an Anthropic-compatible format

const schema = z.object({

title: AI Gateway silently ignores mask parameter for OpenAI inpainting (gpt-image-1)
body:
### Description

When using `generateImage()` with `@ai-sdk/gateway` and providing a `mask` parameter for OpenAI inpainting (`gpt-image-1`), the Gateway **silently ignores the mask** and generates a completely new image instead of editing only the masked region.

The same image + mask + prompt sent directly to OpenAI's `/v1/images/edits` endpoint produces correct inpainting — only the masked area is regenerated while unmasked areas are preserved.

### Reproduction

```ts
import { gateway } from '@ai-sdk/gateway';
import { generateImage } from 'ai';

const result = await generateImage({
  model: gateway.imageModel('openai/gpt-image-1'),
  prompt: {
    text: 'Premium food photography of a gourmet burger...',
    images: [sourceImageUint8Array],
    mask: maskUint8Array, // RGBA PNG, transparent=edit, opaque=preserve
  },
  size: '1024x1536',
  providerOptions: {
    openai: { quality: 'high' },
  },
});
```

### Evidence

**Setup:**
- Source image: 1024×1536 PNG photo of a burger with a branded flag on top
- Mask: 1024×1536 RGBA PNG, ~15.7% transparent (ellipse over the burger area), rest opaque (preserve flag, fries, background)

**Via Gateway** — mask completely ignored, entire image regenerated from scratch:
- The flag, fries, background, composition — everything is different
- No warnings or errors returned

**Via direct OpenAI API** — mask correctly applied:
```ts
const formData = new FormData();
formData.append('model', 'gpt-image-1');
formData.append('image', imageFile);
formData.append('mask', maskFile);
formData.append('prompt', prompt);
formData.append('size', '1024x1536');
formData.append('quality', 'high');

await fetch('https://api.openai.com/v1/images/edits', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}` },
  body: formData,
});
```
- Only the burger (masked area) was regenerated
- Flag, fries, background — preserved from original

### Analysis

I traced the code through the SDK:

1. **`ai` core** (`generate-image.ts` → `normalizePrompt()`): Correctly extracts `mask` from the prompt object
2. **`@ai-sdk/gateway` client** (`index.js` ~line 1030): Correctly encodes mask via `maybeEncodeImageFile()` and includes it in the JSON body sent to the Gateway server:
   ```js
   ...mask && { mask: maybeEncodeImageFile(mask) }
   ```
3. **Gateway server**: Receives the mask in the request body but appears to route to OpenAI's `/v1/images/generations` instead of `/v1/images/edits`, silently dropping the mask parameter.

Server-side logs confirm the mask reaches `generateImage()`:
```
Prompt type: object, keys: text,images,mask
```

### Expected Behavior

When `mask` is provided in the prompt, the Gateway should:
1. Detect that this is an inpainting request (image + mask present)
2. Route to OpenAI's `/v1/images/edits` endpoint (not `/v1/images/generations`)
3. Send the request as multipart/form-data with `image` and `mask` files (as required by OpenAI's edits API)

### Actual Behavior

The Gateway ignores the `mask` parameter entirely and generates a completely new image as if no mask was provided. No warning or error is returned.

### Versions

- `ai`: 6.0.158
- `@ai-sdk/gateway`: 3.0.95
- Node/Bun: Bun 1.3.11
- OS: Windows (production: Linux)

### Additional context

This is related to how OpenAI's image API has two separate endpoints:
- `/v1/images/generations` — text-to-image (no mask support)
- `/v1/images/edits` — inpainting (requires image + mask as multipart files)

The Gateway needs to dispatch to the correct endpoint based on whether a mask is present in the request.

title: providerOptions.gateway.order not respected when routing via providerOptions.gateway.models — unexpected provider (deepinfra) selected
body:
## Summary

When using the Vercel AI gateway with `providerOptions.gateway.order` to restrict upstream provider routing, the `order` constraint is **not applied** to models selected via `providerOptions.gateway.models`. This causes traffic to route through unexpected providers (e.g. deepinfra) that are not listed in `order`.

## Reproduction

```ts
import { createGateway } from '@ai-sdk/gateway';
import { generateText, Output } from 'ai';

const gateway = createGateway({ apiKey: process.env.VERCEL_AI_API_KEY });

await generateText({
  model: gateway('openai/gpt-5.1'),
  output: Output.object({ schema }),
  messages: prompt,
  providerOptions: {
    gateway: {
      order: ['openai', 'google', 'azure'], // deepinfra NOT listed
      models: [
        'google/gemini-2.5-flash',
        'openai/gpt-5-mini',
        'xai/grok-4.1-fast-non-reasoning',  // xai routed through deepinfra internally
      ],
    },
  },
});
```

## Expected Behavior

- `order: ['openai', 'google', 'azure']` should restrict ALL upstream routing — including for models selected from `gateway.models` — to only the listed providers.
- If `xai/grok-4.1-fast-non-reasoning` is in `gateway.models` but `xai` / `deepinfra` is not in `order`, the gateway should skip that model or throw a clear error.

## Actual Behavior

- The gateway internally selects `xai/grok-4.1-fast-non-reasoning` from the `gateway.models` fallback list and routes it through **deepinfra** as the upstream backend.
- `order` is silently ignored for models picked via `gateway.models`; it only applies to provider routing for the **primary** model.
- There is no warning or error indicating that an unlisted provider was used.

## Root Cause (observed)

`providerOptions.gateway.order` and `providerOptions.gateway.models` are two independent routing mechanisms. The `order` constraint is applied at the provider level for the explicitly requested model, but it is not enforced when the gateway internally selects a fallback from the `models` list. The `models` list can reference model IDs whose backends map to providers outside `order` (e.g. `xai/*` → deepinfra).

## Impact

- Requests unexpectedly leave the intended provider boundary (compliance, cost, latency implications).
- No observability: there is no log, header, or metadata in the response indicating which provider was actually used.

## Environment

- `ai` SDK version: `6.0.116`
- `@ai-sdk/gateway` (latest)
- Runtime: Node.js v20.9.0

title: providerOptions.google.thinkingConfig.includeThoughts: false ignored for gateway-fallback models — thinking tokens break Output.object() parsing
body:
## Summary

When using `generateText` with `Output.object({ schema })` through the Vercel AI gateway, setting `providerOptions.google.thinkingConfig.includeThoughts: false` is **not forwarded** to the Google/Gemini backend when the model is selected via gateway-internal fallback (`providerOptions.gateway.models`). Gemini 2.5 thinking models return raw thinking tokens in the response, which break structured output parsing and throw `AI_NoObjectGeneratedError`.

## Reproduction

```ts
import { createGateway } from '@ai-sdk/gateway';
import { generateText, Output } from 'ai';

const gateway = createGateway({ apiKey: process.env.VERCEL_AI_API_KEY });

await generateText({
  model: gateway('openai/gpt-5.1'),
  output: Output.object({ schema }),
  messages: prompt,
  providerOptions: {
    google: {
      thinkingConfig: {
        thinkingBudget: 128,
        includeThoughts: false,  // <-- explicitly disabled
      },
    },
    gateway: {
      order: ['openai', 'google', 'azure'],
      models: [
        'google/gemini-2.5-flash',  // thinking model — selected as fallback
        'openai/gpt-5-mini',
      ],
    },
  },
});
```

## Expected Behavior

- `providerOptions.google.thinkingConfig.includeThoughts: false` should be forwarded to the Google API for **any** Gemini model the gateway routes to, whether it is the primary model or a fallback from `gateway.models`.
- The structured output response should be clean JSON, parseable by `Output.object()`.

## Actual Behavior

- When the gateway falls back to `google/gemini-2.5-flash` (a thinking model), `thinkingConfig` is **not applied**.
- Gemini returns a response with thinking tokens prepended:
  ```
  <thinking>
  ...internal reasoning...
  </thinking>
  {"score": 7, ...}
  ```
- `Output.object({ schema })` → `parseCompleteOutput` fails to JSON-parse this mixed response.
- Throws: `AI_NoObjectGeneratedError: No object generated: could not parse the response.`

## Stack Trace

```
AI_NoObjectGeneratedError: No object generated: could not parse the response.
    at Object.parseCompleteOutput (node_modules/ai/dist/index.js:3421:15)
    at async generateText (node_modules/ai/dist/index.js:4185:12)
```

## Root Cause (observed)

`providerOptions.google.thinkingConfig` is only applied when a Google model is the **explicitly requested** model. When the Vercel gateway internally selects a Google model from the `gateway.models` fallback list, the provider-specific options are not forwarded to the backend. The gateway makes the fallback call without the `thinkingConfig`, so thinking tokens are included by default for Gemini 2.5 series models.

## Impact

- **Production breakage**: `AI_NoObjectGeneratedError` on every request that falls back to a Gemini 2.5 thinking model via `gateway.models`.
- The error is non-retryable from the SDK's perspective (it's a parsing error, not a network/rate-limit error), so all retries also fail.
- `includeThoughts: false` gives a false sense of safety — users cannot trust it suppresses thinking tokens through the gateway fallback path.

## Workaround

Remove all Gemini 2.5 thinking models (`gemini-2.5-flash`, `gemini-2.5-pro`) from `gateway.models` when using `Output.object()`, or replace them with non-thinking variants (`gemini-2.0-flash`).

## Environment

- `ai` SDK version: `6.0.116`  
- `@ai-sdk/provider-utils` version: `4.0.19`
- `@ai-sdk/gateway` (latest)
- Runtime: Node.js v20.9.0

title: Expose existing `createMCPClient({ name })` value on client-side `dynamic-tool` parts in `useChat`
body:
### Description

`createMCPClient()` in `@ai-sdk/mcp` already supports a `name` property on the server side.

I would like that existing `name` value to also be propagated to the client-side `dynamic-tool` parts returned through `useChat`.

## Current setup

Before `streamText`, MCP clients are configured like this:

```ts
createMCPClient({
  transport: {
    type: "http",
    url,
  },
  name: "MyMCPServer",
});
````

Here, `name` is already defined server-side.

On the client side, a tool result currently looks like this:

```json id="n2r4j1"
{
  "type": "dynamic-tool",
  "toolName": "my_tool_name",
  "toolCallId": "call_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "state": "output-available",
  "input": {},
  "output": {}
}
```

I would like the existing server-side `name` value to be included there as well, for example:

```json id="p6x8k3"
{
  "type": "dynamic-tool",
  "name": "MyMCPServer", // display MCP client name
  "toolName": "my_tool_name",
  "toolCallId": "call_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "state": "output-available",
  "input": {},
  "output": {}
}
```

## Why this is useful

Right now, when tools are provided from multiple MCP servers, the client UI can only distinguish them by tool name.

That makes MCP-aware UI construction harder, especially when:

* different MCP servers expose similarly named tools
* the UI wants to group tool calls/results by MCP server
* the UI wants to explicitly show which MCP server handled a given tool call

If the existing `name` value from `createMCPClient()` were exposed in the `dynamic-tool` part, it would be much easier to build a clearer client-side UI.

## Proposal

Please propagate the already-supported `name` from `createMCPClient()` into the corresponding client-side `dynamic-tool` part returned by `useChat`.


Thanks!

title: [@ai-sdk/mcp] Streamable HTTP transport does not downgrade `mcp-protocol-version` header after version negotiation (breaks servers like Figma Dev Mode MCP)
body:
## Summary

The `HttpMCPTransport` (and `SseMCPTransport`) in `@ai-sdk/mcp` always emits `mcp-protocol-version: <LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION>` in every HTTP request, ignoring the version that was actually negotiated with the server during `initialize`. This violates the MCP spec and causes post-initialization requests to fail against any server that does not (yet) support the client's latest version — notably **Figma Dev Mode MCP Server**, which supports up to `2025-06-18` as of April 2026.

## Spec reference

> The protocol version sent by the client **SHOULD** be the one negotiated during initialization.
>
> If the server receives a request with an invalid or unsupported `MCP-Protocol-Version`, it **MUST** respond with `400 Bad Request`.

— https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/transports (Protocol Version Header section, same wording in 2025-11-25)

The official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` client respects this: after `initialize`, it stores `result.protocolVersion` and uses it in every subsequent request's `mcp-protocol-version` header.

## Observed behavior (repro against real Figma Desktop MCP)

```
>>> GET  http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp                mcp-protocol-version: 2025-11-25
<<< 400
>>> POST http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp (initialize)   mcp-protocol-version: 2025-11-25
<<< 200   response body: { ..., "protocolVersion": "2025-06-18", ... }   <- server negotiated DOWN
>>> POST http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp (notifications/initialized)   mcp-protocol-version: 2025-11-25
<<< 400   error: "Unsupported protocol version (supported versions: 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05, 2024-10-07)"
```

`createMCPClient({ transport: { type: 'http', url: ... } })` never resolves — the follow-up `notifications/initialized` request is rejected because the client keeps sending its own `LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION` in the header instead of the negotiated `2025-06-18`.

## Expected behavior

After `initialize` returns a `protocolVersion`, the transport should use that exact string in the `mcp-protocol-version` header for every subsequent request (per the spec).

## Minimal reproduction

```js
// Node 22+, @ai-sdk/mcp@1.0.36 (and 2.0.0-beta.25, also affected)
import { createMCPClient } from "@ai-sdk/mcp";

// 1. Start Figma Desktop, enable Dev Mode MCP Server in Preferences (exposes port 3845)
// 2. Run:
const client = await createMCPClient({
  transport: { type: "http", url: "http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp" },
});
// Throws:
//   MCP HTTP Transport Error: POSTing to endpoint (HTTP 400):
//   {"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"Bad Request: Unsupported protocol version ..."}}
```

Direct curl with `2025-06-18` in both body and header succeeds — confirming the server is fine and the bug is purely in the client's post-init header handling.

## Affected versions

Reproduced in:
- `@ai-sdk/mcp@1.0.36` (latest on the 1.x line)
- `@ai-sdk/mcp@2.0.0-beta.25` (latest beta)

In both, `commonHeaders()` in `HttpMCPTransport` and `SseMCPTransport` hardcodes:
```js
"mcp-protocol-version": LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION
```
No logic exists to store or emit the negotiated `result.protocolVersion`.

## Related

- #13023 added `2025-11-25` to `SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS` but did not address the header-downgrade issue.
- #7575 / #10315 are the same class of version-support bugs, also not addressing header downgrade.

## Suggested fix

Add a `protocolVersion` field to each transport, set by the client after successful `initialize`:

```diff
 async commonHeaders(base) {
   const headers = {
     ...this.headers,
     ...base,
-    "mcp-protocol-version": LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
+    "mcp-protocol-version": this.protocolVersion ?? LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
   };
   // ...
 }
```

And in `DefaultMCPClient.init()`, right after the `SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS.includes(result.protocolVersion)` check:

```diff
 this.serverCapabilities = result.capabilities;
+if (this.transport) this.transport.protocolVersion = result.protocolVersion;
 this._serverInfo = result.serverInfo;
```

I've validated this exact patch locally via `pnpm patch` — it makes the Figma Dev Mode MCP handshake succeed end-to-end (6 tools discovered, `notifications/initialized` now returns 200). Happy to open a PR.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 15 (Darwin 24.6.0)
- Node: 22.14.0
- `@ai-sdk/mcp`: 1.0.36 and 2.0.0-beta.25
- MCP server: Figma Dev Mode MCP Server (Figma Desktop, built-in — supports up to `2025-06-18`)

title: gateway.getAvailableModels() throws on cohere/rerank-v3.5: schema enum missing "reranking"
body:
## Description

`gateway.getAvailableModels()` started throwing today (2026-04-14) because the Vercel AI Gateway now serves `cohere/rerank-v3.5` with `modelType: "reranking"`, but the SDK's hardcoded Zod enum in `packages/gateway/src/gateway-fetch-metadata.ts` only allows `"embedding" | "image" | "language" | "video"`.

The validation failure on the success body is then caught and re-validated against the *error* response schema, which surfaces a misleading `GatewayResponseError: Invalid error response format: Gateway request failed`. The actual cause is buried several levels deep in `cause.cause.cause`.

This is the same class of bug as #12732 (filed 2026-02-20, still open), which was triggered the previous time the gateway added a new modelType (`"video"`).

## Reproduction

```ts
import { gateway } from '@ai-sdk/gateway';

const { models } = await gateway.getAvailableModels();
// Throws: GatewayResponseError: Invalid error response format: Gateway request failed
//   → cause: APICallError: Invalid JSON response
//   → cause: AI_TypeValidationError on path ["models", 69, "modelType"]
//   → cause: ZodError: Invalid option: expected one of "embedding"|"image"|"language"|"video"
```

The offending model in the live response (verified via direct `curl` to `https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v3/ai/config` with the `ai-gateway-protocol-version: 0.0.1` header):

```json
{
  "id": "cohere/rerank-v3.5",
  "name": "Cohere Rerank 3.5",
  "modelType": "reranking",
  "specification": {
    "specificationVersion": "v3",
    "provider": "bedrock",
    "modelId": "cohere/rerank-v3.5",
    "type": "reranking"
  }
}
```

Current modelType distribution in the gateway response: `language: 184, embedding: 24, image: 26, video: 23, reranking: 1`.

## Root cause

`packages/gateway/src/gateway-fetch-metadata.ts` line ~108:

```ts
modelType: z.enum(['embedding', 'image', 'language', 'video']).nullish(),
```

`"reranking"` is missing from this enum. Verified against `main` HEAD on 2026-04-14 — the enum is unchanged.

PR #13890 (`feat(gateway): add reranking model support`, merged 2026-04-07) added the `gateway.rerankingModel()` API and `GatewayRerankingModel` class but did not touch the metadata schema. PR #14407 (`chore(gateway): add reranking to model settings generation config`, merged 2026-04-13) added `"reranking"` only to the model-settings generation script, with the maintainer noting in the PR body *"no reranking models in prod yet, so no output change"* — which is no longer true as of today.

## Suggested fix

Two options:

1. **Minimal:** widen the enum to include `"reranking"`:
   ```ts
   modelType: z.enum(['embedding', 'image', 'language', 'video', 'reranking']).nullish(),
   ```
2. **Future-proof (recommended):** replace the enum with `z.string().nullish()` so the SDK never breaks again when the gateway adds another modelType. The error path that swallows the success-body validation failure into a misleading `"Invalid error response format"` should also be improved (separate concern, but related).

Same root cause as #12732 — option 2 would close both.

## AI SDK Version

```
@ai-sdk/gateway: 3.0.88 (also verified against 3.0.96 latest 3.x and 4.0.0-beta.50; bug present in all)
ai: 6.0.146
```
