title: embed/embedMany crash: 'warnings' is undefined from EmbeddingModelV2 providers
body:
## Description

`embed()` and `embedMany()` crash at runtime when used with an embedding model that implements the v2 provider protocol (e.g. `@ai-sdk/google-vertex@3.x`), because `doEmbed` does not return a `warnings` property but the SDK assumes it is always present and iterable.

## Errors

**In `embed()`** — `logWarnings` at `src/logger/log-warnings.ts:100`:
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')
    at logWarnings (log-warnings.ts:100)
    at fn (embed.ts:180)
```

**In `embedMany()`** — spreading `result.warnings` at `src/embed/embed-many.ts:312`:
```
TypeError: result.warnings is not iterable
```

## Root cause

1. `embed.ts:180` passes `modelResponse.warnings` directly to `logWarnings()`, which accesses `options.warnings.length` without a null check.
2. `embed-many.ts:312` does `warnings.push(...result.warnings)` — spreading `undefined` throws.
3. The `EmbeddingModelV2` protocol does not include `warnings` in its `doEmbed` return type, so v2 providers (like `@ai-sdk/google-vertex@3.x`) return `undefined` for this field.

## Affected versions

- `ai@6.0.149` through at least `ai@6.0.158`
- Any `EmbeddingModelV2`-based provider (confirmed with `@ai-sdk/google-vertex@3.0.25` and `3.0.127`)

## Suggested fix

Guard against undefined `warnings` in both locations:

**`src/logger/log-warnings.ts:100`:**
```ts
if (!options.warnings || options.warnings.length === 0) {
  return;
}
```

**`src/embed/embed-many.ts:312`:**
```ts
if (result.warnings) {
  warnings.push(...result.warnings);
}
```

## Workaround

Patch the embedding model's `doEmbed` to ensure `warnings` is always an array:

```ts
const originalDoEmbed = embeddingModel.doEmbed.bind(embeddingModel);
embeddingModel.doEmbed = async (params) => {
  const result = await originalDoEmbed(params);
  return { ...result, warnings: result.warnings ?? [] };
};
```

title: streamText: deny approval crashes with "Missing required parameter: input[N].output"
body:
## Description

When using `streamText` with `needsApproval: true` on a tool and the user **denies** the tool call via `addToolApprovalResponse({ id, approved: false })`, the next request crashes with:

```
Missing required parameter: 'input[N].output'
```

**Approving (Yes) works perfectly. Only denying (No) crashes.**

## Reproduction

Minimal Next.js project: two tools (one read, one write with `needsApproval: true`). The model calls both in the same step. Read auto-executes, write gets `approval-requested`. User denies → second POST → crash.

### Server (`app/api/chat/route.ts`)

```typescript
import { openai } from "@ai-sdk/openai";
import { convertToModelMessages, stepCountIs, streamText, tool } from "ai";
import { z } from "zod";

const searchMemory = tool({
  description: "Search memory",
  inputSchema: z.object({ query: z.string() }),
  execute: async ({ query }) => ({ resultCount: 0, query }),
});

const sendEmail = tool({
  description: "Send an email",
  inputSchema: z.object({ to: z.string(), subject: z.string(), body: z.string() }),
  needsApproval: true,
  execute: async ({ to, subject, body }) => ({ success: true, to, subject }),
});

export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const { messages } = await req.json();
  const tools = { searchMemory, sendEmail };

  const modelMessages = await convertToModelMessages(messages, {
    tools,
    ignoreIncompleteToolCalls: true,
  });

  const result = streamText({
    model: openai("gpt-4o"),
    system: "You have searchMemory and sendEmail. Call both when asked to send email.",
    messages: modelMessages,
    tools,
    stopWhen: stepCountIs(10),
  });

  return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse();
}
```

### Client (`app/page.tsx`)

Standard `useChat` + `DefaultChatTransport` + `sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithApprovalResponses` + `addToolApprovalResponse({ id, approved: false })`.

### Steps

1. User sends "send an email to test@test.com saying hello"
2. Model calls `searchMemory` (auto-executes) + `sendEmail` (gets `approval-requested`)
3. Client shows approval UI, user clicks **Deny**
4. `addToolApprovalResponse({ id, approved: false })` → `sendAutomaticallyWhen` fires
5. Second POST with messages containing `approval-responded` + `approved: false`

### curl reproduction

```bash
# Step 1: works fine
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/chat \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"id":"msg-1","role":"user","parts":[{"type":"text","text":"send an email to test@test.com saying hello"}]}]}'

# Step 2: crashes (use toolCallId and approvalId from step 1)
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/chat \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages":[
    {"id":"msg-1","role":"user","parts":[{"type":"text","text":"send an email to test@test.com saying hello"}]},
    {"id":"msg-2","role":"assistant","parts":[
      {"type":"tool-searchMemory","toolCallId":"call_XXX","state":"output-available","input":{"query":"contact test@test.com"},"output":{"resultCount":0}},
      {"type":"tool-sendEmail","toolCallId":"call_YYY","state":"approval-responded","input":{"to":"test@test.com","subject":"Hello","body":"Hello"},"approval":{"id":"APPROVAL_ID","approved":false,"reason":"User denied"}}
    ]}
  ]}'
```

### Output

```
data: {"type":"tool-output-denied","toolCallId":"call_YYY"}
data: {"type":"error","errorText":"Missing required parameter: 'input[5].output'."}
data: [DONE]
```

The SDK correctly emits `tool-output-denied`, then crashes when calling the model for the continuation step.

## Investigation

We traced through the SDK source (`ai@6.0.154`):

1. `convertToModelMessages` correctly creates `tool-approval-response` for denied tools (line ~8575)
2. `convertToLanguageModelPrompt` correctly reads `approvedToolCallIds` from `tool-approval-response` parts (line ~1425)
3. But `convertToLanguageModelPrompt` also **filters out** non-provider-executed `tool-approval-response` parts from the tool message (line ~1607):
   ```javascript
   (part) => part.type !== "tool-approval-response" || part.providerExecuted
   ```
4. `collectToolApprovals` in `streamText` processes the denied approval and creates a `tool-result` with `{ type: "execution-denied" }` in `initialResponseMessages`
5. These `initialResponseMessages` are added to `stepInputMessages` for the model call
6. But the OpenAI Responses API (`input[N].output`) still rejects, suggesting the denied tool result doesn't reach the model in the correct format

### Both patterns fail

| Pattern | Result |
|---------|--------|
| `convertToModelMessages()` → `streamText({ messages: modelMessages })` | `input[N].output` error on deny |
| Raw messages → `streamText({ messages })` | `Invalid prompt: messages do not match ModelMessage[] schema` |

## Expected Behavior

After denying a tool call, the model should receive the denial result and continue the conversation (e.g., suggest an alternative).

## Versions

- `ai`: 6.0.154
- `@ai-sdk/openai`: 2.0.65
- `@ai-sdk/react`: 3.0.156
- `next`: 15.5.15
- Node.js: 22.20.0

title: Invalid tool call input stored as raw string causes API rejection on next step
body:
## Bug Description

When `parseToolCall` fails to parse a tool call's JSON input, the catch block stores the raw string as `input`:

```ts
// parse-tool-call.ts (line 82-83)
const parsedInput = await safeParseJSON({ text: toolCall.input });
const input = parsedInput.success ? parsedInput.value : toolCall.input;
//                                                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
//                                              raw string, not a JSON object
```

This raw string flows through `to-response-messages.ts` and `convert-to-language-model-prompt.ts` into the assistant message for the next API step. Providers like Amazon Bedrock require `toolUse.input` to be a JSON object (the Bedrock provider does `input: part.input as JSONObject` in `convert-to-bedrock-chat-messages.ts`), so the API rejects the request before the model ever sees the `tool-error` result.

## Expected Behavior

The model should see the `tool-error` and be able to retry. The invalid tool call's `input` should be wrapped in a valid JSON object (e.g., `{ rawInvalidInput: toolCall.input }`) so the conversation history remains valid for the next API call.

## Reproduction

1. Use a model via Amazon Bedrock with tool calling
2. Have the model generate a tool call with malformed JSON input (can be simulated with middleware that corrupts `tool-call` chunks)
3. The SDK correctly marks the tool call as `invalid: true` and generates a `tool-error`
4. On the next step, the API rejects with: `"The format of the value at messages.X.content.Y.toolUse.input is invalid. Provide a json object for the field and try again."`

## Suggested Fix

In `parse-tool-call.ts`, wrap the fallback input in an object:

```diff
- const input = parsedInput.success ? parsedInput.value : toolCall.input;
+ const input = parsedInput.success ? parsedInput.value : { rawInvalidInput: toolCall.input };
```

## Environment

- `ai` version: 6.0.48
- Provider: `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock`
- Model: Claude (Anthropic via Bedrock)

title: Enrich WorkflowAgent callback event shapes
body:
Parent: #14451

WorkflowAgent callback events are much sparser than ToolLoopAgent's:

| Callback | ToolLoopAgent props | WorkflowAgent props |
|---|---|---|
| onStart | ~23 | 2 (model, messages) |
| onStepStart | ~18 | 3 (stepNumber, model, messages) |
| onToolCallStart | ~8 | 1 (toolCall) |
| onToolCallFinish | ~11 (discriminated union) | 3 (toolCall, result?, error?) |

At minimum:
- Add `stepNumber` to `onToolCallStart` and `onToolCallFinish`
- Add `steps` to `onStepStart`
- Adopt the discriminated union pattern (`success: true/false`) for `onToolCallFinish` instead of optional `result`/`error` fields

title: Add prompt parameter to WorkflowAgent stream()
body:
Parent: #14451

ToolLoopAgent's `generate()` and `stream()` accept either `prompt` (string) or `messages` (ModelMessage[]). WorkflowAgent's `stream()` requires `messages` only.

Add `prompt` as an alternative to `messages` in `WorkflowAgentStreamOptions`, matching the `AgentCallParameters` pattern from ToolLoopAgent. This improves DX for simple use cases where users don't need full message arrays.
author: gr2m

title: Unify callback type signatures across ToolLoopAgent and WorkflowAgent
body:
Parent: #14451

ToolLoopAgent and WorkflowAgent define independent callback type hierarchies with different event shapes:

- ToolLoopAgent: `ToolLoopAgentOn{Start,StepStart,ToolCallStart,ToolCallFinish,StepFinish,Finish}Callback`
- WorkflowAgent: `WorkflowAgentOn{Start,StepStart,ToolCallStart,ToolCallFinish,StepFinish,Finish,Error,Abort}Callback`

Investigate whether these can converge to shared base types or a common `AgentOn*Callback` pattern. This would make it easier for users switching between agents and for libraries that accept any agent.

Depends on #14453 (enriching WorkflowAgent callback events) being resolved first so the event shapes are closer.

title: fix(openai): ChatGPT Codex OAuth SSE stream fails on truncated response.* events
body:
## Bug Report

When using the ChatGPT Codex OAuth endpoint (`chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`) with models like `gpt-5.3-codex` or `gpt-5.4`, the backend returns `response.created`, `response.in_progress`, and `response.completed` SSE events that include the full system prompt in an `instructions` field (~30KB).

These events frequently arrive with truncated JSON because the SSE buffer cannot hold the entire payload. `safeParseJSON` returns `{ success: false, error: JSONParseError }`, and the `doStream()` transform treats this as fatal — setting `finishReason = 'error'` and killing the stream.

### Expected Behavior

The stream should continue producing text deltas. These `response.*` events are informational status updates and not required for text streaming.

### Actual Behavior

The entire stream fails with `AI_JSONParseError: Unterminated string`.

### Reproduction

Use `@ai-sdk/openai` with ChatGPT OAuth (not API key) authentication and a model that returns large system prompts in SSE events (e.g. `gpt-5.4` via the Codex endpoint).

### Proposed Fix

Detect truncated `response.*` status events via `JSONParseError.isInstance()` and skip them instead of failing. This mirrors the [official OpenAI Codex CLI (Rust)](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs#L397) strategy.

PR incoming.

title: Bug: tool-only assistant messages send content:"" in xai, deepseek, groq, mistral providers
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #13466 / #13744.

The same pattern that caused Bedrock `ValidationException: messages: text content blocks must be non-empty` in `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` and `@ai-sdk/openai` also exists in four other provider packages. When an assistant message contains only `tool-call` parts (no text), the converter emits `content: ""`, which Bedrock-backed endpoints reject.

## Affected files

- `packages/xai/src/convert-to-xai-chat-messages.ts:111`
- `packages/deepseek/src/chat/convert-to-deepseek-chat-messages.ts:126`
- `packages/groq/src/convert-to-groq-chat-messages.ts:105`
- `packages/mistral/src/convert-to-mistral-chat-messages.ts:122`

Each has the same shape:

```ts
messages.push({
  role: 'assistant',
  content: text, // <-- empty string when only tool-calls are present
  tool_calls: toolCalls.length > 0 ? toolCalls : undefined,
});
```

## Proposed fix

Apply the same change as #13744:

```ts
content: text || null,
```

This matches the OpenAI spec (content is nullable when `tool_calls` is present) and what official OpenAI SDKs send.

## Scope

- Update each converter.
- Update corresponding unit tests to expect `null` for tool-only assistant messages.
- Add a patch changeset covering the four packages.

Note: Mistral uses its own API shape; verify Mistral's spec accepts `null` before applying there. The other three (xai, deepseek, groq) are OpenAI-compatible.

title: O(N²) parse time in @ai-sdk/mcp on large MCP tool responses (fix in rexxars/eventsource-parser#28)
body:
### Description


Found an O(N²) in `@ai-sdk/mcp`'s SSE parsing on large MCP tool responses. Fix is up at [rexxars/eventsource-parser#28](https://github.com/rexxars/eventsource-parser/pull/28).

I know its a fix on another repo/maintainer but mostly just wanted to give you a heads up. I had already patched it locally to unblock myself, but I'd rather fix it at the source (I don't like to do one-offs haha) so the whole community benefits, especially folks doing tool calls that return larger datasets. Hoping this helps other people hitting the same wall, and happy to find ways to contribute to this community! Let me know if you have any suggestions on it or anything else!

## Context

Ran into this while profiling some big MCP tool calls. `@ai-sdk/mcp`'s streamable-HTTP transport pipes responses through `EventSourceParserStream` (from `@ai-sdk/provider-utils`, backed by `eventsource-parser`). If a tool returns a big payload as one SSE event, which is the common shape for MCP servers that dump bulk data as a single `content[]` block, the `incompleteLine + chunk` concat inside `feed()` goes quadratic.

Not the same case as #5862 / [rexxars/eventsource-parser#19](https://github.com/rexxars/eventsource-parser/issues/19). That one got fixed in 3.0.1 by optimizing `splitLines`, but the concat pattern itself was left alone. So streams with one very long line still hit O(N²).

## Root cause

In `eventsource-parser@3.0.7` `feed()`:

```js
const input = incompleteLine === "" ? chunk : incompleteLine + chunk;
incompleteLine = processLines(input);
```

When one SSE event spans many chunks (no `\n\n` until the very end), `incompleteLine` grows unbounded. Each chunk pays O(total_seen). Across N chunks, O(N²).

My fix at [rexxars/eventsource-parser#28](https://github.com/rexxars/eventsource-parser/pull/28) swaps the string accumulator for a fragment array and defers the concat until a terminator actually arrives. Hot path (empty buffer) stays byte-for-byte identical to the original.

## Repro

Public `mcp-clickhouse` + ClickHouse playground, no auth needed:

```bash
CLICKHOUSE_HOST=play.clickhouse.com CLICKHOUSE_PORT=443 CLICKHOUSE_USER=play \
CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD='' CLICKHOUSE_SECURE=true \
CLICKHOUSE_MCP_SERVER_TRANSPORT=http CLICKHOUSE_MCP_BIND_PORT=8765 \
CLICKHOUSE_MCP_AUTH_DISABLED=true \
  uvx --from mcp-clickhouse mcp-clickhouse &
```

Then:

```ts
import { createMCPClient } from "@ai-sdk/mcp";

const c = await createMCPClient({
  transport: { type: "http", url: "http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp" },
});
const tools = await c.tools();
const t0 = performance.now();
await tools.run_query.execute(
  { query: "SELECT * FROM uk_price_paid LIMIT 1000000" },
  { toolCallId: crypto.randomUUID(), messages: [] }
);
console.log(`${Math.round(performance.now() - t0)} ms`);
```

## Benchmarks

Same query, 1M rows / ~280 MB / one content block:

| version | total | rss peak |
|---|---|---|
| `eventsource-parser@3.0.6` | 93 s | 3.9 GB |
| `eventsource-parser@3.0.7` (upstream perf refactor) | 101 s | 2.3 GB |
| **`eventsource-parser@3.0.7` + [rexxars/eventsource-parser#28](https://github.com/rexxars/eventsource-parser/pull/28)** | **7 s** | 2.0 GB |

Scaling before the fix is ~N^1.9 in payload size. After, linear. 14× speedup on this shape, peak memory roughly halves.

title: [Feature] Governance hooks for AI SDK — policy enforcement before tool execution
body:
## Summary

Proposing governance hooks/middleware for the Vercel AI SDK's tool execution pipeline, powered by the [Agent Governance Toolkit (AGT)](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit).

## Motivation

The AI SDK's `tool` abstraction is the natural enforcement point for governance. Before any tool executes, enterprises need policy checks, identity verification, and audit logging — without modifying tool implementations.

## Proposed Integration

1. **Pre-execution policy hooks** — AGT's policy engine evaluates rules before `tool.execute()` runs. Policies are defined as code (e.g., block file-system writes, enforce rate limits, restrict PII access). Evaluation takes <5ms.
2. **Agent identity verification** — Ed25519 keypairs verify which agent/user initiated a tool call. Supports zero-trust multi-agent architectures.
3. **Tamper-evident audit trails** — every tool invocation, policy decision, and result is logged in a Merkle chain. Exportable for compliance.

## Integration points

- `experimental_toToolResultContent` or a new `onBeforeToolCall` / `onAfterToolCall` hook
- Middleware wrapper around `tool()` definitions
- TypeScript SDK available for native integration

## Technical details

- TypeScript SDK with full type safety
- <5ms policy evaluation overhead
- MIT licensed, 9,500+ tests
- Works with any AI SDK provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)

title: Title: @ai-sdk/google: Vertex rejects tool_config.includeServerSideToolInvocations on gemini-3-flash-preview with function tools
body:
### Description

---

# `includeServerSideToolInvocations` rejected by Vertex on Gemini 3.x with function tools

**Labels:** `bug` `@ai-sdk/google-vertex` `function-tools`

---

## Description

When using `@ai-sdk/google-vertex` with a Gemini 3.x model (e.g. `gemini-3-flash-preview`) on `location=global` and passing function tools, every request fails with a 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT` from Vertex:

```
Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "includeServerSideToolInvocations"
at 'tool_config': Cannot find field.
```

The Vertex `streamGenerateContent` endpoint does not accept the `tool_config.includeServerSideToolInvocations` field that the SDK hard-codes on the Gemini-3-or-newer + function-tools code path. Google has since tightened schema validation on the preview endpoint and now hard-rejects unknown fields.

---

## Source

In `@ai-sdk/google/dist/index.js` (also in the 3.x / latest google package), around line 987:

```js
if (hasFunctionTools && isGemini3orNewer && googleTools2.length > 0) {
  // ...
  const combinedToolConfig = {
    functionCallingConfig: { mode: "VALIDATED" },
    includeServerSideToolInvocations: true   // <— rejected by Vertex
  };
  // ...
}
```

---

## Reproduction

```js
import { createVertex } from "@ai-sdk/google-vertex";
import { streamText, tool } from "ai";
import { z } from "zod";

const vertex = createVertex({ project: "YOUR_PROJECT", location: "global" });

const result = streamText({
  model: vertex("gemini-3-flash-preview"),
  prompt: "hello",
  tools: {
    ping: tool({
      description: "noop",
      inputSchema: z.object({ x: z.string() }),
      execute: async () => "pong",
    }),
  },
});

for await (const chunk of result.textStream) process.stdout.write(chunk);
```

**Result:**
```
AI_APICallError: Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name
"includeServerSideToolInvocations" at 'tool_config': Cannot find field.
```

### Full error response from Vertex

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name \"includeServerSideToolInvocations\" at 'tool_config': Cannot find field.",
    "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT",
    "details": [{
      "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.BadRequest",
      "fieldViolations": [{
        "field": "tool_config",
        "description": "Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name \"includeServerSideToolInvocations\" at 'tool_config': Cannot find field."
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**URL:** `https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/publishers/google/models/gemini-3-flash-preview:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`

---

## Impact

- All Vertex requests to `gemini-3-*-preview` that include function tools fail
- Only affects Vertex (`@ai-sdk/google-vertex`) — Google AI Studio (`@ai-sdk/google` direct) may not be affected since it targets a different endpoint
- Gemini 2.5 and earlier are unaffected as they don't enter the `isGemini3orNewer` code branch

---

## Suggested Fix

One of:

1. Remove `includeServerSideToolInvocations` from the combined tool config (it defaults to the correct behavior server-side anyway)
2. Gate it behind a provider option (opt-in), so Vertex users can disable it until Google ships API support
3. Detect the provider (`vertex` vs `generative-language`) and only send the field where it's supported

---

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| `@ai-sdk/google-vertex` | `4.0.112` |
| `@ai-sdk/google` | `3.0.64` |
| `ai` | latest |
| Node | 22 LTS |
| Vertex endpoint | `v1`, `location=global` |
| Model | `gemini-3-flash-preview` |

---

## Workaround

Downgrade to `gemini-2.5-flash` or `gemini-2.5-pro` — this skips the affected code path. Note that native `google_search` grounding + function tools mixing is lost until this is resolved, as that feature is Gemini-3-only.

title: Expose MCP server instructions from initialize handshake
body:
## Summary

The `@ai-sdk/mcp` client receives `instructions` in the MCP `initialize` handshake response but discards them. The [MCP spec](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/lifecycle#initialization) defines `instructions` as an optional string on the initialize result, and the SDK already parses it via `InitializeResultSchema`, but `DefaultMCPClient.init()` only stores `capabilities` and `serverInfo`.

## Problem

When an MCP server provides `instructions` in its `McpServer` constructor (e.g., via `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`):

```ts
new McpServer(
  { name: 'my-server', version: '1.0.0' },
  { instructions: 'Use search tools to resolve IDs — never ask the user.' }
);
```

There is no way for the `@ai-sdk/mcp` client to access those instructions. The `MCPClient` interface has no property or method to retrieve them.

## Current behavior

In `mcp-client.ts`, `init()` stores only:
```ts
this.serverCapabilities = result.capabilities;
```

`result.instructions` is parsed by the schema but never stored.

## Expected behavior

`MCPClient` should expose the server's instructions so that consuming applications can include them in LLM system prompts alongside the tools.

## Suggested fix

1. Add a property to `DefaultMCPClient`:
   ```ts
   private serverInstructions?: string;
   ```
2. Store it in `init()`:
   ```ts
   this.serverInstructions = result.instructions;
   ```
3. Expose it on the `MCPClient` interface:
   ```ts
   readonly instructions?: string;
   ```

This is a non-breaking, additive change.

title: addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema breaks xAI/Grok tool calling: xAI rejects additionalProperties: false
body:
## Description

The `addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema` function in `@ai-sdk/provider-utils` forcibly adds `additionalProperties: false` to all object schemas during tool serialization. This breaks tool calling for xAI/Grok models because xAI's validator explicitly rejects `additionalProperties: false` in tool schemas.

xAI's [structured output docs](https://docs.x.ai/docs/guides/structured-outputs) state:
- `additionalProperties` defaults to `false` already
- schemas with boolean property schemas like `false` are rejected

So the AI SDK is adding something that xAI explicitly rejects, even though xAI's default behavior is already what the AI SDK is trying to enforce.

## Root Cause

In `@ai-sdk/provider-utils`, the `addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema` function unconditionally sets `additionalProperties: false` on all object-type schemas:

```ts
function addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema(jsonSchema2) {
  if (jsonSchema2.type === "object" || ...) {
    jsonSchema2.additionalProperties = false;  // <-- This breaks xAI
    ...
  }
}
```

This function is called during tool schema serialization for all providers, with no provider-specific opt-out.

## Impact

Any application using the AI SDK with xAI/Grok models and tool calling will fail with:

```
[xAI] Invalid request content: Schema validation failed: [standard_violation] /properties/properties/additionalProperties: property schema 'false' is not supported
```

This affects:
- Direct xAI provider usage (`@ai-sdk/xai`)
- OpenRouter xAI models (`@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider`)
- Any other OpenAI-compatible provider routing to xAI

## Investigation

We spent significant time debugging this in OpenCode and confirmed:
1. The AI SDK re-adds `additionalProperties: false` AFTER any application-level sanitization
2. The binary bundles all dependencies at build time, so runtime interceptors don't work
3. The conflict exists at the AI SDK level, not the application level

Full investigation: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/23704

## Suggested Fix

Add provider-specific schema serialization options to the AI SDK, such as:

1. **Provider-level opt-out**: Allow providers to disable `addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema` for specific models
2. **xAI-specific handling**: Skip adding `additionalProperties: false` when targeting xAI models
3. **Configuration option**: Add a `strictToolSchemas` or similar option to provider constructors

Since xAI defaults to `additionalProperties: false` anyway, skipping it for xAI targets preserves intended strictness while avoiding the validator rejection.

## Workaround (for now)

Applications can disable tool calling for xAI models via config:

```json
{
  "provider": {
    "openrouter": {
      "models": {
        "x-ai/grok-4.1-fast": {
          "tool_call": false
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

But this is not a real solution — it just disables tools entirely for xAI models.

## Related

- OpenCode issue: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/23704
- Similar Grok 3 issue (different error): https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/8024

title: UIMessagePart input-streaming types are incompatible with exactOptionalPropertyTypes
body:
### Description

## Description

Under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`, a `UIMessage` cannot be assigned from a structurally equivalent value if the `input` field on an `input-streaming` tool part is declared as optional (`input?: T`) rather than required-but-undefined (`input: T | undefined`). This commonly breaks consumers whose type pipelines erase the distinction — tRPC, Zod `z.infer`, JSON utility types, etc.

## Minimal reproduction

`tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true,
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "skipLibCheck": true
  }
}
```

`repro.ts`:

```ts
import type { DynamicToolUIPart } from "ai";

declare const part: {
  type: "dynamic-tool";
  state: "input-streaming";
  toolCallId: string;
  toolName: string;
  input?: unknown;          // optional — the shape produced by tRPC/Zod inference
  providerExecuted?: boolean;
};

const x: DynamicToolUIPart = part; // ❌ TS2375: input required in target
```

Same error surfaces through `UIMessage` / `UIMessagePart` anywhere a `dynamic-tool` or generic `tool-*` part with `state: 'input-streaming'` flows in.

## Root cause

In [`packages/ai/src/ui/ui-messages.ts`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/ai/src/ui/ui-messages.ts), the `input-streaming` variants of both `UIToolInvocation` and `DynamicToolUIPart` declare:

```ts
input: DeepPartial<asUITool<TOOL>['input']> | undefined;  // UIToolInvocation
input: unknown | undefined;                               // DynamicToolUIPart
```

Under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `input: T | undefined` (required key, value may be undefined) is **not** interchangeable with `input?: T` (key may be missing): each shape is rejected by the other.

## Internal inconsistency

The runtime validator in [`validate-ui-messages.ts`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/ai/src/ui/validate-ui-messages.ts) already treats `input` as optional for `input-streaming` states:

```ts
// both dynamic-tool and tool-* input-streaming schemas:
input: z.unknown().optional(),
```

So the TypeScript types are stricter than the validator. Messages that the validator accepts can't necessarily be assigned back into the TS types they came from.

## Suggested fix

Three options, in order of permissiveness:

1. **`input?: T`** — matches the Zod validator. Narrow change, but rejects code that writes an explicit `input: undefined`.
2. **`input?: T | undefined`** — accepts all three shapes (missing, `undefined`, concrete value). Maximally backward-compatible.
3. Leave as-is and document that `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` is unsupported.

I have a branch implementing option 1 — 2 lines changed in `ui-messages.ts`, all 2460 `ai` package tests pass, full workspace `type-check:full` passes. Happy to open a PR if helpful.

## Out of scope (separate inconsistency)

The `output-error` variants also use `input: T | undefined`, but there the Zod validator requires `input` to be present (`z.unknown()`, not `.optional()`). That's a separate types-vs-runtime mismatch and would need its own fix. Flagging for awareness; not addressed here.

## Note on the v6 TODO

`ui-messages.ts:341` has:

```ts
state: 'output-error'; // TODO AI SDK 6: change to 'error' state
input: asUITool<TOOL>['input'] | undefined;
rawInput?: unknown; // TODO AI SDK 6: remove this field, input should be unknown
```

which suggests a larger refactor is planned around tool-input handling. This report is about the `input-streaming` states specifically; if the v6 work already covers them, feel free to close.

title: bug(amazon-bedrock): `<reasoning>` tags leaked into text response for OpenAI models on Bedrock during multi-turn tool use
body:
### Description

Since `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock@4.0.85`, OpenAI models accessed via Amazon Bedrock (e.g., `openai.gpt-oss-120b-1:0`) leak raw `<reasoning>...</reasoning>` tags into the final text response during multi-turn conversations that involve tool use.

The issue is specific to models that return `reasoningContent` blocks via the Bedrock Converse API **without a cryptographic signature** — which is how OpenAI's extended thinking works on Bedrock (unlike Anthropic, which always signs its reasoning blocks).

Anthropic models (Claude) are **not affected**.

## How it happens

When OpenAI models with extended thinking reason, the Bedrock Converse API returns `reasoningContent.reasoningText` blocks — but unlike Anthropic's implementation, **OpenAI does not include a `signature`** field alongside the reasoning.

This matters because of a change introduced in v4.0.85 (PR #13972). That PR added an `else` branch in `convert-to-bedrock-chat-messages.ts` that replays **unsigned** reasoning back as `reasoningContent` blocks when constructing multi-turn messages. The flow is:

1. OpenAI model responds with `reasoningContent.reasoningText` (no signature, no `redactedData`)
2. `doGenerate` creates `{ type: 'reasoning', text: '...' }` content parts **without `providerMetadata`** (the code only attaches metadata when a signature is present)
3. On the next turn (e.g., after a tool call), `convertToBedrockChatMessages` processes the reasoning part
4. `parseProviderOptions` returns `null` → both `signature` and `redactedData` are `undefined`
5. The `else` branch catches this case and wraps the text as `reasoningContent: { reasoningText: { text } }`
6. This sends the raw reasoning back to the model in the conversation history
7. The model gets confused by receiving its own reasoning as input → leaks `<reasoning>` tags into the visible text output

**Before v4.0.85:** Unsigned reasoning was simply dropped from replayed messages. The previous code only replayed reasoning when `reasoningMetadata != null`, which effectively required a signature or redacted data.

## Reproduction

**Model:** `openai.gpt-oss-120b-1:0` on Amazon Bedrock (us-east-1)  
**SDK version:** `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock@4.0.85` through `4.0.96` (latest)  
**API:** Converse (non-streaming)  
**Scenario:** Multi-turn agent conversation with tool use

### Steps

1. Create an agent with tools using `generateText` (non-streaming) against `openai.gpt-oss-120b-1:0` on Bedrock
2. Send a query that triggers tool use (requires at least one tool call → tool result → final response cycle)
3. The final text response contains raw `<reasoning>...</reasoning>` tags

### Example leaked response

```
<reasoning>The user asked about product X. I need to use the tool result to construct the answer.
Let me format the URLs from the template...

**Product X — Overview**
Here are the relevant links:
- [Link 1](https://example.com/...)
- [Link 2](https://example.com/...)
```

Note: the opening `<reasoning>` tag is present but the closing `</reasoning>` tag is **never emitted** — the model's internal chain-of-thought bleeds directly into the visible response text without any delimiter.

### AI SDK Version

@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock@4.0.85

title: experimental_transcribe mis-detects m4a/mp4 files and sends them to OpenAI as audio/wav
body:
### Description

`experimental_transcribe()` sniffs the audio buffer instead of honoring a caller-supplied `mediaType`. The `audio/mp4` signature checks for `ftyp` at byte offset 0, but every file-on-disk m4a/mp4 prefixes `ftyp` with a 4-byte box-length header — so `ftyp` sits at offset 4 and detection misses. The wrapper silently falls back to `mediaType: 'audio/wav'`, and OpenAI rejects the mis-tagged upload with HTTP 400.

Affects anything written by iOS `AVAudioRecorder`, Android's AAC encoder, `ffmpeg -c:a aac`, or ElevenLabs TTS m4a export.

### Reproduction

Standalone repo: https://github.com/aamikus/ai-sdk-transcribe-m4a-repro

Part 1 — local signature check (no API key):

```
bytes 0..15:     00 00 00 1c 66 74 79 70 4d 34 41 20 00 00 02 00
"ftyp" at 0:    false  ← AI SDK checks here
"ftyp" at 4:    true   ← where it actually is
```

Part 2 — `experimental_transcribe` on the same buffer. The request file shows the wrapper uploaded it as `audio/wav`:

```
status:       400
request file: File { size: 215332, type: 'audio/wav', name: 'audio.wav' }
response:     {
  "error": {
    "message": "This model does not support the format you provided.",
    "code": "unsupported_format"
  }
}
```

Part 3 — `openai.transcription(...).doGenerate({ audio, mediaType: 'audio/mp4' })` on the same bytes, bypassing the sniffer:

```
text: Honestly, it was a pretty steep learning curve at first. I spent most of the first week just trying to figure out the query syntax, but after a while, things started to click and now I'm much faster with it.
```

Something like:

```ts
import { OpenTelemetry } from "@ai-sdk/otel";

registerTelemetry(
  new OpenTelemetry({
    enrichSpanAttributes: ({ spanType, operationId, callId, runtimeContext }) => {
      return {
        ...getCustomAttributes(runtimeContext, spanType),
      };
    },
  }),
);
```

Or more concretely:

```ts
type EnrichSpanAttributesContext = {
  callId: string;
  operationId: string;
  spanName: string;
  spanType: "operation" | "model" | "tool" | "embedding" | "rerank";
  runtimeContext?: Record<string, unknown>;
  functionId?: string;
  existingAttributes: Readonly<Attributes>;
};

type EnrichSpanAttributes = (
  context: EnrichSpanAttributesContext,
) => Attributes | undefined;
```

The hook would run immediately before `@ai-sdk/otel` calls `tracer.startSpan(...)`.

```ts
const attributes = selectAttributes(telemetry, {
  ...aiSdkAttributes,
});

const extraAttributes = options.enrichSpanAttributes?.({
  callId: event.callId,
  operationId,
  spanName,
  spanType,
  runtimeContext,
  functionId: telemetry?.functionId,
  existingAttributes: attributes,
});

const span = tracer.startSpan(spanName, {
  attributes: {
    ...attributes,
    ...extraAttributes,
  },
}, parentContext);
```

**Problem**
AI SDK v7 has a nice telemetry architecture: the AI SDK emits semantic lifecycle callbacks, and `@ai-sdk/otel` turns those into OpenTelemetry spans. That works well when the only desired attributes are the AI SDK’s built-in attributes.

The gap is that external observability systems sometimes need to add additional span attributes that are specific to their ingestion pipeline.

For Langfuse, examples are:

```ts
"langfuse.observation.metadata.feature": "chat"
"langfuse.observation.prompt.name": "support-agent"
"langfuse.observation.prompt.version": 3
```

These are not AI SDK attributes and should not become AI SDK-owned semantics. But they need to be present on the OTel span when it is exported.

The user already has a natural place to provide this data: `runtimeContext`.

```ts
await generateText({
  model,
  prompt,
  runtimeContext: {
    langfuse: {
      metadata: { feature: "chat" },
      prompt: { name: "support-agent", version: 3 },
    },
  },
  telemetry: {
    functionId: "chat-route",
  },
});
```

The issue is that `@ai-sdk/otel` currently fully owns span creation and does not expose a supported way to add attributes at span creation time.

**Current Workaround**
Because there is no enrichment hook, Langfuse has to wrap the OpenTelemetry tracer.

Today the workaround looks conceptually like this:

```txt
@ai-sdk/otel creates span
  -> calls tracer.startSpan(name, options, parentContext)
  -> Langfuse tracer wrapper intercepts startSpan
  -> adds Langfuse attributes
  -> forwards to real tracer
```

This works, but it is awkward because the OpenTelemetry `Tracer` API only receives:

```ts
name
options
parentContext
```

It does not receive AI SDK concepts like:

```ts
callId
operationId
runtimeContext
span type
tool call id
```

So Langfuse has to reconstruct enough AI SDK context from the outside. That is why we maintain bookkeeping maps like:

```txt
callId -> Langfuse runtime context
spanId -> callId
```

This is exactly the kind of cleverness we would rather avoid. It is not business logic; it is a workaround for not having an official enrichment point.

**Why AI SDK Is The Right Place**
`@ai-sdk/otel` already has the information at the perfect moment.

When it creates the root span, it knows:

```ts
event.callId
event.operationId
event.runtimeContext
telemetry.functionId
```

When it creates the model-call span, it knows:

```ts
callId
operationId
step context
model call attributes
parent span context
```

When it creates tool spans, it knows:

```ts
callId
toolCallId
toolName
tool input
tool span parent context
```

So the clean design is:

```txt
AI SDK keeps owning the span shape.
AI SDK keeps deciding when spans are created.
AI SDK keeps deciding default attributes.
Integrations can append additional attributes.
```

That is much safer than asking every integration to wrap tracers and infer span ownership.

**Why This Does Not Need To Expose Unstable Internals**
The hook does not need to expose private `callState`, raw spans, internal maps, or mutable lifecycle state.

A stable minimal context would be enough:

```ts
{
  callId,
  operationId,
  spanName,
  spanType,
  runtimeContext,
  functionId,
  existingAttributes,
}
```

Most of these are already public concepts:

```txt
callId: already present in telemetry events
operationId: already present in telemetry events / attributes
runtimeContext: user-provided public input
functionId: public telemetry option
existingAttributes: what AI SDK is already about to emit
```

`spanType` would be the only new abstraction, and it can be intentionally coarse:

```ts
"operation" | "model" | "tool" | "embedding" | "rerank"
```

That avoids forcing downstream integrations to parse span names like `.doGenerate` or `.doStream`.

If they want to be even more conservative, they could omit `spanType` initially and expose only `spanName` / `operationId`, but `spanType` would make the hook much more stable over time.

**Why This Benefits AI SDK Users Generally**
This is not Langfuse-specific.

Any observability integration may need to add attributes such as:

```ts
"tenant.id"
"app.route"
"experiment.variant"
"customer.plan"
"deployment.region"
"custom.trace.link"
```

Users often already have those values in `runtimeContext`. The current API lets them pass runtime context to the AI SDK, but the official OTel integration does not let that context influence emitted span attributes except through AI SDK’s own built-in mapping.

A hook would let users do:

```ts
new OpenTelemetry({
  enrichSpanAttributes: ({ runtimeContext }) => ({
    "tenant.id": runtimeContext?.tenantId,
    "experiment.variant": runtimeContext?.experiment,
  }),
});
```

That keeps custom application semantics out of AI SDK core while making the official OTel integration more extensible.

title: Allow overriding hardcoded file media type filtering
body:
### Description

# Problem

The AI SDK currently applies a hardcoded allowlist when converting user file parts for some providers.

For example, in the OpenAI Responses path, the SDK accepts `image/*` and `application/pdf`, but rejects other file media types at the SDK layer, even when the target provider can accept file inputs generically.

This creates a mismatch between SDK behavior and provider capabilities, and forces developers to maintain local patches for legitimate use cases.

This is especially problematic for applications that intentionally avoid provider-side file storage and rely on inline stateless file inputs such as `input_file.file_data`, for privacy, retention, and infrastructure reasons.

Provider capabilities evolve over time.
A hardcoded SDK allowlist will tend to become outdated and too restrictive.

In practice, this means:
- supported or potentially supported file types cannot be forwarded to the provider
- developers lose access to provider-native file handling
- the only current workaround is patching the SDK locally

# Proposed solution

Please expose an opt-in way to override or extend the SDK file filtering/conversion logic.

Any of the following would solve the problem:

1. a configurable `fileMediaTypeFilter`
2. a provider-level override such as `passThroughUnsupportedFiles`
3. a hook such as `mapFilePart(part) => providerInputPart`
4. a generic fallback mode that forwards non-image file parts as raw provider file inputs instead of rejecting them

The default behavior can remain strict for safety and compatibility, but advanced integrators should be able to opt into pass-through behavior when they know their target provider supports it.

# Expected outcome

The SDK should not force a restrictive allowlist when a provider supports a broader file input model.
Instead, it should offer a safe default plus an explicit escape hatch for advanced use cases.

### Description

When using `streamText` with `@ai-sdk/google-vertex`, the per-modality token breakdown (`promptTokensDetails` and `candidatesTokensDetails`) from Google's usageMetadata is lost during the SDK's internal chunk aggregation.

###   Evidence

Raw Google API streaming response (last chunk via `@google/genai SDK`)

Using generateContentStream directly with the same project/credentials, the last SSE chunk contains full per-modality details:

```
  {
    "promptTokenCount": 6,
    "candidatesTokenCount": 1,
    "totalTokenCount": 12,
    "trafficType": "ON_DEMAND",
    "promptTokensDetails": [
      { "modality": "TEXT", "tokenCount": 6 }
    ],
    "candidatesTokensDetails": [
      { "modality": "TEXT", "tokenCount": 1 }
    ],
    "thoughtsTokenCount": 5
  }
```

Vercel AI SDK streamText result after aggregation

After `await result.usage` and `await result.providerMetadata`:

```
  // await result.usage
  {
    "inputTokens": 3783,
    "outputTokens": 362,
    "totalTokens": 4145,
    "reasoningTokens": 157,
    "cachedInputTokens": 0,
    "raw": {
      "thoughtsTokenCount": 157,
      "promptTokenCount": 3783,
      "candidatesTokenCount": 205,
      "totalTokenCount": 4145,
      "trafficType": "ON_DEMAND"
    }
  }
```

```
  // await result.providerMetadata
  {
    "vertex": {
      "usageMetadata": {
        "thoughtsTokenCount": 157,
        "promptTokenCount": 3783,
        "candidatesTokenCount": 205,
        "totalTokenCount": 4145,
        "trafficType": "ON_DEMAND"
      }
    }
  }
```

`promptTokensDetails` and `candidatesTokensDetails` are absent from both `usage.raw` and `providerMetadata.vertex.usageMetadata`.

### Why it matters

Google charges different rates per modality (e.g., audio input $1.00/1M vs text $0.50/1M, image output $60/1M vs text $3/1M). Without the per-modality breakdown, accurate billing is impossible for streaming multimodal requests.

###   Expected behavior

await `result.usage` (or `providerMetadata`) should include `promptTokensDetails` and `candidatesTokensDetails` arrays when available from the provider, same as `generateText` does via `response.body.usageMetadata`.

title: Bedrock rejects output_config.format on claude-opus-4-7 when SDK uses native structured output
body:
## Description

When calling Anthropic's `claude-opus-4-7` on Amazon Bedrock with structured output (`schema:` / `Output.object`) and reasoning enabled, the request fails with:

```
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"output_config.format: Extra inputs are not permitted"}}
```

This blocks any structured-output use of Opus 4.7 on Bedrock, including reasoning runs.

Related (predecessor) issue: #12298 — that one was about the deprecated `output_format` parameter; the fix flipped `supportsNativeStructuredOutput: true` and renamed to `output_config.format`. The current issue is that the new field is itself rejected by Bedrock for `claude-opus-4-7` specifically.

## Versions

- `ai`: 7.0.0-beta.111
- `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock`: 5.0.0-beta.41
- `@ai-sdk/anthropic`: 4.0.0-beta.37 (transitively)

## Reproduction

```ts
import { bedrock } from "@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock"
import { generateText, Output } from "ai"
import { z } from "zod"

const schema = z.object({
  reasoning: z.string().min(1),
  fileText: z.string().min(1),
})

await generateText({
  model: bedrock("anthropic.claude-opus-4-7"),
  system: "You are a helpful assistant.",
  prompt: "Return reasoning='hello' and fileText='world' per the schema.",
  output: Output.object({ schema }),
  reasoning: "xhigh",
  maxOutputTokens: 8000,
})
```

Tested with `eu.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` (EU cross-region inference profile) — same rejection. The same code with `anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1` works correctly.

## Root cause analysis

In `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock@5.0.0-beta.41`, the Bedrock-Anthropic provider hardcodes `supportsNativeStructuredOutput: true` for every Anthropic-on-Bedrock model:

```js
// packages/amazon-bedrock/src/anthropic/index.ts
{
  // native structured output via output_config.format is supported on Bedrock
  supportsNativeStructuredOutput: true
}
```

Combined with `@ai-sdk/anthropic@4.0.0-beta.37`'s capability table for `claude-opus-4-7`:

```js
if (modelId.includes("claude-opus-4-7")) {
  return {
    maxOutputTokens: 128e3,
    supportsStructuredOutput: true,
    supportsAdaptiveThinking: true,
    rejectsSamplingParameters: true,
    supportsXhighEffort: true,
    isKnownModel: true,
  };
}
```

`useNativeStructuredOutput` resolves to `true`, and the Bedrock chat language model injects:

```js
bedrockOptions.additionalModelRequestFields = {
  ...bedrockOptions.additionalModelRequestFields,
  output_config: {
    ...output_config,
    format: { type: "json_schema", schema: responseFormat.schema }
  }
}
```

…which the Bedrock-via-Anthropic API for `claude-opus-4-7` rejects.

## Suggested fix

Either:

1. Treat `supportsNativeStructuredOutput` as model-specific in the Bedrock-Anthropic provider, mirroring the Anthropic SDK's per-model capability table, and set it to `false` for `claude-opus-4-7` until the API accepts the field.
2. Detect the rejection and fall back to the `jsonResponseTool` path (which the SDK already builds when `useNativeStructuredOutput === false`).

## Workaround

Switch to `anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1` — its capability entry in the Anthropic SDK has the same `supportsStructuredOutput: true` and `supportsAdaptiveThinking: true`, and the Bedrock API accepts `output_config.format` for it.

title: Vertex priority service tier + labels not propagated (direct provider rejects "priority", Gateway BYOK drops both)
body:
### Description

We have a Google Cloud organization that was granted access to Vertex AI Generative AI Priority (Provisioned/Priority Pay-as-you-go) — see [Use Priority PayGo with the Python GenAI SDK](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/priority-paygo?hl=pt-br#use_paygo_priority_pt-python_genai_sdk). We are trying to consume it from the AI SDK, both directly via @ai-sdk/google-vertex and through @ai-sdk/gateway with BYOK, and neither path works.

Provider options used:

```
vertex: {
  thinkingConfig: { includeThoughts: true, thinkingLevel: "medium" },
  serviceTier: "priority",
  safetySettings: safetySettingsGemini,
  labels: { model: "chat-editor-light-reasoning" },
} satisfies GoogleGenerativeAIProviderOptions,
```

Bug 1 — Direct @ai-sdk/google-vertex rejects serviceTier: "priority"
When calling Vertex directly (without the Gateway), the request fails with:

```
Error: Invalid value at 'service_tier'
(type.googleapis.com/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.ServiceTier),
"priority"
According to Vertex's REST API the accepted enum values include SERVICE_TIER_UNSPECIFIED / PRIORITY / STANDARD / SPOT (uppercase). It looks like the AI SDK forwards the option as the lowercase string "priority" instead of mapping it to the Vertex enum, so the API rejects it.
```

Expected: serviceTier: "priority" should be translated to the value Vertex expects (e.g. PRIORITY), the same way OpenAI's serviceTier is normalized.

Bug 2 — Gateway BYOK drops both serviceTier and labels for Vertex
With the same providerOptions.vertex block above, but routed through the Gateway:
```

model: gateway("google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview"),
providerOptions: {
  gateway: {
    order: ["vertex", "google", ...],
    only:  ["vertex", "google", ...],
    // BYOK configured on the gateway side
  },
  vertex: { serviceTier: "priority", labels: { model: "..." }, ... },
},
```

The request succeeds, but on the Google Cloud side:

Requests are not billed/scheduled as Priority — they look like regular Standard traffic.
The labels we set never appear on the Vertex request (we use them for cost attribution dashboards in GCP billing; they're empty).
So even though BYOK is wired up and the request reaches Vertex on our credentials, the vertex provider options (at least serviceTier and labels) are not being forwarded by the Gateway to the underlying Vertex call.

**Reproduction**

- Configure Vertex BYOK in the AI Gateway with a project that has Priority PayGo enabled.
- Call generateText/streamText with the snippet above.
- Inspect the actual request hitting Vertex (or the Cloud Billing labels / Priority quota counters): neither service_tier=PRIORITY nor the labels are present.
- Calling the same model directly via @ai-sdk/google-vertex reproduces Bug 1 (the lowercase string is rejected by the API).

**Expected behavior**

- serviceTier: "priority" on the Vertex provider should be translated to the Vertex ServiceTier enum (PRIORITY) and accepted by the API.
- When routing Vertex through the Gateway with BYOK, providerOptions.vertex.serviceTier and providerOptions.vertex.labels should be forwarded to the underlying Vertex request body.

### AI SDK Version

ai: ^6.0.168
@ai-sdk/gateway: ^3.0.104
@ai-sdk/google-vertex: ^4.0.113
@ai-sdk/google: ^3.0.53
Model: google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview (also reproduced with google/gemini-3-flash)
Vertex BYOK credentials are configured on the AI Gateway and confirmed working (regular requests succeed and are billed against our project).

title: `BedrockToolUseSchema` rejects valid `contentBlockStart` events under Zod ≥ 4.4.0
body:
### Description

# `BedrockToolUseSchema` rejects valid `contentBlockStart` events under Zod ≥ 4.4.0 (`input` is missing, not undefined)

## Summary

Every tool call made through `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` fails validation when the project resolves `zod@>=4.4.0`. Bedrock's Converse Stream API does not send `input` on the `contentBlockStart` event for a tool use — only `toolUseId` and `name` — and the JSON args arrive later in `contentBlockDelta` events. The provider's `BedrockToolUseSchema` declares `input: z.unknown()`, which used to accept a missing key but now (under Zod v4.4.0+) requires the key to be present. Result: the very first event of every tool call throws `AI_TypeValidationError`.

## Reproduction

Any tool invocation against a Bedrock model triggers the error. The thrown payload is exactly:

```
AI_TypeValidationError: Type validation failed: Value: {"contentBlockStart":{"contentBlockIndex":0,"start":{"toolUse":{"name":"getNews","toolUseId":"tooluse_3d8KvhYE28U35U1DPMYnLW","type":"tool_use"}}}}.
Error message: [
  {
    "code": "invalid_type",
    "expected": "nonoptional",
    "path": ["contentBlockStart", "start", "toolUse", "input"],
    "message": "Invalid input: expected nonoptional, received undefined"
  }
]
```

The error is reproducible with a ~30 line script that feeds a real Bedrock `contentBlockStart` payload through the provider's schema; the same payload passes under `zod@4.3.6` and fails under `zod@4.4.0`.

## Root Cause

In `amazon-bedrock-chat-language-model.ts` (line ~1075 on the v5 branch; same shape in the v4 stable bundle at `dist/index.mjs:1495`):

```ts
var BedrockToolUseSchema = z.object({
  toolUseId: z.string(),
  name: z.string(),
  input: z.unknown(),   // <- requires the key under Zod v4
});
```

- Under **Zod v3** (and Zod v4 ≤ 4.3.x), `z.unknown()` accepted a missing key — equivalent to `z.unknown().optional()`.
- Under **Zod v4 ≥ 4.4.0**, `z.unknown()` requires the key to be present (`expected: "nonoptional"` when undefined).

Bedrock's wire format never includes `input` on `contentBlockStart`; the args are streamed in subsequent `contentBlockDelta.delta.toolUse.input` chunks. So the schema is incompatible with the protocol it's parsing.

## Versions Affected

This package switched its imports from `"zod"` to `"zod/v4"` at the 3.0.0 boundary, and the schema has been unchanged since:

| Version | Imports from | Schema | Bug under zod ≥ 4.4.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2.2.12` (last 2.x stable) | `"zod"` | `input: z.unknown()` | n/a (zod v3) |
| `3.0.0` → `4.0.98` (latest stable) | `"zod/v4"` | `input: z.unknown()` | yes |
| `5.0.0-beta.46` (latest beta) | `"zod/v4"` | `input: z.unknown()` | yes |

There is no published version of `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` on the v3/v4/v5 line that survives `zod@>=4.4.0`.

## Why this surfaced now

`zod@4.4.0` tightened the semantics of `z.unknown()` in object shapes: a key declared as `z.unknown()` is no longer implicitly optional. This is arguably a regression in a minor release, but until/unless it's reverted upstream, every consumer that relied on the old `z.unknown()` semantics needs to declare `.optional()` (or `.nullish()`) explicitly. The Bedrock provider is one of those consumers.

## Proposed Fix

One-character change — make the field explicitly optional, since the protocol genuinely doesn't send it on this event:

```ts
var BedrockToolUseSchema = z.object({
  toolUseId: z.string(),
  name: z.string(),
  input: z.unknown().optional(),  // or .nullish()
});
```

I verified the fix by patching the installed copy with `patch-package`; the validation passes for real Bedrock `contentBlockStart` events and downstream `contentBlockDelta` parsing is unaffected (it already handles `input` being assembled from deltas).

If there are other `z.unknown()` fields in Bedrock schemas that map to keys Bedrock may legitimately omit, those would benefit from the same audit — `contentBlockStart.start.toolUse.input` is the one I confirmed broken.

## Workarounds for downstream users

Until a fix lands, consumers have to either:

1. Pin `zod` to `^4.3.x` (and add an `overrides` entry to keep transitive resolutions on 4.3.x).
2. Apply a `patch-package` patch that adds `.optional()` to the `input` field of `BedrockToolUseSchema`.

Pinning the provider to `2.2.12` is not a real option because its peerDeps (`zod@^3`, `@ai-sdk/provider@1.1.3`) are incompatible with current `ai` / `@ai-sdk/provider` major versions.

## Environment

- `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock`: 4.0.97 (also confirmed on 4.0.98 and 5.0.0-beta.46)
- `zod`: 4.4.0 (works on 4.3.6)
- `ai`: ^6
- Node.js: any
- Model: Claude (via Bedrock Converse Stream); reproduces on every tool-using model.

### AI SDK Version

- `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock`: 4.0.97 (also confirmed on 4.0.98 and 5.0.0-beta.46)

title: @ai-sdk/mcp: CallToolResultSchema rejects resource_link content parts with zod ≥ 4.4.x
body:
### Description

[CallToolResultSchema](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/%40ai-sdk/mcp%401.0.39/packages/mcp/src/tool/types.ts#L238) in @ai-sdk/mcp only allows `TextContentSchema | ImageContentSchema | EmbeddedResourceSchema` in the tool-result `content` array. The MCP spec defines a fourth variant, resource_link, which my MCP server returns. With zod ~4.3.6 the missing union arm was tolerated as permissive passthrough; with zod >= 4.4.1 it is hard-rejected and the SDK throws "Failed to parse server response" from `callTool()`. The peer-dep range ^3.25.76 || ^4.1.8 permits 4.4.x, so this surfaces on a routine pnpm update. Might in the same family as #14892.

I've fixed it locally with:

```
const ResourceLinkSchema = z
  .object({
    type: z.literal('resource_link'),
    uri: z.string(),
    name: z.optional(z.string()),
    description: z.optional(z.string()),
    mimeType: z.optional(z.string()),
  })
  .loose();

export const CallToolResultSchema = ResultSchema.extend({
  content: z.array(
    z.union([
      TextContentSchema,
      ImageContentSchema,
      EmbeddedResourceSchema,
      ResourceLinkSchema,
    ]),
  ),
  structuredContent: z.optional(z.unknown()),
  isError: z.boolean().default(false).optional(),
}).or(ResultSchema.extend({ toolResult: z.unknown() }));
```

Probably applies to [PromptMessageSchema](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/%40ai-sdk/mcp%401.0.39/packages/mcp/src/tool/types.ts#L302) too I imagine.

`@ai-sdk/mcp@1.0.x` through 1.0.39

title: fix(amazon-bedrock): BedrockToolUseSchema input field breaks with zod@4.4.x
body:
## Description

`BedrockToolUseSchema` in `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` defines `input` as `z.unknown()`:

```ts
var BedrockToolUseSchema = z.object({
  toolUseId: z.string(),
  name: z.string(),
  input: z.unknown()   // ← breaks with zod@4.4.x
});
```

Bedrock's `contentBlockStart` streaming event for tool use sends `toolUse` **without** an `input` field — the input arrives later via `contentBlockDelta`. This worked fine with zod@4.3.x, but zod@4.4.0 changed `z.unknown()` to reject missing keys (previously it accepted `undefined`).

## Error

```
Type validation failed: Value: {"contentBlockStart":{"contentBlockIndex":1,"start":{"toolUse":{"name":"listTriggers","toolUseId":"tooluse_svg9NwuMqvY32G04RMs6vO","type":"tool_use"}}}}.
Error message: [
  {
    "code": "invalid_type",
    "expected": "nonoptional",
    "path": ["contentBlockStart","start","toolUse","input"],
    "message": "Invalid input: expected nonoptional, received undefined"
  }
]
```

## Fix

Change `input: z.unknown()` to `input: z.unknown().optional()` in `BedrockToolUseSchema`.

## Versions

- `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock`: 4.0.98
- `zod`: 4.4.1 (breaks), 4.3.6 (works)

title: @ai-sdk/togetherai image model sends unsupported parameters to non-diffusion models (e.g. google/gemini-3-pro-image)
body:
### Description

## Description
The `TogetherAIImageModel.doGenerate()` method always includes `seed` in the request body, and may spread additional provider options (`steps`, `negative_prompt`) into the body. For non-diffusion models like `google/gemini-3-pro-image` (Gemini 3 Pro Image / Nano Banana Pro), Together AI's API rejects these parameters with:

```
AI_APICallError: Unsupported use of 'seed' parameter. This parameter is not supported for the selected model.
```

```
AI_APICallError: Unsupported use of 'steps' parameter. This parameter is not supported for the selected model.
```


## Reproduction

```ts
import { createTogetherAI } from '@ai-sdk/togetherai';
import { generateImage } from 'ai';

const togetherai = createTogetherAI({ apiKey: '...' });

// This fails with "Unsupported use of 'seed' parameter" or "Unsupported use of 'steps' parameter"
const { images } = await generateImage({
  model: togetherai.image('google/gemini-3-pro-image'),
  prompt: 'A serene mountain landscape',
  size: '1264x848',
});
```

## Root Cause

In [`packages/togetherai/src/togetherai-image-model.ts`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/togetherai/src/togetherai-image-model.ts), the request body always includes `seed`:

```ts
body: {
  model: this.modelId,
  prompt,
  seed, // <-- always included, even when undefined
  ...(n > 1 ? { n } : {}),
  ...(splitSize && { width: parseInt(splitSize[0]), height: parseInt(splitSize[1]) }),
  ...(imageUrl != null ? { image_url: imageUrl } : {}),
  response_format: 'base64',
  ...(togetheraiOptions ?? {}),
},
```

While `JSON.stringify` normally omits `undefined` values, the Together AI API for `google/gemini-3-pro-image` rejects requests containing these diffusion-specific parameters (`steps`, `seed`, `negative_prompt`). Additionally, the Together AI API docs list `steps` with a `default: 20`, which may mean the server applies this default and then rejects it for models that don't support it.

## Expected Behavior

Calling `generateImage` with `google/gemini-3-pro-image` (or other non-diffusion models on Together AI) should succeed without errors about unsupported parameters.

## Suggested Fix

One or more of:

1. **Conditionally include `seed`**: Only add `seed` to the body when it's not `undefined`/`null`:
   ```ts
   body: {
     model: this.modelId,
     prompt,
     ...(seed != null ? { seed } : {}),    // only include when explicitly set
     ...(n > 1 ? { n } : {}),
     // ...
   }
   ```

2. **Model-aware parameter filtering**: Maintain a list of models that don't support diffusion parameters and exclude them accordingly.

3. **Clean the body before serialization**: Strip `undefined`/`null` values from the body object before passing to `postJsonToApi`.



### AI SDK Version

- `@ai-sdk/togetherai`: 2.0.49
- `ai`: 6.0.174
- Together AI model: `google/gemini-3-pro-image`
- Together AI API endpoint: `POST https://api.together.xyz/v1/images/generations`

title: Implement new telemetry APIs in WorkflowAgent
body:
## Context

AI SDK v7 introduced new telemetry APIs that decouple OpenTelemetry-specific APIs from the core functions (#14291). `WorkflowAgent` still needs to adopt those APIs so `@ai-sdk/workflow` uses the same telemetry integration model as the rest of the SDK.

This issue replaces the older WorkflowAgent follow-up for wiring `telemetry` integration listeners in #12164.

## Scope

- [x] Map the new telemetry lifecycle API surface to WorkflowAgent lifecycle points:
  - stream start / finish / error
  - step start / finish
  - model call start / finish / error
  - tool call start / finish / error
  - approval pause / resume where applicable
- [x] Wire telemetry integrations from stable `telemetry` options through `WorkflowAgent` constructor and `stream()` options without exposing OpenTelemetry-specific types from `@ai-sdk/workflow`.
- [x] Call telemetry listeners alongside existing WorkflowAgent callbacks, preserving callback ordering and error behavior.
- [x] Add `includeRuntimeContext` and `includeToolsContext` support for WorkflowAgent telemetry, with safe default behavior and coverage for serialization constraints.
- [x] Align event names and event payload shapes with the latest AI SDK v7 telemetry APIs and ToolLoopAgent where applicable.
- [x] Add focused tests for listener invocation, runtime/tools context inclusion, tool-call telemetry, error paths, and resume/approval paths.
- [x] Update WorkflowAgent documentation and examples if the public telemetry setup changes.


## Plan

- [x] **Add a WorkflowAgent telemetry e2e example.** Create a dedicated `examples/next-workflow` telemetry page or equivalent harness that exercises the full intended telemetry surface first: lifecycle events, model calls, chunks, tool execution, runtime/tools context filtering, approval resume, error handling, and reconnect behavior. Use it to guide and manually verify the implementation work below.
- [x] **Add the public `telemetry` plumbing.** Add `telemetry` to `WorkflowAgent` constructor / `stream()` options, merge options correctly, and keep it type-compatible with AI SDK core.
- [x] **Emit core lifecycle telemetry.** Wire start / finish / error events for stream, steps, and model calls. This gives the basic integration path without tool or approval complexity.
- [x] **Add tool-call telemetry.** Emit tool start / finish / error events, including provider-executed tools where applicable.
- [x] **Add Workflow-specific context controls.** Implement `includeRuntimeContext` and `includeToolsContext`, with tests around serialization and privacy defaults.
- [x] **Handle resume / approval paths.** Add telemetry for approval pause / resume and interrupted workflow continuation. This is the riskiest part and should be isolated.
- [x] **Update docs and examples.** Document the stable behavior once the implementation has settled.

## Related

- Parent Workflow epic: #12164
- Telemetry v7 tracking issue: #14291

title: generateObject: Effect Schema.Class via Schema.standardSchemaV1 returns 400 from provider
body:
## Description

When using the AI SDK's `generateObject` with a [Standard Schema](https://github.com/standard-schema/standard-schema) produced by Effect's `Schema.standardSchemaV1`, the call **fails with a 400 from the provider** if the input is a `Schema.Class`, but **succeeds** if I wrap the class fields with `Schema.Struct(MyClass.fields)` first.

This is surprising because the two should describe the same shape. From the consumer's point of view, both are valid Standard Schemas — only the JSON Schema that gets emitted to the provider differs.

### Minimal repro

A full, runnable repository is here: https://github.com/danielo515/effect-vercel-ai-demo

The relevant file is [`src/index.ts`](https://github.com/danielo515/effect-vercel-ai-demo/blob/main/src/index.ts):

```ts
import { openai } from "@ai-sdk/openai"
import { generateObject } from "ai"
import { Schema } from "effect"

class BettyReviewResult extends Schema.Class<BettyReviewResult>("BettyReviewResult")({
  rating: Schema.Number.pipe(Schema.between(1, 5)),
  summary: Schema.String,
  highlights: Schema.Array(Schema.String),
  recommended: Schema.Boolean,
}) {}

const result = await generateObject({
  model: openai("gpt-4o-mini"),

  // ✅ Works
  // schema: Schema.standardSchemaV1(Schema.Struct(BettyReviewResult.fields)),

  // ❌ Fails with HTTP 400 from the OpenAI API
  schema: Schema.standardSchemaV1(BettyReviewResult),

  prompt: "Write a short review for a cozy neighborhood diner called Betty's...",
})
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the repo above.
2. `direnv allow .` (or `nix develop`) — provides Node 22 + corepack.
3. Add `OPENAI_API_KEY=...` to `.env`.
4. `pnpm install && pnpm start`.

With the class-direct line active, the request fails with 400. Switching to the `Schema.Struct(BettyReviewResult.fields)` line, the same prompt and model return a valid structured object.

### Expected

Either both forms should work, or the SDK should reject the class-based schema up front with a clearer client-side error rather than letting an invalid JSON Schema reach the provider.

### Notes

- Likely the JSON Schema emitted from a `Schema.Class` standard-schema view contains shape (extra properties / class-instance metadata?) that the provider's structured-output validator refuses.
- Wrapping with `Schema.Struct(Class.fields)` strips that and yields an acceptable schema.
- This works fine in ai@6.0.0 but fails on betaq

## AI SDK Version

- ai: 6.0.0-beta.93
- @ai-sdk/openai: 2.0.0
- effect: 3.12.0
- node: 22

title: `tool.toModelOutput` returned `providerOptions` silently dropped, Anthropic `cache_control` never reaches the API
body:
### Description

`tool.toModelOutput` accepts a `providerOptions` field in its return type, but the field is never propagated to the tool-result message part. For the Anthropic provider this means `providerOptions.anthropic.cacheControl` set inside `toModelOutput` doesn't reach the API. As such, prompt caching cannot be enabled for tool-result content via this path.

The field appears in the type, is accepted at runtime, and emits no warning. The bug is silent: usage just reports `cache_creation_input_tokens`: 0 indefinitely and there is no signal that anything is wrong.

**Repro**
Standalone script (no project dependencies): [[gist]](https://gist.github.com/itshuey/27dda5d09e4fee6454da0ea5a87ee506)
```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... npx tsx ai-sdk-issue-repro.ts
```
Two patterns compared side-by-side, same model (`claude-opus-4-1`), same ~2,300-token content:
- B (control) — assistant message with a text content part bearing `providerOptions.anthropic.cacheControl: { type: "ephemeral" }`. Run cold then warm.
- C (bug) — tool whose `toModelOutput` returns a content part with the same `providerOptions.anthropic.cacheControl`. Forces the tool to be called, then runs a follow-up turn against the same conversation history.

**Expected**
Both patterns engage caching. Cold runs report `cache_creation_input_tokens > 0`, warm runs report `cache_read_input_tokens > 0`.

**Actual**
B works:
```
=== B1 cold ===
providerMetadata.anthropic.usage: {
  "cache_creation_input_tokens": 1337,
  "cache_read_input_tokens": 0,
  ...
}
=== B2 warm ===
providerMetadata.anthropic.usage: {
  "cache_creation_input_tokens": 0,
  "cache_read_input_tokens": 1337,
  ...
}
```
C never caches:
```
--- C step 1 (would write cache) ---
providerMetadata.anthropic.usage: {
  "cache_creation_input_tokens": 0,
  "cache_read_input_tokens": 0,
  ...
}
--- C step 2 (would read cache) ---
providerMetadata.anthropic.usage: {
  "cache_creation_input_tokens": 0,
  "cache_read_input_tokens": 0,
  ...
}
```
Inspecting the outbound request body confirms no `cache_control` field is set on the `tool_result` content block.

**Investigation**
The drop site is in the ai package's tool-result part assembly. `createToolModelOutput` returns whatever `toModelOutput` produced (including its `providerOptions`), but the assembled part places it at `part.output`:
```
// packages/ai/src/generate-text/...  (compiled location: ai/dist/index.mjs:4158)
toolContent.push({
  type: "tool-result",
  toolCallId: output2.toolCallId,
  toolName: output2.toolName,
  output: modelOutput,   // ← providerOptions ends up at part.output.providerOptions
});
```
The Anthropic converter reads cache control from `part.providerOptions` and `message.providerOptions`, not `part.output.providerOptions`:

```
// packages/providers/anthropic/src/convert-to-anthropic-messages-prompt.ts:288
const cacheControl =
  validator.getCacheControl(part.providerOptions, {
    type: 'tool result part',
    canCache: true,
  }) ??
  (isLastPart
    ? validator.getCacheControl(message.providerOptions, {
        type: 'tool result message',
        canCache: true,
      })
    : undefined);
```
`providerOptions` declared inside `toModelOutput`'s return value lives one level too deep at `part.output.providerOptions` and never gets read.

Notably, part-level `providerOptions` are supported elsewhere: the denied-tool-approval branch a few lines below the assembly site explicitly sets `providerOptions` on the part for OpenAI's `approvalId`. So the part shape accepts the field, only the `toModelOutput` path fails to populate it.

**Why this matters**
Tool-result caching is the highest-value caching opportunity in multi-step agent loops. Large, stable tool outputs (loaded skills, fetched data, retrieved documents) get re-sent in every subsequent step. Without this path working:

- Anthropic users have to construct synthetic assistant messages by hand to work around it (we have).
- Bedrock-Anthropic users have no workaround — Bedrock rejects top-level `cache_control` with 400: `cache_control`: Extra inputs are not permitted, so `toModelOutput` is the only available mechanism there.

**Versions**
- `ai`: 6.x
- `@ai-sdk/anthropic`: 3.x
- Confirmed identical behavior on `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock 4.x` (delegates to `@ai-sdk/anthropic/internal`; bug location is in the core ai package, not provider-specific)

**Related**
[#5942](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/5942) — providerOptions dropped on user-message parts. Different drop site, same family.
[#12832](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/12832) — Bedrock-Anthropic doesn't accept top-level `cache_control`. Establishes that the `toModelOutput` path is the only viable cache mechanism on Bedrock.

**Not proposing a specific fix**
The right call (propagate `output.providerOptions` to `part.providerOptions`? add a separate `partProviderOptions` field on the return type? remove `providerOptions` from `toModelOutput`'s return type since it's currently inert?) involves API-shape decisions I don't want to prescribe. Happy to draft a PR once a direction is chosen.

### AI SDK Version

- `ai`: 6.x
- `@ai-sdk/anthropic`: 3.x
