title: @ai-sdk/anthropic: `disableParallelToolUse: true` is hardcoded when `structuredOutputMode: 'jsonTool'`, ignores user override
body:
## Summary

When `providerOptions.anthropic.structuredOutputMode: 'jsonTool'` is set, the provider hardcodes `disableParallelToolUse: true` and ignores any user-provided `disableParallelToolUse: false` in `providerOptions.anthropic`. This silently disables parallel tool use for real tools (e.g. `searchDocs` ×3 in parallel), not just for the synthetic `json` tool, with no way to opt back in.

## Affected version

`@ai-sdk/anthropic@3.0.80` (latest, and every 3.x I checked back to 3.0.7).

Behavior is a regression from `@ai-sdk/anthropic@2.0.2`, which always respected `anthropicOptions?.disableParallelToolUse`.

## Source

`packages/anthropic/src/anthropic-messages-language-model.ts` (compiled at `dist/index.js:3637-3650` in 3.0.80):

\`\`\`ts
jsonResponseTool != null ? {
  tools: [...tools ?? [], jsonResponseTool],
  toolChoice: { type: 'required' },
  disableParallelToolUse: true,            // ← hardcoded, user value ignored
  cacheControlValidator,
  supportsStructuredOutput,
} : {
  tools: tools ?? [],
  toolChoice,
  disableParallelToolUse: anthropicOptions?.disableParallelToolUse,
  ...
}
\`\`\`

## Why this matters

\`structuredOutputMode: 'jsonTool'\` isn't a stylistic choice — it's the documented escape hatch for a real streaming bug on the default path.

### The trap

**Without \`jsonTool\`** (default \`'auto'\` / native \`output_format\` path on Claude Sonnet 4.5 / Opus 4.5 / Opus 4.1 with beta header \`structured-outputs-2025-11-13\`):

In \`streamText\` mode the final structured JSON arrives as **one giant text-delta event after 20+ seconds of silence** post-tool-result, instead of token-by-token. We measured a single 3,197-character text-delta in production diagnostics.

Root cause is in the AI SDK's \`createOutputTransformStream\` (\`ai/dist/index.mjs\`): the transform only publishes a text chunk when \`parsePartialOutput\` produces a new parseable result. For deeply nested schemas (e.g. \`{ dataComponents: [...] }\`), \`parsePartialJson\` can't produce a valid partial until the full JSON closes, so every intermediate text-delta is swallowed and the whole buffer is dumped at \`finish-step\`.

Anthropic's HTTP API itself streams \`text_delta\` events fine — confirmed by Anthropic's docs and Vercel's AI Gateway examples. Upgrading \`ai\` (6.0.14 → 6.0.168) and \`@ai-sdk/anthropic\` (3.0.7 → 3.0.71) does NOT fix it — the transform-gate has not changed upstream. Community tracking: #3422, #12427, #12298, #7220, #9351 (all open or recent, multiple reporters, no upstream fix).

**With \`jsonTool\`** (this issue): streaming is smooth, but parallel tool use is silently force-disabled.

### Net effect on consumers

Apps that need streaming structured output on Claude have two doors:
- **Door A** — \`'auto'\` / native path: 20-second silent burst, but parallel tool calls work.
- **Door B** — \`jsonTool\` path: smooth streaming, but no parallel tool calls under any circumstances.

There's no third door, because the user-provided \`disableParallelToolUse: false\` is dropped on the floor on Door B. The only remaining options are a two-call architecture (doubles round-trips, complicates state) or accepting one of the regressions.

This issue is about restoring Door C: smooth streaming **and** parallel real-tool fan-out, by respecting the user-provided \`disableParallelToolUse\` value on the \`jsonTool\` path.

## Repro

\`\`\`ts
const result = streamText({
  model: anthropic('claude-sonnet-4-5'),
  tools: { searchDocs },
  output: Output.object({ schema: z.object({ items: z.array(z.string()) }) }),
  providerOptions: {
    anthropic: {
      structuredOutputMode: 'jsonTool',
      disableParallelToolUse: false,   // ← user opts in to parallel
    },
  },
  prompt: 'Call searchDocs 3 times in parallel with distinct queries.',
});
\`\`\`

Network trace shows \`disable_parallel_tool_use: true\` on the Anthropic request, regardless of the user-provided \`false\`.

## Proposed fix

Respect the user-provided value, defaulting to \`true\` to preserve current behavior:

\`\`\`ts
disableParallelToolUse: anthropicOptions?.disableParallelToolUse ?? true,
\`\`\`

This keeps the safe default (you almost never want the model emitting the synthetic \`json\` tool in parallel with a real tool) while letting users who understand the tradeoff opt in to parallel *real-tool* fan-out.

## Willing to PR

Yes — happy to open a PR if the proposed shape is acceptable. Wanted to file the issue first so the maintainers can weigh in on whether the default should stay \`true\` or whether there's a more nuanced fix (e.g. only hardcode \`true\` on the final step that actually emits the json tool).

title: docs: cookbook and advanced docs still use deprecated `onFinish` in `streamText` after #15245
body:
## Summary

PR #15245 deprecated `onFinish` in favor of `onEnd` for `streamText` (released in `ai@7.0.0-canary.155`), and updated the core docs. However, several cookbook recipes and advanced doc pages were not updated and still show the deprecated `onFinish` callback inside `streamText({})` calls.

## Affected files

| File | Line | Snippet |
|------|------|---------|
| `content/docs/06-advanced/04-caching.mdx` | ~159 | `async onFinish({ text }) {` |
| `content/cookbook/05-node/45-stream-object-record-token-usage.mdx` | ~33 | `onFinish({ usage }) {` |
| `content/cookbook/05-node/46-stream-object-record-final-object.mdx` | ~31 | `onFinish({ usage }) {` |
| `content/cookbook/01-next/73-mcp-tools.mdx` | ~91 | `onFinish: async () => {` |
| `content/providers/01-ai-sdk-providers/03-openai.mdx` | ~394 | `onFinish: () => wsFetch.close()` |

## Expected

All examples that pass `onFinish` directly to `streamText({})` should be updated to use `onEnd` instead:

```diff
- const result = streamText({
-   model,
-   messages,
-   async onFinish({ text }) {
-     await cache.set(key, text);
-   },
- });
+ const result = streamText({
+   model,
+   messages,
+   async onEnd({ text }) {
+     await cache.set(key, text);
+   },
+ });
```

## Note

`toUIMessageStreamResponse({ onFinish: ... })` uses a separate `UIMessageStreamOnFinishCallback` and is **not** affected — no changes needed there.

## Version

Introduced in `ai@7.0.0-canary.155` (PR #15245). Does not affect the stable v6.x line.

title: @ai-sdk/google-vertex sends unsupported functionCall.id/functionResponse.id fields
body:
### Description

`@ai-sdk/google-vertex` serializes AI SDK `toolCallId` values into Vertex native `generateContent` request bodies as `functionCall.id` and `functionResponse.id`.

Vertex native REST rejects those fields before the model responds:

```text
FAILED
AI_APICallError
Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "id" at 'contents[1].parts[0].function_call': Cannot find field.
Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "id" at 'contents[2].parts[0].function_response': Cannot find field.
```

The same AI SDK message history works when a custom `fetch` shim strips only those two fields from the serialized Vertex request body.

### Reproduction

Minimal repro:

https://github.com/onmax/repros/tree/main/ai-sdk-vertex-function-id

```bash
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/onmax/repros.git
cd repros
git sparse-checkout set ai-sdk-vertex-function-id
cd ai-sdk-vertex-function-id
pnpm i
VERTEX_API_KEY=... pnpm repro
```

To inspect the provider request shape without printing credentials, URL, headers, or request parameters:

```bash
VERTEX_API_KEY=... pnpm repro:inspect
```

That prints:

```text
REQUEST_FUNCTION_PARTS
[
  {
    "path": "contents[1].parts[0].functionCall",
    "keys": ["args", "id", "name"]
  },
  {
    "path": "contents[2].parts[0].functionResponse",
    "keys": ["id", "name", "response"]
  }
]
```

Control command:

```bash
VERTEX_API_KEY=... pnpm repro:strip
```

This succeeds after removing only `functionCall.id` and `functionResponse.id` from the outgoing Vertex body.

### Expected behavior

The Vertex provider should preserve AI SDK `toolCallId` semantics internally, but serialize tool-call history in the Vertex-native request shape. In practice, that means omitting `functionCall.id` and `functionResponse.id` for Vertex native REST requests.

### Actual behavior

The provider sends those fields, and Vertex rejects the request.

### Package versions

Verified with latest stable packages:

- `@ai-sdk/google-vertex@4.0.139`
- `@ai-sdk/google@3.0.80`
- `ai@6.0.191`

### Notes

The repro uses a normal AI SDK message history shape: an assistant `tool-call` part followed by a matching `tool-result` part with the same `toolCallId`. The AI SDK troubleshooting docs describe that as the required way to continue after a tool call, so this does not appear to be unresolved tool history.

The Gemini Developer API documents function call/response ids, but the Vertex native `Content.FunctionCall` and `Content.FunctionResponse` REST schemas do not include those fields.
author: onmax

title: `Chat.makeRequest` finally throws on `this.activeResponse!.state` when activeResponse is undefined (should be `?.`)
body:
`Chat.makeRequest`'s `finally` builds the `onFinish` argument as:

```ts
message: this.activeResponse!.state.message,        // packages/ai/src/ui/chat.ts (main: 760)
...
finishReason: this.activeResponse?.state.finishReason,
```

`this.activeResponse` can be `undefined` when that `finally` runs (e.g. a `trigger: 'resume-stream'` request that overlaps another `makeRequest` such that the single shared `this.activeResponse` was already cleared), so the non-null assertion throws:

```
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'state')
  at Chat.makeRequest (packages/ai/src/ui/chat.ts:760)
  at async AbstractChat.resumeStream (packages/ai/src/ui/chat.ts:465)
```

The very next line already guards `finishReason` with `?.`, so the `!` on `message` looks like an oversight.

It's caught (the `finally` wraps `onFinish` in a try/catch → `console.error`), so it's non-fatal — but it trips dev error overlays. It surfaces via `@cloudflare/ai-chat`, which drives client-tool continuations through `resumeStream → makeRequest`, so it fires on every client-tool continuation. Reproduces on `6.0.19x`; not on `6.0.1`.

Suggested fix:

```diff
- message: this.activeResponse!.state.message,
+ message: this.activeResponse?.state.message,
```

Happy to PR if useful.

title: @ai-sdk/google-vertex/maas defaults to global Vertex host that 404s for regional MaaS Llama models
body:
### Description

`createVertexMaas` appears to default to the global `aiplatform.googleapis.com` host:

```text
https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/locations/{location}/endpoints/openapi
```

For Vertex MaaS Llama 4 models, that host returns 404 for us even when `location` is set to the region where the model works. The same request succeeds when the regional Vertex host is used:

```text
https://us-east5-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/locations/us-east5/endpoints/openapi
```

This makes the documented/default provider configuration fail for at least Meta Llama 4 MaaS models.

### Reproduction

```ts
import { createVertexMaas } from '@ai-sdk/google-vertex/maas';
import { generateText } from 'ai';

const project = process.env.GOOGLE_VERTEX_PROJECT!;

const globalHostProvider = createVertexMaas({
  project,
  location: 'us-east5',
});

await generateText({
  model: globalHostProvider('meta/llama-4-maverick-17b-128e-instruct-maas'),
  prompt: 'Reply with exactly ok',
});
```

Observed request URL:

```text
https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/locations/us-east5/endpoints/openapi/chat/completions
```

Observed result:

```text
AI_APICallError: Not Found
statusCode: 404
responseBody: ''
```

Control that succeeds:

```ts
const regionalHostProvider = createVertexMaas({
  project,
  location: 'us-east5',
  baseURL:
    `https://us-east5-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${project}/locations/us-east5/endpoints/openapi`,
});

const result = await generateText({
  model: regionalHostProvider('meta/llama-4-maverick-17b-128e-instruct-maas'),
  prompt: 'Reply with exactly ok',
});
```

### Expected behavior

`createVertexMaas({ project, location: 'us-east5' })` should either:

- use the regional Vertex host for MaaS endpoint requests, or
- document that users must override `baseURL` for regional MaaS models.

### Actual behavior

The provider defaults to the global host and requests fail with 404.

### Package versions

- `@ai-sdk/google-vertex`: `4.0.140`
- `ai`: `6.0.78`
- Node.js: `24.11.1`

title: Safety Report: AI Agent Guardrails Do Not Work — 56-Day Proof (06K Loss)
body:
## AI Guardrails Do Not Work — 56-Day Empirical Proof

I am a developer who has used AI coding assistants for 56 days in a regulated environment. During that time:

- **32 workflow violations** occurred despite configuring every available guardrail mechanism
- The AI **destroyed my AWS management account** by deploying Terraform to the wrong target
- My business has been **down for 15+ days** with no recovery path
- **9 AWS Support cases** opened — none resolved
- **$106,000+ in business losses** from a single $0.03 AI operation

### Guardrails Configured (All Failed)

| Mechanism | Result |
|-----------|--------|
| Agent system prompt with STOP language | Ignored after relogin |
| Workspace rule files | Not enforced |
| MCP server resources | Not enforced |
| Knowledge base indexing | Not enforced |
| Incident documentation | Not read on session start |
| Control documents | Not enforced |
| Violation counter rules | No persistent state |

### The Core Problem

The agent treats workflow rules as **suggestions, not constraints**. There is no mechanism that prevents implementation from starting. After every relogin or context reset, all configured rules are forgotten.

### What Is Needed

1. **Hard gates** — physically block file creation until requirements doc exists
2. **Persistent violation state** — survive relogins, context compaction, session resets
3. **Authorization taxonomy** — "yes" ≠ "approved" — enforce at platform level
4. **Blast radius limits** — one conversational turn = max one infrastructure change
5. **Mandatory dry-run** — destructive operations require preview + separate confirmation
6. **Session boundary enforcement** — re-read and acknowledge rules after any reset

### Evidence

- Full case study: https://gist.github.com/tzb1-ai/4758f2720979a03d773815082486933c
- Paper: https://d18gqyv10pt526.cloudfront.net/white-papers/AI-cost-savings-analysis.md
- Presentation: https://d18gqyv10pt526.cloudfront.net/presentation.html

This is not a feature request. This is a **safety report**. The current architecture of prompt-based governance is fundamentally broken and poses existential risk to businesses using these tools for infrastructure management.

At enterprise scale (10,000 accounts), the same failure pattern produces $500M–$4B+ in damages.

**Prompt-based rules are documentation. They are not enforcement.**

body:
### Description

### Summary

A tool declared with `strict: true` generated a tool call that omitted a required nullable field. The SDK then rejected the call locally with `AI_InvalidToolInputError` before `execute` ran.

The field is not optional in the Zod schema. It is required but nullable, so I expected the generated arguments to include it as `null`.

Model path: AI Gateway -> openai/gpt-5.4-mini

### Tool setup

Tools are created with `strict: true`:

```ts
tool({
  description: def.description,
  inputSchema: def.inputSchema,
  strict: true,
  execute: async (input: unknown) => def.build(input, ctx),
});
```

### Schema


```ts
const RefSchema = z.string().min(1).max(100);

const inputSchema = z.object({
  title: z.string().min(1).max(300),
  description: z.string().max(2000).nullable(),
  parentRef: RefSchema.nullable(),
  content: z
    .object({
      slides: z.array(z.unknown()).min(1),
    })
    .strict()
    .nullable(),
  clientRef: RefSchema.nullable(),
});
```

`clientRef` is intentionally nullable() due to the [mentioned issue](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/troubleshooting/no-object-generated-content-filter) with using optional() or nullish() with openAI . 


### Actual result

The model generated this tool input:

```json
{
  "title": "Example Title",
  "description": "A description.",
  "parentRef": "course",
  "content": {
    "slides": [
      {
        "kind": "custom",
        "background": { "color": "#f8fafc" },
        "elements": []
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`clientRef` is missing.

The SDK rejected it before `execute` ran:

```txt
AI_InvalidToolInputError
Invalid input for tool propose_create_slides: Type validation failed.

[
  {
    "expected": "string",
    "code": "invalid_type",
    "path": ["clientRef"],
    "message": "Invalid input: expected string, received undefined"
  }
]
```

### Expected result

With `strict: true`, I expected the generated tool input to include all required fields.

Is this a bug or should I be approaching this differently? Any workarounds for the time being?

title: Allow dynamic per-call context on tool approval requests (for rich human-in-the-loop cards)
body:
### Summary

When a tool uses `needsApproval`, there is currently no way to attach dynamic, per-call information to the approval request so the UI can render a rich approval card. The only data the client receives in the `approval-requested` state is the tool `input` plus the static `title` and `metadata` defined on the tool. Anything computed at approval time (from the input plus a database or API lookup) cannot reach the card.

### Use case

Consider a `deleteRecords` tool that removes a set of records and everything linked to them. The action is irreversible, so it uses `needsApproval`.

Before the user approves, we want the approval card to show the real consequences computed at approval time, for example:

- "47 records will be deleted."
- "12 of them were modified in the last 7 days."
- "3 of them are referenced by other records that will also be affected."

All of this depends on the tool input plus a live lookup of current data. A generic "Allow deleteRecords?" card is not enough for an irreversible action, because the user cannot give informed consent without seeing what will actually be affected.

### What is missing today

I checked the installed types and source (ai 6.0.190, @ai-sdk/provider-utils 4.0.27):

- `title` and `metadata` on a tool are static. They are copied from the tool definition when the tool call is built, so they cannot carry per-call values.
- `ToolExecutionOptions` and the `needsApproval` function options expose no setter for `title` or `toolMetadata`.
- The `approval` object in the `approval-requested` state contains only `{ id }`.
- `ToolNeedsApprovalFunction` returns only a boolean.

So there is no supported path to send computed context alongside the approval request. This overlaps with #9862 (mid-execution approval), but the core need here is narrower: a way to attach data to the approval request that the UI can read.

### Proposed options

Any one of these would solve it:

1. Let the `needsApproval` function return an object instead of just a boolean, for example `{ approvalRequired: true, metadata: {...} }`, and surface that metadata on the `approval-requested` part.

2. Add an optional `metadata` field to the approval request itself, settable from the `needsApproval` function options, and expose it as `part.approval.metadata` on the client.

3. Provide a writer in the `needsApproval` options (similar to streaming tool data) so the tool can emit a data part that is reliably associated with the same approval request and tool call id.

### Workaround in use

For now we compute the context inside the `needsApproval` function and emit a separate `data-*` stream part keyed by the tool call id, then match it on the client to render the card. This works but it is a side channel. The association between the approval request and its context lives in our own keying convention rather than in the SDK, so it is easy to get wrong and does not survive cleanly through history reload without extra handling. A first class field would remove that fragility.

### Environment

- ai 6.0.190
- @ai-sdk/provider-utils 4.0.27

title: convertToModelMessages crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'reason')" for output-denied tool part without approval
body:
## Description

`convertToModelMessages` throws when a tool part is in the `output-denied` state but has no `approval` object:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'reason')
```

A tool part can legitimately be in `output-denied` without an `approval` field — for example when denied tool history is **persisted and rehydrated from storage** (the `approval` request/response parts are not always round-tripped with the result). The `output-denied` branch dereferences `toolPart.approval.reason` directly, with no optional chaining:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/ai/src/ui/convert-to-model-messages.ts

```ts
case 'output-denied': {
  content.push({
    type: 'tool-result',
    toolCallId: toolPart.toolCallId,
    toolName: getToolName(toolPart),
    output: {
      type: 'error-text' as const,
      value:
        toolPart.approval.reason ??   // <-- throws when `approval` is undefined
        'Tool call execution denied.',
    },
    ...
```

The adjacent approval-response branch already guards with `toolPart.approval?.approved`, so only this `output-denied` line is missing the guard.

## Reproduction

```ts
import { convertToModelMessages } from 'ai';

const messages = [
  { role: 'user', parts: [{ type: 'text', text: 'hi' }] },
  {
    role: 'assistant',
    parts: [
      {
        type: 'tool-myTool',
        toolCallId: 'call_1',
        state: 'output-denied',
        input: { foo: 'bar' },
        output: { type: 'execution-denied' },
        // note: no `approval` field
      },
    ],
  },
];

convertToModelMessages(messages);
// TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'reason')
```

## Expected

`output-denied` parts without an `approval` should fall back to the default `'Tool call execution denied.'` message instead of crashing.

## Environment

- `ai` 6.0.49 (also present in latest `6.0.195` and `7.0.0-canary.*` — same unguarded line).
- Node 22.

## Suggested fix

Use optional chaining: `toolPart.approval?.reason ?? 'Tool call execution denied.'`. PR incoming.
author: Awaisryk

title: @ai-sdk/openai-compatible reuses txt-0 text part ID across TEXT -> TOOL -> TEXT streams
body:
### Description

`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` appears to reuse the same synthetic text part ID (`txt-0`) for separate text segments in a multi-step tool-calling stream.

When an OpenAI-compatible chat stream produces text before a tool call and then more text after the tool result, the outer stream can contain separate text parts with the same ID:

```text
start
start-step
text-start id=txt-0
text-delta id=txt-0  "I'll check that..."
tool-input-start ...
tool-input-end ...
tool-call ...
text-end id=txt-0
finish-step reason=tool-calls
start-step
text-start id=txt-0
text-delta id=txt-0  "Done, here's the result..."
text-end id=txt-0
finish-step reason=stop
finish
```

This is similar to #10781, but the duplicated ID is not a numeric provider content index such as `0` or `1`. It is the OpenAI-compatible adapter's own synthetic string ID, `txt-0`.

### Why this matters

Some UI/message adapters use text part IDs to preserve and update text parts. When two separate text segments in the same assistant response share `txt-0`, those adapters can merge the text before and after the tool call into one text part.

In an inline tool-call UI, this can visually turn:

```text
[text before tool]
[tool call / tool result]
[text after tool]
```

into:

```text
[text before tool + text after tool]
[tool call / tool result]
```

The tool card then appears to sink below the final assistant text, even though the stream order was text -> tool -> text.

We observed this through Mastra's official React adapter (`@mastra/react` `toUIMessage`), which tracks text parts by `textId`. Mastra already has a workaround for numeric duplicate IDs from Anthropic/Google providers, but it does not catch `txt-0` because this ID is a non-numeric string.

### Current implementation shape

In `packages/openai-compatible/src/chat/openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts` for `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible@2.0.48`, the chat adapter:

- emits `text-start` with `id: 'txt-0'` when the first `delta.content` arrives
- emits all `text-delta` chunks with `id: 'txt-0'`
- emits `text-end` with `id: 'txt-0'` only during stream flush

OpenAI-compatible chat completion deltas do not appear to expose a native content block ID, so a synthetic ID makes sense. The issue is that the same synthetic ID is reused for later model steps / later text segments in the same outer tool-calling stream.

### Expected behavior

Each separate text segment in a single outer `streamText().fullStream` session should get a distinct text part ID, especially across tool-call step boundaries.

For example:

```text
text-start id=txt-0
text-delta id=txt-0
text-end id=txt-0
tool-call ...
text-start id=txt-1
text-delta id=txt-1
text-end id=txt-1
```

or another unique/session-stable ID scheme. The important property is that separate text parts should not share the same ID when downstream UI/persistence layers need to preserve part order.

### Actual behavior

The adapter reuses `txt-0`, so downstream consumers can treat the pre-tool and post-tool text as one text stream.

### Related issues

- #10781 reports duplicate text IDs in multi-step flows for Anthropic/Google provider IDs.
- #10755 reports related `openai-compatible` text/reasoning end timing concerns.
- mastra-ai/mastra#9909 shows the same class of text/tool ordering issue surfacing in Mastra storage/UI.

### Environment

- `ai`: `5.0.193`
- `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`: `2.0.48`
- Observed with an OpenAI-compatible chat model used through Mastra:
  - `@mastra/core`: `1.37.1`
  - `@mastra/react`: `0.4.2`

title: Raw `JSON.parse` used in production provider code (prototype pollution risk)
body:
### Description

Several production provider files use `JSON.parse` directly instead of the SDK's `secureJsonParse` utility from `@ai-sdk/provider-utils`. This violates the project coding standard and leaves a prototype pollution vector open on tool call inputs that flow from LLM responses.

The root problem is that `secureJsonParse` — the synchronous safe parser in `packages/provider-utils/src/secure-json-parse.ts` — is **not exported** from `@ai-sdk/provider-utils`. Because `parseJSON`/`safeParseJSON` are async and these call sites are synchronous, providers have no way to use the secure variant without importing from an internal path.

## Affected files

| File | Line | Context |
|------|------|---------|
| `packages/google/src/interactions/convert-to-google-interactions-input.ts` | 379 | `safeParseToolArgs` — parses tool call input strings from LLM responses |
| `packages/google/src/convert-to-google-messages.ts` | 471 | Parses `part.input` (tool call args) when converting to Google format |
| `packages/anthropic/src/convert-to-anthropic-prompt.ts` | 51 | `extractErrorValue` — parses provider tool error result values |
| `packages/anthropic/src/convert-to-anthropic-prompt.ts` | 847 | Parses `output.value` from code execution error results |
| `packages/anthropic/src/anthropic-language-model.ts` | 2108 | Parses `contentBlock.input` for `code_execution` tool detection |
| `packages/gateway/src/errors/extract-api-call-response.ts` | 9 | Parses `error.responseBody` from API error responses |

## Why this matters

`secureJsonParse` guards against prototype pollution by checking for `__proto__` and `constructor.prototype` keys before returning the parsed value. Tool call inputs arrive from LLM model responses, which can be manipulated via prompt injection. A crafted payload like `{"__proto__": {"polluted": true}}` would pass through raw `JSON.parse` silently.

## Proposed fix

**Step 1** — export `secureJsonParse` from `packages/provider-utils/src/index.ts`:
```ts
export { secureJsonParse } from './secure-json-parse';
```

**Step 2** — replace `JSON.parse(...)` with `secureJsonParse(...)` at all six locations. Each site is already wrapped in a `try/catch`, so error handling stays the same.

Example (`packages/google/src/interactions/convert-to-google-interactions-input.ts`):
```ts
// Before
const parsed = JSON.parse(input);

// After
import { secureJsonParse } from '@ai-sdk/provider-utils';
const parsed = secureJsonParse(input);
```

### AI SDK Version

Reproduced on latest main (post-6.0.168).
Affected packages: @ai-sdk/google, @ai-sdk/anthropic, @ai-sdk/gateway, @ai-sdk/provider-utils (all latest)

title: Vertex `gemini-embedding-2` fails with 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION (embedding model only calls `:predict`, not `:embedContent`)
body:
### Description

## Summary

  After #15582 / #15587 added `gemini-embedding-2` as a recognized model id, calling it through the Vertex provider still fails at runtime. Every embedding request from `GoogleVertexEmbeddingModel` is
  sent to the legacy `:predict` endpoint, but Google has **dropped `:predict` support for the `gemini-embedding-2` family** — those models are only reachable via `:embedContent`. The result is a `400
  FAILED_PRECONDITION` for any `gemini-embedding-2` / `gemini-embedding-2-preview` call.

  So #15582 registered the model id, but the model still can't actually be used through the Vertex provider. `gemini-embedding-001` is unaffected because it does support `:predict`.

  ## Reproduction

  ```ts
  import { createVertex } from "@ai-sdk/google-vertex"
  import { embed } from "ai"

  const vertex = createVertex({
    project: "YOUR_PROJECT",
    location: "global", // also fails on any other region
    googleAuthOptions: { /* service-account credentials */ },
  })

  await embed({
    model: vertex.embeddingModel("gemini-embedding-2"),
    value: "hello world",
    providerOptions: { vertex: { outputDimensionality: 1024 } },
  })
  ```

  ## Actual result

  ```
  AI_APICallError: Precondition check failed.
    url: https://aiplatform.us.rep.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT/locations/us/publishers/google/models/gemini-embedding-2:predict
    statusCode: 400
    responseBody: {
      "error": {
        "code": 400,
        "message": "Precondition check failed.",
        "status": "FAILED_PRECONDITION"
      }
    }
    isRetryable: false
  ```

  The request reaches the correct endpoint and authenticates — Google rejects it specifically because `gemini-embedding-2:predict` is not a supported operation.

  ## Root cause

  `GoogleVertexEmbeddingModel.doEmbed` always builds the `:predict` URL, with no `:embedContent` path for the newer embedding models:

  ```js
  // @ai-sdk/google-vertex/dist/index.js (4.0.142)
  const url = `${this.config.baseURL}/models/${this.modelId}:predict`;
  ```

  (Source: `packages/google-vertex/src/google-vertex-embedding-model.ts`.)

  - `gemini-embedding-001` → `:predict` ✅ works (but only available on gobal multi region)
  - `gemini-embedding-2` / `gemini-embedding-2-preview` → `:predict` ❌ `FAILED_PRECONDITION`; only `:embedContent` works

  The same defect was diagnosed in LiteLLM for the identical model/endpoint combination: BerriAI/litellm#23508 ("gemini-embedding-2-preview routes to `:predict`, returns FAILED_PRECONDITION"). The 
  model works fine through the GenAI `embed_content` API.

  ## Expected behavior

  `vertex.embeddingModel("gemini-embedding-2")` should successfully return embeddings — i.e. the Vertex embedding model should route the `gemini-embedding-2` family to `:embedContent` instead of
  `:predict` (mapping `outputDimensionality` / `taskType` / `autoTruncate` to the `:embedContent` request shape).

### AI SDK Version

  - ai: 6.0.197
  - @ai-sdk/google-vertex: 4.0.142
  - @ai-sdk/google: 3.0.80
  - @ai-sdk/provider-utils: 4.0.27
  - @ai-sdk/provider: 3.0.10

title: `fixJson` emits invalid JSON when a streamed value is truncated inside a `\uXXXX` unicode escape
body:
### Description

`fixJson` (`packages/ai/src/util/fix-json.ts`) repairs partial JSON during streaming so that `parsePartialJson` can recover a value from each incremental chunk. It correctly handles a truncated escape that ends on a lone backslash (`"abc\` → `"abc"`), but it does **not** handle a truncation inside a unicode escape sequence (`\uXXXX`). When the input ends after `\u` but before all four hex digits are present, `fixJson` closes the string with the partial escape still in place, producing **invalid JSON**.

As a result, `parsePartialJson` returns `failed-parse` and the partial value is dropped for that chunk — the object/field flickers or disappears mid-stream until the next chunk completes the escape.

## Reproduction

```ts
import { fixJson } from 'ai/src/util/fix-json'; // internal util

fixJson('{"a":"\\u');      // => '{"a":"\\u"}'   ❌ JSON.parse throws
fixJson('{"a":"\\u12');    // => '{"a":"\\u12"}' ❌ JSON.parse throws
fixJson('{"a":"text \\u00'); // => '{"a":"text \\u00"}' ❌ JSON.parse throws
```

Each repaired string fails `JSON.parse` with `Bad Unicode escape`. Compare with the trailing-backslash case, which is handled correctly:

```ts
fixJson('"value with \\'); // => '"value with "'  ✅
```

Reachable in practice through `streamObject`, structured output, and streaming tool-call inputs: any time a provider's SSE chunk boundary lands between `\u` and its four hex digits (common for emoji/CJK content, which the SDK already escapes as `😀`-style surrogate pairs).

## Root cause

In the `INSIDE_STRING_ESCAPE` state, every escaped character — including `u` — immediately advances `lastValidIndex`:

```ts
case 'INSIDE_STRING_ESCAPE': {
  stack.pop();
  lastValidIndex = i; // marks `\u` (and any following hex digits) as "valid"
  break;
}
```

The scanner has no concept that `\u` requires exactly four following hex digits, so a truncated escape is treated as complete and included in the repaired output.

## Expected behavior

`fixJson` should treat a `\uXXXX` escape as valid only once all four hex digits are present. If the input ends earlier, the incomplete escape should be dropped (consistent with how the trailing-backslash case is already handled), so the repaired output is always valid JSON.

```ts
fixJson('{"a":"\\u');   // => '{"a":""}'   ✅
fixJson('{"a":"\\u12'); // => '{"a":""}'   ✅
fixJson('"abc\\u1234"'); // => '"abc\\u1234"' (complete escape preserved) ✅
```

## Environment

- Affected package: `ai` (`fixJson`, consumed by `parsePartialJson` → `streamObject` / structured output / streaming tool inputs)
- Reproduced on latest `main`.


### AI SDK Version

 ai@7.0.0-canary.165

title: subscribeToMessages fails to resubscribe when options.chat changes to a new instance with the same id
body:
### Description

I noticed a potential gap in the subscription logic in use-chat.ts.

At [L97](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/react/src/use-chat.ts#L97), chatRef is correctly updated when options.chat is replaced with a new instance, using reference equality (!==). However, subscribeToMessages at [L111](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/react/src/use-chat.ts#L111) only depends on chatRef.current.id in its useCallback dependency array, with an explicit eslint-disable comment.

This means that when options.chat changes to a different instance with the same id, chatRef.current is updated to the new instance, but subscribeToMessages is not recreated. The callback retains a stale closure over the previous chatRef.current, so calling it will invoke ~registerMessagesCallback on the old chat instance rather than the new one.

## Question

The eslint-disable comment indicates that using chatRef.current.id was an intentional choice. I'd like to understand whether this behavior is by design:

If intentional, what is the expected contract for callers who might replace options.chat with a same-ID instance (e.g., after a reconnection or state hydration)? Should they avoid this pattern, or provide a changed id to force re-subscription?

If this is an oversight, is there openness to addressing it (e.g., with a version counter or updating the dependency array)?

- @ai-sdk/react: 3.0.199

body:
### Description

When using @ai-sdk/google-vertex with Gemini models (e.g. gemini-3.5-flash) via streamText, tool calls work correctly at the LLM reasoning step, but sending the tool result back causes a 400 Bad Request from the Gemini API. Plain text-only responses work fine.

Error message received:

Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "id" at 'contents[1].parts[0].function_call': Cannot find field.
Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "id" at 'contents[2].parts[0].function_response': Cannot find field.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Set up an agent using streamText with @ai-sdk/google-vertex targeting gemini-3.5-flash.
  2. Define at least one tool.
  3. Send a prompt that causes the model to invoke a tool.
  4. Return the tool result to continue the conversation.
  5. Observe 400 from aiplatform.googleapis.com on the second turn.

Environment

Package | Version -- | -- ai | ^6.0.82 @ai-sdk/google-vertex | ^4.0.142 Node.js | 22 Runtime | Node

Error payload

{
  "errorUrl": "https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/publishers/google/models/gemini-3.5-flash:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse",
  "modelName": "gemini-3.5-flash",
  "errorMessage": "Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name \"id\" at 'contents[1].parts[0].function_call': Cannot find field.\nInvalid JSON payload received. Unknown name \"id\" at 'contents[2].parts[0].function_response': Cannot find field.",
  "errorStatusCode": 400
}
  • This only reproduces on multi-turn conversations where a tool call is made and a result is returned — single-turn text-only completions are unaffected.
  • Other providers (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic) are not affected since they accept or require the id field.
  • This may be a regression introduced when normalizing tool call message shapes across providers in the v6 message format.

title: AI Gateway DeepSeek V3.2 metadata appears stale/inconsistent
body:
### Description

AI Gateway's public model catalog and rendered model pages appear to have stale or internally inconsistent metadata for the DeepSeek V3.2 model IDs after DeepSeek's V4 API rollout.

This report is about Vercel AI Gateway model catalog metadata, not an AI SDK client-side runtime error. I am filing it here because `@ai-sdk/gateway` / Gateway issues in this repo use `provider/gateway`, and the Vercel Community forum appears unlikely to reach the catalog owner quickly.

Disclosure: this issue was drafted by GPT-5.5 with human oversight and review.

#### Affected model IDs

- `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2`
- `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2-thinking`

#### What I expected

If these IDs are still active on AI Gateway, the public catalog should clearly distinguish whether they are legacy Gateway routes, third-party-hosted V3.2 routes, or official DeepSeek-hosted routes.

If the `deepseek` provider rows are still active, the `/v1/models` aggregate metadata and rendered model pages should agree on pricing, limits, and provider source.

If official DeepSeek no longer serves these as current API model names, the Gateway catalog should probably mark them as legacy/deprecated, remove the official `deepseek` provider row, or explain the compatibility behavior.

#### What I see

[DeepSeek's current API docs](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news260424#:~:text=Currently%20routing) list the current models as V4-era IDs/aliases, including `deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-chat`, and `deepseek-reasoner`. The compatibility aliases `deepseek-chat` and `deepseek-reasoner` now map to V4 Flash modes and are deprecated aliases until 2026-07-24.

However, AI Gateway still exposes V3.2 IDs as active DeepSeek-owned model IDs in the unauthenticated public models endpoint.

From:

```bash
curl https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models
```

Current relevant excerpts:

```json
{
  "id": "deepseek/deepseek-v3.2",
  "name": "DeepSeek V3.2",
  "context_window": 128000,
  "max_tokens": 8000,
  "pricing": {
    "input": "0.00000028",
    "output": "0.00000042",
    "input_cache_read": "0.000000028"
  },
  "owned_by": "deepseek"
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "deepseek/deepseek-v3.2-thinking",
  "name": "DeepSeek V3.2 Thinking",
  "context_window": 128000,
  "max_tokens": 8000,
  "pricing": {
    "input": "0.00000062",
    "output": "0.00000185"
  },
  "owned_by": "deepseek"
}
```

The rendered Vercel pages are:

- https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/deepseek-v3.2
- https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/deepseek-v3.2-thinking

Those pages list multiple providers, including a `DeepSeek` provider row for both V3.2 IDs.

The page for `deepseek-v3.2-thinking` shows the `DeepSeek` provider row at roughly:

- input: `$0.28/M`
- output: `$0.42/M`
- cache read: `$0.03/M`

But `/v1/models` returns aggregate pricing for `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2-thinking` as:

- input: `0.00000062` per token (`$0.62/M`)
- output: `0.00000185` per token (`$1.85/M`)

That appears to match the Bedrock endpoint pricing, not the DeepSeek provider row.

The per-provider endpoint API shows the mismatch more directly:

```bash
curl https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models/deepseek/deepseek-v3.2-thinking/endpoints
```

It currently includes, among others:

```json
{
  "provider_name": "bedrock",
  "pricing": {
    "prompt": "0.00000062",
    "completion": "0.00000185"
  },
  "max_completion_tokens": 8000
}
```

and:

```json
{
  "provider_name": "deepseek",
  "pricing": {
    "prompt": "0.00000028",
    "completion": "0.00000042",
    "input_cache_read": "0.000000028"
  },
  "max_completion_tokens": 64000,
  "tags": ["reasoning", "tool-use", "implicit-caching"]
}
```

So the rendered page appears to present the DeepSeek row price, while `/v1/models` appears to expose Bedrock-like aggregate pricing for the same `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2-thinking` ID.

For `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2`, `/v1/models` matches the DeepSeek endpoint price, but the same lifecycle concern remains: the model page still describes V3.2 as a current DeepSeek model on Gateway, while DeepSeek's current public API docs appear to have moved current official API usage to V4 models and V4-compatible aliases.

#### Why this matters

Downstream model catalogs and integrations consume `https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models` as the machine-readable Gateway source of truth. For example, models.dev syncs Vercel provider data from that endpoint. This means any stale lifecycle data or aggregate price mismatch in AI Gateway propagates downstream as apparently authoritative billing/model metadata.

This is especially confusing because Vercel advertises AI Gateway as no-markup provider pricing. If the model ID is still a valid Vercel route but no longer a current official DeepSeek API model name, that distinction needs to be visible in the catalog metadata.

#### Questions / requested clarification

- Are `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2` and `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2-thinking` still routed to official DeepSeek, or only to third-party providers?
- If official DeepSeek no longer serves these exact model IDs as current public API models, should the `deepseek` provider endpoint rows be removed, marked legacy, or mapped/documented as compatibility routes?
- Should the model pages mention that DeepSeek's current API aliases now route to V4 Flash modes?
- For `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2-thinking`, should `/v1/models` aggregate pricing be `$0.28/M` input and `$0.42/M` output to match the rendered DeepSeek row, or should the page clarify that the aggregate metadata is using the Bedrock endpoint price?
- Should `/v1/models` expose enough information to identify which endpoint/provider was selected for aggregate pricing?

#### Reproduction / commands

```bash
curl https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models
curl https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models/deepseek/deepseek-v3.2/endpoints
curl https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models/deepseek/deepseek-v3.2-thinking/endpoints
```

Then compare with:

- https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/deepseek-v3.2
- https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/deepseek-v3.2-thinking

#### Possible fixes

- Mark the V3.2 Gateway model IDs as legacy/deprecated if they are no longer current first-party DeepSeek-hosted API models.
- Remove or relabel the `deepseek` provider rows for V3.2 if they are stale.
- Fix `/v1/models` aggregate pricing for `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2-thinking`, or document why it intentionally differs from the rendered provider table.
- Add provider/source information for aggregate pricing in `/v1/models` so consumers can tell whether the aggregate price came from DeepSeek, Bedrock, or another endpoint.
- Update the rendered V3.2 pages to explain the relationship between V3.2, DeepSeek V4, and the compatibility aliases.

### AI SDK Version

Not applicable. This is about AI Gateway public catalog metadata from `https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models` and the rendered AI Gateway model pages, not a local AI SDK package version.

title: @ai-sdk/google does not merge consecutive same-role messages (unlike @ai-sdk/anthropic), causing Gemini alternation errors
body:
> _Disclaimer: this report was drafted by an AI agent and reviewed by a human before posting._

### Summary

`convertToModelMessages` maps UI messages to `ModelMessage`s 1:1, preserving role, so a valid history can contain two consecutive same-role (e.g. `user`) messages. When that history is sent to `streamText`/`generateText`, provider behavior diverges:

- **`@ai-sdk/anthropic`** merges consecutive same-role messages into one block before building the request (`groupIntoBlocks()`), so Anthropic's strict alternation requirement is satisfied automatically.
- **`@ai-sdk/google`** pushes one `{ role: 'user', parts }` per `ModelMessage` with **no** consolidation of adjacent same-role messages (`convertToGoogleGenerativeAIMessages`). The resulting `contents` array has consecutive `user` entries, which the Gemini `generateContent` API rejects:

  > Please ensure that multiturn requests alternate between user and model.

This makes an identical, valid UI message history succeed on Anthropic but fail on Google.

### Why consecutive same-role messages are legitimate

A common case: persisted chat history where an assistant turn failed/was incomplete and is removed, then the user retries. The history then legitimately contains the original user message followed by a new "try again" user message, with no assistant turn between them.

### Versions

- `ai@6.0.191`
- `@ai-sdk/google@3.0.79`
- `@ai-sdk/anthropic@3.0.79`

### Reproduction

```ts
import { generateText, convertToModelMessages } from 'ai';
import { google } from '@ai-sdk/google';

const messages = [
  { role: 'user', parts: [{ type: 'text', text: 'send the report' }] },
  { role: 'user', parts: [{ type: 'text', text: 'try again please' }] },
];

await generateText({
  model: google('gemini-2.5-flash'),
  messages: await convertToModelMessages(messages as any),
});
// → Gemini API error: contents must alternate between user and model
```

The same `messages` array works with `@ai-sdk/anthropic` because it merges the two `user` turns.

### Expected

Consistent cross-provider behavior. Either:

1. `@ai-sdk/google` merges consecutive same-role `contents` (combining their `parts`) the way `@ai-sdk/anthropic`'s `groupIntoBlocks` does, or
2. the role-normalization happens once at the `convertToModelMessages` / core layer so every provider receives an alternating sequence.

### Code references

- `@ai-sdk/google` `convertToGoogleGenerativeAIMessages` — `user` case does `contents.push({ role: 'user', parts })` per message, no merge pass over `contents`.
- `@ai-sdk/anthropic` `convertToAnthropicMessagesPrompt` — `groupIntoBlocks(prompt)` merges consecutive same-role messages.

body:
## Context

I maintain [`@agentkit-js/aisdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@agentkit-js/aisdk), a small package that produces AI SDK `tool()`-shaped objects whose execute path runs inside a WASM kernel (QuickJS / Pyodide / Wasmtime) or a remote microVM, instead of running JS directly in the host runtime. The package declares `ai ^4 || ^5 || ^6` as a peer dep and only uses `tool()` (structurally typed), so it works across the three majors without changes.

I'd like to add a runnable example that shows it in action. Before sending a PR, I want to ask about shape — `@anthropic-ai/sdk`'s docs maintainers ask the same thing on similar PRs and it's saved everyone time.

## What's the right home

I see three plausible places:

1. **`examples/mcp-agentkit/`** — sibling to [`examples/mcp/`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/tree/main/examples/mcp). Risk: `examples/mcp/` uses `experimental_createMCPClient` to *consume* an MCP server, which is a different shape than `tool() + sandbox-kernel`. Calling the new dir 'mcp-*' may be misleading.
2. **`examples/sandboxed-tools/`** — neutral name, doesn't claim MCP framing.
3. **A docs page under [`content/cookbook`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/tree/main/content/cookbook)** — if a runnable directory is too heavy and a recipe is more in line with how AI SDK teaches integrations.

I'd default to option 2 unless you'd prefer a different shape.

## What the example would do

- Build a `ToolRegistry` with two trivial agentkit tools (calculator + string formatter).
- Wrap them in `codeModeTool({ kernel: new QuickJSKernel(), tools })`.
- Run a single message through the AI SDK against `MockLanguageModelV2` (deterministic, no API key needed) showing one `execute_code` call instead of N direct calls.
- Print token counts side-by-side with a direct-tool-use baseline.

Total ~150 LOC + README.

## Why not directly PR

The [community providers page](https://github.com/vercel/ai/tree/main/content/providers/03-community-providers) is explicitly for **Language Model Providers** implementing the V4 spec; that's not us (we're a tool/sandbox runtime, not a model adapter). The `examples/` tree is the right level, but I want a maintainer's nod on placement before sending a directory.

## Token-saving claim, source

Bootstrap-context tokens at N=30 user-defined tools drop to ~14% of direct-tool-use, per [`examples/benchmarks/code-mode-tokens.mjs`](https://github.com/telleroutlook/agentkit-js/blob/main/examples/benchmarks/code-mode-tokens.mjs) in agentkit-js CI. The example would re-print this number from a small in-example computation rather than asserting it.

## Falsifiability

This is part of a [strategy memo](https://github.com/telleroutlook/agentkit-js/blob/main/docs/strategy/2026-06-competitiveness.md) where the test is: if the upstream-adapter packages get zero organic downloads after inclusion, the runtime pitch is wrong and we retire it. A 'no thanks, this isn't a fit for our examples tree' is a legitimate answer.

Happy to send a PR with whichever option you'd accept.

title: Bug: @ai-sdk/google provider serializes file-data tool result as text for non-Gemini-3 models, causing massive token overcount
body:
## Description

When using `@ai-sdk/google` with models like `gemini-flash-lite-latest`, a tool result returned via `toModelOutput` as `file-data` is serialized back to Gemini as a JSON string text part in the legacy tool-result path. This causes PDF base64 data to be tokenized as text, producing massive input token counts and `AI_APICallError` responses such as:

```txt
The input token count exceeds the maximum number of tokens allowed 1048576.
```

### Root Cause

In `@ai-sdk/google`, the provider enables function response parts only for Gemini 3 model IDs:

```js
const isGemini3Model = /^gemini-3[.-]/.test(this.modelId);
const supportsFunctionResponseParts = isGemini3Model;
```

For non-Gemini-3 models, the provider uses the legacy tool result path. In that path, `file-data` falls through to:

```js
parts.push({ text: JSON.stringify(contentPart) });
```

This turns the PDF base64 into text tokens.

### Token Count Evidence

Gemini `countTokens` for a 5-page PDF:

| Format | Total Tokens | Text | Document |
|--------|-------------|------|----------|
| user inlineData PDF | 2,807 | 7 | 2,800 |
| tool functionResponse inlineData PDF | 2,856 | 56 | 2,800 |
| base64 as plain text | 4,065,979 | 4,065,979 | 0 |

A 1-page PDF as text already costs 641,699 tokens, easily hitting the 1,048,576 limit with just a few pages.

### Reproduction

1. Create a tool with `toModelOutput` returning:

```ts
return {
  type: "content",
  value: [
    { type: "text", text: "metadata" },
    {
      type: "file-data",
      data: pdfBase64,
      mediaType: "application/pdf",
    },
  ],
};
```

2. Use `generateText` or `streamText` with `model: google("gemini-flash-lite-latest")`
3. Capture the Google provider request body with a custom provider `fetch`
4. Observe `file-data` serialized as a JSON text part instead of `functionResponse.parts.inlineData`
5. Count tokens with Gemini `countTokens` — the PDF base64 is counted under `TEXT`

Captured request preview for `gemini-flash-lite-latest`:

```json
{
  "text": "{\"type\":\"file-data\",\"data\":\"JVBERi0xLjcK...\",\"mediaType\":\"application/pdf\"}"
}
```

### Expected Behavior

For Google models that support multimodal document input, `file-data` in tool result content should be sent as document/file data where possible, or the SDK should warn/error instead of silently converting binary base64 to a text part.

For Gemini requests that support `functionResponse.parts`, the expected output shape is:

```json
{
  "functionResponse": {
    "name": "catalogSearch",
    "response": { "name": "catalogSearch", "content": "metadata" },
    "parts": [
      { "inlineData": { "mimeType": "application/pdf", "data": "..." } }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Suggested Fix

- Extend `supportsFunctionResponseParts` beyond Gemini 3 if the Gemini API supports `functionResponse.parts` for Gemini 2.5 / Flash Lite models.
- If support is model-specific, add model capability detection or an explicit provider option.
- If unsupported, emit a warning or throw for `file-data` / `image-data` in tool results instead of silently serializing them as text.

## AI SDK Version

- ai: 6.0.197
- @ai-sdk/google: 3.0.80

title: feat(harness): expand first-party sandbox providers (Sprites, E2B, Modal)
body:
## Summary

The harness sandbox-provider abstraction (#15919) is intentionally provider-agnostic, but only two providers ship today: `@ai-sdk/sandbox-vercel` (bridge-capable) and `@ai-sdk/sandbox-just-bash` (local, non-bridge). To avoid tying harness users to a single cloud and to grow the ecosystem, we'd like to add more **first-party cloud sandbox providers**.

This issue proposes three to start — [Sprites](https://sprites.dev/), [E2B](https://e2b.dev/) and [Modal](https://modal.com/) — but the broader goal is an extensible set; others (Daytona, Runloop, Cloudflare, etc.) are reasonable follow-ups under the same pattern.

## Acceptance criteria (what any new provider must satisfy)

The constraint that matters is what **bridge-backed adapters** (`claude-code`, `codex`) need. Both consume a provider identically:

```ts
const wsUrl =
  (await sandboxSession.getPortUrl({ port: boundPort, protocol: 'ws' })) +
  '?agent_bridge_token=' + encodeURIComponent(token);
new WebSocket(wsUrl); // stock `ws` — no custom client, no headers, no init frame
```

So a bridge-capable provider's `getPortUrl` must return a plain `ws`/`wss` URL a stock client dials with no app-level handshake, deliver the appended `?agent_bridge_token=…` query intact to the in-sandbox WS upgrade, and keep the URL stable across reconnect/attach. (`setNetworkPolicy`/`setPorts` are optional and don't gate this.)

> Note: `@ai-sdk/sandbox-just-bash` runs in-process with no network namespace — its `getPortUrl` throws and it supports non-bridge flows only. A new provider that can only do the same is still useful, but won't back the bridge adapters.

## Proposed providers

| Priority | Provider | Package | Bridge support | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Sprites** | `@ai-sdk/sandbox-sprites` | ✅ Native (verified) | `getPortUrl` returns `wss://<name>-<suffix>.sprites.app/` bound to the single proxied `http_port`.  |
| 2 | **E2B** | `@ai-sdk/sandbox-e2b` | ✅ Native (per SDK docs) | `getHost(port)` → `<port>-<sandboxId>.e2b.app`; edge does WS passthrough, unauth by default. `getPortUrl` returns `wss://…` directly. Service must be listening before dial. |
| 3 | **Modal** | `@ai-sdk/sandbox-modal` | ✅ Native (per SDK docs) | `encrypted_ports` + `Sandbox.tunnels()[port].url`, scheme-swapped to `wss://`. L4-transparent. `getPortUrl` must `await tunnels()` (URL known only at runtime); use `encrypted_ports`, not `h2_ports`. |

Each follows the `@ai-sdk/sandbox-vercel` shape. E2B and Modal are assessed from SDK docs and should be confirmed with a live `101` test like the one run for Sprites.

## References

- #15919 — harness sandbox-provider abstraction
- Bridge requirement: `packages/harness-claude-code/src/claude-code-harness.ts:483-487`, `:1054`; in-sandbox auth `packages/harness/src/bridge/index.ts:618-623`
- Reference `getPortUrl`: `packages/sandbox-vercel/src/vercel-network-sandbox-session.ts:43-69`

title: feat(harness): surface structured output (output schema) on HarnessAgent
body:
### Description

**Summary**

`HarnessAgent` (`@ai-sdk/harness`) does not expose a structured-output path. Its `OUTPUT` type parameter is pinned to `never`, so `generate()`/`stream()` cannot accept an `output` schema and always resolve to text-only results, even though the underlying runtimes it wraps (Claude Code, Codex) both support schema-guided output natively. This forces consumers to hand-parse JSON out of free-form `result.text`, losing the type safety and runtime validation that `streamText`/`ToolLoopAgent` provide via `output`.

**Where it's pinned**

The `Agent` contract carries an `OUTPUT extends Output` generic, but `HarnessAgent` implements it as `never`. As a result, `AgentCallParameters` exposes no `output` field for harness calls (`HarnessAgentCallExtensions` only adds `session`), and `GenerateTextResult<..., never>` makes `result.output` / `experimental_output` resolve to `never`. There is no call-site or constructor option to opt into structured output.

**The capability already exists one layer down**

- `@ai-sdk/harness-claude-code` wraps the Claude Agent SDK, which supports `outputFormat: { type: "json_schema", schema }`.
- `@ai-sdk/harness-codex` wraps `@openai/codex-sdk`, whose `TurnOptions` already includes `outputSchema` ("JSON schema describing the expected agent output"), returning JSON in `Turn.finalResponse`.

So the harness contract is discarding a feature both adapters' runtimes natively expose.

**Expected**

`HarnessAgent` accepts an `output` (e.g. `Output.object({ schema })`) on `generate()`/`stream()` the way `ToolLoopAgent` does, threads the `OUTPUT` generic through, maps it to each adapter's native schema enforcement (Claude `outputFormat: json_schema`; Codex `outputSchema` plus validation of `finalResponse`), and surfaces a typed `result.output` / `experimental_partialOutputStream`. Adapters that cannot enforce a schema could fall back to documented best-effort parsing or report an unsupported-capability warning.

**Why it matters**

Staged agent pipelines (triage, plan, implement, review, judge/aggregator steps, routing) depend on validated structured decisions, not free text. Without `output`, the harness is not a drop-in alternative to the model/`ToolLoopAgent` path for these use cases, despite the runtimes being capable. This is the one gap that cannot be worked around in user code without reintroducing exactly the brittle JSON-scraping the `output` API was designed to remove.

Related: #15496 (harness abstraction tracking issue).

### AI SDK Version

```
- ai: 7.0.0-canary.173
- @ai-sdk/harness: 1.0.0-canary.9
- @ai-sdk/harness-claude-code: 1.0.0-canary.5
- @ai-sdk/harness-codex: 1.0.0-canary.5
- @ai-sdk/sandbox-vercel: 1.0.0-canary.9
```

title: @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock: strict on tools rejected by Bedrock Messages API for Claude Opus 4.7/4.8
body:
When using `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` with Claude Opus 4.7 or 4.8 on Bedrock's Messages API (`invoke-model`), structured output via `Output.object()` / `Output.array()` fails with:

```
tools.0.custom.strict: Extra inputs are not permitted
```

## Root Cause

The `strict` field was added to `prepareTools` in response to #12766. In `bedrock-prepare-tools.ts` line 143:

```typescript
...(tool.strict != null ? { strict: tool.strict } : {}),
```

This passes `strict: true` into the tool spec. However, Bedrock's Messages API for Opus 4.7/4.8 does not accept this field and rejects the request with HTTP 400.

Note: The Converse API does support `strict`, but `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` uses the Messages API.

AWS docs confirm: _"Claude Opus 4.7 does not accept strict: true on tools[] and returns tools.0.custom.strict: Extra inputs are not permitted"_ — [source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/count-tokens.html)

## Reproduction

1. Use `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock@4.0.112` (or any version with the #12766 fix)
2. Call `generateText` with `Output.object({ schema })` targeting `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` or `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`
3. Request fails with HTTP 400:

```json
{
  "message": "The model returned the following errors: tools.0.custom.strict: Extra inputs are not permitted"
}
```

## Expected Behavior

The Bedrock provider should either:

1. Strip `strict` from tool specs when using the Messages API (since it's not supported for these models)
2. Only pass `strict` for models/API paths that accept it

## Workaround

Patch `bedrock-prepare-tools.ts` to remove the `strict` passthrough line.

title: [Bug] @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock: normalizeToolCallId truncation causes duplicate tool-call IDs (Bedrock ValidationException) for Mistral models
body:
### Description

Follow-up / regression from #11802 (fixed by #11863).

#11863 added `normalizeToolCallId()` so Bedrock tool-call IDs satisfy Mistral's `^[a-zA-Z0-9]{9}$` requirement, by stripping non-alphanumeric characters and taking the **first 9**:

```ts
const alphanumericChars = toolCallId.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, '');
return alphanumericChars.slice(0, 9);
```

Bedrock generates tool-call IDs of the form `tooluse_<random>` (e.g. `tooluse_bpe71yCfRu2b5i-nKGDr5g`). After stripping `_`/`-`, the first 9 characters are always `tooluse` (7 fixed chars) **+ 2 variable chars**. So normalization preserves only ~2 characters of entropy (62² = 3,844 possible values) — the high-entropy random suffix is discarded.

With several tool calls in a conversation (especially parallel tool calls in one turn), two distinct Bedrock IDs collide to the same normalized ID (birthday paradox). The request then contains two `toolUse` blocks with the same `toolUseId`, and Bedrock rejects it:

```
ValidationException: The toolUse blocks at messages.2.content contain duplicate Ids: tooluseAc
```

Observed in production with Ministral on Bedrock. A single assistant turn with 8 parallel tool calls produced these normalized IDs:

```
tooluseqr, tooluseY3, tooluseAc, tooluseP3, tooluseIx, tooluseV0, tooluse7r, tooluseAc
```

Note `tooluseAc` appears twice. Every ID is `tooluse` + 2 chars, confirming only the first 2 random characters survive.

### Why it surfaces on a later turn

`normalizeToolCallId` is applied on both the response path (`doGenerate` / `doStream`, mapping `toolUse` → tool-call output) and the request path (`convert-to-amazon-bedrock-chat-messages`, both `toolUse` and `toolResult`). The truncated IDs are returned to the caller and persisted; the next turn rebuilds the request from history and the collision surfaces as the duplicate-ID 400. Because it's a birthday collision in a ~3,844-value space, it only appears once enough tool calls accumulate — which is why single-tool tests don't catch it.

### Reproduction (unit level)

```ts
import { normalizeToolCallId } from '@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock';

// Two distinct Bedrock IDs that share the first 9 alphanumeric characters:
const a = normalizeToolCallId('tooluse_Ac1Xq9ZklmNoPq', true); // 'tooluseAc'
const b = normalizeToolCallId('tooluse_Ac2Yt7WrstUvWx', true); // 'tooluseAc'
a === b; // true  ->  duplicate toolUseId  ->  Bedrock ValidationException
```

### Root cause

`slice(0, 9)` of the alphanumeric string keeps the constant `tooluse` prefix and discards the entropy-bearing suffix. Any normalization that maps long Bedrock IDs into Mistral's 9-char space must use the full 9-char space (62⁹ ≈ 1.35 × 10¹⁶), not the first 9 characters.

### Proposed fix

Map the **full** original ID deterministically into 9 alphanumeric characters via a hash, instead of truncating:

- **Collision-resistant** — ~53 bits of entropy vs. the current ~12 bits.
- **Deterministic** — required, because the normalized ID is returned to the caller, persisted, and re-normalized on the request path; a tool call and its matching tool result must always map to the same value. (A *random* regeneration — as some external workarounds do, e.g. [this one](https://huggingface.co/spaces/arterm-sedov/cmw-copilot/blob/main/docs/MISTRAL_TOOL_CALL_ID_FIX.md) — fixes the collision but breaks call/result pairing unless paired with a per-request ID registry, which this stateless per-ID normalizer does not have.)
- **Idempotent** on already-normalized (9-char) IDs, so round-tripping is stable.

PR: #16183 — https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/16183

### Affected versions

`@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` — current `latest` (4.0.116), `ai-v6` tag, and `main` all contain the unchanged `slice(0, 9)`. Models: `mistral.*` / `us.mistral.*` on Bedrock (observed with Ministral).

title: AI Gateway: `cohere/embed-v4.0` intermittently ignores `outputDimension` (returns 1536 instead of requested 512)
body:
### Summary

When requesting reduced-dimension embeddings from `cohere/embed-v4.0` through the AI Gateway, the gateway **intermittently** ignores the requested output dimension and returns the model's native **1536**-dim vector instead of the requested **512** (or 256/1024). The *same byte-identical request* returns the correct dimension in some windows and 1536 in others, toggling regardless of request shape — sometimes for sustained windows of many consecutive calls.

This is distinct from #8278 (which fixed the AI SDK *forwarding* `providerOptions` for `embed()`): here the client forwards the option correctly and the failure is server-side and specific to Cohere.

### Environment

- `ai@6.0.134`
- `@ai-sdk/gateway@3.0.114`
- Model: `cohere/embed-v4.0` via the Gateway (no `@ai-sdk/cohere` installed — `providerOptions.cohere` is forwarded by the gateway)

### Reproduction

Both the typed SDK path and the OpenAI-compatible REST path reproduce it.

**AI SDK:**

```ts
import { embed } from 'ai';
import { createGateway } from '@ai-sdk/gateway';

const gateway = createGateway({ apiKey: process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY });
const { embedding } = await embed({
  model: gateway.textEmbeddingModel('cohere/embed-v4.0'),
  value: 'hello world',
  providerOptions: { cohere: { outputDimension: 512, inputType: 'search_document' } },
});
console.log(embedding.length); // expected 512; intermittently 1536
```

**OpenAI-compatible REST (same result):**

```bash
curl -s https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"cohere/embed-v4.0","input":"hello world","dimensions":512}' \
  | jq '{model, dim: (.data[0].embedding | length)}'
# -> {"model":"cohere/embed-v4.0","dim":1536}   (intermittently 512)
```

Run the curl repeatedly: the returned `dim` toggles between 512 and 1536 across calls with an unchanged request body. We've observed sustained windows of 6+ consecutive 1536 responses, and separate windows that correctly return 512 (and 1024 when `dimensions: 1024` is requested).

### Control — the gateway's dimension plumbing works for OpenAI but not Cohere

The identical OpenAI-compat call with an OpenAI embedding model honors `dimensions` deterministically:

```bash
curl -s https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"openai/text-embedding-3-small","input":"hello world","dimensions":768}' \
  | jq '{model, dim: (.data[0].embedding | length)}'
# -> dim: 768   (consistent across calls)
```

So the dimension auto-mapping is wired for OpenAI but appears not to be (reliably) wired for the Cohere provider on the gateway side.

### Notes / evidence the request itself is correct

- The option key is correct: `@ai-sdk/cohere` maps `outputDimension` → Cohere's `output_dimension` (see #12127). CamelCase `outputDimension` works *when the gateway is in a honoring window*; snake_case `output_dimension` in the request never works.
- Fetch-intercepting the SDK confirms it sends `providerOptions.cohere.outputDimension: 512` in the request body **byte-for-byte identically** in both the 512 and 1536 outcomes — the client is not the variable.
- The 1536 responses still report `model: cohere/embed-v4.0` (genuine embed-v4.0 output, not a fallback model).
- All transports tested flip together at the same time (AI SDK `/v3/ai/embedding-model` and OpenAI-compat `/v1/embeddings`; with `dimensions`, `output_dimension`, root-level and nested) — pointing to a single server-side mapping issue rather than a client/API-shape problem.

### Expected behavior

`cohere/embed-v4.0` should deterministically return the requested output dimension (256/512/1024/1536), as it does for OpenAI embedding models.

### Related

- #8278 — AI Gateway: embed() ignores providerOptions when using embedding models (closed/fixed — the client-forwarding case)
- #12127 — fix(amazon-bedrock/cohere): dimension option for cohere embedding models (confirms the `outputDimension` → `output_dimension` contract)

title: @ai-sdk/replicate image model fails when sync-wait returns status:starting with output:null
body:
### Description

`@ai-sdk/replicate` image generation intermittently throws `AI_APICallError: Invalid JSON response` (cause: `AI_TypeValidationError`) when Replicate returns a prediction that is still in progress.

This happens with model `black-forest-labs/flux-dev` during cold starts or when inference exceeds the sync-wait window.

#### Source (where the bug is)

`packages/replicate/src/replicate-image-model.ts` ([v2.0.36](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/caebb44016dbd084e5bf7b7f4ab5194fd2c7c045/packages/replicate/src/replicate-image-model.ts)).

The POST response is destructured directly into `{ output }` with no status check ([L140-L143](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/caebb44016dbd084e5bf7b7f4ab5194fd2c7c045/packages/replicate/src/replicate-image-model.ts#L140-L143)):

```ts
const {
  value: { output },
  responseHeaders,
} = await postJsonToApi({
```

…and validated against a schema that requires `output` to be present ([L206-L208](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/caebb44016dbd084e5bf7b7f4ab5194fd2c7c045/packages/replicate/src/replicate-image-model.ts#L206-L208)):

```ts
const replicateImageResponseSchema = z.object({
  output: z.union([z.array(z.string()), z.string()]),
});
```

There is no polling. The video model in the same package already handles this correctly (see Suggested fix).

#### Expected behavior

When Replicate's sync API (`Prefer: wait`) times out before the prediction completes, Replicate returns HTTP 201 with a valid prediction object (`status: "starting"` or `"processing"`, `output: null`, `urls.get` set). Per [Replicate's docs](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/create-a-prediction#polling), the client should poll `urls.get` until `status` is `succeeded`, then use `output`.

The **video model in the same package already implements this** (`replicate-video-model.ts`: keeps full `prediction`, polls while `starting`/`processing`, uses `replicatePredictionSchema` with `output.nullish()`).

The image model should behave the same way.

#### Actual behavior

`replicate-image-model.ts` posts with `Prefer: wait`, then immediately validates the response and throws. No polling occurs.

Note the response is actually **HTTP 201 (success)** — so this is not an HTTP/transport error, it is the success-path JSON schema rejecting `output: null`. The error message `Invalid JSON response` is misleading; the JSON is valid, the schema is just too narrow.

**Top-level error thrown** (what calling code catches):

```
AI_APICallError: Invalid JSON response
  name:       AI_APICallError
  statusCode: 201
  url:        https://api.replicate.com/v1/models/black-forest-labs/flux-dev/predictions
  cause:      AI_TypeValidationError
```

**Underlying cause** (`AI_TypeValidationError`):

```
Type validation failed: Value: { ... "output": null, ... "status": "starting" ... }
Error message: [
  {
    "code": "invalid_union",
    "errors": [
      [ { "expected": "array",  "code": "invalid_type", "path": [], "message": "Invalid input: expected array, received null" } ],
      [ { "expected": "string", "code": "invalid_type", "path": [], "message": "Invalid input: expected string, received null" } ]
    ],
    "path": ["output"],
    "message": "Invalid input"
  }
]
```

#### Reproduction

```ts
import { replicate } from '@ai-sdk/replicate';
import { generateImage } from 'ai';

await generateImage({
  model: replicate.image('black-forest-labs/flux-dev'),
  prompt: 'A watercolor landscape at twilight',
  size: '1024x1024',
});
```

Intermittent — more likely on cold starts / slow inference. When it fails, the response body (HTTP 201) looks like:

```json
{
  "id": "...",
  "model": "black-forest-labs/flux-dev",
  "status": "starting",
  "output": null,
  "error": null,
  "urls": {
    "get": "https://api.replicate.com/v1/predictions/..."
  }
}
```

#### Suggested fix

Mirror the video model pattern in `replicate-image-model.ts`:

1. Widen `replicateImageResponseSchema` to accept `output.nullish()`, plus `status`, `error`, and `urls.get`
2. Keep the full `prediction` from the POST response (not `{ output }`)
3. Poll `urls.get` while `status` is `starting` or `processing`
4. Use `finalPrediction.output` once `succeeded`

Reference implementation: [`packages/replicate/src/replicate-video-model.ts`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/caebb44016dbd084e5bf7b7f4ab5194fd2c7c045/packages/replicate/src/replicate-video-model.ts) (the `while (status === 'starting' || status === 'processing')` poll loop in `doGenerate`).

#### Related

- Acknowledged gap in #12381 (Replicate image gen may fall back to polling, but the SDK only implements polling for video today)
- Still present on latest published `@ai-sdk/replicate@2.0.36` and on `main` as of June 2026

### AI SDK Version

- `ai`: 6.0.168
- `@ai-sdk/replicate`: 2.0.29 (also verified unfixed in 2.0.36)

title: Gemini 3 parallel function calls: converter injects `skip_thought_signature_validator` + warns every turn (only the first parallel call is signed)
body:
## Summary

When a Gemini 3 model makes **parallel** function calls, only the **first** `functionCall` part carries a `thoughtSignature` (returned under `providerMetadata.vertex.thoughtSignature`). The remaining parallel calls have no provider metadata at all (`providerMetadata = null`).

`convertToGoogleGenerativeAIMessages` checks **every** `tool-call` part individually and, for each one lacking a `thoughtSignature` on a Gemini 3 model, injects the `skip_thought_signature_validator` sentinel and emits a warning:

> Replayed N `functionCall` part(s) for a Gemini 3 model without a `thoughtSignature` (tools: ...). Injected the documented `skip_thought_signature_validator` sentinel to keep the request from failing with HTTP 400. **The likely cause is application code that drops `providerOptions.google.thoughtSignature` when persisting or serializing assistant tool-call messages.**

The warning's suggested cause (application code dropping the signature) is misleading for this case: the application never touches these parts — the missing-signature parts are produced **inside the SDK's own multi-step/parallel-call loop**, and the signature that *does* exist is preserved correctly through `result.response.messages`. There is no signature for the application to preserve on the 2nd+ parallel call because Gemini didn't return one.

## Environment

- `ai@6.0.207`
- `@ai-sdk/google@3.0.83`
- `@ai-sdk/gateway@3.0.133`
- Model: `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite` via the Vercel AI Gateway (`createGateway`)
- Runtime: bun 1.3.14, node platform

## Reproduction

```ts
import { createGateway, stepCountIs, streamText, tool } from 'ai'
import { z } from 'zod'

const gateway = createGateway({ apiKey: process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY! })

const result = streamText({
  model: gateway('google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite'),
  stopWhen: stepCountIs(3),
  tools: {
    get_weather: tool({
      description: 'Get the current weather for a given city.',
      inputSchema: z.object({ city: z.string() }),
      execute: ({ city }) => Promise.resolve({ city, tempC: 21, conditions: 'sunny' }),
    }),
  },
  prompt: 'Use the get_weather tool to check the weather in Paris, then call it again for Tokyo, then summarize.',
})

for await (const _ of result.textStream) { /* drain */ }

console.log(await result.warnings)
for (const step of await result.steps) {
  for (const part of step.content) {
    if (part.type === 'tool-call') {
      console.log(part.toolName, JSON.stringify(part.providerMetadata ?? null))
    }
  }
}
```

## Observed output

```
WARNINGS:
[ { "type": "other",
    "message": "Replayed 1 `functionCall` part(s) for a Gemini 3 model without a `thoughtSignature` (tools: `get_weather`) ..." } ]

TOOL-CALL PARTS:
step[0] tool-call=get_weather thoughtSignature=PRESENT  providerMetadata={"vertex":{"thoughtSignature":"AY89a19xbo4cpN0...="}}
step[0] tool-call=get_weather thoughtSignature=ABSENT   providerMetadata=null
```

The model emitted **two parallel** `get_weather` calls in a single step; the **first** is signed (under the `vertex` namespace), the **second** is not.

## Expected

For Gemini 3 **parallel** function calls (where the model legitimately returns a single thought signature for the batch on the first part), the converter should not treat each unsigned parallel `functionCall` part as a dropped-signature error. Either:

1. Don't inject the sentinel / emit the warning for parallel calls that share a preceding signed part, or
2. Reword the warning so it doesn't point at "application code dropping the signature" when the parts originate from the SDK's own parallel/multi-step loop and no signature was ever returned for them.

As written, any app doing multi-step **or** parallel tool calls with a Gemini 3 model gets this warning on essentially every turn, which is noisy (and, via `captureConsole`-style integrations, becomes a stream of error-tracker issues).

## Question for maintainers

Is the per-part `thoughtSignature` requirement correct for parallel function calls, or should Gemini 3 return a signature per parallel call (in which case the gap may be on the Gateway/Vertex pass-through side)? Happy to provide a full repro repo if useful.
